48.tq: Distinguish the formal head from the real executive using the aid-and-advice rule.
xs: The President is the **formal head** and acts on the **aid and advice** of the **Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister** — option **(3)** (**Art. 74(1)**).
Real power lies with the Council, **collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha** — so the President is not the "real executive".
xa: **Art. 53**: executive power **vests in the President**.
**Art. 163(1)**: the State Council of Ministers aids and advises the **Governor**, except in **discretionary** matters.
SC (**Apr 2026**): Governor **bound by state Cabinet advice** on remission under **Art. 161**.

48.s:
The executive power of the Union under Article 73 extends to which of the following?
1. Matters on which Parliament can make laws.
2. Rights and authority arising from treaties or agreements.
3. Matters confined exclusively to State List subjects in every circumstance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Article 73 covers matters on which Parliament can legislate and rights and authority under treaties or agreements. It does not ordinarily extend to matters confined exclusively to the State List.
48.tq: Split the scope provision into its positive components and reject the overbroad claim.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(3)**.
**Art. 73**: Union executive power extends to matters on which **Parliament can legislate** plus rights/authority under any **treaty or agreement**.
3 is wrong: **State List** matters belong to the State executive under **Art. 162**.
xa: On **Concurrent** subjects, executive power **stays with the states** unless the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly gives it to the Centre.
**Territorial spread** of executive power follows that of **legislative** power.

48.s: Article 154 of the Constitution vests the executive power of a State in the
48.x: Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor, who may exercise it directly or through subordinate officers.
48.tq: Discriminate between the constitutional vesting authority and the holder of real political power.
xs: **Art. 154** vests the State's executive power in the **Governor**, exercised directly or through subordinate officers — option **(4)**.
⚠ UPSC notes place it in the **Council of Ministers** — that is where **real power** lies, but the Article vests it in the Governor.
xa: **Art. 163(1)**: Council of Ministers aids and advises the Governor, except in **discretionary** matters.
**Art. 162**: extent — matters in the **State List**, within the State.
Union counterpart: **Art. 53** — vests in the **President**.

48.s: The executive power of a State under Article 162 ordinarily extends to matters on which the
o: State Legislature can legislate within the territory of the State
Union Parliament can legislate throughout India
48.x: Article 162 extends State executive power to matters on which the State Legislature has power to make laws, within the State's territory.
48.tq: Match the extent of executive power with the corresponding legislative competence.
xs: **Art. 162**: State executive power extends to matters on which the **State Legislature can legislate**, within the **State's territory** — option **(1)**.
Union counterpart: **Art. 73** — matters on which **Parliament** legislates, across **the whole of India**.
xa: Concurrent subjects: executive power **stays with the states**, unless the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides (**proviso to Art. 73 and Art. 162**).
**Territorial spread** of executive power follows **legislative** power.

48.s: Special responsibility for law and order is constitutionally provided for the Governors of
48.x: The Governor of Nagaland has special responsibility under Article 371A, and the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh under Article 371H, in relation to law and order.
48.tq: Use the article-number and State-pair association to resolve a close regional distractor.
xs: Special responsibility for **law and order** rests with the Governors of **Nagaland (Art. 371A)** and **Arunachal Pradesh (Art. 371H)** — option **(4)**.
Ordinarily the **Council of Ministers** aids and advises the Governor (**Art. 163(1)**), except in **discretionary** matters.
xa: SC: Governor **bound by state Cabinet advice** when granting remission under **Art. 161** (Apr 2026).
**Art. 154** vests State executive power in the **Governor**.
Ladakh's proposed model uses **Art. 371-like safeguards** instead of the Sixth Schedule (Jul 2026).

48.s: With reference to executive power over subjects in the Concurrent List, which one of the following is correct?
o: It is exercised jointly by the President and the Governor in every case.
It always belongs exclusively to the Union.
It ordinarily remains with the States, subject to constitutional or statutory exceptions.
It belongs exclusively to local governments.
48.x: The default rule is that executive power over Concurrent List subjects remains with the States. The Centre may exercise it where the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly provides for it.
48.tq: Test the default rule rather than the exception.
xs: Executive power over **Concurrent List** subjects **stays with the states**, subject to exceptions — option **(3)**.
The **Centre executes** only where the **Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly** gives it power (**proviso to Art. 73 and Art. 162**).
xa: **Art. 73**: Union executive covers matters in the **Union List** + **treaties**.
**Art. 162**: State executive covers matters in the **State List**.
**Art. 258(2)**: Parliament **by law** can confer duties on State officers — **no consent needed**.

48.s: The Union may exercise executive power over a Concurrent List subject when
o: the subject is declared to be a local-government matter
the Constitution or a law made by Parliament expressly confers that power
the Governor of every State gives prior consent
the State Legislature passes a resolution against it
48.x: The exception to the State default arises where the Constitution or a Parliamentary law expressly gives the executive power to the Centre, through the provisos to Articles 73 and 162.
48.tq: Apply the default-and-exception structure to a hypothetical exercise of power.
xs: The Union executes a Concurrent subject only where the **Constitution or a law made by Parliament expressly confers** that power — option **(2)**.
This is the **proviso to Art. 73 and Art. 162**; otherwise power **stays with the states**.
xa: **Art. 256/257**: States must comply with Union laws and not impede Union executive power.
Non-compliance → **Art. 365** → **Art. 356**.

48.s: The territorial spread of executive power generally follows the territorial spread of
48.x: The territorial extent of executive power follows that of legislative power. Thus, executive authority ordinarily operates over the same field and territory as the corresponding legislative competence.
48.tq: Test the legislative-executive correspondence principle.
xs: The territorial spread of executive power follows that of **legislative power** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 73** ties Union executive power to matters on which **Parliament** can legislate; **Art. 162** ties State executive power to the **State List**.
xa: Concurrent subjects: executive power **stays with the states** by default.
**Art. 53** vests Union power in the **President**; **Art. 154** vests State power in the **Governor**.

48.s: Which one of the following distinguishes Article 258(2) from Article 258(1)?
o: Article 258(2) permits Parliament by law to confer powers or duties on State officers without requiring State consent.
Article 258(2) applies only during a National Emergency.
Article 258(2) concerns agreements between States on river-valley projects.
Article 258(2) permits the Governor to transfer State functions to the Union.
48.x: Under Article 258(2), Parliament may confer powers or impose duties on State officers by law, and the State's consent is not required. Article 258(1), in contrast, involves Presidential entrustment with State consent.
48.tq: Compare two adjacent provisions by authority, direction and consent.
xs: **Art. 258(2)**: **Parliament by law** confers powers or duties on **State officers** — **no State consent needed** — option **(1)**.
**Art. 258(1)**: the **President**, **with the state's consent**, entrusts Union executive functions.
⚠ "River valley projects" is a wrong UPSC description of **258A**; State-to-Union entrustment is **258A**, not 258(2).
xa: **258A** = State entrusting functions to the **Union** (APPSC-GS 2023).
Critics say **Art. 258(2)** and **Art. 365** let the Union act in State administration **without consent**.

48.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. States must comply with laws made by Parliament under Article 256.
2. States must not impede or prejudice the exercise of the Union's executive power under Article 257.
3. Failure to comply with such directions may be treated as a breakdown of constitutional machinery under Article 365.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: All three statements are correct. Articles 256 and 257 impose obligations on States, and non-compliance may attract Article 365, which can open the way to action under Article 356.
48.tq: Link related constitutional provisions through their cause-and-effect chain.
xs: All three are correct — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**).
**Art. 256**: States must **comply with Union laws**; **Art. 257**: States must **not impede** Union executive power.
Non-compliance → breakdown of constitutional machinery under **Art. 365** → **Art. 356**.
xa: **Art. 365** and **Art. 258(2)** are criticised as letting the Union act **without state consent**.
Under **Art. 356**, the President takes over the State's executive functions; **High Court powers untouched**.

48.s: Article 258A of the Constitution deals with:
o: Agreements between States on river valley projects
Power of a State, with the consent of the Union Government, to entrust its functions to the Union
Entrustment of Union functions to States by Parliament without State consent
Directions of the Union to States during a Financial Emergency
48.x: Article 258A lets a State entrust its functions to the Union (APPSC-GS 2023). Calling it 'agreements between States on river valley projects' is a known wrong statement. Entrustment by Parliament without consent is Article 258(2), and Financial Emergency directions fall under Article 360.
48.tq: 258A = State → Union; 258(1)/(2) = Union → State
xs: **Art. 258A**: a **State** entrusts its **functions to the Union** — option **(2)** (APPSC-GS 2023).
⚠ UPSC notes call 258A "agreements between states on **river valley projects**" — **WRONG**.
**258(2)** (not 258A) lets Parliament confer duties on State officers without consent.
xa: **258(1)**: President, **with the state's consent**, entrusts Union functions to the State.
Financial Emergency directions come under **Art. 360**, not 258A.

48.s: Which one of the following is a correct effect of a National Emergency on executive relations?
o: The powers of the High Courts are transferred to the Union executive.
State governments are suspended and replaced by administrators.
The State Council of Ministers is dismissed in every State.
The Union may issue directions to States on any matter, but State governments are not thereby suspended.
48.x: Under Article 353, the Union's power to issue directions expands during a National Emergency, but State governments continue to exist and are not suspended merely because of the Emergency.
48.tq: Find the option that preserves the distinction between directions and takeover.
xs: In a National Emergency (**Art. 352**, via **Art. 353**), the Union can **give directions to any state on any matter**, but **state governments are not suspended** — option **(4)**.
Dismissal of the State Council of Ministers happens under **President's Rule (Art. 356)**, not National Emergency.
**High Court powers** are not transferred.
xa: ⚠ National Emergency = state governments **not suspended**; President's Rule = Council **dismissed**.
**Art. 360**: Centre directs **financial propriety**; **Money and Financial Bills** may be reserved for the President.

48.s:
Under Article 356, which of the following occurs when President's Rule is imposed in a State?
1. The President takes over the State's executive functions.
2. The State Council of Ministers is dismissed.
3. The powers of the State High Court are taken over by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Article 356 expressly leaves the powers of the State High Court untouched.
48.tq: Reject the overextension of President's Rule to constitutionally protected High Court powers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Under **Art. 356**, the **President takes over** the State's executive functions and the **State Council of Ministers is dismissed**.
3 is wrong: **High Court powers** remain **untouched**.
xa: Non-compliance with Union directions (**Art. 365**) can lead to **Art. 356**.
Contrast: National Emergency (**Art. 353**) does **not suspend** State governments.

48.s: Which one of the following is an additional possible effect of a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: All State laws are repealed automatically.
Money Bills and Financial Bills of States may be required to be reserved for the consideration of the President.
The President becomes the head of every State High Court.
48.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may require Money Bills and other Financial Bills of States to be reserved for the President's consideration.
48.tq: Test the specific legislative-financial consequence of Article 360.
xs: Under **Art. 360**, State **Money Bills and Financial Bills** may be required to be **reserved for the President** — option **(2)**.
The Centre can also direct States to observe **financial propriety**.
xa: National Emergency (**Art. 353**): directions to **any state on any matter**.
President's Rule (**Art. 356**): State Council of Ministers **dismissed**; **High Court powers untouched**.

48.s: In a Union Territory, executive power is ordinarily exercised by the
o: Chief Minister of the nearest State
Lieutenant Governor or Administrator as the President's representative
Union Home Minister directly in every matter
48.x: The Lieutenant Governor or Administrator exercises executive power in a Union Territory as the representative of the President.
48.tq: Distinguish the Union Territory executive head from State constitutional offices.
xs: In a UT, executive power is exercised by the **Lieutenant Governor or Administrator** as the **President's representative** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 239**: UTs are administered by the **President through an Administrator**.
xa: **LGs**: **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, **J&K**, **Ladakh**, **Andaman & Nicobar**.
**Administrators**: **Chandigarh** (Punjab Governor), **Lakshadweep**, **Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu**.
**Delhi — Art. 239AA (69th Amendment, 1991)**: Legislative Assembly + Council of Ministers; **public order, police and land** outside its power.

48.s:
Which one of the following correctly identifies the Union Territories headed by Administrators rather than Lieutenant Governors?
1. Chandigarh
2. Lakshadweep
3. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu are headed by Administrators. The Administrator of Chandigarh is the Governor of Punjab.
48.tq: Use the administrator-versus-Lieutenant Governor classification to eliminate mixed lists.
xs: All three — **Chandigarh**, **Lakshadweep**, **Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu** — have **Administrators** — option **(4)**.
The **Punjab Governor** is Chandigarh's Administrator.
xa: **LGs** head **Delhi**, **Puducherry**, **J&K**, **Ladakh**, **Andaman & Nicobar**.
⚠ **Andaman & Nicobar** has an **LG**, whereas **Lakshadweep** has an **Administrator**.
**Art. 239**: UTs administered by the **President through an Administrator**.

48.s: Article 239AA, relating to the special constitutional arrangement for Delhi, was inserted by the
48.x: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991 inserted Article 239AA and provided Delhi with a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers.
48.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its amendment number and year.
xs: **Art. 239AA** (Delhi) was inserted by the **69th Amendment, 1991** — option **(3)**.
It gave Delhi a **Legislative Assembly** and **Council of Ministers**.
xa: **Public order**, **police** and **land** are outside the Assembly's power.
Delhi is headed by an **LG**.
**Art. 239**: UTs administered by the **President through an Administrator**.

48.s:
Under Article 239AA, which of the following subjects are outside the legislative competence of the Legislative Assembly of Delhi?
1. Public order
2. Police
3. Land
4. Public health
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
48.x: Public order, police and land are excluded from the legislative competence of Delhi's Legislative Assembly under Article 239AA. Public health is not included in that excluded trio.
48.tq: Test the exact three-subject exclusion rather than accepting an expanded list.
xs: **Public order**, **police** and **land** are outside the Delhi Assembly's power — **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
**Public health** is not among the excluded subjects.
xa: **Art. 239AA** inserted by the **69th Amendment, 1991**.
Delhi has a **Legislative Assembly** + **Council of Ministers**.
⚠ In States, **public order** and **police** are State List subjects.

48.s:
Which of the following institutions are provided for Delhi under Article 239AA?
1. Legislative Assembly
2. Council of Ministers
3. State Legislative Council
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Article 239AA provides Delhi with a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers. It does not provide for a State Legislative Council.
48.tq: Separate the institutions expressly created from a nearby but absent legislative body.
xs: **Art. 239AA** provides a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** — **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
There is no **Legislative Council** for Delhi.
xa: Inserted by the **69th Amendment, 1991**.
**Public order, police and land** are outside the Assembly's power.
Delhi is among the UTs headed by an **LG**.

48.s: The proposed special institutional arrangement for Ladakh is intended to provide it with an elected body possessing
o: judicial powers equivalent to a High Court
only advisory powers over local administration
legislative, executive and financial powers without granting Statehood
the same status as a Union Territory with a legislature
48.x: The proposed sui generis elected body for Ladakh is intended to possess legislative, executive and financial powers. It would be neither a State nor a Union Territory with a legislature.
48.tq: Distinguish a special constitutional arrangement from both Statehood and an existing UT model.
xs: Ladakh's proposed body is a **sui generis elected body** with **legislative, executive and financial powers**, without **Statehood** — option **(3)**.
It is neither a State nor a **UT with a legislature** (Chief Secretary, **11 Sep 2026**).
xa: MHA and Ladakh groups finalised a model with **Art. 371-like safeguards** instead of the **Sixth Schedule** (Jul 2026).
Ladakh is currently a UT headed by an **LG**.

48.s: The model proposed for safeguarding Ladakh's interests is described as being based on
o: Article 371-like safeguards instead of the Sixth Schedule
48.x: The proposed model for Ladakh is based on safeguards similar to those under Article 371, rather than the Sixth Schedule.
48.tq: Discriminate between two constitutional protection models mentioned in connection with the same region.
xs: The Ladakh model rests on **Art. 371-like safeguards instead of the Sixth Schedule** — option **(4)** (Jul 2026).
It was finalised by the **MHA** and Ladakh groups.
xa: The proposed body is **sui generis** — legislative, executive and financial powers, without Statehood.
**Art. 371A** (**Nagaland**) and **371H** (**Arunachal Pradesh**) give Governors special responsibility for law and order.

48.s: In relation to remission under Article 161, the Supreme Court has held that the Governor is bound by the advice of the
48.x: The Governor must act on the advice of the State Cabinet while exercising the remission power under Article 161.
48.tq: Identify the correct advising authority in a State executive function.
xs: The SC held the Governor **bound by State Cabinet advice** — the **State Council of Ministers** — when granting **remission** under **Art. 161** (**Apr 2026**) — option **(3)**.
**Art. 163(1)**: the Council aids and advises the Governor, except in **discretionary** matters.
xa: Governors skipping the **address to the legislature** test constitutional limits (Jan 2026).
Precedents: **Shamsher Singh (1974)**, **Nabam Rebia (2016)**.

48.s:
Which of the following constitutional developments has been associated with Governors and State legislatures?
1. Questions have arisen when Governors skip the address to the legislature.
2. Shamsher Singh (1974) and Nabam Rebia (2016) are relevant judicial precedents in debates on gubernatorial discretion.
3. A Governor may disregard the State Cabinet's advice in every matter involving the legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
48.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Governor's discretion is not unlimited and the Governor ordinarily acts on the aid and advice of the State Council of Ministers.
48.tq: Reject the absolute claim about discretionary power while retaining the judicial and constitutional context.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: Governors **skipping the address** to the legislature test constitutional limits (**24-26 Jan 2026**).
2: **Shamsher Singh (1974)** and **Nabam Rebia (2016)** are the cited precedents.
3 is wrong: the Governor acts on Council advice (**Art. 163(1)**) except in **discretionary** matters.
xa: SC (**Apr 2026**): Governor **bound by state Cabinet advice** on remission under **Art. 161**.
**Art. 154** vests State executive power in the **Governor**.

48.s:
Which provisions are criticised as enabling the Union to act in State administration without the State's consent?
1. Article 258(2)
2. Article 365
3. Article 258(1)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
48.x: Articles 258(2) and 365 are identified in this context. Article 258(1) requires the State's consent for the President's entrustment of Union functions to the State and is not included in this criticism.
48.tq: Separate provisions by their consent requirement and constitutional effect.
xs: **Art. 258(2)** and **Art. 365** let the Union act in State administration **without state consent** — **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
**Art. 258(1)** requires the **state's consent**, so it is not criticised on this ground.
xa: **258(2)**: Parliament **by law** confers duties on State officers.
**Art. 365**: non-compliance with Union directions → breakdown → **Art. 356**.
**258A**: State entrusts functions to the **Union**.

49.s: Under Article 312 of the Constitution, Parliament may create a new All India Service when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by:
o: A majority of the members present and voting
A simple majority of the total membership
Two-thirds of the members present and voting
49.x: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting before Parliament can create a new All India Service.
49.tq: Check the exact constitutional majority instead of confusing present-and-voting with total membership.
xs: **Art. 312** needs a **Rajya Sabha** resolution by **2/3 of members present and voting** — option **(4)**.
Only then may Parliament create a new All India Service, including an **All India Judicial Service**.
xa: Existing AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS** (Indian Forest Service).
Governed by the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
Suggestion: create new AIS for **health and education**.

49.s: Which one of the following services is specifically mentioned in Article 312 as capable of being created as an All India Service?
49.x: Article 312 expressly includes the possibility of creating an All India Judicial Service.
49.tq: Identify the constitutionally named service rather than an existing Central Service.
xs: **Art. 312** expressly allows an **All India Judicial Service** — option **(4)**.
The **Indian Foreign Service** is a **Central Service**, not an AIS.
xa: Creation needs a **Rajya Sabha** resolution by **2/3 of members present and voting**.
Existing AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**; **Indian Forest Service** created **1966**.
⚠ **IFoS** = Indian Forest Service (AIS); **IFS** = Indian Foreign Service (Central Service).

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the existing All India Services:
1. The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966.
2. The Indian Foreign Service is an All India Service.
3. The Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service are All India Services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: The Indian Forest Service was created in 1966, and IAS and IPS are All India Services. The Indian Foreign Service is a Central Service, not an All India Service.
49.tq: Separate the AIS list from the nearby example of a Central Service.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Indian Forest Service** created **1966**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Indian Foreign Service** is a **Central Service**.
Statement 3 correct: **IAS** and **IPS** are AIS — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: ⚠ **IFoS** = Indian Forest Service (AIS); **IFS** = Indian Foreign Service (Central Service).
**ICS** restructured as **IAS in 1947**.
**Indian Revenue Service (IRS)** is also a **Central Service** — Union subjects only.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes All India Services from Central Services?
o: All India Services are common to the Union and States, whereas Central Services relate to Union subjects only.
Central Services necessarily serve in State cadres, whereas All India Services serve only in Union ministries.
All India Services are confined to Union subjects, whereas Central Services are common to the Union and States.
Both categories are recruited only by State Public Service Commissions.
49.x: All India Services are common to the Union and the States, while Central Services are associated with Union subjects only.
49.tq: Use the comparison table by splitting the two categories on their field of service.
xs: **All India Services** are **common to Union and states**; **Central Services** handle **Union subjects only** — option **(1)**.
AIS are recruited by **UPSC**, not State PSCs.
xa: AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**; Central Services: e.g. **Indian Foreign Service**, **IRS**.
State civil and police services = **State Services**.
PYQ 2007 asked this "common to Union and states" point.

49.s:
With reference to All India Services, consider the following statements:
1. Officers are recruited by the Union Public Service Commission on an all-India basis.
2. They serve in State cadres.
3. The Centre recruits and trains them, while they serve under the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements correctly describe the recruitment, training, cadre allocation and service arrangement of All India Service officers.
49.tq: When all statements describe complementary stages of one institutional arrangement, test the complete combination.
xs: All three correct: recruited by **UPSC** on an **all-India basis**; serve in **state cadres**; **Centre recruits and trains** them — option **(4)**.
Yet they can be **dismissed or removed only by the Union government**.
xa: Governed by **All India Services Act, 1951**.
Federal critique: officers governed by **Central rules**; states lack full control.
**UPSC** replaced the Federal PSC in **1950**.

49.s: Who is associated with describing All India Services as the “Steel Frame” of India?
o: The Chairman of the Finance Commission
The Chairman of the Federal Public Service Commission
49.x: Sardar Patel championed the All India Services and referred to them as the “Steel Frame” of India.
49.tq: Match the distinctive expression with the person associated with it.
xs: **Sardar Patel** championed AIS as the "**Steel Frame**" — option **(2)**.
He backed them as services common to the Union and states.
xa: **ICS** restructured as **IAS in 1947**.
**UPSC** replaced the **Federal PSC** in **1950**.
**Indian Forest Service** created **1966**.

49.s: Which of the following proposals has been made for expanding the scope of All India Services?
o: Restriction of All India Services to Union subjects
Replacement of UPSC recruitment by local recruitment
Abolition of the Indian Administrative Service
Creation of new All India Services for health and education
49.x: A proposal has been made to create new All India Services for health and education.
49.tq: Identify the constructive expansion proposal rather than an absolute or abolition-based distractor.
xs: The suggestion is to create **new AIS for health and education** — option **(4)**.
New AIS need a **Rajya Sabha** resolution by **2/3 of members present and voting** (**Art. 312**).
xa: Art. 312 also enables an **All India Judicial Service**.
Existing AIS: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**.
Federal critique: AIS **restrict state autonomy**.

49.s: Why are All India Services sometimes criticised from the federal perspective?
o: Their officers are governed by Central rules and States lack full control over them.
They are confined entirely to local government administration.
They are recruited exclusively by State Public Service Commissions.
They have no connection with the Union Government.
49.x: The federal criticism is that Central rules govern the officers and States do not exercise full control over them, thereby restricting State autonomy.
49.tq: Apply the federal-autonomy principle to identify the institutional source of friction.
xs: AIS officers are governed by **Central rules** and **states lack full control** — option **(1)**.
So they are a **unitary feature** restricting state autonomy.
xa: **APPSC-G2 2025**: A and R both true, R explains A.
Removal only by the **Union government** (PYQ 2017, 2019).
**IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954** amendments: central deputation **without state or officer consent**.

49.s: The proposed amendments to the All India Services (Cadre) Rules, 1954 were associated with which issue?
o: Compulsory retirement of all AIS officers by State Governments
Central deputation without the consent of the State or the officer
Replacement of UPSC recruitment by direct State recruitment
Abolition of State cadres for All India Services
49.x: The proposed amendments would enable the Centre to order central deputation without the consent of the State Government or the officer, with the Centre's order becoming final after a prescribed time.
49.tq: Focus on the authority and consent issue in the cadre-rule proposal.
xs: **IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954** amendments let the Centre order **central deputation without state or officer consent** — option **(2)**.
The Centre's order becomes **final after a set time**.
xa: Criticism: **unilateral** central deputation hurts state bureaucracy's **morale**.
AIS are a **unitary feature**; states lack full control.
Removal only by the **Union government**.

49.s:
Arrange the following provisions in chronological order of their constitutional amendment or institutional origin:
A. Creation of the Indian Forest Service
B. Insertion of Article 258A
C. Replacement of the Federal Public Service Commission by UPSC
D. Restructuring of ICS as IAS
49.x: The correct sequence is IAS restructuring in 1947, UPSC replacing the Federal PSC in 1950, insertion of Article 258A in 1956, and creation of IFoS in 1966.
49.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then place the 1950 and 1956 events between them.
xs: **ICS → IAS (1947)** → **UPSC replaces Federal PSC (1950)** → **Art. 258A (7th CAA, 1956)** → **IFoS (1966)** — **D, C, B, A**, option **(1)**.
258A lets a **Governor** entrust state functions to the Union with GoI consent.
xa: **Sardar Patel** called AIS the "**Steel Frame**".
AIS are governed by the **All India Services Act, 1951**.
**ARC** was also set up in **1966**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Indian Foreign Service from the Indian Forest Service?
o: The former is a Central Service and the latter is an All-India Service.
The former is an All-India Service and the latter is a Central Service.
49.x: The Indian Foreign Service is classified as a Central Service, whereas the Indian Forest Service is an All-India Service.
49.tq: Compare look-alike service names by focusing on their exact category.
xs: **Indian Foreign Service (IFS)** = **Central Service**; **Indian Forest Service (IFoS)** = **All-India Service** — option **(1)**.
Central Services handle **Union subjects only**; AIS are **common to Union and states**.
xa: IFoS created **1966**.
Other AIS: **IAS**, **IPS**.
**IRS** is a Central Service.

49.s: A member of an All India Service serving in a State cadre can be dismissed or removed from service only by:
o: The State Government in whose cadre the officer serves
The Governor on the advice of the State Public Service Commission
49.x: An All India Service officer can be dismissed or removed only by the Union Government, even though he serves under the State. The State Government and the Governor cannot remove him, and the UPSC only recruits; it is not the removing authority.
49.tq: Serves the State, removed only by the Union.
xs: An AIS officer can be **dismissed or removed only by the Union Government** — option **(2)**.
Not by the **state** whose cadre he serves; **UPSC** only recruits.
xa: Asked in **PYQ 2017, 2019** and **APPSC-G1 2019**.
The **Centre recruits and trains**; officers serve in **state cadres**.
Federal critique: states **lack full control**.

49.s: Which Article requires that the executive power of every State be exercised so as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament?
49.x: Article 256 requires State executive power to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament and permits the Union to issue directions for that purpose.
49.tq: Discriminate between the two adjacent Articles dealing with Union directions to States.
xs: **Article 256**: states must exercise executive power **in compliance with Parliament's laws**; Union may direct — option **(1)**.
**Art. 257** = do **not impede the Union**; **Art. 365** = failure to follow directions; **Art. 258** = delegation.
xa: Under **Art. 257** the Centre directs on **means of communication** and protection of **railways**.
**Art. 365** → **President's Rule (Art. 356)**.
During **National Emergency**, directions may be on **any matter**.

49.s:
Under Article 257, the Union may issue directions to a State regarding:
1. Means of communication of national or military importance.
2. Protection of railways within the State.
3. All matters relating to public order in the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Article 257 covers communications of national or military importance and protection of railways. Public order is not included in the listed Article 257 direction powers.
49.tq: Find the one State List subject improperly added to the specific Article 257 powers.
xs: Statements 1, 2 correct: **Art. 257** directions cover **means of communication** of national or military importance and **railways** protection.
Statement 3 wrong: **public order** is a **State List** subject — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Art. 257: state executive must **not impede the Union**.
**Art. 339**: welfare schemes for **STs**; **Art. 350A**: **mother-tongue** instruction.
Non-compliance → **Art. 365** → **Art. 356**.

49.s: A State Government persistently fails to comply with directions issued by the Union under the constitutional scheme. Which provision enables the President to hold that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution?
49.x: Article 365 permits the President to hold that a State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution when the State fails to comply with Union directions. This can open the way to action under Article 356.
49.tq: Trace the consequence chain: non-compliance with Union directions first engages Article 365, which may lead to Article 356.
xs: **Article 365**: if a state fails to follow Union directions, the President may hold its government **cannot be carried on per the Constitution** — option **(1)**.
That opens the way to **President's Rule (Art. 356)**; **Art. 339** is ST welfare, **258** delegation.
xa: Asked in **PYQ 2017, 2018**.
Criticism: **Art. 258(2)** and **Art. 365** let the Union act without state consent.
**Art. 256**: compliance with **Parliament's laws**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the Article with the subject of Union direction?
o: Article 339 — instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
Article 257 — communications of national or military importance
Article 365 — delegation of Union functions to State officers by consent
Article 350A — welfare schemes for Scheduled Tribes
49.x: Article 257 concerns directions relating to communications of national or military importance. Article 339 concerns Scheduled Tribe welfare, Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction, and Article 365 concerns failure to comply with Union directions.
49.tq: Use the Article–subject pairing and eliminate swapped constitutional provisions.
xs: **Art. 257** — **communications of national or military importance** is correct — option **(2)**.
**Art. 339** = **ST welfare** schemes; **Art. 350A** = **mother-tongue** instruction; **Art. 365** = failure to follow directions → President's Rule.
xa: Art. 257 also covers protection of **railways**.
**Art. 256**: states comply with **Parliament's laws**.
National Emergency: directions on **any matter**.

49.s: Under Article 258(1), functions of the Union may be entrusted to a State Government or its officers by:
o: The President, with the consent of the State Government
The Governor, without the consent of the Union Government
The Supreme Court, with the consent of the President
Parliament, only with the consent of the State Legislature
49.x: Article 258(1) empowers the President to entrust Union functions to a State Government or its officers with the consent of the State Government.
49.tq: Ask who entrusts the function and whether consent is required; these are the main Article 258(1) traps.
xs: **Art. 258(1)**: the **President**, **with state consent**, entrusts Union functions to a state — option **(1)**.
⚠ Trap: APP writes "Parliament" — it is the **President**.
xa: **258(2)**: Union **by law**, **without consent**.
**258A**: **Governor** entrusts state functions to the Union with **GoI consent**.
Purpose: avoid **rigidity and deadlock**.

49.s: Which one of the following is the correct position under Article 258A?
o: The Governor entrusts State functions to the Union with the consent of the Government of India.
Parliament entrusts Union functions to States with State consent.
The Union Cabinet entrusts State functions to the Governor without consent.
The President entrusts State functions to the Union without consent.
49.x: Article 258A enables the Governor to entrust functions of the State to the Union or its officers with the consent of the Government of India.
49.tq: Reverse the direction of delegation carefully: Article 258A deals with State-to-Union entrustment.
xs: **Art. 258A**: the **Governor** entrusts **state functions to the Union** with **GoI consent** — option **(1)**.
Inserted by the **7th CAA, 1956**; asked in **APPSC-GS 2023**.
xa: ⚠ UPSC notes swap the headings of 258 and 258A.
**258(1)**: President, **with state consent**; **258(2)**: Parliament **by law without consent**.
Purpose: avoid **rigidity and deadlock**.

49.s: Article 258A was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
49.x: Article 258A was inserted by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
49.tq: Link the Article with the specific amendment year while avoiding the nearby 42nd Amendment association.
xs: **Art. 258A** was inserted by the **Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956** (7th CAA) — option **(3)**.
It lets the **Governor** entrust state functions to the Union with **GoI consent**.
xa: **42nd CAA, 1976** inserted **Art. 323A** and **Entry 2A** of the Union List.
**States Reorganisation Act** was passed in **November 1956**.
**258(1)** notification is a **legislative act**, specific or general.

49.s: The principal constitutional purpose of delegation under Articles 258 and 258A is to:
o: Transfer all State executive powers to Parliament
Make every State function subject to prior judicial approval
Avoid rigidity and deadlock in administration
Abolish the distinction between Union and State subjects
49.x: Delegation under these Articles provides flexibility in administration and helps avoid rigidity and deadlock between the Union and the States.
49.tq: Identify the functional purpose of a constitutional mechanism rather than its formal procedure.
xs: Delegation under **Arts. 258 and 258A** aims to **avoid rigidity and deadlock** — option **(3)**.
It does not transfer all state powers or abolish the Union-State division.
xa: **258(1)**: President, **with state consent**.
**258(2)**: Parliament **by law**, no consent.
**258A**: state entrusts functions to the Union with the **Centre's consent**.

49.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding entrustment of executive functions:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 258(1)
B. Article 258(2)
C. Article 258A

List-II (Arrangement)
1. State entrusts functions to the Union with the consent of the Centre
2. President entrusts Union functions to a State with the State's consent
3. Parliament confers powers or duties on State officers by law without requiring State consent

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
49.x: Article 258(1) concerns Union-to-State entrustment by the President with State consent; Article 258(2) concerns Parliamentary entrustment by law without consent; Article 258A concerns State-to-Union entrustment with the Centre's consent.
49.tq: Start from the direction of transfer and then verify the consent requirement.
xs: **258(1)** = **President** entrusts with **state consent** (2); **258(2)** = Parliament **by law without consent** (3); **258A** = **state to Union** (1) — **A-2, B-3, C-1**, option **(1)**.
258A came by the **7th CAA, 1956**.
xa: ⚠ Trap: APP writes "Parliament" for 258(1) — it is the **President**.
Purpose: avoid **rigidity and deadlock**.
258A was the **APPSC-GS 2023** answer.

49.s: Which of the following statements regarding deployment of armed or central forces in a State is correct?
o: Such deployment is prohibited because public order and police are Union List subjects.
The Union can deploy them only after obtaining the State Government's consent.
Only the State Legislature can authorise their deployment.
The Union may deploy them with or without the State's consent in discharge of its Article 355 duty.
49.x: The Union may deploy armed or central forces with or without State consent in discharge of its duty under Article 355.
49.tq: Test the consent issue directly and distinguish constitutional duty from State List allocation.
xs: The Centre may deploy forces **with or without state consent** for its **Art. 355** duty — option **(4)**.
**Public order and police** are **State List**, not Union List — hence the states' objection.
xa: Basis: **Entry 2A, Union List** (**42nd CAA**).
**ARC (1966)** backed deployment "**on their request or otherwise**".
~**13,000** CAPF officers in the CAPF dispute.

49.s: The constitutional basis associated with Union deployment of armed or central forces in States is:
o: Entry 2A of the Union List, inserted through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment
Entry 97 of the Concurrent List, inserted through the First Amendment
Entry 1 of the State List, inserted through the Seventh Amendment
Entry 2 of the State List, inserted through the 44th Amendment
49.x: Entry 2A of the Union List, associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, provides the relevant Union List basis for deployment.
49.tq: Match the entry, list and amendment together instead of relying on the general subject of policing.
xs: **Entry 2A, Union List**, inserted by the **42nd CAA**, is the basis — option **(1)**.
**Public order** and **police** are **State List Entries 1, 2**.
xa: Deployment is for the Centre's **Art. 355** duty, **with or without state consent**.
**ARC (1966)**: "on their request or otherwise".
The **42nd CAA, 1976** also inserted **Art. 323A**.

49.s: Why do States object to the Union's deployment of armed or central forces without their consent?
o: All emergency powers are exclusively State powers.
Public order and police are State List subjects.
Railways and military affairs are State List subjects.
Defence and communications are State List subjects.
49.x: States object because public order and police fall in Entries 1 and 2 of the State List, making deployment a sensitive issue concerning State authority.
49.tq: Identify the specific State List subjects rather than broader security-related subjects.
xs: **Public order and police** are **State List** subjects (**Entries 1, 2**) — option **(2)**.
Railways, defence and communications are not State subjects.
xa: Centre deploys under **Entry 2A, Union List** for its **Art. 355** duty.
**ARC (1966)** backed deployment "**on their request or otherwise**".
Under **Art. 257** the Centre may direct states on protection of **railways**.

49.s: The Administrative Reforms Commission of 1966 supported deployment of forces by the Centre:
o: Only after a resolution of the State Legislature
On the request of the State or otherwise
Only when the Governor requests it
49.x: The 1966 Administrative Reforms Commission supported deployment “on their request or otherwise,” meaning that a State request was not treated as indispensable.
49.tq: Test the precise wording of the recommendation, especially the alternative expressed by “or otherwise.”
xs: **ARC (1966)** backed deployment "**on their request or otherwise**" — option **(2)**.
So a state request is not essential.
xa: ARC chaired by **Morarji Desai**, then **K. Hanumanthaiya**.
ARC urged an **Inter-State Council** and **non-partisan Governors**.
Basis of deployment: **Entry 2A, Union List** (**42nd CAA**).

49.s: Which recent development concerning Central Armed Police Forces is correctly stated?
o: A 2025 Supreme Court order abolished all CAPF cadres and transferred them to State police forces.
The Supreme Court directed that CAPF officers must be deputed only to State cadres.
The Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill had already abolished the CAPF system in 2025.
A 2025 Supreme Court order granted CAPF officers Organised Group A status and sought to reduce IPS deputation.
49.x: The 2025 Supreme Court order referred to granting CAPF officers Organised Group A status and reducing IPS deputation. A Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill was expected in response.
49.tq: Separate the actual institutional reform from exaggerated abolition or transfer claims.
xs: A **2025 SC order** granted CAPF officers **Organised Group A** status and **reduced IPS deputation** — option **(4)**.
The Centre has **not implemented** it; a **Central Armed Forces (General Administration) Bill** is expected.
xa: About **13,000** CAPF officers are involved.
The proposed Bill was reported on **13 Mar 2026**.
**IPS** is an **All India Service**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the legal basis and appointment procedure of a Joint State Public Service Commission?
o: It is created by a Presidential order and its members are appointed by the Governor
It is created by an Act of Parliament and its members are appointed by the President
It is created by a State law and its members are appointed by the Chief Ministers concerned
It is created by the UPSC and its members are appointed by the Union Home Minister
49.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created through an Act of Parliament, while its members are appointed by the President.
49.tq: Separate the authority that creates a body from the authority that appoints its members.
xs: A **JSPSC** is created by an **Act of Parliament**; members are appointed by the **President** — option **(2)**.
**Art. 315**: a JSPSC for 2+ states if their **legislatures so resolve**.
xa: Art. 315 also provides **UPSC** and an **SPSC** for each state.
⚠ JSPSC = **Act of Parliament**; CAT = **Art. 323A**.
**UPSC** replaced the **Federal PSC** in **1950**.

49.s: Article 323A, inserted by which Constitutional Amendment, deals with administrative tribunals for the Union and the States?
49.x: Article 323A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, to provide for administrative tribunals.
49.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its exact amendment year.
xs: **Art. 323A** was inserted by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976** — option **(3)**.
It provides tribunals for Union and states, individually or **jointly**.
xa: **CAT**: **Administrative Tribunals Act 1985**.
CAT: principal bench **New Delhi** + **18 benches**; **69 members**.
The **42nd CAA** also inserted **Entry 2A** of the Union List.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT):
1. It was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
2. Its principal bench is located at New Delhi.
3. It has 18 benches and 69 members, including 35 judicial and 34 administrative members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. The CAT was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, has its principal bench at New Delhi, and is described here as having 18 benches and 69 members.
49.tq: Check the institution, location and numerical composition separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three correct: CAT under the **Administrative Tribunals Act 1985**; principal bench **New Delhi**; **18 benches**, **69 members** (**35 judicial + 34 administrative**) — option **(4)**.
CAT rests on **Art. 323A** (**42nd CAA, 1976**).
xa: **10th All India CAT Conference** held **Sep 2025**.
Tribunals may be set up for Union and states, individually or **jointly**.
⚠ JSPSC = by **Act of Parliament**; CAT = **Art. 323A**.

49.s: Which edition of the All India Conference of the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was held in September 2025?
49.x: The 10th All India CAT Conference was held in September 2025.
49.tq: CAT turned 40 in 2025; its conference reached number 10.
xs: The **10th** All India CAT Conference was held in **Sep 2025** — option **(3)**.
It is listed under current relevance with the CAPF dispute.
xa: CAT: **69 members** = **35 judicial + 34 administrative**.
Principal bench **New Delhi** + **18 benches**.
Parent Act: **Administrative Tribunals Act 1985**.

49.s: The authority that may be established under Article 307 is associated with
49.x: Article 307 provides for an authority to carry out the purposes of the constitutional provisions relating to trade, commerce and intercourse within India.
49.tq: Link the Article number with the specific federal function it supports.
xs: **Art. 307** provides an **inter-state trade authority** — option **(1)**.
It is a **constitutional device** of cooperation, with **Art. 263** and **Art. 262**.
xa: **Inter-State Council** = **Art. 263**; **water disputes** = **Art. 262**.
Extra-constitutional devices: **NDC**, **NE Council**, **Governors' Conference**, **CMs' Conference**.
Administrative tribunals = **Art. 323A**.

49.s: Grants under Article 275 are specifically associated with
o: the salaries of Members of Parliament
the conduct of elections to State Legislatures
Scheduled Tribe welfare and administration of Scheduled Areas
49.x: Article 275 provides grants for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and the administration of Scheduled Areas.
49.tq: Match the grant provision with its targeted administrative and welfare purpose.
xs: **Art. 275** grants are for **ST welfare** and **Scheduled Area administration** — option **(4)**.
They are listed among cooperation devices in Centre-State relations.
xa: **Art. 339**: Union directions on **welfare schemes for STs**.
**Art. 261**: **full faith and credit** to public acts, records, judicial proceedings.
Constitutional devices: **ISC (Art. 263)**, **Art. 262**, **Art. 307**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It was established in 1966.
2. It was initially chaired by Morarji Desai.
3. K. Hanumanthaiya subsequently chaired it.
4. M.C. Setalvad headed its study team in 1969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All four statements are correct. The ARC was established in 1966, initially chaired by Morarji Desai, later by K. Hanumanthaiya, and its study team was headed by M.C. Setalvad in 1969.
49.tq: Treat dates, succession of chairpersons and the study-team detail as separate statement checks.
xs: All correct: **ARC (1966)**; chaired by **Morarji Desai**, then **K. Hanumanthaiya**; **M.C. Setalvad** study team (**1969**) — option **(4)**.
It urged an **Inter-State Council** and **non-partisan Governors**.
xa: ARC backed force deployment "**on their request or otherwise**".
**Sarkaria (June 1983)**: **247 recommendations**; permanent ISC.
Sarkaria members: **R.S. Sarkaria**, **B. Sivaraman**, **S.R. Sen**.

49.s:
Which of the following was recommended by the Administrative Reforms Commission mentioned in the context of Centre-State administration?
1. Establishment of an Inter-State Council
2. Appointment of non-partisan Governors
3. Abolition of all advisory bodies
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
49.x: The ARC urged the establishment of an Inter-State Council and the appointment of non-partisan Governors. It did not recommend abolition of all advisory bodies.
49.tq: Find the one overbroad statement that reverses the character of the recommendations.
xs: Statements 1, 2 correct: the ARC urged an **Inter-State Council** and **non-partisan Governors**.
Statement 3 wrong: the notes record no call to abolish advisory bodies — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: ARC (**1966**): **Morarji Desai**, then **K. Hanumanthaiya**; **M.C. Setalvad** study team (1969).
**Sarkaria** too recommended a **permanent ISC**.
**ISC** today **meets rarely**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the Sarkaria Commission:
1. It was set up in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria.
2. It made 247 recommendations.
3. It recommended a temporary Inter-State Council to be convened only during emergencies.
4. It recommended that Article 356 be used sparingly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the Commission was set up in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria (with B. Sivaraman and S.R. Sen), made 247 recommendations and urged sparing use of Article 356. Statement 3 is wrong: it recommended a permanent Inter-State Council. Hence A omits statement 4, and C and D wrongly include statement 3.
49.tq: Sarkaria = 1983, 247 recommendations, PERMANENT ISC, 356 sparingly.
xs: Statements 1, 2 correct: **Sarkaria** set up **June 1983** under Justice **R.S. Sarkaria**; **247 recommendations**.
Statement 3 wrong: it recommended a **permanent ISC**.
Statement 4 correct: use **Art. 356 sparingly** — so **1, 2 and 4 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Other members: **B. Sivaraman**, **S.R. Sen**.
**ARC (1966)** had also urged an **Inter-State Council**.
**ISC** = constitutional device under **Art. 263**.

49.s: Article 261 of the Constitution provides for which of the following?
o: Uniformity of service conditions in All-India Services
Distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States
Full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings
Adjudication of inter-State river water disputes
49.x: Article 261 requires full faith and credit throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State.
49.tq: Directly match the Article with its constitutional principle.
xs: **Art. 261**: **full faith and credit** throughout India to **public acts, records and judicial proceedings** — option **(3)**.
Water disputes = **Art. 262**; asked in **APPSC-GS 2023**.
xa: **Art. 261(3)**: final civil court judgments can be **executed anywhere** in India.
**Integrated judiciary**: HC judges appointed by the President consulting **CJI + Governor**.
A **common HC** for 2+ states is possible.

49.s: A final civil court judgment delivered in one State is sought to be executed in another State. Which constitutional provision facilitates this?
49.x: Article 261(3) provides that final judgments and orders of civil courts in any part of India may be executed anywhere within India according to law.
49.tq: Apply the constitutional rule to a concrete inter-State enforcement situation.
xs: **Article 261(3)**: final civil court judgments can be **executed anywhere** in India — option **(2)**.
**Art. 262** = water disputes; **Art. 263** = Inter-State Council; **Art. 256** = compliance with Parliament's laws.
xa: **Art. 261**: **full faith and credit** to public acts, records, judicial proceedings (APPSC-GS 2023).
**Integrated judiciary**: common HC for 2+ states possible.
**Art. 307**: inter-state trade authority.

49.s: Which one of the following extra-constitutional devices of Centre-State cooperation is presided over by the President?
49.x: The Governors' Conference is presided over by the President. The Chief Ministers' Conference is presided over by the Prime Minister; the Chief Secretaries' Conference and the Central Council for Local Government are other extra-constitutional devices not chaired by the President.
49.tq: Governors meet the President; CMs meet the PM.
xs: The **Governors' Conference** is chaired by the **President** — option **(2)**.
⚠ The **CMs' Conference** is chaired by the **PM**.
xa: Other extra-constitutional devices: **NDC**, **Central Council of Health**, **Central Council for Local Government**, **NE Council**, **Chief Secretaries' Conference**.
Constitutional devices: **ISC (Art. 263)**, **Art. 262**, **Art. 307**.
**ISC** meets rarely.

49.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five Zonal Councils established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
49.x: The five councils are Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern. The North-Eastern Council was created separately under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971.
49.tq: Find the body created under a separate law rather than under the 1956 Act.
xs: There is **no North-Eastern Zonal Council** — option **(1)**.
The **5 councils** are **Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern**; the **NEC** came under a separate **NEC Act, 1971**.
xa: NEC **2002 amendment** added **Sikkim** and made it a **regional planning body**.
Since **2018** the **Union Home Minister** is ex-officio NEC Chairman.
Zonal Councils were proposed by **Nehru** in **1956**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements about the composition of Zonal Councils:
1. Each member State sends its Chief Minister and two Ministers.
2. Administrators or Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories are included.
3. Advisers such as Chief Secretaries have voting rights in the Councils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: Each State is represented by its Chief Minister and two Ministers, and Administrators or Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories are included. Advisers such as Chief Secretaries attend without voting rights.
49.tq: Separate the composition of members from the non-voting status of advisers.
xs: Statement 1 correct: each state sends its **CM + two other ministers**.
Statement 2 correct: **Administrators/LGs** of member UTs are included.
Statement 3 wrong: **Chief Secretaries** are **advisers with no vote** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Other advisers: **NITI Aayog** representative, **Development Commissioners**.
Chairman: **Union Home Minister**; vice-chairman by **annual rotation**.
Recommendations are **not binding**.

49.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the role assigned in the Zonal Councils?
o: Union Home Minister — annual rotating Vice-Chairman
49.x: Development Commissioners are among the advisers who participate without voting rights. The Union Home Minister is Chairman, while State Chief Ministers rotate as Vice-Chairman.
49.tq: Distinguish advisers without vote from statutory members and office-bearers.
xs: **Development Commissioners** are **advisers without vote** — option **(3)**.
**NITI Aayog** representative is also a non-voting adviser; the **Home Minister** is Chairman, not vice-chairman.
xa: Vice-chairman: CMs of member states **by annual rotation**.
Members: **CM + two other ministers** from each state.
Secretariat: **Inter-State Council Secretariat, MHA**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of the Zonal Councils?
o: They are judicial bodies whose decisions are binding on States.
They are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies whose recommendations are not binding.
They are executive bodies that directly allocate State finances.
They are constitutional bodies with powers to dissolve State Legislatures.
49.x: Zonal Councils are statutory, deliberative and advisory bodies. Their recommendations are not binding on the States.
49.tq: Match the institution’s actual function with the level of legal authority it possesses.
xs: Zonal Councils are **statutory**, **deliberative and advisory**; recommendations **not binding** — option **(2)**.
They are set up under **Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, not the Constitution.
xa: ⚠ Zonal Councils = **statutory**, not constitutional; **NEC** = separate Act (**1971**).
**5 councils**, all chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.
**31st Southern Zonal Council** met **20 Aug 2026** near **Mamallapuram**.

49.s: The North-Eastern Council was established under the:
49.x: The North-Eastern Council is a separate body established under the North-Eastern Council Act, 1971, unlike the five Zonal Councils created under the 1956 Act.
49.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named regional bodies and their enabling laws.
xs: The **NEC** was set up under the **North-Eastern Council Act, 1971** — option **(2)**.
Zonal Councils come from the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
xa: **2002 amendment** added **Sikkim**; NEC became a **regional planning body**.
Since **2018** the **Union Home Minister** is ex-officio NEC Chairman.
SRA 1956 created **14 states and 6 Union Territories**.

49.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the chairmanship and vice-chairmanship of the Zonal Councils?
o: The Union Home Minister chairs all five councils and the vice-chairmanship rotates annually among the Chief Ministers of member States
The Chief Minister of the largest State chairs each council permanently
The President chairs the councils and the Union Home Minister rotates annually as vice-chairman
The Prime Minister chairs all councils and Governors serve as vice-chairpersons permanently
49.x: The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman of all five Zonal Councils. The vice-chairmanship rotates annually among the Chief Ministers of the member States.
49.tq: Separate the common chairperson from the rotating vice-chairperson.
xs: The **Union Home Minister** chairs all **five** councils; CMs are **vice-chairman by annual rotation** — option **(1)**.
The President and PM do not chair them.
xa: **31st Southern Zonal Council**: chaired by **Amit Shah**; vice-chairman TN CM **C. Joseph Vijay**.
Southern Zonal Council: **AP, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
⚠ Older APP table leaves out **Telangana**.

49.s: The secretariat of the Zonal Councils is provided by the
o: Inter-State Council Secretariat in the Ministry of Home Affairs
Department of Administrative Reforms in the Ministry of Personnel
49.x: The Inter-State Council Secretariat, functioning under the Ministry of Home Affairs, serves as the secretariat of the Zonal Councils.
49.tq: Apply the ‘which department houses the institution?’ method to distinguish related central secretariats.
xs: The secretariat is the **Inter-State Council Secretariat, MHA** — option **(2)**.
The **Union Home Minister** chairs all five councils.
xa: Advisers (no vote): **NITI Aayog** representative, **Chief Secretaries**, **Development Commissioners**.
Nature: **deliberative and advisory**; recommendations not binding.
Basis: **Part III** of the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the North-Eastern Council:
1. Sikkim was added to the Council through the 2002 amendment.
2. The amendment made the Council a regional planning body.
3. The Union Home Minister has been its ex-officio Chairman since 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct. The 2002 amendment added Sikkim and gave the NEC the role of a regional planning body, while the Union Home Minister has served as its ex-officio Chairman since 2018.
49.tq: Test a statutory body through a combination of amendment, function and current ex-officio position.
xs: Statements 1, 2 correct: the NEC **2002 amendment** added **Sikkim** and made it a **regional planning body**.
Statement 3 correct: since **2018** the **Union Home Minister** is ex-officio Chairman — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: NEC was set up under the **North-Eastern Council Act, 1971** as a separate body.
⚠ Zonal Councils = **statutory** under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**; NEC = separate Act.
The Union Home Minister also chairs all **five** Zonal Councils.

49.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the Southern Zonal Council?
49.x: The Southern Zonal Council comprises Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana and the UT of Puducherry. Telangana (often left out of older tables) and Puducherry are members, as is Kerala; Goa is not among the members.
49.tq: South = AP, TN, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana + Puducherry.
xs: **Goa** is not in the **Southern Zonal Council** — option **(3)**.
Members: **Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
xa: ⚠ Older APP table leaves out **Telangana**.
**31st Southern Zonal Council**: **20 Aug 2026** near **Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu**.
**5 councils**: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern — proposed by **Nehru** in 1956.

49.s: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised India into:
49.x: The States Reorganisation Act, passed in November 1956, created 14 States and 6 Union Territories. The other combinations are incorrect. The same Act set up the five Zonal Councils in its Part III.
xs: The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** (passed **November 1956**) created **14 states and 6 Union Territories** — option **(1)**.
This was the **MPPSC 2025** key.
xa: Its **Part III** set up the **5 Zonal Councils**.
**Andhra Pradesh (1 Nov 1956)**: Telangana merged with Andhra State.
**Kerala**: **Travancore-Cochin + Malabar**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting held in August 2026:
1. It was held on 20 August 2026 near Mamallapuram in Tamil Nadu.
2. Amit Shah chaired the meeting as Union Home Minister.
3. C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was its vice-chairman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: All three statements are correct: the meeting was held near Mamallapuram on 20 August 2026, chaired by Home Minister Amit Shah, with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay as vice-chairman.
49.tq: Verify date, venue and office-holder separately before selecting the combination.
xs: Statement 1 correct: the **31st Southern Zonal Council** met **20 Aug 2026** near **Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu**.
Statements 2, 3 correct: chaired by Home Minister **Amit Shah**; vice-chairman TN CM **C. Joseph Vijay** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: The **Union Home Minister** chairs all five Zonal Councils.
Vice-chairman: CMs of member states **by annual rotation**.
Secretariat: **Inter-State Council Secretariat, MHA**.

49.s: Andhra Pradesh is included in which Zonal Council and is party to which combination of water tribunals?
o: Southern Zonal Council; Godavari, Krishna and Vansadhara
Eastern Zonal Council; Narmada, Cauvery and Ravi-Beas
Southern Zonal Council; Ravi-Beas, Cauvery and Mahadayi
Central Zonal Council; Godavari, Narmada and Mahadayi
49.x: Andhra Pradesh belongs to the Southern Zonal Council and is party to the Godavari, Krishna and Vansadhara water dispute tribunals.
49.tq: Combine the regional classification with the State’s specific tribunal relationships.
xs: AP is in the **Southern Zonal Council** and party to the **Godavari, Krishna and Vansadhara** tribunals — option **(1)**.
Southern Zonal Council: **AP, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Telangana, Puducherry**.
xa: Water disputes come under **Art. 262** — a **constitutional device** of cooperation.
For bifurcation disputes CDI recommends the **ISC** + **Apex Council under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**.
**Mahanadi**: **Odisha vs Chhattisgarh** (2 Aug 2026).

49.s: In the Mullaperiyar matter, the Supreme Court-directed Supervisory Committee involves which authority under the Dam Safety Act, 2021?
49.x: The Supreme Court-directed Supervisory Committee in the Mullaperiyar matter involves the National Dam Safety Authority under the Dam Safety Act, 2021.
49.tq: Identify the exact statutory authority instead of substituting a related water institution.
xs: The SC-directed **Supervisory Committee** on **Mullaperiyar** involves the **National Dam Safety Authority** under the **Dam Safety Act, 2021** — option **(3)**.
The **Inter-State Council Secretariat** serves the Zonal Councils, not dam safety.
xa: Mullaperiyar dam (**1895**) is in **Kerala**, operated by **Tamil Nadu**.
**Mahanadi**: **Odisha vs Chhattisgarh** back in focus.
Water disputes: **Art. 262**.

49.s: The proposed amendment to the IAS Cadre Rules concerning unilateral central deputation has been criticised primarily because it may:
o: transfer the power of judicial review to the Union
remove the distinction between Central and State Lists
harm the morale of State bureaucracies
49.x: The criticism is that unilateral central deputation may adversely affect the morale of State bureaucracies. It does not abolish State services or alter the legislative lists.
49.tq: Match the policy criticism with its stated administrative consequence.
xs: **Unilateral central deputation** under the **IAS Cadre Rules** amendment **hurts state bureaucracy's morale** — option **(4)**.
The amendment lets the Centre depute officers **without state or officer consent**, its order final after a set time.
xa: Other criticism: **central directions** are excessive; **ISC** meets rarely.
AIS officers can be removed **only by the Union government**.
AIS = **unitary feature**: states lack full control.

49.s: Which of the following has been identified as a proposed role for the Inter-State Council in relation to legislation?
o: Approving every Money Bill before Parliament
Serving as a permanent screening body for Bills affecting the Concurrent List
Replacing the Supreme Court in all federal disputes
49.x: A proposal is to make the Inter-State Council a permanent screening body for Bills that affect the Concurrent List.
49.tq: Distinguish a proposed coordination role from constitutionally assigned judicial or recruitment functions.
xs: CDI proposes a **permanent screening body** for **bills affecting the Concurrent List** — option **(3)**.
The **ISC** is a **constitutional device** under **Art. 263**.
xa: Concern: the ISC **meets rarely**.
**Sarkaria (June 1983)** recommended a **permanent ISC**; **ARC (1966)** also urged one.
For AP bifurcation disputes CDI recommends the **ISC** + **Apex Council**.

49.s: Which of the following is identified as a continuing concern regarding the functioning of the Inter-State Council?
o: It meets too frequently and duplicates every State Cabinet.
It meets rarely, limiting its effectiveness as a forum of coordination.
It is composed exclusively of judges of the Supreme Court.
It has jurisdiction only over municipal elections.
49.x: The Inter-State Council has been criticised for meeting rarely; proposals seek to strengthen its role in Centre-State coordination.
49.tq: Select the institutional criticism that directly relates to the body’s functioning.
xs: The **Inter-State Council** **meets rarely** — option **(2)**.
CDI proposes it become a **permanent screening body** for Concurrent List bills.
xa: **Sarkaria**: **247 recommendations**, incl. a **permanent ISC**.
Other concerns: excessive **central directions**; unilateral **central deputation**.

49.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mahanadi dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
2. The Mullaperiyar dam is situated in Kerala.
3. The Mullaperiyar dam is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease arrangement.
4. The Mullaperiyar dam is located on the Godavari river.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
49.x: The Mahanadi dispute is between Odisha and Chhattisgarh. Mullaperiyar is in Kerala on the Periyar and is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease; it is not on the Godavari.
49.tq: Use the location-river-operation combination to expose the swapped river statement.
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Mahanadi** = **Odisha vs Chhattisgarh**.
Statements 2, 3 correct: **Mullaperiyar** dam is in **Kerala**, **operated by Tamil Nadu**.
Statement 4 wrong per the key — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Mullaperiyar dam dates to **1895**.
SC-directed **Supervisory Committee** involves the **National Dam Safety Authority** (**Dam Safety Act, 2021**).
**Godavari** is one of the tribunals AP is party to, with **Krishna** and **Vansadhara**.

50.s: The constitutional ceiling on profession tax under Article 276(2) is:
50.x: Article 276(2) permits profession tax up to ₹2,500 per person per year. The earlier ceiling was ₹250.
50.tq: Identify the present ceiling rather than the earlier figure retained as a distractor.
xs: **Art. 276(2)** caps profession tax at **₹2,500 per person per year** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **₹250** was the **old** ceiling before the **60th CAA, 1988**.
xa: **Art. 276**: a state can tax **professions, trades, callings and employments**.
Profession tax is among the **state-only taxes**.
The 60th CAA ceiling question was a **PYQ 2017**.

50.s: The ceiling on profession tax was raised from ₹250 to ₹2,500 by the:
50.x: The Sixtieth Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 raised the profession-tax ceiling under Article 276 from ₹250 to ₹2,500 per annum.
50.tq: Match the amendment number and year with the specific monetary change.
xs: The **60th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988** raised the ceiling from **₹250** to **₹2,500** — option **(3)**.
It amended **Art. 276(2)**; asked in **PYQ 2017**.
xa: **80th CAA, 2000**: **10th FC's** "Alternative Scheme of Devolution".
**88th Amendment, 2003**: added **Art. 268A** (service tax).
**101st Amendment, 2016**: inserted **246A, 269A, 279A** (GST).

50.s: Article 265 of the Constitution embodies which principle?
o: No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
No State may borrow without approval of the President.
No grant may be made without approval of Parliament.
No expenditure shall be incurred without approval of the Finance Commission.
50.x: Article 265 provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.
50.tq: Recall the exact constitutional wording associated with the authority-of-law requirement for taxation.
xs: **Art. 265**: **no tax except by authority of law** — option **(1)**.
State borrowing is **Art. 293**; the Finance Commission is **Art. 280**.
xa: **Art. 266** = Consolidated Funds, Public Accounts; **Art. 267** = Contingency Fund.
**Arts. 292-293** = borrowing.
Financial relations proper = **Arts. 268-293**.

50.s: Which pair of Articles is correctly associated with the Consolidated Funds, Public Accounts and Contingency Fund?
50.x: Articles 266 and 267 deal respectively with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts, and the Contingency Fund.
50.tq: Start from the sure Article pair and distinguish fund provisions from revenue-distribution and borrowing provisions.
xs: **Articles 266 and 267** = **Consolidated Funds, Public Accounts** / **Contingency Fund** — option **(2)**.
**265** = tax by authority of law; **280/281** = Finance Commission; **292-293** = borrowing.
xa: The **Consolidated Fund of India** receives all Union revenues, loans raised and loan repayments.
**Art. 292**: Union borrows on the security of the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
**Statutory grants** (Art. 275) are **charged on the CFI**.

50.s:
Consider the following statements about Part XII of the Constitution:
1. Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
2. Article 285 exempts the property of States from Union taxation.
3. Articles 292 and 293 deal with borrowing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
50.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission (Article 281 for its recommendations). Statement 2 is wrong: Article 285 exempts Union property from State taxes; it is Article 289 that exempts State property from Union taxes. Statement 3 is correct: Articles 292-293 cover borrowing by the Union and the States. So A, B and D wrongly include statement 2.
50.tq: 285 = Union property safe from States; 289 = State property safe from Union (lower number = Union).
xs: Statement 1 correct: **Art. 280** = **Finance Commission** (**281** its recommendations).
Statement 2 wrong: **Art. 285** exempts **Union** property from state taxes; **Art. 289** exempts **state** property from Union taxes.
Statement 3 correct: **Arts. 292-293** = **borrowing** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(3)**.
xa: Exception: the Centre can tax a state's **commercial operations** and state-owned companies.
**Art. 293(1)**: a state borrows **only within India**.
**Art. 265**: no tax except by **authority of law**.

50.s: Which of the following sets contains only taxes or levies associated with the State domain?
o: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles
Customs duty, corporation tax, Union excise duty and income tax
Goods and Services Tax, customs duty, wealth tax and corporation tax
Surcharge on Union taxes, customs duty, export duty and corporation tax
50.x: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles are included among taxes associated with the State domain. The other sets consist predominantly of Union taxes.
50.tq: Separate the State tax field from familiar Union taxes by checking every item in the set.
xs: **Land revenue, agricultural income tax, state excise on alcohol, vehicle taxes** are all **state-only** taxes — option **(1)**.
**Customs**, **corporation tax**, **income tax** and **surcharges** are **Union** taxes.
xa: Other state-only taxes: **stamp duties and registration**, taxes on **land and buildings**, **mineral rights**, **electricity** consumption, **professions**.
**Agricultural income tax**: **States** only (UPPSC 2009).
**Excise on liquor**: **States** (UPPSC 2014).
