53.s: At the first CWC-chaired inter-State committee meeting held in January 2026, Andhra Pradesh took which position regarding Telangana’s demand for Krishna waters?
o: It rejected the 50:50 demand as contrary to the KWDT awards and Apex Council decisions.
It transferred the dispute exclusively to the North-Eastern Council.
It agreed to quantify all Krishna and Godavari waters jointly through the Zonal Council.
It accepted an immediate 50:50 division of Krishna waters without reference to earlier decisions.
53.x: Andhra Pradesh rejected Telangana’s 50:50 Krishna demand, stating that it was contrary to the KWDT awards and the decisions of the Apex Council.
53.tq: Identify the State’s legal and institutional basis for rejecting a contemporary inter-State demand.
xs: AP **rejected Telangana's 50:50 Krishna demand** as contrary to the **KWDT awards** and **Apex Council** decisions — so option **(1)** is correct.
This was at the first **CWC-chaired** inter-state committee meeting (**Jan 2026**).
xa: AP also objected to **968 tmcft** of Godavari water for Telangana projects not quantified under the **GWDT award**.
Framework: **KRMB**, **GRMB**, **Apex Council** under APRA **2014**.

53.s: In August 2026, Telangana proposed to raise Karnataka’s unauthorised Krishna projects under which provision and statute?
o: Section 3 of the North-Eastern Council Act
Section 3 of the AP Reorganisation Act
Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act
53.x: Telangana proposed to raise Karnataka’s unauthorised Krishna projects under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act.
53.tq: Match a contemporary dispute with the precise statutory provision invoked.
xs: Telangana planned to use **Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Under Sec. 3 a State complains to the **Centre** about a river dispute.
xa: Telangana also sought **national status** for **Kaleshwaram** and **Palamuru-Rangareddy** at the SZC.
The **31st SZC** met on **20 Aug 2026** at **Mamallapuram**.

53.s: Which pair of projects was associated with Telangana’s demand for national status at the Southern Zonal Council in August 2026?
53.x: Telangana sought national status for the Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy projects at the Southern Zonal Council.
53.tq: Discriminate between similarly located river projects by linking them to the claimant State and demand.
xs: Telangana sought national status for **Kaleshwaram** and **Palamuru-Rangareddy** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pattiseema** and **Polavaram** are AP projects Telangana objects to; **Rayalaseema Lift** is an AP project in dispute.
xa: ⚠ AP objects to **Kaleshwaram**.
The **31st SZC** (**20 Aug 2026**) was chaired by **Amit Shah**.

53.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to Godavari-water frictions:
1. Andhra Pradesh — objection to Kaleshwaram
2. Telangana — objection to Pattiseema and Polavaram
3. Odisha — concern regarding submergence
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
53.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Andhra Pradesh has objected to Kaleshwaram, Telangana has raised objections concerning Pattiseema and Polavaram, and Odisha has raised the issue of submergence.
53.tq: Match each State with the particular project or consequence involved in the river dispute.
xs: **All three pairs** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**AP** objects to **Kaleshwaram**; **Telangana** to **Pattiseema and Polavaram**; **Odisha** on **submergence**.
xa: AP objected to **968 tmcft** of Godavari water for Telangana projects not quantified under the **GWDT award** (Jan 2026).
Godavari Tribunal (**1969**): Maharashtra, Karnataka, AP, MP, Odisha.

53.s: Which of the following best describes a commonly noted limitation of Zonal Councils?
o: They exclusively administer inter-State river-water tribunals.
They are only recommendatory and require greater resources.
They are constitutional courts with binding adjudicatory powers.
They can unilaterally alter awards of water-dispute tribunals.
53.x: Zonal Councils are generally regarded as recommendatory bodies, and their effectiveness is criticised as being constrained by inadequate resources.
53.tq: Distinguish a recommendatory coordination forum from a binding adjudicatory or executive authority.
xs: Zonal Councils are **only recommendatory** and **need more resources** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They are **deliberative and advisory**; recommendations are **not binding**, so they cannot alter tribunal awards or adjudicate.
xa: CMs serve as **vice-chairman by annual rotation**; **2 other ministers** per state are members.
**31st SZC**: **20 Aug 2026**, **Mamallapuram**, chaired by **Amit Shah**.

54.s:
Arrange the following phases of Centre-State relations in chronological order:
A. Coalition era and greater say for the States
B. Decline of Congress dominance and emergence of opposition State governments
C. Congress dominance at the Centre and in the States
54.x: Congress dominance characterised the 1950s and early 1960s, opposition State governments became prominent from the mid-1960s, and the coalition era began in the 1990s.
54.tq: Fix the first and last phases before arranging the middle phase.
xs: The order is **C, B, A** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**C**: **1950s-early 1960s** — Nehru era, **Congress rule** at Centre and states.
**B**: **mid-1960s onwards** — Congress dominance declined; **opposition state governments**; autonomy demands grew.
**A**: **since 1990s** — **coalition era**; greater say for states; more **cooperative federalism**.
xa: In the first phase, states **relied on grants**; calm except **new-state demands**.
Planning grants overlapped the FC until **NITI Aayog, 2015**.

54.s: Which of the following is NOT a factor identified as shaping Centre-State relations in India?
o: The Seventh Schedule and Articles 312 and 356
Judicial decisions such as S.R. Bommai
The exclusive control of local bodies over inter-State trade
54.x: The constitutional design, party politics, planning and judicial decisions are identified factors; exclusive control of local bodies over inter-State trade is not.
54.tq: Find the option outside the identified institutional and political factors.
xs: **Exclusive control of local bodies over inter-State trade** is NOT a listed driver — so option **(4)** is correct.
The listed drivers: **constitutional design** (Seventh Schedule, **Arts. 312, 356**), **planning**, **party politics** and **courts** (**S.R. Bommai, 1994**).
xa: **Planning**: plan grants overlapped the FC until **NITI Aayog, 2015**.
Courts: **S.R. Bommai, 1994** made **Art. 356** reviewable.
Phases: Congress dominance (**1950s**), opposition states (**mid-1960s**), coalition era (**1990s**).

54.s: The decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) is particularly associated with which of the following propositions?
o: The Governor has unlimited discretion in all matters
Article 356 action is completely beyond judicial scrutiny
The GST Council has binding legislative authority
Article 356 action is subject to judicial review
54.x: S.R. Bommai established that the exercise of power under Article 356 is reviewable by the courts.
54.tq: Match the landmark case with its distinctive constitutional principle.
xs: **S.R. Bommai (1994)** held **Art. 356** action **subject to judicial review** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option 2 ("beyond judicial scrutiny") is the opposite of the ruling.
xa: Courts are one of the **drivers** of Centre-State relations, along with constitutional design, planning and party politics.
**Sarkaria** wanted Art. 356 used **very sparingly, as a last resort**.
**Rajamannar** wanted **complete elimination of Art. 356**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the debate on State autonomy in India:
1. Demands for greater State autonomy grew after the Congress lost power in many States in the mid-1960s.
2. Coalition politics after the 1990s led towards more cooperative federalism.
3. The Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited as an argument in favour of greater State autonomy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: autonomy demands grew once the Congress lost many States in the mid-1960s. Statement 2 is correct: coalition politics after the 1990s led to more cooperative federalism. Statement 3 is wrong: the Punjab militancy of the 1980s is cited against greater autonomy, stressing unity and integrity. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
54.tq: Punjab militancy = argument for unity (against autonomy), not for it.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: autonomy demands grew after **Congress lost power in many states in the mid-1960s**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **coalition era** since the **1990s** brought **more cooperative federalism**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Punjab militancy of the 1980s** is cited **against** greater autonomy.
xa: Arguments against autonomy: **unity and integrity**; **regional disparities** need a strong redistributive Centre.
Arguments for: states **lack resources** (UPPSC **2007** key); **linguistic and cultural identity**.

54.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Rajamannar Committee — Tamil Nadu
2. Anandpur Sahib Resolution — Punjab
3. West Bengal memorandum — West Bengal
4. Kerala autonomy demand — Kerala
54.x: The Rajamannar Committee, Anandpur Sahib Resolution and West Bengal memorandum are correctly associated with Tamil Nadu, Punjab and West Bengal respectively. Kerala is the odd one out because it had no formal autonomy demand in this context.
54.tq: Use the odd-one-out pair to test whether a State actually made a formal autonomy demand.
xs: **Pairs 1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajamannar Committee** — **Tamil Nadu** (1969); **Anandpur Sahib Resolution** — **Punjab** (1973); **CPI(M) memorandum** — **West Bengal** (1977).
Pair 4 is wrong: **Kerala** made **no formal autonomy demand** — the odd one out (APPSC-GS **2025** key).
xa: ⚠ **1969 – 1973 – 1977** = **Tamil Nadu – Punjab – West Bengal**.
Punjab and West Bengal wanted the Centre confined to **four subjects**.

54.s:
Which of the following demands was associated with the Tamil Nadu autonomy position?
1. Deletion of Article 356
2. Abolition of the All India Services
3. Abolition of the Planning Commission
4. Restriction of the Centre to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications only
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Tamil Nadu's autonomy position included deletion of Article 356, abolition of the All India Services and abolition of the Planning Commission. Restriction of the Centre to four subjects was specifically associated with Punjab and West Bengal.
54.tq: Separate the Tamil Nadu-specific demands from the common four-subject demand of Punjab and West Bengal.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Tamil Nadu (**DMK**, **Rajamannar**) demanded: **delete Art 356**, **abolish AIS** and **abolish the Planning Commission**.
Statement 4 is wrong: confining the Centre to **four subjects** was the **Punjab and West Bengal** demand.
xa: The Rajamannar Committee was appointed in **1969** (report **1971**); TN Assembly resolution **1974**.
⚠ AIS: **Rajamannar = abolish**; **Sarkaria = strengthen**.

54.s: Punjab and West Bengal demanded that the Union Government should principally confine itself to which of the following subjects?
o: Industry, labour, taxation and social welfare
Agriculture, education, health and local government
Defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency
54.x: Punjab and West Bengal wanted the Centre to be confined to defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency.
54.tq: Recall the four-subject formulation and watch for substitution by State List subjects.
xs: Punjab and West Bengal wanted the Centre confined to **defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Punjab: **Anandpur Sahib Resolution, 1973** (**Akali Dal**); West Bengal: **CPI(M) memorandum, 1977** (**Left Front**).
xa: Tamil Nadu's demand differed: delete **Art 356**, abolish **AIS** and the **Planning Commission**.
⚠ **Kerala** made no formal autonomy demand (APPSC-GS **2025**).

54.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the major themes of State autonomy demands in India?
o: More powers for States, greater own revenue and reduced central administrative control
Uniform language policy imposed by all State governments
Transfer of defence and foreign affairs exclusively to local bodies
Complete abolition of State legislatures and concentration of taxation in the Centre
54.x: State autonomy demands generally sought more powers, greater control over own revenue, less central administrative control and protection of linguistic interests.
54.tq: Choose the option that combines the recurring federal, financial, administrative and linguistic dimensions.
xs: Autonomy demands sought **more powers + own revenue** and **less central administrative control** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Language** also featured (**anti-Hindi in TN**, **Punjabi in Punjab**), which rules out a uniform language policy (option 2).
xa: Main documents: **Rajamannar (1969)**, **Anandpur Sahib (1973)**, **West Bengal memorandum (1977)**.
For autonomy: states **lack resources** for their duties.
Against: **unity and integrity**; **regional disparities**.

54.s: Which one of the following is a principal argument advanced in favour of greater autonomy for the States?
o: Linguistic identity has no bearing on federal relations
Regional disparities can be eliminated only by abolishing the Union
States have no responsibility for public services
States lack adequate resources to discharge the duties assigned to them
54.x: A major argument for greater State autonomy is that States often lack sufficient resources to perform their constitutionally assigned duties.
54.tq: Select the option stating the fiscal-capacity argument without an extreme constitutional claim.
xs: A key argument for autonomy is that **states lack resources for their duties** — so option **(4)** is correct.
UPPSC **2007** key: **A and R true, R explains A**.
xa: Another argument for: **linguistic and cultural identity**, e.g. **resistance to Hindi in TN**.
Arguments against: **unity and integrity**, **regional disparities**, the **Punjab militancy** of the **1980s**.
Devolution: **16th FC** keeps **41%**; states want **50%**.

54.s: Resistance to the imposition of Hindi in Tamil Nadu is cited in federalism debates mainly as an expression of:
o: demand for abolition of the Finance Commission
54.x: The resistance to Hindi in Tamil Nadu illustrates the linguistic and cultural identity argument for greater State autonomy.
54.tq: Link the regional example to the underlying federal principle rather than to an unrelated institutional issue.
xs: Resistance to Hindi in TN expresses **linguistic and cultural identity** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is cited **for** greater state autonomy.
xa: Language demands: **anti-Hindi in TN**, **Punjabi in Punjab**.
The other argument for autonomy: states **lack resources** (UPPSC **2007** key).
TN's **DMK** government appointed the **Rajamannar Committee** in **1969**.

54.s:
Which of the following is an argument advanced against granting greater autonomy to the States?
1. The need to preserve national unity and integrity
2. The existence of regional disparities requiring redistribution by the Centre
3. The need for a strong redistributive Union
4. The complete absence of differences among Indian regions
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: National unity and integrity, regional disparities, and the need for a strong redistributive Centre are arguments against extensive State autonomy. Statement 4 is incorrect because regional disparities do exist.
54.tq: Find the single overstatement that contradicts the stated basis of redistributive federalism.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Arguments against autonomy: **unity and integrity**; **regional disparities** needing a **strong redistributive Centre**.
Statement 4 is wrong: the argument rests on regional disparities **existing**.
xa: The **Punjab militancy of the 1980s** is also cited against autonomy.
Arguments for: states **lack resources**; **linguistic and cultural identity**.

54.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Rajamannar Committee — DMK government of Tamil Nadu — 1969
2. Anandpur Sahib Resolution — Shiromani Akali Dal — 1973
3. Memorandum on Centre-State relations — CPI(M)-led West Bengal government — 1977
54.x: All three associations are correct. The Rajamannar Committee was appointed in 1969, the Anandpur Sahib Resolution dates to 1973, and the West Bengal memorandum was issued in 1977.
54.tq: Check each autonomy-related document against its political sponsor and year.
xs: **All three pairs** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rajamannar Committee** — **DMK** government of TN — **1969**.
**Anandpur Sahib Resolution** — **Akali Dal** — **1973**.
**Memorandum** — **CPI(M)/Left Front** West Bengal — **1977**.
xa: ⚠ **1969 – 1973 – 1977** = **Tamil Nadu – Punjab – West Bengal**.
Rajamannar reported in **1971**; the TN Assembly resolution came in **1974**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about the Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) and Centre-State relations:
1. The ARC was appointed by the Centre in 1966.
2. Its study team on Centre-State relations was headed by M.C. Setalvad.
3. The ARC was first chaired by K. Hanumanthaiya and later by Morarji Desai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: the Centre appointed the ARC in 1966 (study team report 1969). Statement 2 is correct: M.C. Setalvad headed the study team. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is reversed - Morarji Desai chaired it first, later K. Hanumanthaiya. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses Setalvad, and any option with 3 is wrong.
54.tq: ARC 1966: Morarji Desai first, then Hanumanthaiya; study team = Setalvad.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **Centre** appointed the ARC in **1966** (study team report **1969**).
Statement 2 is correct: **M.C. Setalvad** headed the study team.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Morarji Desai** chaired it first, **later K. Hanumanthaiya**.
xa: ARC recommended an **Inter-State Council** under **Art. 263**, **non-partisan Governors**, more delegation and finances to states.
Order: State first (**1969**, Rajamannar), then Centre (**1983**, **2007**).

54.s: Which of the following was the first State-level review of Centre-State relations?
54.x: The Rajamannar Committee, appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government, was the first State-level review of Centre-State relations. Its report was submitted in 1971 after its constitution in 1969.
54.tq: Identify the distinctive description rather than relying only on the year.
xs: The **Rajamannar Committee** was the **first State-level** review — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was appointed by the **Tamil Nadu** government in **1969** (report **1971**); **Sarkaria** and **Punchhi** were Central bodies.
xa: Chairman: **Dr P.V. Rajamannar**, former CJ, **Madras HC**.
**3 members**; the **Centre ignored** it.
Also spelt "**Rajmannar**".

54.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government.
2. It consisted of three members.
3. Its recommendations were accepted by the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Centre ignored the Rajamannar Committee's recommendations, so statement 3 is incorrect.
54.tq: Find the statement that reverses the Centre's response to a State-level committee.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: it was appointed by the **Tamil Nadu** government.
Statement 2 is correct: it had **3 members**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **Centre ignored** it.
xa: It recommended **complete elimination of Art. 356**, an **Inter-State Council** under Art. 263, and **abolishing the Planning Commission**.
First **State-level** inquiry (**1969**, report **1971**).

54.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Body — Chairman
1. Administrative Reforms Commission — Morarji Desai
2. Rajamannar Committee — Dr P.V. Rajamannar
3. Sarkaria Commission — Justice R.S. Sarkaria
4. Punchhi Commission — Justice M.M. Punchhi
54.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Morarji Desai initially chaired the ARC, while Dr P.V. Rajamannar, Justice R.S. Sarkaria and Justice M.M. Punchhi chaired the respective committees or commissions.
54.tq: Use direct chairman-name matching and verify all pairs before selecting the comprehensive option.
xs: **All four pairs** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**ARC** — **Morarji Desai** (later **K. Hanumanthaiya**); **Rajamannar** — **Dr P.V. Rajamannar**; **Sarkaria** — **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**; **Punchhi** — **Justice M.M. Punchhi**.
xa: Sarkaria was a **retired SC judge**; the commission dates to **June 1983** (report **1988**).
Rajamannar was a former **CJ, Madras HC**.
ARC study team: **M.C. Setalvad**.

54.s: Which one of the following is the odd one out among bodies associated with reviewing Centre-State relations?
54.x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with State funding of elections (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969), the Sarkaria Commission (1983) and the ARC (1966, Setalvad study team) all reviewed Centre-State relations.
54.tq: Indrajit Gupta = election funding, not federalism.
xs: The **Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)** is the odd one out — so option **(3)** is correct.
It dealt with **State funding of elections** (partial funding in kind to recognised parties), not Centre-State relations.
**Rajamannar (1969)**, **Sarkaria (1983)** and **ARC (1966)** all reviewed Centre-State relations.
xa: Sarkaria made **247 recommendations**.
ARC's study team on Centre-State relations: **M.C. Setalvad**.

54.s: A commission on Centre-State relations was constituted by the Union Government in June 1983 under a retired Supreme Court judge. It is:
54.x: The Sarkaria Commission was set up by the Centre in June 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a retired Supreme Court judge, and reported in 1988 with 247 recommendations. The Rajamannar Committee (1969) was appointed by Tamil Nadu, the ARC dates to 1966, and the Punchhi Commission came later (2007).
54.tq: 1983 + retired SC judge = Sarkaria.
xs: It is the **Sarkaria Commission** — appointed by the Centre in **June 1983** under **Justice R.S. Sarkaria**, a **retired SC judge** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Rajamannar (1969)** was appointed by **Tamil Nadu**; **ARC** dates to **1966**; **Punchhi** came in **2007**.
xa: Sarkaria reported in **1988** with **247 recommendations**.
Its advice led to the **Inter-State Council** in **1990**.
Sarkaria favoured **strengthening** the All India Services.

54.s: Which one of the following was a recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee?
o: Appointment of Governors as recent active politicians
A four-month period for assent to every Bill
Strengthening of the All India Services
54.x: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolishing the Planning Commission, eliminating Article 356 and establishing an Inter-State Council under Article 263.
54.tq: Use the commission-specific recommendation and reject proposals belonging to other bodies.
xs: Rajamannar recommended **abolishing the Planning Commission** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Strengthening AIS** (option 3) was **Sarkaria**; Rajamannar wanted AIS **abolished**.
The **four-month assent** period (option 2) was **NCRWC**; Sarkaria wanted Governors **not recent active politicians** (option 1 is the reverse).
xa: Rajamannar also wanted **complete elimination of Art. 356** and an **Inter-State Council** under Art. 263.
The Planning Commission was criticised for making states "**suppliants for aid**" (Rajamannar).

54.s:
With reference to the Sarkaria Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It favoured a permanent Inter-State Council.
2. It recommended that Article 356 should be used very sparingly and as a last resort.
3. It favoured abolishing the All India Services.
4. It recommended consultation with States on laws relating to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Sarkaria Commission favoured strengthening the All India Services, not abolishing them, so statement 3 is false.
54.tq: Spot the reversed recommendation concerning All India Services.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 4** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
1: a **permanent Inter-State Council**; 2: Art. 356 **very sparingly, as a last resort**; 4: **consult states** on **Concurrent List** laws.
Statement 3 is wrong: Sarkaria wanted AIS **strengthened**, not abolished.
xa: Sarkaria's Governor: an **eminent outsider**, not a recent active politician, with the **CM consulted**.
Also: **floor test**; bills decided within a set period; **247 recommendations**.

54.s: Which of the following was recommended by the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution regarding the Governor's handling of Bills?
o: The Governor should decide Bills only after a referendum
Every Bill should be reserved for the President
Assent should be withheld indefinitely in case of disagreement with the State Cabinet
Assent should be given within about four months
54.x: The NCRWC recommended that assent to Bills should be given within about four months. It also suggested safeguards concerning Article 356 and an order of preference in a hung Assembly.
54.tq: Identify the precise time-bound recommendation and reject extreme alternatives.
xs: **NCRWC** wanted assent **within about four months** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It did not ask that every bill be reserved for the President or that assent be withheld indefinitely.
xa: NCRWC hung-assembly order: **pre-poll alliance**, **largest party**, **post-poll coalition**.
It also proposed **Art. 356 safeguards** and an **All India Judicial Service**.
⚠ **Punchhi** wanted **time-bound disposal** of bills; Sarkaria wanted bills decided within a set period.

54.s: Which of the following is a recommendation associated with the Punchhi Commission?
o: Fixed tenure for Governors and no misuse of discretionary powers
54.x: The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed tenure for Governors, no misuse of discretion, a President-like removal procedure, time-bound disposal of Bills and regular Prime Minister–Chief Minister meetings.
54.tq: Distinguish Punchhi's Governor-related recommendations from the more radical Rajamannar proposals.
xs: **Punchhi** recommended a **fixed tenure for Governors** and **no misuse of discretion** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Abolishing the Planning Commission** and **eliminating Art. 356** (options 1 and 4) were **Rajamannar** proposals.
xa: Punchhi also wanted a **President-like removal (impeachment) procedure** for Governors (APPSC-G1 **2024** key).
Other Punchhi points: **time-bound disposal of bills**, **regular PM-CM meetings**, Art. 356 as a **localised emergency**.

54.s: With regard to residuary powers, which one of the following represents the Sarkaria Commission’s proposal?
o: Residuary taxation should be transferred to the Concurrent List
All residuary powers should be transferred to the States
Residuary powers should be exercised exclusively by the Governor
Parliament should retain taxation-related residuary powers, while the remaining residuary matters should move to the Concurrent List
54.x: The Sarkaria proposal was to retain residuary taxation with Parliament and place the remaining residuary matters in the Concurrent List.
54.tq: Separate residuary taxation from other residuary matters; the distinction is the key trap.
xs: Sarkaria would keep **residuary taxation with Parliament** and move the **rest to the Concurrent List** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option 1 reverses it: taxation stays with **Parliament**.
xa: Sarkaria also proposed **time-bound cesses**.
It wanted states **consulted** on **Concurrent List** laws.
It made **247 recommendations** (report **1988**).

54.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the commission or committee with its position on Article 356?
1. Rajamannar Committee — deletion of Article 356
2. Sarkaria Commission — Article 356 as a last resort
3. Punchhi Commission — localised emergency
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Rajamannar recommended deleting Article 356, Sarkaria treated its use as a last resort, and Punchhi proposed the concept of a localised emergency.
54.tq: Match each body with its distinctive reform position before selecting the combined code.
xs: **All three** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Rajamannar**: **complete elimination of Art. 356**; **Sarkaria**: **very sparingly, as a last resort**; **Punchhi**: a **localised emergency**.
xa: **NCRWC** proposed **Art. 356 safeguards**.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)** made Art. 356 **reviewable**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements regarding tax devolution to the States:
1. The 16th Finance Commission has kept the States' share at 41% for 2026-31.
2. The States have demanded that the share be raised to 50%.
3. The 16th Finance Commission raised the States' share to 50% from 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 16th FC keeps 41% for 2026-31. Statement 2 is correct: States want 50%. Statement 3 is wrong: 50% is the States' demand, not what the 16th FC gave. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the demand, and '2 and 3 only' and '3 only' wrongly accept statement 3.
54.tq: 41% = what the 16th FC kept; 50% = what States demand.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **16th FC** keeps **41%** for **2026-31**.
Statement 2 is correct: states want **50%**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **50%** is only the **demand**, not the FC's award.
xa: **14th FC** gave **42%** devolution.
Divisible pool is about **81%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue as **cesses and surcharges** stay outside it.

54.s:
Which of the following have been proposed as reforms in fiscal federalism?
1. Making the operation of cesses time-bound
2. Bringing off-budget borrowing into the accounts
3. Strengthening State Finance Commissions
4. Removing all forms of tax devolution to the States
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Time-bound cesses, accounting for off-budget borrowing, and stronger State Finance Commissions are reform proposals. Removing all tax devolution is not a proposal stated in this context.
54.tq: Reject the extreme reversal in Statement 4 while retaining the three specific reform measures.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Proposals: **time-bound cesses** (Sarkaria), **bringing off-budget borrowing into the accounts**, **strengthening SFCs** (**2026**).
Statement 4 is wrong: states seek **more** devolution (**50%**), not its removal.
xa: The **16th FC** keeps devolution at **41%** (2026-31).
Cesses (about **18%** of gross tax revenue) are **not shared**.

54.s: Which commission recommended that Governors be removed only through a procedure similar to the impeachment of the President?
54.x: The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed tenure for Governors and a President-like (impeachment) removal procedure (APPSC-G1 2024 key), along with time-bound disposal of Bills and the localised emergency idea. Sarkaria wanted an eminent outsider as Governor, Rajamannar sought deletion of Article 356, and the ARC urged non-partisan Governors.
54.tq: Punchhi = fixed tenure + impeachment-style removal.
xs: **Punchhi** recommended a **President-like removal (impeachment) procedure** for Governors — so option **(2)** is correct (APPSC-G1 **2024** key).
**Sarkaria** wanted an **eminent outsider** as Governor; **Rajamannar** sought deletion of **Art. 356**; **ARC** urged **non-partisan Governors**.
xa: Punchhi also wanted a **fixed tenure** for Governors.
Punchhi: Art. 356 as a **localised emergency**; **regular PM-CM meetings**.

54.s:
Consider the following recommendations:
1. An Inter-State Council under Article 263
2. Non-partisan Governors
3. Complete deletion of Article 356
Which of the above were made by the Administrative Reforms Commission?
54.x: The ARC recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263, non-partisan Governors and more delegation and finances to States. Complete deletion of Article 356 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand, so any option with 3 is wrong, and '1 only' leaves out non-partisan Governors.
54.tq: ARC: ISC + neutral Governors; Rajamannar: delete 356.
xs: **Recommendations 1 and 2** were ARC's — so option **(2)** is correct.
ARC: **Inter-State Council** under **Art. 263**; **non-partisan Governors**; more delegation and finances to states.
Recommendation 3 — **complete deletion of Art. 356** — was **Rajamannar's**.
xa: ARC was appointed in **1966**; study team under **M.C. Setalvad**.
Chaired by **Morarji Desai**, later **K. Hanumanthaiya**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about the Inter-State Council:
1. It was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.
2. It is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
3. Its 11th meeting was held on 16 July 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: the ISC was set up in 1990 under Article 263 on Sarkaria's advice. Statement 3 is correct: its 11th meeting was held on 16 July 2016. Statement 2 is wrong: the Prime Minister chairs the Council; the Home Minister chairs its Standing Committee. So options with 2 are wrong.
54.tq: ISC: 1990, Sarkaria, PM chairs; last meeting 2016.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: set up in **1990** under **Art. 263** on **Sarkaria's** advice.
Statement 2 is wrong: the **PM chairs** the ISC.
Statement 3 is correct: its **11th meeting** was on **16 July 2016**.
xa: LENS (**Feb 2026**) urges reviving it.
Members: CMs, UT administrators, Governors of states under PR + **6 Union Cabinet ministers**; it is **recommendatory**.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about the All India Services:
1. Under Article 312, the All India Services are the IAS, the IPS and the Indian Forest Service.
2. A new All India Service can be created after the Lok Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting.
3. Officers are recruited by the UPSC but serve the States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: Article 312 services are the IAS, IPS and IFoS. Statement 2 is wrong: the resolution must be passed by the Rajya Sabha (two-thirds present and voting), not the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is correct: recruitment is by the UPSC while officers serve the States. So '1 and 3 only'; '1 only' misses statement 3, and options with 2 are wrong.
54.tq: New AIS = Rajya Sabha (the States' House), two-thirds present and voting.
xs: **Statements 1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: **Art 312** AIS = **IAS, IPS, IFoS**.
Statement 2 is wrong: a new AIS needs a **Rajya Sabha resolution** by **two-thirds** present and voting, not the Lok Sabha.
Statement 3 is correct: recruited by the **UPSC**, but officers **serve the states**.
xa: Control: **ultimate with the Centre**, **immediate with the states**.
⚠ AIS: Rajamannar = **abolish**; Sarkaria = **strengthen**.

54.s: Which one of the following best describes the control structure of All India Service officers?
o: Ultimate control rests with the Centre and immediate control with the States
Ultimate control rests with the States and immediate control with the Centre
Both ultimate and immediate control rest exclusively with the Centre
Both levels of control rest exclusively with local governments
54.x: All India Service officers serve the States under immediate State control, while ultimate control rests with the Centre. Their uniform pay scales operate across States.
54.tq: Compare ultimate and immediate control instead of treating administrative control as belonging to one level alone.
xs: AIS: **ultimate control with the Centre**, **immediate control with the states** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is **one service** with **uniform pay scales** across states.
xa: Recruitment is by the **UPSC**; officers serve the states.
AIS under **Art 312**: **IAS, IPS, IFoS**.
Critics say AIS **violate the federal principle**; states cannot fully discipline or remove officers.

54.s:
Which of the following explains why All India Services are viewed as restricting State autonomy?
1. Officers are governed in important respects by Central rules.
2. States cannot fully discipline or remove such officers.
3. Officers are recruited by the Union Public Service Commission but serve in the States.
4. All India Services have no role in Centre-State coordination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and explain the perceived restriction on State autonomy. Statement 4 is false because All India Services are also defended as promoting Centre-State coordination.
54.tq: Reject the absolute negative statement and connect recruitment, rules and disciplinary control.
xs: **Statements 1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Officers are governed by **Central rules**; states **cannot fully discipline or remove** them; recruited by **UPSC** but serving states.
Statement 4 is wrong: AIS are defended for **Centre-State coordination**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025**: AIS **violate the federal principle** — **A and R both true, R explains A**.
In favour: **high standards**, **uniformity**, coordination.

54.s: Which of the following is a justification offered in support of All India Services?
o: They ensure that all officers are controlled only by State governments
They eliminate all State-level administrative discretion
They remove the need for constitutional division of powers
They promote high standards, uniformity and Centre-State coordination
54.x: All India Services are defended on the grounds that they maintain high standards, promote uniformity and facilitate Centre-State coordination.
54.tq: Identify the stated functional justification rather than the criticism based on State autonomy.
xs: AIS are defended for **high standards, uniformity and Centre-State coordination** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Option 1 is wrong: control is shared — **ultimate with the Centre**, **immediate with the states**.
xa: Against: they **violate the federal principle** by restricting state autonomy and patronage.
**Sarkaria** wanted to **strengthen** AIS and create more; **Rajamannar** to **abolish** them.

54.s: Which one of the following correctly explains fiscal centralisation after the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax?
o: GST abolished the divisible pool of Union taxes
GST subsumed several State taxes, while cesses and surcharges remained outside the divisible pool
Cesses and surcharges became part of the divisible pool automatically
State taxes were expanded and all cesses entered the divisible pool
54.x: GST subsumed several State taxes, whereas cesses and surcharges continue to remain outside the divisible pool.
54.tq: Separate the effect of GST from the treatment of cesses and surcharges.
xs: **GST subsumed state taxes**, while **cesses and surcharges stay outside the divisible pool** — so option **(2)** is correct.
GST did not abolish the divisible pool, and cesses did not enter it (options 1, 3, 4 wrong).
xa: The divisible pool is about **81%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue in **2025-26**.
Cesses are about **18%** of gross tax revenue.
States want **50%** devolution vs the **16th FC's 41%**.

54.s: Which one of the following criticisms has been associated with the Planning Commission in the context of Indian federalism?
o: It was a statutory body that collected taxes on behalf of the States
It was a judicial body that adjudicated disputes between States
It was a constitutional body that permanently controlled the State Legislatures
It was an extra-constitutional body that made the States dependent on the Union for aid
54.x: The Planning Commission was criticised as an extra-constitutional institution that made States ‘suppliants for aid’.
54.tq: Identify the institution from its distinctive criticism rather than from its formal name alone.
xs: The Planning Commission was **extra-constitutional** and made states "**suppliants for aid**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
The criticism comes from **Rajamannar** (and LENS Apr **2025**).
xa: Rajamannar wanted the Planning Commission **abolished**.
Plan grants overlapped the FC until **NITI Aayog, 2015**.
Other criticised institutions: **Governor**; **Arts 356, 256, 257, 365**; **cesses and CSS**.

54.s: The appointment of the Governor by which authority is often viewed as a source of central interference in the States?
o: The Chief Minister of the State
The President of India acting on the advice of the Union
54.x: The Governor is appointed by the President, and this Union-linked appointment is criticised as a possible instrument of central interference.
54.tq: Use the ‘who appoints’ approach to distinguish the Union authority from State institutions.
xs: The Governor is **appointed by the Centre** (the President acting on the Union's advice) and seen as **central interference** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The CM, the State Legislature and the Inter-State Council have no role in the appointment.
xa: **Sarkaria**: Governor an **eminent outsider**, not a recent active politician, **CM consulted**.
**Punchhi**: **fixed tenure** and a **President-like removal** procedure.
**ARC**: **non-partisan Governors**.

54.s:
Which of the following Articles are commonly criticised as instruments of Union overreach in the federal structure?
1. Article 356
2. Article 256
3. Article 257
4. Article 365
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Articles 356, 256, 257 and 365 are all identified in federalism debates as provisions that may enable excessive Union intervention.
54.tq: Check the complete constitutional cluster instead of eliminating an Article merely because its subject differs.
xs: **Arts 356, 256, 257 and 365** are all criticised as **tools of Union overreach** — so option **(4)** is correct.
All four are listed together in the table of **institutions criticised as against federal principles**.
xa: Other criticised institutions: the **Planning Commission** (extra-constitutional), the **Governor** (appointed by the Centre).
**Cesses and CSS**: cesses (about **18%** of gross tax revenue) are not shared.
**S.R. Bommai (1994)** made Art. 356 reviewable.

54.s: Cesses are criticised in debates on Indian fiscal federalism primarily because they are generally:
o: limited to non-tax revenue of the Union
imposed by State Legislatures but distributed by the Finance Commission
excluded from the divisible pool shared with the States
54.x: Cesses are not shared with the States through the divisible pool. They constitute about 18% of gross tax revenue, making their use a federal concern.
54.tq: Distinguish a Union tax receipt that is shareable from a cess that is outside the divisible pool.
xs: Cesses are **excluded from the divisible pool** shared with states — so option **(4)** is correct.
Cesses make up about **18%** of gross tax revenue.
xa: The divisible pool is about **81%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue (**2025-26**).
**Sarkaria** proposed **time-bound cesses**.
GST subsumed **state taxes**, adding to fiscal centralisation.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about central agencies and State consent:
1. Under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, the CBI needs the State Government's consent to act in a State.
2. The NIA can investigate scheduled offences anywhere in India without State consent.
3. The Enforcement Directorate can enforce PMLA and FEMA in a State only after obtaining that State's general consent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is correct: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires State consent for the CBI. Statement 2 is correct: under the NIA Act, 2008 the NIA needs no State consent for scheduled offences. Statement 3 is wrong: the ED enforces PMLA, 2002 and FEMA, 1999 nationwide with no State consent needed. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' ignores the NIA, and options with 3 are wrong.
54.tq: Only the CBI needs State consent (DSPE Act Sec. 6); NIA and ED do not.
xs: **Statements 1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is correct: the **CBI** needs consent under **Section 6** of the **DSPE Act, 1946**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **NIA** (**NIA Act, 2008**) acts **without state consent**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **ED** enforces **PMLA, 2002** and **FEMA, 1999** nationwide with **no state consent** needed.
xa: ⚠ Only the **CBI** needs state consent; **NIA** and **ED** do not.
Withdrawing **general consent** forces **case-by-case** consent.

54.s: If a State withdraws general consent to the CBI, what is the immediate legal consequence?
o: The matter automatically goes to the National Investigation Agency
The CBI is permanently barred from investigating all cases in that State
The CBI may investigate without any further approval if the Union Government directs it
Consent has to be obtained on a case-by-case basis
54.x: Withdrawal of general consent means that the CBI must obtain consent separately for each case.
54.tq: Distinguish withdrawal of general consent from a total and permanent prohibition.
xs: Withdrawal of general consent means consent is needed **case-by-case** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The CBI is not barred permanently; it just needs consent under **Section 6** of the **DSPE Act, 1946** for each case.
xa: ⚠ **NIA** and **ED** need **no state consent**.
NIA investigates **scheduled offences** anywhere in India.

54.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Enforcement Directorate — PMLA, 2002 and FEMA, 1999
2. National Investigation Agency — NIA Act, 2008
3. Central Bureau of Investigation — Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
54.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. The ED enforces PMLA and FEMA, the NIA functions under the NIA Act, and the CBI functions under the DSPE Act.
54.tq: Verify each agency against its governing law before selecting the combination.
xs: **All three pairs** are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
xa: CBI needs state consent under **Section 6**.
⚠ Only the **CBI** needs state consent; NIA and ED do not.

54.s:
Consider the following statements about Special Category Status (SCS):
1. SCS is expressly defined in the Constitution.
2. It was granted by the National Development Council.
3. The Gadgil formula included factors such as hilly terrain, tribal population or low density, border location, backwardness and weak finances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Statement 1 is wrong: SCS is not provided for in the Constitution. Statement 2 is correct: it was granted by the National Development Council. Statement 3 is correct: the Gadgil formula criteria were hilly terrain, low density or tribal share, border location, backwardness and weak finances. So '2 and 3 only'.
54.tq: Spot the false constitutional-status claim while retaining the institutional and criteria statements.
xs: **Statements 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 is wrong: SCS is **not in the Constitution**.
Statement 2 is correct: it was **granted by the NDC**.
Statement 3 is correct: **Gadgil formula** — hilly terrain, low density or tribal share, border location, backwardness, weak finances.
xa: Benefit: **90%** Central funding of plan spending.
**14th FC** removed the special/general distinction, meeting gaps via **42%** devolution + **revenue deficit grants**.

54.s: What did the Union Government provide to Andhra Pradesh instead of granting the promised Special Category Status?
o: A separate Finance Commission for Andhra Pradesh
54.x: The Centre subsequently provided a special assistance package in 2016 instead of granting SCS.
54.tq: Separate the assurance of SCS from the substitute measure actually provided.
xs: The Centre gave AP a **special assistance package (2016)** instead of SCS — so option **(2)** is correct.
The SCS promise was **not written into APRA 2014**.
xa: The PM's assurance in the **Rajya Sabha** (**20 Feb 2014**) was SCS for **5 years**.
The Centre's main reason for denial: the **14th FC** (**42%** devolution + revenue deficit grants).
The demand is still alive (**2026**).

54.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Article)
 a. Article 371A
 b. Article 371D
 c. Article 371E
 d. Article 371F

List-II (Subject or State)
 i. Sikkim
 ii. Nagaland
 iii. Local cadres, education and jobs in Andhra Pradesh
 iv. Central University in Andhra Pradesh
54.x: Article 371A relates to Nagaland, Article 371D to local cadres, education and jobs in Andhra Pradesh, Article 371E to a Central University in Andhra Pradesh, and Article 371F to Sikkim.
54.tq: Start with the distinctive Andhra Pradesh pair and then place the State-specific provisions.
xs: Correct code: **a–ii, b–iii, c–iv, d–i** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**371A** — **Nagaland**; **371D** — AP **local cadres, education and jobs**; **371E** — AP **Central University**; **371F** — **Sikkim**.
xa: **FNTA** gives eastern Nagaland autonomy over **46 subjects** without affecting **Art 371A** (2026).
**Ladakh**: Centre offered **Art 371** safeguards instead of the **Sixth Schedule** (2026).
AP's **Six-Point**-linked provision is **Art 371D**.

54.s: Which of the following States is associated with Article 371J?
54.x: Article 371J is associated with Karnataka.
54.tq: Distinguish the final Article 371 provision in the 371F-J group from the north-eastern provisions.
xs: **Article 371J** relates to **Karnataka** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The notes list **371F-J** as **Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal, Goa, Karnataka** — Karnataka is the last, **371J**.
xa: **371** — Maharashtra and Gujarat; **371B-C** — Assam, Manipur.

54.s: The Centre offered safeguards under Article 371 to Ladakh in place of which constitutional arrangement?
54.x: The Centre offered Article 371 safeguards to Ladakh instead of safeguards under the Sixth Schedule.
54.tq: Distinguish the proposed Article 371 route from the Sixth Schedule demand.
xs: For **Ladakh**, the Centre offered **Art 371** safeguards instead of **the Sixth Schedule** (**2026**) — option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 371A** is Nagaland's own provision, and the **Inter-State Council** (Art. 263) is a consultative body — neither is what Ladakh was denied.
xa: **371A** = **Nagaland**; **371D / 371E** = **AP** (local cadres, education and jobs / a Central University).
**FNTA** gives eastern Nagaland autonomy over **46 subjects** without affecting **Art 371A** (2026).
Other 371 provisions: **371** Maharashtra and Gujarat; **371B-C** Assam, Manipur; **371F-J** Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal, Goa, Karnataka.

54.s: The distinction between Special Category Status and the post-14th Finance Commission devolution arrangement is correctly reflected in which statement?
o: Special Category Status provided 90 per cent Central funding of plan spending, while the 14th Finance Commission raised tax devolution to 42 per cent and used revenue deficit grants to address State gaps.
Special Category Status and higher devolution under the 14th Finance Commission were identical arrangements.
Special Category Status provided 42 per cent Central funding, while the 14th Finance Commission reduced devolution to 14 per cent.
The 14th Finance Commission introduced Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh with 90 per cent Central funding.
54.x: Special Category Status involved 90 per cent Central funding of plan spending. The 14th Finance Commission’s 42 per cent devolution and revenue deficit grants were intended to cover State gaps without maintaining a special/general category distinction.
54.tq: Separate the institutional meaning of Special Category Status from the 14th Finance Commission’s devolution formula.
xs: **SCS** gave **90%** Central funding of plan spending, while the **14th FC** raised devolution to **42%** and used **revenue deficit grants** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **14th FC** made **no distinction between special and general category states** — so the two arrangements were not identical.
SCS is granted by the **NDC**, not by any Finance Commission; the 14th FC raised devolution rather than cutting it.
xa: The 14th FC formula was the Centre's **main reason for denying SCS** to AP.
SCS criteria: **hilly terrain**, low density or tribal share, **border location**, backwardness, **weak finances**.
SCS is **not in the Constitution**.

54.s: The Prime Minister's assurance of Special Category Status to the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh was given in the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014 for a period of:
54.x: On 20 February 2014 the Prime Minister assured the Rajya Sabha that AP would get SCS for five years. The promise was not written into APRA 2014, and the Centre later gave a special assistance package (2016) instead. Three, ten and fifteen years are incorrect.
54.tq: 20 Feb 2014, Rajya Sabha, SCS for 5 years.
xs: The PM assured the **Rajya Sabha** on **20 Feb 2014** of SCS for **five years** — option **(2)** is correct.
The promise was **not written into APRA 2014**; three, ten and fifteen years are not the figure given.
xa: The Centre gave a **special assistance package (2016)** instead of SCS.
The demand is still alive (**2026**); AP's angle also includes the end of **revenue deficit grants** and **Art 371D**.
⚠ SCS is granted by the **NDC**; the **14th FC** (**42%**) removed the special/general distinction.

54.s: The unanimous resolution of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in 2026 was primarily concerned with demanding:
o: the abolition of the GST Council
the replacement of elected State governments
a fair share of tax devolution
54.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly unanimously resolved in favour of a fair share of tax devolution for the States.
54.tq: Identify the immediate fiscal demand instead of choosing unrelated constitutional reforms.
xs: The **Tamil Nadu Assembly's** unanimous resolution (**Aug 2026**) sought **a fair share of tax devolution** — option **(4)** is correct.
It concerned devolution; **Art 371D** is an AP provision, unrelated to the TN resolution.
xa: TN's **Kurian Joseph Committee** (Part I, **16 Feb 2026**) seeks a "**structural reset**".
The **131st Amendment Bill 2026** (Lok Sabha expansion) was **defeated**, sharpening the **North-South** debate.

54.s:
Which combination is identified as contributing to centralisation in contemporary federalism debates?
1. Cesses
2. Centrally Sponsored Schemes
3. Goods and Services Tax
4. State Finance Commissions
Which of the statements given above are correct?
54.x: Cesses, Centrally Sponsored Schemes and GST are cited in debates on centralisation. State Finance Commissions are institutions for strengthening local fiscal devolution, not an instrument listed in this criticism.
54.tq: Separate mechanisms criticised for centralisation from an institution intended to deepen devolution.
xs: **1, 2 and 3 only** — option **(2)**: **cesses**, **centrally sponsored schemes** and **GST** are cited as tools of centralisation (2026).
**GST subsumed state taxes**; **cesses and surcharges** stay outside the divisible pool; CSS carry central conditions.
**State Finance Commissions** are not listed — strengthening SFCs is a 2026 **reform proposal**.
xa: Cesses are about **18%** of gross tax revenue and are **not shared**.
Divisible pool = about **81%** of Centre's gross tax revenue in **2025-26**.
Also criticised: **Arts 356, 256, 257, 365** as tools of Union overreach.

54.s: Which one of the following is specifically associated with the Andhra Pradesh angle in debates on Indian federalism?
o: The abolition of the State Finance Commission
The transfer of all residuary taxation to local bodies
Article 356 and the Punjab Accord only
54.x: The Andhra Pradesh-specific concerns highlighted are the demand for Special Category Status and Article 371D.
54.tq: Recognise the State-specific pair rather than selecting general federal provisions.
xs: The AP angle in federalism debates is **Special Category Status** and **Article 371D** — option **(1)** is correct.
AP's list also includes the **end of revenue deficit grants**; Art. 356 and Punjab are not AP-specific.
xa: **371D / 371E**: AP's local cadres, education and jobs / a **Central University**.
PM's SCS assurance: **Rajya Sabha**, **20 Feb 2014**, for **5 years**.
Instead the Centre gave a **special assistance** package (**2016**).

54.s: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, concerning Lok Sabha expansion, sharpened which broader debate?
o: The debate over judicial review and parliamentary privileges
The debate over conversion of all taxes into cesses
The debate over abolition of local governments
54.x: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill relating to Lok Sabha expansion sharpened the North–South debate.
54.tq: Connect the named constitutional amendment with the specific political debate it intensified.
xs: The defeat of the **131st Amendment Bill 2026** (Lok Sabha expansion) sharpened **the North-South debate** (May 2026) — option **(1)** is correct.
It concerned representation, not judicial review, cesses or local government.
xa: TN Assembly passed a unanimous resolution for a **fair share of tax devolution** (**Aug 2026**).
**Kurian Joseph Committee** (TN) Part I, **16 Feb 2026**, seeks a "**structural reset**".
States want **50%** devolution vs the **16th FC's 41%**.

54.s: Which statement correctly identifies the ‘first’ and ‘last’ institutional facts mentioned in relation to Indian federalism?
o: The Inter-State Council was the first State-level inquiry, and Rajamannar was set up in 1990
Punchhi was the first State-level inquiry, and the Planning Commission was set up in 1990
Sarkaria was the first State-level inquiry, and the GST Council was set up in 1990
Rajamannar was the first State-level inquiry, and the Inter-State Council was set up in 1990
54.x: The Rajamannar Committee is regarded as the first State-level inquiry, while the Inter-State Council was set up in 1990.
54.tq: Use the first/last clues directly and keep the inquiry distinct from the later coordinating institution.
xs: **Rajamannar was the first State-level inquiry**, and the **Inter-State Council was set up in 1990** — option **(4)** is correct.
The ISC (Art. 263) came in **1990** on **Sarkaria's** advice; **Sarkaria** and **Punchhi** were Centre-appointed, not state-level.
xa: Rajamannar: appointed by **Tamil Nadu**, **1969** (report **1971**), **3 members**; the Centre ignored it.
The ISC is **chaired by the PM**, with CMs and **6 Union Cabinet ministers**; 11th meeting **16 July 2016**.
**Sarkaria**: **June 1983** (report **1988**), **247 recommendations**.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted primarily to study:
o: The recruitment rules of All-India Services
The reorganisation of districts in Tamil Nadu
The distribution of seats in Parliament
55.x: Its principal task was to study Centre-State relations and recommend measures for greater State autonomy.
55.tq: Directly test the committee’s terms of reference using related but narrower subjects as distractors.
xs: The Rajamannar Committee was formed to study **Centre-State relations** — option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC 2018** key).
Its formal name was the **Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee**.
xa: Appointed by **Tamil Nadu** in **1969** (report **1971**) — the **first state-level** review.
Chairman **Dr. P.V. Rajamannar**, former CJ of the **Madras High Court**.
Set up by the **DMK** government under **Karunanidhi**.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about the terms of reference of the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was required to identify the causes of unitary tendencies in the working of the Constitution.
2. It was required to suggest measures securing the utmost autonomy for the States.
3. It was required to strengthen the Centre’s control over education and health.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
55.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the committee sought to reduce central control, including over subjects such as education and health.
55.tq: Separate the autonomy-oriented terms of reference from their exact opposite.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: it had to **identify the causes of unitary tendencies** in the Constitution's working.
Statement 2 is correct: it had to suggest steps for the **utmost autonomy** for states without compromising unity.
Statement 3 is wrong: it sought to **end** the Centre's control over **education and health**.
xa: Finding: the states had become "**administrative units of the Centre**".
Arts **256, 257 and 365** enabled this overreach.
It took forward **C.N. Annadurai's 1967** view that the Union need not control health and education.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about the findings of the Rajamannar Committee:
1. Despite the federal form, central dominance had turned the States into 'administrative units of the Centre'.
2. Articles 256, 257 and 365 were seen as enabling this central overreach.
3. Articles 280 and 282 were identified as the main instruments of this overreach.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: the committee found the States reduced to administrative units of the Centre. Statement 2 is correct: Articles 256, 257 and 365 were named as enabling this. Statement 3 is wrong: the Articles named were 256, 257 and 365, not 280 and 282. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the Articles, and options with 3 are wrong.
55.tq: Overreach Articles = 256, 257, 365 (directions to States and the penalty for not following them).
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: despite the federal form, states had become "**administrative units of the Centre**".
Statement 2 is correct: Arts **256, 257 and 365** enabled this overreach.
Statement 3 is wrong: Arts 280 and 282 were not the Articles named.
xa: It recommended **deleting Art 356** entirely — with Arts 256, 257 and 365 gone, the Centre's override would end.
It wanted the **Finance Commission** revitalised so states depend less on the Centre.
It wanted the **Planning Commission** abolished as extra-constitutional.

55.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was set up in 1969 and reported in 1971.
2. Its formal name was the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee.
3. Its chairman, Dr. P.V. Rajamannar, was a former Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: appointed in 1969, report in 1971. Statement 2 is correct: the formal name is the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee. Statement 3 is wrong: P.V. Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the formal name, and options with 3 are wrong.
55.tq: Tamil Nadu committee, so the chairman came from the Madras High Court.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: set up in **1969**, reported in **1971**.
Statement 2 is correct: formal name **Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee**.
Statement 3 is wrong: Rajamannar was a former CJ of the **Madras High Court**, not Bombay.
xa: Members: **A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar** and **P. Chandra Reddy** (three in all).
Also spelt "**Rajmannar**", including in the Group-II syllabus.

55.s:
Which of the following persons were members of the Rajamannar Committee besides its Chairman?

xs: The other two members were **A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar** and **P. Chandra Reddy** — **1 and 2 only**, option **(3)**.
**R.S. Sarkaria** chaired the Centre's **Sarkaria Commission** (**1983**), not part of Rajamannar.
xa: Chairman: **Dr. P.V. Rajamannar**, former CJ of the **Madras High Court**.
The committee had **three members** in all.
Set up by the **DMK** government under **Karunanidhi** in **1969**.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee was set up by the DMK government under:
55.x: The committee was set up by the DMK government under M. Karunanidhi, who carried forward C.N. Annadurai’s earlier autonomy position.

xs: The committee was set up by the **DMK** government under **M. Karunanidhi** — option **(4)** is correct.

xa: The DMK slogan "**autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre**" continues today (**2026**).

55.s: Which one of the following is a correct distinction concerning P.V. Rajamannar?
o: He chaired the Rajamannar Committee and also the Fourth Finance Commission.
He was a member of the Fourth Finance Commission but did not chair the Rajamannar Committee.
He chaired the Punchhi Commission and the First Finance Commission.

55.x: P.V. Rajamannar chaired the Rajamannar Committee and also chaired the Fourth Finance Commission.

xs: **P.V. Rajamannar** **chaired the Rajamannar Committee and also the Fourth Finance Commission** — option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ This is the noted trap: don't confuse the two roles of the same person.
**Punchhi** was chaired by **M.M. Punchhi** and **Sarkaria** by **R.S. Sarkaria**.
xa: Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the **Madras High Court**.
The committee: **1969**, report **1971**, appointed by **Tamil Nadu**.

55.s:
Which of the following were recommendations of the Rajamannar Committee?
1. Immediate setting up of a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263
2. Revitalising the Finance Commission and widening revenue devolution to the States
3. Strengthening the Governor system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
55.x: Statement 1 is correct: Rajamannar wanted a permanent ISC under Article 263 at once. Statement 2 is correct: it wanted the Finance Commission revitalised and devolution widened so States depend less on the Centre. Statement 3 is wrong: it wanted central control reduced and did not seek a stronger Governor (APPSC-G2 2017 key). So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses the Finance Commission point, and options with 3 are wrong.
55.tq: In 'NOT a Rajamannar recommendation', pick the option that strengthens the Centre or the Governor.
xs: Statements **1 and 2 only** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: a permanent **ISC under Art 263**, immediately.
Statement 2 is correct: **revitalise the Finance Commission** and **widen** revenue devolution.
Statement 3 is wrong: it did **not** seek a stronger Governor (**APPSC-G2 2017** key); it wanted central control **reduced**.
xa: It also sought to **delete Art 356** and **abolish IAS, IPS and IFS**.
It wanted the **Planning Commission** abolished.
Exam angle: in "NOT a Rajamannar recommendation", pick the option that **strengthens the Centre or the Governor**.

55.s: With reference to Article 356, the Rajamannar Committee recommended:
o: Its complete deletion from the Constitution
Its wider application during constitutional emergencies
Its transfer from the Constitution to ordinary law
Its use only with the approval of the Inter-State Council
55.x: The committee recommended the complete elimination of Article 356 as part of reducing central control over the States.
55.tq: Use a direct constitutional-provision question with nearby but reversed recommendations as distractors.
xs: Rajamannar recommended **complete deletion** of **Article 356** from the Constitution — option **(1)** is correct.
It sought to cut central control — wider use or ISC-gated use was not its proposal.
xa: With Arts **256, 257 and 365** also gone, the Centre's override would end.
⚠ Contrast: **Sarkaria** wanted Art 356 used **very sparingly, as a last resort** — not deleted.
It also recommended **abolishing** the All-India Services and the **Planning Commission**.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee viewed the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body because it:
o: controlled the recruitment to All-India Services
appointed the Governors of the States
alone decided grants to the States
55.x: The committee criticised the Planning Commission as an extra-constitutional body that alone decided grants to the States and recommended its abolition.
55.tq: Identify the specific institutional function attached to the body rather than its general description.
xs: Rajamannar called the **Planning Commission** extra-constitutional because it **alone decided grants to the States** — option **(4)** is correct.
It recommended **abolishing** it.
xa: It wanted the **Finance Commission** revitalised and revenue devolution **widened**.
It wanted the **All-India Services** (IAS, IPS, IFS) abolished to cut central administrative control.
It wanted a permanent **Inter-State Council** under **Art 263**.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Rajamannar Committee’s position on the Governor?
o: The Governor should replace the elected State government during ordinary disagreements.
The Governor should exercise greater control over State administration.
Central control over the States should be reduced; strengthening the Governor was not sought.
The Governor should be appointed by the Inter-State Council.
55.x: The committee wanted central control over the States reduced and did not recommend strengthening the Governor system.
55.tq: Use the ‘not recommended’ distinction in a power-and-authority question.
xs: Rajamannar held that **central control over the States should be reduced**; **strengthening the Governor was not sought** — option **(3)** is correct.
"Strengthening the Governor system" was the wrong option in **APPSC-G2 2017**.
xa: Exam angle: any option that **strengthens the Centre or the Governor** is NOT a Rajamannar recommendation.
It recommended **deleting Art 356** entirely.
The States had become "**administrative units of the Centre**", it found.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolition of the All-India Services primarily to:
o: Reduce central administrative control over State governments
Transfer recruitment to the Planning Commission
Create a separate service for each district
Increase the control of the Union over State governments
55.x: Abolition of the All-India Services was recommended to reduce central administrative control over State governments.
55.tq: Link the institutional recommendation with its stated federal objective.
xs: Abolition of the **IAS, IPS and IFS** was to **reduce central administrative control over State governments** — option **(1)** is correct.
It aimed at less Union control, not more — so option 4 is the reverse.
xa: ⚠ **UPSC 1993** key: ending IAS and IPS = **Rajamannar**; the **Dhebar, Kalelkar and Kher** commissions did not.
It also recommended deleting **Art 356** and abolishing the **Planning Commission**.
It was the **first state-level** committee on Centre-State relations.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended transferring subjects from the Union and Concurrent Lists to the:
55.x: It recommended moving subjects from the Union and Concurrent Lists to the State List to enlarge State autonomy.
55.tq: Test the direction of transfer within the Seventh Schedule.
xs: Rajamannar recommended moving subjects from the Union and Concurrent Lists to the **State List** — option **(2)** is correct.
There is no Emergency or Local Government List; **residuary powers** were to go to the **states**.
xa: Examples: **stock exchanges**, **futures markets**, **oil fields**, **trade unions**, **industrial disputes**, **inland waterway navigation**, **factories**, **electricity**, **publishing**.
End the Centre's control over **education and health**.
⚠ Contrast **Sarkaria**: residuary powers other than taxation → **Concurrent List**.

55.s: Which one of the following was NOT among the examples of subjects proposed for transfer to the State List?
55.x: Inland waterway navigation, industrial disputes, and oil fields regulation and development were cited examples. Foreign affairs was not among them.
55.tq: Identify the unrelated Union subject inserted into a specific transfer list.
xs: **Foreign affairs** was NOT among the subjects proposed for transfer — option **(3)** is the answer.

The examples were **inland waterway navigation**, **industrial disputes**, **oil fields** (regulation and development), **stock exchanges**, **trade unions**, **factories**, **electricity**, **publishing**.
xa: Subjects were to move from the **Union and Concurrent Lists** to the **State List**.
Central control over **education and health** was to end.
**Residuary powers** were to go to the **states**.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly contrasts the Rajamannar and Sarkaria positions on residuary powers?
o: Rajamannar assigned them to the States, whereas Sarkaria placed residuary powers other than taxation in the Concurrent List.
Rajamannar placed them in the Concurrent List, whereas Sarkaria assigned them to the States.
Rajamannar assigned them to local bodies, whereas Sarkaria assigned them to the Union.
Both assigned all residuary powers to the Union.
55.x: Rajamannar recommended that residuary powers go to the States, while the Sarkaria position concerned the Concurrent List for residuary powers other than taxation.
55.tq: Compare two similarly named federal-reform positions by isolating the decisive difference.
xs: **Rajamannar** gave residuary powers to the **States**; **Sarkaria** put **residuary powers other than taxation** in the **Concurrent List** — option **(1)** is correct.
Sarkaria would keep residuary **taxation** with **Parliament**.
xa: Rajamannar also wanted more **Concurrent** subjects moved to the **State List**.
Sarkaria: **1983** (report **1988**), chaired by **R.S. Sarkaria**.
⚠ The **Inter-State Council (1990)** came through **Sarkaria**, not Rajamannar.

55.s: The Rajamannar Committee recommended ending central control over which pair of subjects?
55.x: The committee sought to end central control over education and health and to move more Concurrent subjects to the State List.
55.tq: Test the exact subject pair associated with devolution of powers.
xs: Rajamannar sought to end the Centre's control over **education and health** — option **(3)** is correct.
This echoed **C.N. Annadurai's 1967** view that the Union need not control such subjects.
xa: It recommended moving more **Concurrent subjects** to the **State List**.
Examples for transfer: **stock exchanges**, **oil fields**, **trade unions**, **industrial disputes**, **electricity**.
**Residuary powers** were to go to the **states**.

55.s: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly adopted a State autonomy resolution on the basis of the Rajamannar report in:
55.x: The Tamil Nadu Assembly adopted the State autonomy resolution in April 1974 on the basis of the report.

xs: The TN Assembly adopted a **state autonomy resolution in April 1974** based on the report — option **(2)** is correct.
**1969** is when the committee was appointed and **1971** when it reported; **1983** is the **Sarkaria** year.
xa: The **Centre ignored** the report; no action was taken.
Its value: it put **state autonomy on the national agenda**.
DMK slogan: "**autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre**".

55.s: Which slogan is associated with the DMK’s position on Centre-State relations?
o: Autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre

xs: The DMK slogan is "**autonomy for the States, federalism at the Centre**" — option **(3)** is correct.
It continues in DMK politics today (**2026**).
xa: The TN Assembly's **state autonomy resolution** was adopted in **April 1974**.
The DMK government under **Karunanidhi** set up the Rajamannar Committee in **1969**.
TN's **Kurian Joseph Committee** (**April 2025**) consciously follows Rajamannar.

55.x: The Centre ignored the report and took no action on its recommendations.
55.tq: Test the actual governmental response, not the report’s later influence.
xs: The **Centre ignored** the report and **took no action** on it — option **(1)** is correct.
No Rajamannar recommendation was implemented — not Art 356, not via amendment or the Finance Commission.
xa: Its value: it put **state autonomy on the national agenda**.
The **Inter-State Council (1990)** came through **Sarkaria**, not Rajamannar.
The TN Assembly passed its **autonomy resolution** in **April 1974**.

55.s: The principal historical value of the Rajamannar report lay in the fact that it:

Placed State autonomy on the national agenda

xs: Rajamannar's value lay in that it **placed state autonomy on the national agenda** — option **(3)** is correct.
The Centre **ignored** it: it neither created the ISC nor abolished the Planning Commission.
xa: The **ISC (1990)** came through **Sarkaria**.
It was the intellectual base for later demands — the **Anandpur Sahib Resolution** and the **West Bengal memorandum**.
It was the **first** committee on Centre-State relations appointed by a state.

55.s: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 through the influence of the:

xs: The **Inter-State Council (1990)** came through the **Sarkaria Commission** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Rajamannar** had urged an ISC under **Art 263**, but the **Centre ignored** its report.
xa: Sarkaria: appointed by the **Centre**, **1983** (report **1988**), chaired by **R.S. Sarkaria**.

Report years: **1971**, **1988**, **2010**, and Kurian Joseph Part I on **16 Feb 2026**.

55.s: Which one of the following statements about the significance of the Rajamannar Committee is correct?

Both were later **state autonomy** demands, built on the first state-appointed inquiry.
xa: It placed **state autonomy on the national agenda**, though the **Centre ignored** it.
TN's own follow-up: the **April 1974** state autonomy resolution.
The **Kurian Joseph Committee** (**April 2025**) consciously follows Rajamannar.

55.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kurian Joseph Committee in relation to the Rajamannar Committee?
o: It was appointed by Tamil Nadu in 1969 and chaired by P.V. Rajamannar.
It was appointed by Tamil Nadu in April 2025 and consciously followed the Rajamannar approach.
