69.tq: Suspension by the appointing authority; removal only by the President.
xs: The **Governor of the State** may suspend an **SPSC** member during the SC inquiry — option **(1)**.
For a **UPSC** member, it is the **President** who suspends.
xa: Removal is always by the **President** (**Art. 317**).
⚠ SPSC: **Governor appoints**, **President removes** (**APPSC 2019**).
SC's advice on misbehaviour is **binding**.

69.s: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is appointed by ______ and can be removed by ______.
69.x: The Chairman of an SPSC is appointed by the Governor but can be removed only by the President, a favourite exam trap (APPSC 2019).
69.tq: Governor appoints, President removes.
xs: SPSC Chairman: appointed by **the Governor**, removed by **the President** — option **(4)**.
**APPSC 2019** asked exactly this; it is the favourite trap.
xa: SPSC members **resign to the Governor**.
Term: **6 years or age 62**.
Removal grounds under **Art. 317**: insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity, misbehaviour (via **Supreme Court**).

69.s: Under Article 320, the Union Public Service Commission conducts examinations primarily for appointment to
o: only Group B and Group C posts
69.x: UPSC conducts examinations for appointment to All-India services, Central services and Group-A services. Group B and C posts and the highest diplomatic posts are outside the stated purview.
69.tq: Distinguish the principal examination mandate from categories expressly excluded from consultation.
xs: UPSC conducts exams for **All-India, Central and Group-A services** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Group B/C posts** and the **highest diplomatic posts** are outside UPSC's purview; State services are for the **SPSC**.
xa: Consulted on **methods of recruitment**, **promotion and transfer**, **suitability of candidates**.
Consulted on **disciplinary matters** and temporary appointments of **more than one year**.
Functions are in **Art. 320**.

69.s: Which one of the following is NOT ordinarily a matter on which the Union Public Service Commission is consulted?
o: Suitability of candidates for appointment, promotion or transfer
Methods of recruitment to civil services and posts
Manner of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
69.x: The manner of reservation for SCs and STs is outside UPSC's consultation function. Recruitment methods, promotion and transfer principles, and candidate suitability are matters for consultation.
69.tq: Find the excluded subject rather than selecting a familiar UPSC function.
xs: **Manner of reservation for SCs and STs** is **not** a UPSC function — option **(4)** (**APPSC-G1 2022**).
Methods of recruitment, **promotion and transfer** principles and **suitability** of candidates are consultation matters.
xa: Also excluded: **claims of SCs/STs**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**, **Group B/C** posts.
Posts may be excluded by **regulations**, laid before Parliament for **14 days**.
UPSC is not concerned with **classification, pay or training**.

69.s:
Consider the following matters:
1. Claims of SCs and STs to services and posts
2. Temporary appointments for less than one year
3. Temporary appointments for more than one year
4. Group B and Group C posts
Which of the above are generally outside the consultation of UPSC?
69.x: Claims of SCs and STs, temporary appointments of less than one year, and Group B and C posts are excluded. Temporary appointments exceeding one year are ordinarily subject to consultation.
69.tq: Split the options using the critical duration distinction of less than or more than one year.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 4 are outside — option **(1)** **1, 2 and 4 only**.
**Claims of SCs/STs**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**, and **Group B/C** posts are excluded.
**Item 3** is inside: temporary appointments of **more than one year** need consultation.
xa: Also excluded: **reservations** of posts and the **highest diplomatic posts**.
Consulted on **disciplinary matters**: censure, withholding increments, demotion, compulsory retirement, removal.
Consulted on **extension of service/re-employment**.

69.s: Which one of the following statements best describes the legal effect of advice given by UPSC?
o: The advice can be rejected only by Parliament
The advice is advisory, and action taken without consultation is not invalid merely for that reason
The advice has no relevance in disciplinary matters
The advice is binding and any departure automatically invalidates the appointment
69.x: UPSC advice is advisory rather than binding. A decision taken without consultation does not become invalid solely because consultation was omitted.
69.tq: Apply the directory-versus-mandatory distinction to an administrative decision.
xs: UPSC advice is only **advisory**; a decision taken **without consultation is still valid** — option **(2)**.
Consultation is **directory, not mandatory**; it is not binding, and it does cover **disciplinary matters**.
xa: Selection confers **no right to the post** (SC).
Non-acceptance must be approved by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
Non-accepted cases go in a **memorandum** with the annual report.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 321:
1. The functions of the UPSC can be extended by an executive order of the President.
2. Extended functions may cover the personnel system of local bodies, corporate bodies and public institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is wrong: under Article 321 functions are extended only by an Act of Parliament (State Legislature for an SPSC), not by executive order. Statement 2 is correct: such an Act may cover the personnel system of local bodies, corporate bodies and public institutions. So '2 only'.
69.tq: Art. 321 needs a law, never an executive order.
xs: Only statement 2 is correct — option **(2)** **2 only**.
**Statement 1** wrong: under **Art. 321** functions are extended by an **Act** of Parliament/State Legislature, not an executive order.
**Statement 2** correct: such an Act may cover **local bodies**, **corporate bodies**, corporations and **public institutions**.
xa: Posts may be **excluded** by **regulations**, laid before Parliament for **14 days**.
Advice is only **advisory**.
**Art. 322**: expenses on the **Consolidated Fund**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President (the Governor for an SPSC) may, by regulations, exclude posts from consultation with the Public Service Commission.
2. Such regulations must be laid before Parliament or the State Legislature for at least 30 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
69.x: Statement 1 is correct: the President (Governor for an SPSC) may exclude posts by regulations. Statement 2 is wrong: the regulations are laid before Parliament or the Legislature for 14 days, not 30. So '1 only'.
69.tq: Exclusion regulations = 14 days before the legislature.
xs: Only statement 1 is correct — option **(1)** **1 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: the **President** (Governor for SPSC) may **exclude posts** by regulations.
**Statement 2** wrong: regulations are laid for **14 days**, not 30.
xa: Functions are **extendable** only by an **Act** (**Art. 321**).
Excluded anyway: **reservations**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**, **Group B/C** posts.
PSCs are not concerned with **classification, pay or training**.

69.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes UPSC from the Central Vigilance Commission in disciplinary matters?
o: Only UPSC is consulted on disciplinary matters
Only CVC is consulted on disciplinary matters
Both may be consulted on disciplinary matters, with UPSC having the stated edge in this area
Neither body has any role in disciplinary matters
69.x: The disciplinary role is shared by UPSC and the Central Vigilance Commission. CVC was established in 1964 and given statutory status in 2003, while UPSC retains the stated edge in this area.
69.tq: Avoid the exclusive-word trap by recognizing overlapping institutional roles.
xs: **Both** are consulted on disciplinary matters, with **UPSC having the edge** — option **(3)**.
The **CVC** was set up in **1964** and made **statutory** in **2003**.
xa: UPSC disciplinary matters: **censure**, **withholding increments**, **demotion**, **compulsory retirement**, **removal**.
UPSC advice is only **advisory**.
Non-acceptance needs the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.

69.s: The State Public Service Commission is commonly described as the watchdog of the
69.x: The SPSC is described as the watchdog of the merit system in public services.
69.tq: Recall the distinctive institutional description without confusing it with financial or electoral oversight.
xs: The SPSC is the "**watchdog of the merit system**" — option **(4)**.
It guards merit-based **recruitment**, **promotion and transfer** in State services.
xa: SC in **TNPSC v A. Balasubramaniam (1994)**: PSC **independence** is essential to fair administration.
Current concern: **crisis of trust** in State PSCs — **paper leaks**, flawed evaluation, delays, litigation.
SPSC: **Governor appoints**, **President removes**.

69.s: Which one of the following is outside the principal concern of a State Public Service Commission?
o: Classification, pay and training of government employees
Advice on promotion and transfer principles
69.x: An SPSC is not concerned with classification, pay or training. Its principal concerns include recruitment, promotion, transfer and candidate suitability.
69.tq: Identify the administrative personnel subjects expressly placed outside the Commission's concern.
xs: PSCs are **not concerned with classification, pay or training** — option **(3)** is the answer.
**Recruitment**, **suitability** of candidates and **promotion and transfer** principles are core consultation matters.
xa: Excluded: **reservations**, temporary appointments of **less than a year**.
Functions extendable only by an **Act** (**Art. 321**).
Advice is **advisory**, consultation **directory, not mandatory**.

69.s: In the case of the UPSC, the memorandum accompanying the annual report relates to:
o: Cases in which the Commission's advice was not accepted
The annual expenditure of every State PSC
The personal assets of Commission members
The number of candidates appearing for examinations
69.x: The UPSC annual report is accompanied by a memorandum explaining cases in which its advice was not accepted.
69.tq: Identify the specific content of the accompanying memorandum.
xs: The memorandum explains **cases where advice was not accepted** — option **(1)**.
UPSC reports to the **President**, laid before **both Houses** with that memorandum (**Art. 323**).
xa: Every non-acceptance must be approved by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
SPSC reports to the **Governor** → **State Legislature**, with a similar memorandum.
JSPSC reports to **each concerned Governor**.

69.s: Which authority must approve every case in which the advice of the UPSC is not accepted?
o: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
The Union Public Service Commission itself
69.x: Every case of non-acceptance of UPSC advice must be approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet; an individual ministry cannot reject the advice on its own.
69.tq: Ask which authority would perform the specific approval function.
xs: The **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet** must approve every non-acceptance — option **(3)**.
A **ministry cannot reject** UPSC advice on its own.
xa: Non-accepted cases are listed in a **memorandum** laid before **both Houses**.
Advice is **advisory**; consultation **directory, not mandatory**.
Reports: **Art. 323**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding annual reports of Public Service Commissions:
1. The UPSC submits its report to the President.
2. The UPSC report is laid before both Houses of Parliament.
3. An SPSC submits its report to the Governor.
4. The Governor lays the SPSC report before the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All four statements are correct. The UPSC report follows the President-Parliament route, while an SPSC report follows the Governor-State Legislature route.
69.tq: Trace and compare the two reporting chains.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**UPSC** → **President** → **both Houses** (with memorandum on non-accepted advice).
**SPSC** → **Governor** → **State Legislature** (with a similar memorandum).
xa: **JSPSC** → **each concerned Governor** → his Legislature.
Non-acceptance needs the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**.
Provision: **Art. 323**.

69.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission can be established only when which of the following conditions is fulfilled?
o: The Governors of two or more States issue a joint notification.
The Parliament passes an Act on the request of two or more State Legislatures.
The President issues an executive order on his own initiative.
The UPSC recommends its establishment to the Union Cabinet.
69.x: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by an Act of Parliament following a request from the legislatures of two or more States.
69.tq: Ask which authority performs the job and identify the required initiating condition.
xs: A JSPSC is created by an **Act of Parliament** on request of **two or more State Legislatures** — option **(2)**.
It is a **statutory**, not constitutional, body.
xa: Chairman and members are **appointed, suspended and removed by the President**.
Term: **6 years or 62**.
Example: **Punjab and Haryana**, briefly after **1966**.

69.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before Parliament
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before each concerned State Legislature by the Governor
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before the Supreme Court
Joint State Public Service Commission — annual report laid before the UPSC
69.x: The Joint State Public Service Commission submits its report to each concerned Governor, who lays it before the relevant State Legislature.
69.tq: Trace the reporting chain from the Commission to the legislature.
xs: JSPSC report goes to **each concerned Governor**, who lays it before **the State Legislature** — option **(2)**.
It does not go to **Parliament** (that is the UPSC route), the **Supreme Court** or the **UPSC**.
xa: UPSC → **President** → **both Houses**.
SPSC → **Governor** → **State Legislature**.
JSPSC members **resign to the President**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements about a Joint State Public Service Commission:
1. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
2. Their service conditions and the number of members are fixed by the President.
3. A member submits resignation to the concerned Governor.
4. The normal term is six years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. A member of a Joint Commission resigns to the President, not to the concerned Governor, making statement 3 incorrect.
69.tq: Use the authority-based trap in the resignation provision.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct — option **(1)** **1, 2 and 4 only**.
**Statements 1, 2** correct: the **President** appoints, and fixes **number and service conditions**.
**Statement 3** wrong: JSPSC members **resign to the President**.
**Statement 4** correct: term **6 years or 62**.
xa: Created by an **Act of Parliament** on request of **two or more state legislatures** — **statutory** body.
Report goes to **each concerned Governor**.
Example: **Punjab and Haryana** after **1966**.

69.s: Punjab and Haryana had a Joint State Public Service Commission for a brief period after:
69.x: Punjab and Haryana had a Joint State Public Service Commission briefly after the reorganisation associated with 1966.
69.tq: Distinguish the specific reorganisation year from nearby constitutional dates.
xs: Punjab and Haryana had a JSPSC briefly after **1966** — option **(3)**.
**1956** is when APPSC was formed; **1950** is when UPSC was formed.
xa: A JSPSC is a **statutory** body, created by an **Act of Parliament**.
It needs a request from **two or more state legislatures**.
The **President** appoints and removes its members; term **6 years or 62**.

69.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission came into existence on which date?
69.x: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission came into existence on 1 November 1956, with the formation of Andhra Pradesh.
69.tq: Use the precise date rather than the related formation year.
xs: APPSC came into existence on **1 November 1956**, with the formation of Andhra Pradesh — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2023** key).
**1 Oct 1926** is the first PSC; **26 Jan 1950** is when the UPSC was formed.
xa: It merged the **Andhra PSC (1953)** and the **Hyderabad PSC**.
After bifurcation (**2014**), Telangana got **TSPSC**.
APPSC: **Governor of AP** appoints; **President** removes.

69.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was formed by merging which of the following?
69.x: The APPSC was formed by merging the Andhra Public Service Commission, established in 1953, and the Hyderabad Public Service Commission.
69.tq: Test the exact institutional predecessors of the body.
xs: APPSC merged the **Andhra PSC** (**1953**) and the **Hyderabad PSC** — option **(2)**.
The merger matched the formation of **Andhra Pradesh** itself.
xa: Formed on **1 November 1956**.
After **2014**, APPSC continues for residuary AP; Telangana got **TSPSC**.
Term: **6 years / age 62**.

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission:
1. It continues to serve the residuary State of Andhra Pradesh after the 2014 bifurcation.
2. Telangana obtained the Telangana State Public Service Commission after bifurcation.
3. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the Governor of Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: All three statements are correct. After bifurcation, APPSC continued for residuary Andhra Pradesh, Telangana constituted TSPSC, and the Governor appoints APPSC members.
69.tq: Check each institutional consequence of bifurcation separately.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Statements 1, 2**: after **2014**, APPSC continues for **residuary AP**; Telangana got **TSPSC**.
**Statement 3**: chairman and members are appointed by the **Governor of AP**.
xa: Strength is fixed by the **Governor**; removal is by the **President**.
Term: **6 years / age 62**.
Origin: **1 November 1956**.

69.s: Which one of the following functions is performed by the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission in addition to recruitment to State services?
o: Conducting examinations for the lower judicial service
Auditing the accounts of the State Government
Appointing judges of the High Court
69.x: The APPSC conducts recruitment examinations for State services and examinations for the lower judicial service under Article 234.
69.tq: Distinguish a recruitment function from constitutional appointments and auditing.
xs: APPSC also conducts **lower judicial service examinations** (**Art. 234**) — option **(1)**.
Audit, appointing High Court judges and local-body elections are not PSC functions.
xa: Main function: **State service recruitment**.
APPSC is an **SPSC** under **Art. 315**.
SPSC = "**watchdog of the merit system**".

69.s: The Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission is appointed by ______ and can be removed by ______.
o: the Governor of Andhra Pradesh; the Governor of Andhra Pradesh
the President; the Governor of Andhra Pradesh
the Governor of Andhra Pradesh; the President
the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh; the President
69.x: The Governor of AP appoints the APPSC Chairman and members, but only the President can remove them (Art 317), so C is right. A is the classic trap: the Governor appoints but cannot remove. B reverses the two roles. D is wrong because the Chief Minister does not appoint PSC members. Members hold office for 6 years or until age 62.
69.tq: SPSC/APPSC: Governor appoints, President removes.
xs: APPSC Chairman: appointed by **the Governor of Andhra Pradesh**, removed by **the President** — option **(3)**.
⚠ The Governor appoints but **cannot remove**; the **Chief Minister** has no role.
xa: Removal under **Art. 317**: misbehaviour only after **Supreme Court** reference.
Term: **6 years / age 62**.
PYQ: **APPSC-GS 2023**.

69.s: The Supreme Court stressed the importance of Public Service Commission independence in which of the following cases?
69.x: In T.N. PSC v. A. Balasubramaniam (1994), the Supreme Court stressed that PSC independence is essential for fair administration.
69.tq: Discriminate carefully among the case name, year and institution instead of accepting a familiar-looking combination.
xs: **TNPSC v A. Balasubramaniam (1994)**: PSC **independence** is essential to fair administration — option **(2)**.
The year is **1994**, and the PSC is **Tamil Nadu's** — not 2004, Bihar or UPSC.
xa: SPSC = "**watchdog of the merit system**".
Current: **crisis of trust** in State PSCs (**Dec 2025**).

69.s: Who was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination?
69.x: Satyendranath Tagore was the first Indian to clear the Indian Civil Service examination, in 1864.
69.tq: Use the first-person-in-history cue and avoid confusing it with later examination reform committees.
xs: **Satyendranath Tagore** was the first Indian to clear the ICS (**1864**) — option **(1)**.
He cleared it decades before simultaneous exams began in India in **1922**.
xa: Simultaneous ICS exams in India from **1922** (**Allahabad**).
First PSC chairman (**1926**): **Sir Ross Barker**.
**Lee Commission** (**1924**) recommended the PSC.

69.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the present concerns associated with State Public Service Commissions:
1. Paper leaks have affected public confidence.
2. Flawed evaluation has led to disputes.
3. Delays and litigation have emerged as significant concerns.
4. Telangana examinations in 2023 and Bihar examinations in 2024 are cited in this context.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
69.x: Paper leaks, flawed evaluation, delays and litigation are identified as major concerns, with the Telangana 2023 and Bihar 2024 examinations cited as examples.
69.tq: Treat the examples in the final statement as factual anchors and verify the broader concerns around them.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Paper leaks**, **flawed evaluation**, **delays** and **litigation** drive the **crisis of trust** in State PSCs (**Dec 2025**).
Examples: **Telangana 2023** and **Bihar 2024** exams.
xa: Reform is needed to **protect merit**.
SC in **TNPSC v A. Balasubramaniam (1994)** stressed PSC independence.

69.s: Satyendranath Tagore was selected for the Indian Civil Service in 1863 and cleared the examination in:
69.x: Satyendranath Tagore was selected in 1863 and is recorded as the first Indian to clear the ICS in 1864.
69.tq: Distinguish the selection year from the year associated with clearing the examination.
xs: **Satyendranath Tagore** cleared the ICS in **1864** — option **(3)**.
Selected in **1863** per the question, he is recorded as clearing it in **1864**.
xa: He was the **first Indian** to clear the ICS.
Simultaneous exams in India came from **1922**, at **Allahabad**.
**Montagu-Chelmsford** reforms brought the 1922 change.

69.s: The simultaneous conduct of the Indian Civil Service examinations in India began in 1922 at:
69.x: From 1922, the Indian Civil Service examinations were conducted simultaneously in India at Allahabad.
69.tq: Separate the starting year from the examination venue and identify the precise location.
xs: Simultaneous ICS exams were held in India from **1922** at **Allahabad** — option **(2)**.
This came in the context of the **Montagu-Chelmsford** reforms, not the 1935 Act.
xa: The **GoI Act 1919** first provided for a Public Service Commission.
**Lee Commission** (**1924**) → PSC on **1 Oct 1926**.
**Satyendranath Tagore**: first Indian to clear the ICS (**1864**).

69.s: Public Service Commissions in India are often described as the:
o: Friend, philosopher and guide of the Public Accounts Committee
69.x: Public Service Commissions are called the watchdog of the merit system because they ensure recruitment to civil services on merit.
69.tq: PSC guards merit like a watchdog.
xs: Public Service Commissions are called the "**Watchdog of the merit system**" — so option **(2)** is correct.
They recruit on **merit** and advise on **promotion and transfer** and **suitability of candidates**.
xa: SC in **TNPSC v A. Balasubramaniam (1994)**: PSC **independence** is essential to fair administration.
Current concern: a **crisis of trust** in State PSCs (**Dec 2025**) — **paper leaks**, flawed evaluation, delays, litigation.
UPSC is an **independent constitutional body** (**Articles 315-323**, **Part XIV**).

69.s: The Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission was established in:
69.x: The APPSC was established in 1956, the year Andhra Pradesh was formed; its members are appointed by the Governor but removed by the President.
69.tq: New State, new Commission: both 1956.
xs: APPSC was established in **1956** — on **1 November 1956**, with the formation of Andhra Pradesh — so option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **1953** is the **Andhra PSC**, one of the two bodies merged into APPSC; **1950** is when the **UPSC** was formed.
xa: APPSC merged the **Andhra PSC (1953)** and the **Hyderabad PSC**.
APPSC: **Governor appoints**, **President removes** (PYQ **APPSC-GS 2023**).
After bifurcation (**2014**), APPSC continues for residuary AP; Telangana got **TSPSC**.

70.s:
With reference to the Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. It is a quasi-judicial constitutional body.
3. It is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: All three statements are correct. Article 280 provides for a quasi-judicial Finance Commission constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier.
70.tq: Verify the constitutional article, institutional character and periodicity together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2 and 3**.
**Statement 1**: the FC is constituted under **Article 280**.
**Statement 2**: it is a **quasi-judicial** constitutional body.
**Statement 3**: the **President** constitutes it **every fifth year or earlier**.
xa: Composition: **Chairman + 4 members** (**Art. 280(1)**).
⚠ **APPSC-G2 2025** trap: "**Article 290** provides for the FC" is wrong — Art. 290 deals with **pensions**.
**Art. 281**: recommendations + explanatory memorandum laid before **each House of Parliament**.

70.s: The Finance Commission consists of:
o: A Chairman and four members appointed by the President
A Chairman and three members appointed by Parliament
A Chairman and four members appointed by the Prime Minister
70.x: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
70.tq: Test composition and appointing authority in the same question.
xs: The FC has **a Chairman and four members appointed by the President** — so option **(1)** is correct (**Art. 280(1)**).
Members are neither elected nor appointed by **Parliament** or the **Prime Minister**; Parliament only fixes **qualifications**.
xa: Qualifications: **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**.
Term: as the **President** specifies; members are **eligible for reappointment**.
Constituted **every fifth year or earlier**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the members of the Finance Commission:
1. Their term is specified by the President.
2. They are eligible for reappointment.
3. Their term is fixed permanently by the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: The President specifies the term, and members are eligible for reappointment. The Constitution does not permanently prescribe one fixed term.
70.tq: Identify the true provisions and reject the absolute claim about a permanently fixed term.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: the term is **as the President specifies**.
**Statement 2** correct: members are **eligible for reappointment**.
**Statement 3** wrong: the Constitution fixes no permanent term.
xa: Composition: **Chairman + 4 members**.
Qualifications are fixed by **Parliament** under the **FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951**.
The FC is a **quasi-judicial** body.

70.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are prescribed by Parliament under the:
70.x: Parliament prescribed the qualifications through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, also referred to in abbreviated form as the Finance Commission Act, 1951.
70.tq: Distinguish the exact statutory title from plausible but nonexistent titles.
xs: Parliament fixed qualifications in the **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The APP notes call it the **Finance Commission Act, 1951**; the other names are invented.
xa: Chairman: **experience in public affairs**.
Members: a **High Court judge** (or qualified to be one), an expert in **government finance and accounts**, one with **financial matters and administration** experience, one with **economics**.
Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**.

70.s: Which of the following is the prescribed qualification for the Chairman of the Finance Commission?
o: Service as a Governor of a State
Experience exclusively as a High Court Chief Justice
Membership of Parliament for ten years
70.x: The Chairman must have experience in public affairs.
70.tq: Match the office with its exact statutory qualification rather than a prestigious but unstated qualification.
xs: The Chairman must have **experience in public affairs** — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **High Court judge** qualification is for a **member**, not the Chairman.
xa: Other members: **government finance and accounts**, **financial matters and administration**, **economics**.
Act: **FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**.
**P.V. Rajamannar** chaired the **4th FC**.

70.s: Under Article 281, the President is required to place before each House of Parliament:
o: Only the report of the Comptroller and Auditor General
The recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken
The recommendations after approval by the Supreme Court
70.x: Article 281 requires the President to lay the Finance Commission’s recommendations together with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken before each House of Parliament.
70.tq: Test the constitutional procedure and watch for the omission of the explanatory memorandum.
xs: Under **Art. 281**, the President lays **the recommendations along with an explanatory memorandum on action taken** before **each House of Parliament** — option **(3)**.
No role for the **CAG** or **Supreme Court** here.
xa: Recommendations are **advisory, not binding**.
**P.V. Rajamannar** (**4th FC**): should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
**16th FC** report was tabled in Parliament on **1 Feb 2026**.

70.s: Which Article provides for the Finance Commission, while Article 290 deals with pensions?
70.x: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, whereas Article 290 deals with pensions. Article 281 concerns laying the recommendations before Parliament.
70.tq: Separate the look-alike constitutional article numbers by their subjects.
xs: **Article 280** provides for the FC; **Article 290** deals with **pensions** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 281** is about laying the recommendations before Parliament.
xa: ⚠ **APPSC-G2 2025**: "Article 290 provides for the FC" was the **incorrect** statement.
**Art. 280(1)**: **Chairman + 4 members** appointed by the President.
The FC is a **quasi-judicial** constitutional body.

70.s:
Which combination correctly represents the prescribed areas of expertise for Finance Commission members?
1. Government finance and accounts
2. Financial matters and administration
3. Economics
4. Monetary policy operations as a compulsory qualification
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
70.x: Special knowledge of Government finance and accounts, wide experience in financial matters and administration, and special knowledge of economics are prescribed areas. Compulsory experience in monetary policy operations is not prescribed.
70.tq: Separate the listed statutory qualifications from an unrelated financial-sector qualification.
xs: Items 1, 2 and 3 are prescribed — option **(1)** **1, 2 and 3 only**.
Members need expertise in **government finance and accounts**, **financial matters and administration**, or **economics**.
**Item 4** wrong: **monetary policy operations** is not a prescribed qualification.
xa: The fourth member: a **High Court judge** or one qualified to be one.
Chairman: **experience in public affairs**.
Act: **FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**.

70.s: The recommendations of the Finance Commission are generally:
o: Judicial orders enforceable without further governmental action
Legally binding in every respect on the Union Government
Binding only on State Governments and never considered by the Union
Advisory and not binding, though they are ordinarily not rejected without compelling reasons
70.x: Finance Commission recommendations are not legally binding. However, the Rajamannar view emphasises that they should not ordinarily be rejected without compelling reasons.
70.tq: Distinguish constitutional recommendation from binding adjudication and note the convention of reasoned acceptance.
xs: FC recommendations are **advisory and not binding**, but not to be rejected **without compelling reasons** — option **(4)**.
This is the view of **P.V. Rajamannar** (**4th FC**).
xa: The President lays them with an **explanatory memorandum** before **each House** (**Art. 281**).
**16th FC** devolution was **accepted** by the Centre in the **Budget 2026-27** speech.
**14th FC** report: accepted on **24 Feb 2015**.

70.s: Which major change was associated with the 14th Finance Commission?
o: A shift towards tax devolution as the main route, along with ignoring the Plan/non-Plan distinction
A shift from tax devolution to exclusive grants
Introduction of the GDP criterion for the first time
70.x: The 14th Finance Commission made tax devolution the main route instead of grants and ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction.
70.tq: Test the direction of policy change by contrasting devolution with grants.
xs: The **14th FC** made **tax devolution the main route** instead of grants and **ignored the Plan/non-Plan distinction** — option **(2)**.
The **GDP criterion** came first with the **16th FC**, not the 14th.
xa: 14th FC raised the vertical share from **32%** to **42%** — the **largest increase ever**.
14th FC made **no distinction** between special and general category states.
Award period: **2015-20**; constituted **2 Jan 2013**.

70.s: Under the 14th Finance Commission’s allocation formula for local-body grants, the weights assigned to the 2011 population and area were respectively:
70.x: The allocation was based on the 2011 population with a 90% weight and area with a 10% weight.
70.tq: Recall the exact pair of weights and their order.
xs: **2011 population 90%** and **area 10%** — option **(2)** is correct.
The weights add to **100**: population dominates, area is a small corrective.
xa: 14th FC local-body grants: **₹2,87,436 crore**, as **basic and performance grants**.
Panchayats got **₹2,00,292 crore**.
14th FC used both **1971 and 2011** population.

70.s: Which of the following was an additional consideration introduced by the 15th Finance Commission?
70.x: The 15th Finance Commission added demographic performance and tax effort as new criteria. It did not retain the earlier share: it cut the States' vertical share from 42% to 41% because of J&K's change of status.
70.tq: Identify the new criteria rather than a feature associated with an earlier commission.
xs: The **15th FC** added **demographic performance** and **tax effort** — option **(1)**.
The Plan/non-Plan distinction was **ignored** by the **14th FC**; tax devolution was not abolished.
xa: 15th FC weights: demographic performance **12.5**, tax and fiscal effort **2.5**.
15th FC was the **first to cut** the vertical share (**42 to 41%**), due to **J&K's change of status**.
16th FC **dropped** tax and fiscal effort.

70.s: The increase in the States' share in the divisible pool recommended by the 14th Finance Commission was described as:
o: a temporary increase applicable for one year
70.x: The 14th Finance Commission's increase of the States' share to 42 per cent was the largest increase ever.
70.tq: Identify the precise comparative description rather than a numerical distractor.
xs: The **14th FC** raise from **32%** to **42%** was the **largest increase ever** — option **(3)**.
The **first reduction** came later, with the **15th FC** (**42 to 41%**).
xa: **15th FC**: **41%** — the **first to cut** the share.
Criticism: after the 42% raise, the Centre increased **non-shareable cesses**.

70.s: Which Finance Commission recommended a National Disaster Response Reserve (NDRR)?
70.x: The 13th Finance Commission recommended the National Disaster Response Reserve (APPSC-GS 2023 key); it also set the States' share at 32%. The 14th FC is known for raising the share to 42%. The 15th FC is known for adding demographic performance and tax effort. The 12th FC is not linked to the NDRR.
70.tq: NDRR = 13th FC (32% share).
xs: The **13th Finance Commission** (13th FC) recommended the **National Disaster Response Reserve (NDRR)** — option **(2)** (**APPSC-GS 2023** key).
The **14th FC** is known for the **42%** share; the **15th FC** for **demographic performance** and **tax effort**.
xa: 13th FC vertical share: **32%**.
**16th FC disaster corpus**: **₹2.04 lakh crore**; sharing **90:10** NE/Himalayan, **75:25** others.
16th FC proposed **heatwaves and lightning** as new notified disasters.

70.s: The award period of the 15th Finance Commission was:
70.x: The 15th FC gave a first report for 2020-21 and a main report for 2021-26. '2020-25' is the trap figure that appears in some sources. 2015-20 was the 14th FC's period and 2026-31 is the 16th FC's. The 15th FC cut the share to 41% because of J&K's change of status.
xs: The 15th FC covered **2020-21 (first report) and 2021-26** — option **(3)**.
⚠ **2020-25** is a trap figure in APP notes; **2015-20** is the **14th FC**; **2026-31** is the **16th FC**.
xa: 15th FC constituted in **Nov 2017**.
It used **2011** population.
It cut the vertical share to **41%**.

70.s: The total grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission amounted to:
70.x: The 16th Finance Commission recommended total grants of ₹9.47 lakh crore.

**Revenue-deficit grants** were **discontinued**.
xa: Local-body grants: **₹7.91 lakh crore**.

2. Rural local bodies get about ₹3.56 lakh crore and urban local bodies about ₹4.35 lakh crore.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
70.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 16th FC local-body grants total ₹7.91 lakh crore. Statement 2 is wrong: the figures are reversed - rural local bodies get about ₹4.35 lakh crore and urban local bodies about ₹3.56 lakh crore. Statement 3 is correct: the urban share is 45%. So options A, C and D, which include statement 2 or leave out 1 or 3, are wrong; B is right.
70.tq: Rural gets the bigger slice (4.35 > 3.56); urban's 45% is a rise, not a majority.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: local-body grants total **₹7.91 lakh crore**.
**Statement 2** wrong: figures reversed — **rural ₹4.35 lakh crore**, **urban ₹3.56 lakh crore**.
**Statement 3** correct: urban share is **45%**.
xa: Urbanisation premium: **₹10,000 crore**.
Some figures put urban at **₹3.5 lakh crore**.
A **duly constituted ULB** is needed to draw 16th FC grants.

70.x: Heatwaves and lightning were proposed as new notified national disasters.

xs: The 16th FC proposed **heatwaves and lightning** as new notified/national disasters — option **(2)**.

xa: Disaster corpus: **₹2.04 lakh crore**.
Sharing: **90:10** for NE/Himalayan states; **75:25** for others.
AP's disaster grant: **₹6,125 crore**.

xs: State deficits are capped at **3% of GSDP** — option **(2)**.

**Statement 3**: **first** to use **Contribution to GDP** (**10%**).

**Statement 1**: submitted to the President in **Nov 2025**.
**Statement 2**: tabled in Parliament on **1 Feb 2026**.
**Statement 3** wrong: the devolution was **accepted** in the **Budget 2026-27** speech.

**Demographic performance**, **forest and ecology** and **area** were already in the 15th FC.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission criteria:
1. The weight for area declined from 15% under the 15th Finance Commission to 10% under the 16th Finance Commission.

3. Tax and fiscal effort was dropped by the 16th Finance Commission.
4. Demographic performance was reduced from 12.5% to 10%.

70.x: All four statements are correct. Area and demographic performance received lower weights, forest and ecology remained unchanged, and tax and fiscal effort was dropped.

xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** **1, 2, 3 and 4**.
**Area**: **15 → 10**; **forest and ecology**: **10** in both.
**Tax and fiscal effort**: **dropped**; **demographic performance**: **12.5 → 10**.
xa: **Income distance**: **45 → 42.5**.
New: **Contribution to GDP**, **10%**.

70.s: The divisible pool of Central taxes is calculated by deducting which of the following from gross tax revenue?
o: Cesses, surcharges and cost of collection
States’ share and Finance Commission grants
Only customs duties and Union excise
70.x: The divisible pool is gross tax revenue minus cesses, surcharges and the cost of collection. The net proceeds are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
70.tq: Apply the formula by identifying the deductions rather than the items included in the pool.
xs: The divisible pool excludes **cesses, surcharges and cost of collection** — option **(1)**.
The **16th FC**'s **41%** applies only to this divisible pool.
xa: Criticism: rising **cesses and surcharges** shrink the divisible pool.
After the 14th FC's **42%**, the Centre increased **non-shareable cesses**.
FM: total transfers **₹25.44 lakh crore** for 2026-27.

70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission award covers the period from 2026 to 2031.

xs: It follows the 15th FC's **2021-26** period.
xa: Constituted on **31 Dec 2023**.
Report to President **Nov 2025**; tabled **1 Feb 2026**.

70.x: T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda and Soumya Kanti Ghosh were members of the 16th FC. P.V. Rajamannar chaired the 4th Finance Commission and is known for the view that FC recommendations should not be rejected without very compelling reasons.
70.tq: 16th FC members: Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh.

16th FC members: **T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh**.

**Statement 1**: **revenue-deficit grants discontinued**.
**Statement 2**: disaster corpus **₹2.04 lakh crore**.
**Statement 3** wrong: ratios reversed — **90:10** for NE/Himalayan, **75:25** for others.

70.s: Which of the following correctly states the allocations for Andhra Pradesh under the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026–31?
o: Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; disaster: ₹6,125 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹12,158 crore; urban local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; disaster: ₹5,000 crore
Rural local bodies: ₹16,627 crore; urban local bodies: ₹6,125 crore; disaster: ₹12,158 crore

70.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission allocation for Andhra Pradesh is ₹16,627 crore for rural local bodies, ₹12,158 crore for urban local bodies and ₹6,125 crore for disaster-related grants.

70.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It was rejected in Parliament in 2014 and replaced by a constitutional tax devolution formula.

xa: 14th FC panchayats: **₹2,00,292 crore**, as **basic and performance grants**.
15th FC: urban local bodies share **36%**.
16th FC: urban share **45%**.

70.s: Which of the following correctly represents the 16th Finance Commission’s grants for rural and urban local bodies?
o: Rural ₹4.4 lakh crore; urban ₹4.4 lakh crore
Rural ₹4.4 lakh crore; urban ₹3.6 lakh crore
Rural ₹3.6 lakh crore; urban ₹3.6 lakh crore
Rural ₹3.6 lakh crore; urban ₹4.4 lakh crore
70.x: The 16th FC's ₹7.91 lakh crore local-body grants split into about ₹4.35 lakh crore (≈₹4.4 lakh crore) for rural and ₹3.56 lakh crore (≈₹3.6 lakh crore) for urban local bodies, the urban share being 45%. D reverses the two figures.
70.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban figures in a paired comparison.
xs: **Rural ₹4.4 lakh crore; urban ₹3.6 lakh crore** — option **(2)** (exact: **₹4.35** and **₹3.56 lakh crore**).
⚠ Option (4) reverses them; rural is the larger share.
xa: Total local-body grants: **₹7.91 lakh crore**.
Urban share: **45%**.
Urbanisation premium: **₹10,000 crore**.

70.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the share of States in the divisible pool of central taxes:
1. The 14th Finance Commission raised it from 32% to 42%.
2. The 15th Finance Commission recommended 41%, the fall reflecting the change in status of Jammu and Kashmir.
3. The 16th Finance Commission reduced it to 40%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
70.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the 16th Finance Commission retained the States' share at 41%.
70.tq: 42 then 41, and 41 stays.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 2**: 15th FC — **41%**, due to **J&K's change of status**.
**Statement 3** wrong: the 16th FC **retained 41%**.
xa: 16th FC's 41% excludes **cesses and surcharges**.
FM: states got the **full 41%**.

70.s: Which one of the following pairs of Finance Commission and award period is correctly matched?
70.x: The 16th FC covers 2026-27 to 2030-31. The 14th FC covered 2015-20, and the 15th FC gave reports for 2020-21 and for 2021-26.
70.tq: Five-year blocks: 2015, 2020, 2026 (15th FC had an extra year).
xs: **16th Finance Commission — 2026-27 to 2030-31** is correctly matched — option **(3)**.
**14th FC** covered **2015-20**; **15th FC** gave reports for **2020-21** and **2021-26**.
xa: ⚠ "**2020-25**" for the 15th FC is a trap in APP notes.
14th FC constituted **2 Jan 2013**; 16th FC **31 Dec 2023**.

70.s: The 15th Finance Commission was the first Finance Commission to:
o: cut the States' vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent
recommend a 50 per cent share to the States
70.x: The 15th Finance Commission was the first to reduce the vertical share from 42 per cent to 41 per cent, largely in the context of the change in Jammu and Kashmir's status.
70.tq: Test a first-in-series fact against nearby but unsupported reforms.
xs: The **15th FC** was the **first to cut** the vertical share, **42 to 41%** — option **(1)**.
The cut reflected **J&K's change of status**.
xa: **14th FC**: largest increase ever (**32 → 42%**).
**16th FC**: first to use **Contribution to GDP** (**10%**).
15th FC added **demographic performance** and **tax effort**.

70.s: The rising use of cesses and surcharges is criticised because it:
o: shrinks the divisible pool available for sharing
raises the States' vertical share automatically
increases the divisible pool available for tax devolution
70.x: Cesses and surcharges are not generally part of the divisible pool, so their increasing use shrinks the pool available for devolution.
70.tq: Trace the fiscal cause-and-effect relationship in a policy scenario.
xs: Rising **cesses and surcharges** **shrink the divisible pool** available for sharing — so option **(1)** is correct.
The divisible pool **excludes cesses, surcharges and cost of collection**, so more cesses mean less to share with states.
They do not raise the states' share or enlarge the pool; the **16th FC** kept the share at **41%**.
xa: After the **14th FC** raised the share to **42%**, the Centre increased **non-shareable cesses**.
FM: states got the **full 41%**; total transfers **₹25.44 lakh crore** for 2026-27.
Southern states call their shares unfair — Karnataka **4.13%** (15th: **3.64%**; 14th: **4.71%**).

70.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh Finance Minister's statement, the State lost up to what amount in Central grants after the 16th Finance Commission dropped revenue deficit grants?
70.x: Andhra Pradesh was stated to have lost up to ₹38,000 crore in Central grants after revenue deficit grants were dropped.
70.tq: Separate the reported loss from the projected revenue deficit.
xs: AP's Finance Minister said the State lost up to **₹38,000 crore** in Central grants — so option **(1)** is correct.
The loss followed the **16th FC** dropping **revenue deficit grants**.
⚠ **₹25.44 lakh crore** is total transfers for 2026-27, and **₹9.47 lakh crore** is the 16th FC's total grants.
xa: Without these grants AP must cut its revenue deficit; the **2026-27 AP Budget** shows **1.1%**.
A **duly constituted ULB** is needed to draw 16th FC grants; ULB elections for **100 of 123** ULBs (**Aug 2026**).
AP's 16th FC share: **4.217%**.

70.s: Which of the following States was specifically associated with fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission provided neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants?
70.x: Kerala was identified as facing fiscal stress because the 16th Finance Commission gave it neither revenue deficit grants nor State-specific grants.
70.tq: Match the State with the specific fiscal consequence.
xs: **Kerala** faces fiscal stress as the 16th FC gives it **no revenue deficit or state-specific grants** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Andhra Pradesh** is linked to the **₹38,000 crore** loss; **Karnataka** to complaints about its **4.13%** share.
xa: Kerala's horizontal share still rose to **2.382%** from **1.92%**.
**Revenue-deficit grants** were **discontinued** by the 16th FC.
State deficits are capped at **3% of GSDP**.

71.s: Under Article 150, the form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the
71.x: Article 150 provides that the form of accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG.
71.tq: Identify the constitutional adviser rather than the body that later scrutinises the accounts.
xs: Under **Art. 150**, the President prescribes the **form of accounts** on the advice of the **Comptroller and Auditor General** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **PAC** examines CAG reports; the **Finance Commission** deals with devolution — neither advises on the form of accounts.
xa: **Art. 148**: appointment, oath, conditions of service; **Art. 149**: duties and powers; **Art. 151**: audit reports.
**1976 amendment** separated **accounts from audit** at the Centre.
The CAG heads the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.

71.s: The official constitutional name of the office is:
71.x: The official name is Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. “Controller” and “Attorney” are not substitutes for the constitutional terms.
71.tq: Discriminate between similar-looking official titles.
xs: The official name is **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India** — so option **(1)** is correct.
⚠ Not "**Controller**", not "**Attorney**", not "Accounts-General".
xa: Yet he is only an **Auditor-General**, not a true Comptroller — he has **no control over the issue of money**.
Called the "**Guardian of the public purse**".
First CAG: **V. Narahari Rao** (**1948**).

71.s:
Match List-I (Article) with List-II (Subject):
List-I
A. Article 148
B. Article 149
C. Article 150
D. Article 151
List-II
1. Audit reports
2. Form of accounts of the Union and States
3. Duties and powers of the CAG
4. Appointment of the CAG
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Article 148 covers the CAG's appointment, oath and conditions of service. Article 149 covers duties and powers. Article 150 covers the form of accounts, which the President prescribes on the CAG's advice. Article 151 covers audit reports. So the answer is A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1. Each other code swaps at least one pair.
71.tq: 148 appoint, 149 duties, 150 accounts form, 151 reports.
xs: **A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Art. 148**: appointment; **Art. 149**: duties and powers.
**Art. 150**: **form of accounts**; **Art. 151**: **audit reports**.
xa: The **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971** was enacted under **Arts. 148-149**.
**Art. 151(2)**: State reports go to the **Governor**.
Oath: before the **President**, form in the **Third Schedule**.

71.s: Who was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
71.x: V. Narahari Rao was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
71.tq: Directly identify the office-holder associated with the beginning of the institution.
xs: **V. Narahari Rao** was the **first CAG** (**1948**) — so option **(3)** is correct.
**K. Sanjay Murthy** is the **current** CAG; **K.C. Venugopal** chairs the **PAC**.
xa: K. Sanjay Murthy is the **15th** CAG (as of **May 2026**).
**Vinod Rai**: CAG of the **2G spectrum (2010)** report; wrote "**When Audit Matters**".
**Ambedkar**: CAG = "most important officer under the Constitution".

71.s: The oath of office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is administered by the President in the form prescribed in the
71.x: The CAG takes the oath before the President, in the form prescribed in the Third Schedule.
71.tq: Separate the Schedule dealing with oath from the Schedule dealing with salary and service conditions.
xs: The CAG takes the oath before the **President** in the form in the **Third Schedule** — option **(3)**.
⚠ The **Second Schedule** holds his **salary**, not the oath.
xa: Appointed by the **President** by **warrant under his hand and seal** (**Art. 148**).
Resigns to the **President**.
Term: **6 years or age 65**.

71.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
o: It is equal to the salary of a High Court judge and is charged on the Contingency Fund of India.
It is equal to the salary of a Supreme Court judge and is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
It is fixed by the Public Accounts Committee and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
It is equal to the salary of the President and is voted annually by Parliament.
71.x: The CAG receives a salary equal to that of a Supreme Court judge. The expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and is not subject to vote.
71.tq: Compare the office-holder’s salary, authority fixing it and fund charged with nearby constitutional offices.
xs: Salary **equal to a Supreme Court judge**, **charged on the Consolidated Fund of India** — option **(2)**.
It is fixed by **Parliament** (**Second Schedule**) and is **not votable** — not a High Court judge's salary, not the Contingency Fund.
xa: Salary, **leave**, pension and retirement age cannot be varied to his disadvantage.
Office expenses, allowances and pensions are also **charged** on the CFI.
**Leave** is granted by the **President**.

71.s:
With reference to the service conditions of the Comptroller and Auditor General, consider the following statements:
1. Leave of the CAG is granted by the President.
2. Salary, leave, pension and retirement age may be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.
3. The salary and service conditions are provided in the Second Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because salary, leave, pension and retirement age cannot be varied to the CAG’s disadvantage after appointment.
71.tq: Find the statement reversing the constitutional protection against disadvantageous alteration of service conditions.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: **leave** is granted by the **President**.
**Statement 2** wrong: these **cannot be varied to his disadvantage** after appointment.
**Statement 3** correct: salary is fixed in the **Second Schedule**.
xa: Salary **equal to an SC judge**.
Expenses **charged** on the **Consolidated Fund of India** — not votable.
**No minister** represents the CAG in Parliament.

71.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General is correct?
o: No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament.
The President represents the CAG in Parliament.
The CAG is represented in Parliament by the Chairperson of the PAC.
A Union Minister represents the CAG in Parliament.
71.x: No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament. The CAG submits audit reports through the constitutionally prescribed channel.
71.tq: Use the institutional-role distinction to avoid assigning parliamentary representation to the wrong authority.
xs: **No Minister represents the CAG in Parliament** — option **(1)**.
His reports reach Parliament via the **President** (**Art. 151**), not through a minister or the PAC chairperson.
xa: The CAG is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**".
Executive accountability to Parliament works mainly through **CAG reports**.
Not eligible for **further office** under GOI or any State after retirement.

71.s: Who is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as mentioned for 2026?
71.x: K. Sanjay Murthy is mentioned as the CAG of India for 2026.
71.tq: Directly test the current office-holder against historical and related names.
xs: **K. Sanjay Murthy** is the current CAG (**8 May 2026**) — option **(3)**.
**V. Narahari Rao** was the **first** CAG; **K.C. Venugopal** chairs the **PAC**.
xa: He is the **15th** CAG.
**Vinod Rai** wrote "**When Audit Matters**" (**2026**).
India hosted the **5th BRICS SAI Leaders' Summit** in 2026.

71.s: Among the following, whose normal constitutional term is the longest in duration?
71.x: The CAG's term is six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier; the other listed posts ordinarily have five-year terms.
71.tq: Compare the numerical term lengths before considering qualifications such as dissolution.
xs: The **Comptroller and Auditor-General** has the longest term — **6 years or 65** — option **(1)** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
**President**, **Vice-President** and **Lok Sabha member**: **5 years**.
xa: **CEC** and **UPSC member** also have **6 years or 65**.
The CAG's term was the **APPSC 2022** key.
Removal: like a **Supreme Court judge**.

71.s:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India:
1. He holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
2. He holds office during the pleasure of the President.
3. He can be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.
4. After ceasing to hold office, he is not eligible for further office under the Government of India or any State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: the term is 6 years or age 65. Statement 2 is wrong: the CAG does not hold office at the President's pleasure. Statement 3 is correct: he is removed like a Supreme Court judge, on an address by both Houses passed with a special majority for proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Statement 4 is correct: he is barred from further office under the Government of India or any State. So '1, 3 and 4 only'.
71.tq: CAG: 6 yrs/65, removed like SC judge, not at pleasure, no post-retirement office.
xs: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct — option **(1)** **1, 3 and 4 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: **6 years or age 65**.
**Statement 2** wrong: he does **not** hold office at the **President's pleasure**.
**Statements 3, 4** correct: removed **like a Supreme Court judge**; **no further office** under GOI or any State.
xa: Removal: address by both Houses with **special majority** for proved **misbehaviour or incapacity**.
Resignation: to the **President**.
Salary **equal to an SC judge**.

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India functions under the legal framework of the
o: CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
71.x: The CAG’s duties, powers and conditions of service are governed by the Comptroller and Auditor General’s Act of 1971, made under Articles 148 and 149.
71.tq: Identify the correct statute by matching the institution with its specific enabling Act.
xs: The CAG works under the **CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971** — option **(2)**.
It was enacted under **Arts. 148-149**.
xa: It covers **State accounts**: compilation and submission to President/Governors/Administrators.
**1976 amendment**: separated **accounts from audit** at the Centre.
The **FC (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act** is **1951** and concerns the Finance Commission, not the CAG.

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the audit jurisdiction of the Comptroller and Auditor General:
1. He audits the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. He audits the Consolidated Funds of States and Union Territories having legislatures.
3. He audits the Contingency Funds and Public Accounts.
4. He audits only expenditure and not receipts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the CAG audits both receipts and expenditure.
71.tq: Reject the exclusive claim that narrows a broad constitutional audit jurisdiction.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1)** **1, 2 and 3 only**.
He audits **receipts and expenditure** of the **Consolidated Fund** of India, each State and each UT with a legislature.
He also audits **Contingency Funds** and **Public Accounts**.
**Statement 4** wrong: he audits **receipts** as well as expenditure.
xa: He also audits **government companies** and bodies **substantially financed** by government.
**Limit**: cannot audit **secret service expenditure**.
Local bodies: only on request of the **President/Governor**.

71.s:
With reference to the audit jurisdiction of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, consider the following statements:
1. He audits bodies substantially financed by the government and government companies.
2. He audits trading, manufacturing and profit-and-loss accounts of government departments.
3. He audits local bodies automatically in every case, without any request.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
71.x: Statement 1 is correct: bodies substantially financed by government and government companies fall within CAG audit. Statement 2 is correct: trading, manufacturing and profit-and-loss accounts of departments are audited. Statement 3 is wrong: local bodies are audited only on the request of the President or the Governor. So A misses statement 2, C and D wrongly include statement 3, and B is right.
71.tq: Local bodies = only on request of President/Governor; watch for 'automatically'.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: bodies **substantially financed** by government and **govt companies**.
**Statement 2** correct: **trading/manufacturing/profit-loss** accounts of departments.
**Statement 3** wrong: **local bodies** are audited only **when requested** by the **President/Governor**.
xa: **Sixth Schedule councils** are also covered.
**Secret service expenditure**: he accepts the competent authority's certificate.
He audits **Contingency Funds** and **Public Accounts** too.

71.s: Why is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India described as only an Auditor-General and not a true Comptroller?
o: He cannot audit the accounts of State Governments.
He cannot audit receipts of the Consolidated Fund.
He cannot submit reports to the President.
He has no control over the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund.
71.x: The CAG audits public finances but does not control the issue or release of money from the Consolidated Fund. This control exists for the Comptroller and Auditor General in Britain.
71.tq: Discriminate between the auditing function and the comptrolling function by focusing on control over release of funds.
xs: He has **no control over the issue or release of money** from the **Consolidated Fund** — option **(4)**.
So he is only an **Auditor-General**; in **Britain** the C&AG does control issue.
He does audit **State** accounts and **receipts**, and reports to the **President**.
xa: ⚠ "**CAG controls the entire financial system**" was the **wrong** statement (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
Official name: **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India**.
Title: "**Guardian of the public purse**".

71.s: Which statement best reflects Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s description of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
o: The principal law officer of the Union
The chief electoral authority of India
The least independent officer under the Constitution
The most important officer under the Constitution
71.x: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described the CAG as the most important officer under the Constitution.
71.tq: Match the quoted assessment with the correct constitutional office.
xs: **Ambedkar** called the CAG "**the most important officer under the Constitution**" — option **(4)**.
He is not the law officer or the electoral authority.
xa: Other title: "**Guardian of the public purse**".
Vis-a-vis PAC: "**friend, philosopher and guide**".
Independence: removed only **like a Supreme Court judge**.

71.s: The separation of accounts from audit at the Union level took place in:
71.x: Accounts were separated from audit at the Centre in 1976. The 1976 amendment relieved the CAG of compiling Union Government accounts through departmentalisation.
71.tq: Distinguish the enactment year from the year of departmentalisation.
xs: Accounts were separated from audit at the Centre in **1976** — option **(2)**.
The **1976 amendment** relieved the CAG of **compiling Union Government accounts** (**departmentalisation**).
⚠ **1971** is the year of the **CAG Act**, not the separation.
xa: The CAG still keeps most **state** accounts.
He heads the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.

71.s: With reference to the accounts of States, which one of the following is correct?
o: The CAG continues to keep most State accounts
The CAG keeps no State accounts after 1976
State accounts are kept by the Public Accounts Committee
All State accounts are kept exclusively by the Union Finance Ministry
71.x: Although Union accounts were separated from audit in 1976, the CAG continues to keep most State accounts.
71.tq: Use the Centre-State contrast to avoid overgeneralisation.
xs: **The CAG continues to keep most State accounts** — option **(1)**.
The **1976** separation of accounts from audit applied only **at the Centre**.
xa: The **1971 Act** provides for compiling State accounts and submitting them to **President/Governors/Administrators**.
**Art. 150**: form of accounts on the **CAG's advice**.
State audit reports go to the **Governor** (**Art. 151(2)**).

71.s: The CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides, among other things, for:
o: Appointment of all State Finance Ministers
Preparation of the Union Budget by the CAG
Conduct of elections to local bodies
Compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators
71.x: The Act provides for compilation of State accounts and their submission to the President, Governors or Administrators. It does not make the CAG the budget-making or election authority.
71.tq: Identify the statutory function without confusing it with executive functions.
xs: The **1971 Act** provides for **compilation of State accounts** and their **submission to the President, Governors or Administrators** — option **(4)**.
It does not make the CAG a **budget**, election or appointing authority.
xa: Enacted under **Arts. 148-149**.
The **1976 amendment** separated accounts from audit at the Centre.
CAG heads the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**.

71.s: Which one of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India is NOT correct?
o: He is called the guardian of the public purse
He heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department
He controls the entire financial system of the country
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called him the most important officer under the Constitution
71.x: C is the incorrect statement (APPSC-G2 2017). The Indian CAG is only an Auditor-General: unlike the British C&AG, he has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund. A, B and D are all correct: he is called the guardian of the public purse, he heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, and Ambedkar called him the most important officer under the Constitution.
71.tq: Indian CAG audits; he does not control the issue of money.
xs: "**He controls the entire financial system of the country**" is wrong — option **(3)** (**APPSC-G2 2017**).
He has **no control over the issue of money** from the Consolidated Fund — he is only an **Auditor-General**.
The rest are true: "**guardian of the public purse**", head of the **Indian Audit and Accounts Department**, and **Ambedkar's** "most important officer".
xa: In **Britain** the C&AG does control issue.
He is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**".

71.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the audit types mentioned for the Comptroller and Auditor General?
1. Compliance audit is obligatory.
2. Financial attest audit is obligatory.
3. Performance audit is discretionary.
4. Performance audit is constitutionally prohibited.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: compliance and financial attest audits are obligatory, while performance audit is discretionary. Statement 4 is false because performance audit is permitted as a discretionary audit.
71.tq: Separate obligatory audit categories from discretionary performance audit and reject the prohibition trap.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1, 2 and 3 only**.
**Compliance** (legal + regulatory) and **financial attest** audits are **obligatory**.
**Performance** audit is **discretionary**; **statement 4** wrong — it is not prohibited.
xa: **Propriety audit** is also discretionary: **wisdom, economy** of expenditure.
Performance audit tests **economy, efficiency, effectiveness** of schemes.
**Social audits** feed CAG performance audits.

71.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a legal and regulatory, or compliance, audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?
o: It examines whether money was legally available and spent according to rules
It measures the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes
It examines only the wisdom and economy of expenditure
It certifies that accounts conform to a prescribed reporting framework
71.x: A legal and regulatory audit is obligatory and examines whether money was legally available and spent in accordance with applicable rules.
71.tq: Match the audit type with its distinctive test.
xs: Compliance audit checks that **money was legally available and spent as rules require** — option **(1)**.
**Economy, efficiency, effectiveness** = **performance** audit; **wisdom and economy** = **propriety**; reporting framework = **financial attest**.
xa: Compliance and financial attest audits are **obligatory**.
Propriety and performance audits are **discretionary**.
Propriety audit **flags extravagance**.

71.s: The primary purpose of a financial attest audit is to determine whether:
o: Accounts are true and conform to the applicable reporting framework
All expenditure was approved by the Public Accounts Committee
Schemes achieved their intended social outcomes
71.x: Financial attest audit is an obligatory audit concerned with the truthfulness of accounts and their conformity with the reporting framework.
71.tq: Use the function-based distinction between similar audit types.
xs: A financial attest audit checks that **accounts are true** and per the **reporting framework** — option **(2)**.
It is an **obligatory** audit.
xa: **Compliance** audit: money legally available and spent as rules require.
**Performance** audit: **economy, efficiency, effectiveness** of schemes (discretionary).
**Propriety**: wisdom, faithfulness, economy (discretionary).

71.s:
Consider the following statements regarding types of audit:
1. Propriety audit examines wisdom, faithfulness and economy in expenditure.
2. Performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes.
3. Both propriety audit and performance audit are obligatory audits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because propriety and performance audits are discretionary, whereas legal-regulatory and financial-attest audits are obligatory.
71.tq: Separate the nature of an audit from the subject it tests.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(3)** **1 and 2 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: propriety audit — **wisdom, faithfulness, economy**.
**Statement 2** correct: performance audit — **economy, efficiency, effectiveness**.
**Statement 3** wrong: both are **discretionary**; **legal-regulatory** and **financial attest** are obligatory.
xa: Propriety audit **flags extravagance**.
**MGNREGA social audit standards**: **2016**.

71.s: Social audits conducted under MGNREGA are relevant to the Comptroller and Auditor-General's performance audits because they:
o: Determine the CAG's term of office
Are conducted exclusively by the CAG
Replace the statutory audit of MGNREGA accounts
71.x: Social audits feed into the CAG's performance audits, which test the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of schemes; MGNREGA social audit standards were issued in 2016. Social audits do not replace the statutory audit, are not done by the CAG alone and have nothing to do with the CAG's term.
71.tq: Apply the relationship between participatory audit and performance audit.
xs: MGNREGA **social audits feed into CAG performance audits** — option **(4)**.
They do not replace statutory audit, are not done by the CAG alone, and have no link to his term.
xa: MGNREGA social audit standards: **2016**.
Performance audit tests **economy, efficiency, effectiveness** — it is **discretionary**.
CAG uses **AI/ML-based** audits to detect welfare fraud.

71.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to audit of public sector entities?
1. DVC — Audited directly by the CAG
2. ONGC — Audited directly by the CAG
3. Central Warehousing Corporation — Private auditors appointed on the CAG's advice, with supplementary audit by the CAG
4. RBI — Supplementary audit by the CAG after appointment of private auditors on its advice
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
71.x: DVC and ONGC are directly audited by the CAG. Central Warehousing Corporation follows the private-auditor and supplementary-audit arrangement; RBI is wholly privately audited, so statement 4 is false.
71.tq: Classify entities by the mode of CAG involvement.
xs: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1, 2 and 3 only**.
**DVC** and **ONGC**: audited **directly** by the CAG.
**Central Warehousing Corp.**: **private auditors** on CAG's advice + CAG **supplementary audit**.
**Pair 4** wrong: **RBI** has a **wholly private audit**.
xa: **IFCI** is in the same group as Central Warehousing Corp.
**LIC** is also wholly privately audited.

71.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sixth Schedule councils may also come within the scope of CAG audit of local bodies.
2. The CAG can audit secret service expenditure in the same manner as ordinary expenditure.
3. In relation to secret service expenditure, the CAG accepts a certificate from the competent authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
71.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because the CAG cannot audit secret service expenditure and instead accepts a certificate from the competent authority.
71.tq: Find the exception to the general audit power.
xs: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — option **(2)** **1 and 3 only**.
**Statement 1** correct: **Sixth Schedule councils** are also covered.
**Statement 2** wrong: he **cannot audit secret service expenditure**.
**Statement 3** correct: he accepts the **competent authority's certificate**.
xa: Local bodies are audited on request of the **President/Governor**.
He audits bodies **substantially financed** by government.

71.s: Which Article of the Constitution specifically deals with the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General?
71.x: Article 151 deals with the submission and laying of the CAG’s audit reports before the appropriate legislature.
71.tq: Distinguish the reporting provision from the neighbouring Articles on appointment, powers and accounts.
xs: **Article 151** deals with **audit reports** — option **(2)**.
**148**: appointment; **149**: duties and powers; **150**: form of accounts.
xa: Union reports → **President** → **both Houses** → **PAC**.
State reports → **Governor** → **state legislature** (**Art. 151(2)**).

71.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three principal Union reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General mentioned in this context?
o: Report on the delimitation of constituencies
71.x: The three Union reports are the Appropriation Accounts Report, Finance Accounts Report and Report on Public Undertakings. Delimitation of constituencies is unrelated to CAG reporting.
71.tq: Identify the unrelated institutional subject among three closely associated CAG reports.
xs: **Delimitation of constituencies** is not a CAG report — option **(3)**.
The three Union reports: **appropriation accounts**, **finance accounts**, **public undertakings**.
xa: PSU reports → **Committee on Public Undertakings**.
Other reports → **PAC**.
Landmark reports: **2G (2010)**, **Coal (2012)**, **Rafale (2019)**.

71.s: Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to public sector undertakings are examined by the
71.x: Reports relating to public sector undertakings are referred to the Committee on Public Undertakings, while the PAC examines the other relevant CAG reports.
71.tq: Separate the two parliamentary committees by the subject of the report they examine.
xs: PSU reports go to the **Committee on Public Undertakings** — option **(1)**.
The **PAC** examines the other Union reports.
xa: PAC: **22 members** (**15 LS + 7 RS**), elected yearly by **STV**.
The CAG is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**".

71.s: The Comptroller and Auditor General is described as the Public Accounts Committee’s
71.x: The CAG acts as the PAC’s friend, philosopher and guide by assisting it in examining audit findings.
71.tq: Recall the distinctive institutional relationship without confusing advisory assistance with membership.
xs: The CAG is the PAC's "**friend, philosopher and guide**" — option **(1)**.
He is not a member, chairperson or appointing authority of the PAC.
xa: PAC chairperson: from the **Opposition since 1967**; currently **K.C. Venugopal**.
PAC set up in **1921**.
PAC recommendations are **not binding**.

71.s: The audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to a State are submitted to the
o: Speaker of the Lok Sabha, who refers them to the PAC
Chief Minister, who lays them before the Legislative Assembly
Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature
