 d. Article 243J

List-II (Subject)
 i. Audit of accounts
 ii. Existing laws and Panchayats continue for a limited period
 iii. Bar on interference by courts in electoral matters
 iv. Part IX not to apply to certain areas
81.x: Article 243M concerns exempted areas, Article 243N permits existing laws to continue for up to one year, Article 243O bars court interference in electoral matters, and Article 243J concerns audit.
81.tq: Begin with Article 243J–audit and distinguish the final three Articles by their sequential subjects.
xs: Correct code: **a–iv, b–ii, c–iii, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**243M** — Part IX not to apply to certain areas; **243N** — existing laws continue up to **one year**.
**243O** — **bar on court interference** in electoral matters; **243J** — **audit**.
xa: ⚠ **243M** = Part IX exemption; **243ZC** = Part IXA exemption.
**243L** — application to Union Territories.

81.s: Under Article 243B of the Constitution, which of the following is the correct three-tier structure of Panchayats?
81.x: Article 243B provides for Panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels.
81.tq: Directly identify the constitutional structure from the three levels.
xs: **Art. 243B**: **village, intermediate and district** levels — option **(3)**.
The three tiers are **compulsory**; State and Union are not panchayat tiers.
xa: States with population **not exceeding 20 lakh** may skip the **intermediate** tier.
AP's intermediate tier: **Mandal Parishad** (Mandal Praja Parishad).
Other names: **Kshetra** (UP), **Janpad** (MP), **Anchalik** (Assam), **Taluk** (Karnataka, Gujarat).

81.s: A State having a population not exceeding 20 lakh may constitutionally dispense with which tier of Panchayati Raj institutions?
81.x: Article 243B permits a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh to omit the intermediate level of Panchayats.
81.tq: Use the population threshold to distinguish the optional intermediate tier.
xs: A state of population **not exceeding 20 lakh** may skip the **intermediate tier** — option **(3)** (Art. **243B**).
The **Gram Sabha** is compulsory in every village, and village and district panchayats remain.
xa: Intermediate and district chairpersons are elected **indirectly**.
Most states call the intermediate tier the **Panchayat Samiti**.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
81.x: Anchalik Panchayat is the name used for the intermediate tier in Assam. Kshetra Panchayat is associated with Uttar Pradesh, Janpad Panchayat with Madhya Pradesh, and Taluk Panchayat with Karnataka and Gujarat.
81.tq: Start from the sure state-specific pair and eliminate swapped locations.
xs: **Anchalik Panchayat — Assam** is correct — option **(3)**.
**Kshetra Panchayat** = **Uttar Pradesh**; **Janpad Panchayat** = **Madhya Pradesh**; **Taluk Panchayat** = **Karnataka, Gujarat**.
xa: AP: **Mandal Parishad** (Mandal Praja Parishad).
**Panchayat Samiti** in most states, e.g. **Rajasthan**, **Maharashtra**.

81.s: In the context of the Panchayati Raj system, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zila Parishads at sub-divisional level — Assam
81.x: Mandal Praja Parishad is associated with Andhra Pradesh. The cited matching facts include Zila Parishads at the sub-divisional level in Assam, tribal councils in Meghalaya and absence of village panchayats in Mizoram.
81.tq: Identify the exact institutional association rather than relying on geographical familiarity.
xs: **Mandal Praja Parishad — Andhra Pradesh** is correct — option **(2)** (UPSC 2000 match).
Zila Parishads at sub-divisional level = **Assam** (option 1 is the real UPSC pairing, but options 3 and 4 swap states).
**Tribal councils** = **Meghalaya**; **no village panchayats** = **Mizoram**.
xa: **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram** are exempted from Part IX (**243M**).
AP tiers: Gram Panchayat — **Mandal Parishad** — Zilla Parishad.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding membership of Panchayats:
1. All members at the three levels are directly elected from territorial constituencies.
2. The Constitution itself prescribes a uniform method for choosing every village chairperson.
3. Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels are elected by and from among the elected members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The method of choosing a village chairperson is left to State law; the Constitution does not prescribe one uniform method.
81.tq: Split the options by checking the constitutional distinction between members and chairpersons.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: **all members** at all three levels are **directly elected** from territorial constituencies.
2 wrong: the **village chairperson** is chosen as **State law** provides.
3: **intermediate and district chairpersons** are elected **indirectly**, by and from among elected members (**Art. 243C**).
xa: ⚠ IYB 2026 speaks of direct election of chairpersons (quoting the original Bill) — follow the Article as enacted.
Minimum age to be a member: **21** (**Art. 243F**).

81.s: If a Panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of its normal term, elections to reconstitute it shall ordinarily be completed within:
o: The remaining period of the original term only
81.x: Elections must ordinarily be completed within six months of dissolution. No election is necessary when the remainder of the Panchayat's term is less than six months.
81.tq: Separate the six-month election deadline from the exception concerning the remaining term.
xs: After early dissolution, elections within **six months** — option **(2)**.
No election is needed if **less than six months** of the term remain.
xa: The reconstituted panchayat serves only the **remainder** of the term.
Normal term: **5 years** (**Art. 243E**).

81.s: A person is disqualified for being chosen as a member of a Panchayat if the person is disqualified under:
o: Only a law made by the Union Parliament
The law relating exclusively to Municipalities
Only the law relating to elections to Parliament
The law for elections to the State Legislature or a law made by the State Legislature
81.x: Article 243F refers to disqualification under the law for elections to the State Legislature or under a law made by the State Legislature.
81.tq: Ask which legislative framework supplies the disqualification rather than focusing only on age.
xs: Disqualification is under **the law for State Legislature elections or a law made by the State Legislature** — option **(4)** (Art. **243F**).
It is not limited to a Union law or the law for **Parliament** elections.
xa: Minimum age to be a member: **21 years**.
**243K** — **State Election Commission** conducts panchayat polls.
**243O** bars courts from interfering in electoral matters.

81.s: Which one of the following is correct regarding a Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution?
o: It serves only for the remainder of the original term.
It always enjoys a fresh five-year term.
It continues until the next general election to the State Legislature.
It serves for six months only.
81.x: A Panchayat constituted after an early dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.
81.tq: Reject the tempting but incorrect assumption that every newly elected Panchayat gets a fresh full term.
xs: A panchayat formed after early dissolution serves **only the remainder** of the original term — option **(1)**.
It does not get a fresh **five-year** term.
xa: Elections must be held within **six months** of dissolution.
No election if the remaining term is **under six months**.

81.s: Which Article provides for the Gram Sabha to exercise such powers and perform such functions at the village level as the State Legislature may provide by law?
81.x: Article 243A deals with the powers and functions of the Gram Sabha, while Article 243(b) defines its composition.
81.tq: Discriminate between the definition provision and the functions provision.
xs: **Article 243A**: the Gram Sabha exercises powers **as the State Legislature provides by law** — option **(2)**.
**243B** = three tiers; **243C** = composition; **243F** = disqualifications.
xa: **Art. 243(b)** defines the Gram Sabha: all persons **registered as voters** of a village.
The Constitution leaves its powers to **States**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements about the Gram Sabha:
1. Its powers are exhaustively specified by the Constitution and cannot be enlarged by State law.
2. It comprises persons registered in the electoral rolls of villages within the Panchayat area.
3. The State Legislature may confer powers and functions on it by law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution leaves the detailed powers and functions of the Gram Sabha to State legislation, so statement 1 is false.
81.tq: Identify the false absolute statement about powers being exhaustively fixed by the Constitution.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
1 wrong: the Constitution **leaves the Gram Sabha's powers to States**.
2: it is all persons **registered in the electoral rolls** of a village in the panchayat area.
3: State Legislature may confer powers by law (**Art. 243A**).
xa: In **Fifth Schedule** areas under **PESA 1996**, the **Gram Sabha is supreme**.
GS NIRNAY (**2023**) is an app on Gram Sabha decisions.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the People's Plan Campaign 'Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas':
1. It has been run from 2 October 2018.
2. Under it, Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) are prepared through Gram Sabhas.
3. The GPDP is a plan for urban ward infrastructure prepared by municipalities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
81.x: Statement 1 is correct: the campaign runs from 2 October 2018. Statement 2 is correct: it prepares GPDPs through Gram Sabhas. Statement 3 is wrong: the GPDP is a Gram Panchayat-level plan for economic development and social justice, not an urban ward plan. So (a) misses statement 2, (c) and (d) wrongly include statement 3; (b) is the answer.
81.tq: GPDP = Gram Panchayat plan for economic development and social justice; anything 'urban' or 'municipal' is the trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: the **People's Plan Campaign** runs from **2 Oct 2018**.
2: it prepares **Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDP)** through **Gram Sabhas**.
3 wrong: GPDP is a **GP-level** plan for **economic development and social justice**, not an urban ward plan.
xa: ⚠ **Kerala People's Plan Campaign 1996** vs national "**Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas**" **2 Oct 2018**.
**e-GramSwaraj**: **2.54 lakh GPs** uploaded GPDP for FY25.

81.s: PESA, 1996 was enacted following the recommendations of which committee?
81.x: PESA followed the recommendations of the Bhuria Committee, constituted in 1995.
81.tq: Avoid the common committee-name trap by linking PESA with the Bhuria Committee.
xs: **PESA 1996** came from the **Bhuria Committee** (**1995**) — option **(2)**.
**Sarkaria** and **Punchhi** are not linked to PESA in the notes.
xa: PESA extends Part IX to **Fifth Schedule** areas in **ten States, including AP**.
It was done under **Art. 243M(4)(b)**.
**30 years of PESA** were marked in **2026**.

81.s: PESA extends Part IX to Scheduled Areas in how many States, as stated in the material?
81.x: PESA is stated to extend Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas in ten States, including Andhra Pradesh.
81.tq: Test the exact number and avoid replacing it with the broader number of tribal-population States.
xs: PESA covers **Fifth Schedule** areas in **ten States**, including **AP** — option **(1)**.
It does not cover every tribal state: **Sixth Schedule** areas stay outside it.
xa: It grew out of the **Bhuria Committee, 1995**.
In AP, PESA applies in the **agency areas**.
The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** oversees PESA.

81.s: Which of the following is NOT a power associated with the Gram Sabha in Scheduled Areas under PESA?
o: Control over village markets and liquor
Compulsory approval of every Union Budget expenditure
Protection of traditions and community resources
81.x: PESA gives Gram Sabhas powers over minor forest produce, village markets and liquor, and protection of traditions and community resources; it does not give them control over the Union Budget.
81.tq: Find the one unrelated power among the PESA-specific Gram Sabha functions.
xs: **Approval of Union Budget expenditure** is not a PESA power — option **(3)**.
PESA Gram Sabha powers: **owns minor forest produce**, controls **village markets and liquor**, protects **traditions and community resources**.
xa: It settles disputes the **customary way**.
It must be **consulted before land acquisition**.
It **approves plans** and **identifies beneficiaries**.

81.s: In Scheduled Areas, the Gram Sabha under PESA must be consulted before:
81.x: PESA requires consultation with the Gram Sabha before land acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
81.tq: Apply the consultation requirement to a land-related administrative decision.
xs: Under PESA the Gram Sabha must be consulted before **land acquisition** — option **(3)**.
This applies in **Fifth Schedule** (Scheduled) areas under **PESA 1996**.
xa: In Fifth Schedule areas the **Gram Sabha is supreme**.
It owns **minor forest produce** and controls village markets and **liquor**.
PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee (1995)**.

81.s:
With reference to the Gram Sabha in Fifth Schedule areas under PESA, 1996, consider the following statements:
1. The Gram Sabha is regarded as supreme and may settle disputes in the customary way.
2. The Gram Sabha approves plans and identifies beneficiaries.
3. The Gram Sabha has only an advisory role, with village markets and liquor controlled by the State Excise Department.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
81.x: Statement 1 is correct: under PESA the Gram Sabha is supreme and settles disputes the customary way. Statement 2 is correct: it approves plans and identifies beneficiaries. Statement 3 is wrong: it is not merely advisory; it controls village markets and liquor. Hence (a) is incomplete, (c) and (d) include the false statement 3; (b) is correct.
81.tq: Under PESA the Gram Sabha is 'supreme' - any statement calling it advisory is false.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: under PESA the **Gram Sabha is supreme** and settles disputes the **customary way**.
2: it **approves plans** and **identifies beneficiaries**.
3 wrong: it is not just advisory — it **controls village markets and liquor**.
xa: It owns **minor forest produce** and must be consulted before **land acquisition**.
PESA covers **ten States**, including AP.

81.s:
With reference to PESA, consider the following statements:
1. It extends Part IX of the Constitution to Fifth Schedule Areas with exceptions.
2. It recognises governance through customary law.
3. It applies to Sixth Schedule tribal areas in the same manner as to Fifth Schedule Areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. PESA applies only to Fifth Schedule Areas and not to Sixth Schedule tribal areas, making statement 3 incorrect.
81.tq: Use the Fifth Schedule–Sixth Schedule distinction as the decisive trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: PESA extends **Part IX** to **Fifth Schedule** areas with changes (**243M(4)(b)**).
2: the Gram Sabha protects **traditions** and settles disputes the **customary way**.
3 wrong: PESA covers **Fifth Schedule** areas only, not **Sixth Schedule** tribal areas.
xa: Sixth Schedule areas of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram** are exempted under **243M**.
**Bhuria Committee 1995** → **PESA 1996**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Part IX of the Constitution:
1. It does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram.
2. It does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas covered by the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
3. It does not apply to hill areas of Manipur having District Councils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: All three statements reflect the exemptions specified under Article 243M for Part IX.
81.tq: Check each listed constitutional exemption before selecting the inclusive code.
xs: All three are exemptions under **Art. 243M** — option **(4)**.
**Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram**; **Fifth and Sixth Schedule** areas; **hill areas of Manipur** with District Councils.
xa: Also exempted: **district-level** panchayats in the **Darjeeling hills**.
⚠ Parallel exemption for municipalities: **243ZC** (Part IXA).
Parliament extended Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas by **PESA 1996**.

81.s: Part IX is not applicable to which of the following areas in West Bengal?
o: All coastal districts of West Bengal
The entire State of West Bengal
81.x: Article 243M excludes the hill council area of Darjeeling district from the application of Part IX.
81.tq: Identify the area-specific exemption rather than treating the exclusion as State-wide.
xs: Part IX does not apply to the **Darjeeling hill council area** — option **(4)**.
Precisely: **district-level** panchayats in the **Darjeeling hills** are exempted (**243M**).
xa: Other exemptions: **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram**; **hill areas of Manipur**.
**West Bengal** was a pioneer of the three-tier system (**1973** Act, **1978** polls).

81.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 243A — Exemption of Sixth Schedule areas from Part IXA
Article 243F — Extension of Part IX through PESA
81.x: Article 243M provides exemptions from Part IX. Article 243ZC concerns corresponding exemptions under Part IXA, Article 243A concerns Gram Sabha powers, and Article 243F concerns disqualifications for Panchayat membership.
81.tq: Match Articles with their subjects and eliminate swapped provision numbers.
xs: **Art. 243M — exemptions from Part IX** is correct — option **(1)**.
**243ZC** = Part **IXA** exemption; **243A** = Gram Sabha powers; **243F** = disqualifications.
xa: PESA used **243M(4)(b)** to extend Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas.
The Gram Sabha is defined at **243(b)**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation of Scheduled Caste seats in Panchayats:
1. SC reservation does not apply in Arunachal Pradesh.
2. The reason is that Arunachal Pradesh has no Scheduled Caste population.
3. This exemption makes Arunachal Pradesh a State to which Part IX does not apply at all.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The absence of SC reservation in Arunachal Pradesh does not mean that Part IX is wholly inapplicable there, so statement 3 is false.
81.tq: Separate an exemption from a particular reservation from total exclusion of the constitutional Part.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 and 2: **SC reservation does not apply in Arunachal Pradesh** because it has **no SC population**.
3 wrong: Part IX is fully exempt only in **Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram** — not Arunachal.
xa: SC/ST reservation is in proportion to **population** (**243D**).
Exempted areas also include **hill areas of Manipur** and the **Darjeeling hills**.

81.s: Which Ministry oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
81.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj oversees Part IX, PESA and District Planning Committees.
81.tq: Identify the responsible ministry by matching it with the cluster of decentralisation functions.
xs: The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** oversees **Part IX**, **PESA** and **District Planning Committees** — option **(2)**.
**MoHUA** runs urban schemes such as **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)**.
xa: It was created on **27 May 2004**.
Its newer tool: **Panchayat Advancement Index** (**2.5 lakh+ GPs**).
Apps: **Meri Panchayat** for citizens; **SabhaSaar**, its first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes.

81.s: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj was created on:
81.x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj was created on 27 May 2004.
81.tq: Recall the exact date associated with the creation of the nodal Ministry.
xs: The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** was created on **27 May 2004** — option **(3)**.
**24 April 1993** is when the **73rd Amendment** came into force.
xa: It oversees Part IX, **PESA** and **District Planning Committees**.
e-Panchayat MMP under **NeGP** (**2006**).

81.s: Parliament extended Part IX to the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled) Areas, with modifications, through the PESA Act, 1996 under:
81.x: Article 243M(4)(b) lets Parliament extend Part IX to Scheduled Areas with exceptions and modifications, which it did through PESA, 1996. Article 243ZC is the parallel exemption in Part IXA, 244A concerns an autonomous State in Assam, and 243D(6) enables backward-class reservation.
81.tq: 243M = exemptions; 243M(4)(b) = route for PESA.
xs: **Article 243M(4)(b)** lets Parliament extend Part IX to **Scheduled Areas** — done by **PESA 1996** — option **(1)**.
**243ZC** is the parallel exemption in **Part IXA**.
xa: PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee, 1995**.
It covers Fifth Schedule areas in **ten States**, including AP.

81.s: Reservation of not less than one-third of the total number of offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women is provided under:
81.x: Article 243D(4) provides reservation of not less than one-third of the offices of chairpersons in Panchayats for women.
81.tq: Discriminate between adjacent constitutional clauses dealing with seats and chairperson posts.
xs: **Article 243D(4)**: **one-third** of seats and **chairperson** posts for women — option **(1)**.
**243E** is about duration; **243C** about composition.
xa: The one-third is a **floor**; many states raised it to **50%**.
**Bihar** was first to give **50%**, in **2006**.
Reserved seats **rotate**.

81.s: Which one of the following statements regarding reservation in Panchayats is correct?
o: Rotation is permitted only for chairperson posts.
Reserved seats are allotted by rotation.
Reserved seats are permanently allotted to the same constituencies.
Only seats reserved for SCs and STs are rotated.
81.x: Seats reserved under Article 243D are allotted by rotation among different constituencies or Panchayats.
81.tq: Use the exact constitutional mechanism rather than the broader reservation percentage.
xs: **Reserved seats are allotted by rotation** — option **(2)**.
Under **Art. 243D(4)**, both seats and chairperson posts for women are reserved, and reserved seats rotate.
xa: SC/ST reservation is in proportion to **population**.
⚠ **Krishna Murthy (2010)**: total vertical reservation normally within **50%**.

81.s: Which State was the first to provide 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies?
81.x: Bihar was the first State mentioned as having raised reservation for women in local bodies to 50 per cent, in 2006.
81.tq: Test the first-adopter trap among States that subsequently provided 50 per cent reservation.
xs: **Bihar** was first to give **50%** reservation to women, in **2006** — option **(3)**.
**Madhya Pradesh** was first to **implement the 73rd** (MPPSC 2015 key).
xa: **AP**, **Himachal Pradesh**, **Madhya Pradesh** and **Sikkim** meet **50%** exactly.
Women = **12.14 lakh (49.75%)** of **24.41 lakh** elected panchayat representatives.

81.s:
Which of the following States or Union Territories was listed as meeting exactly the 50 per cent quota for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions?
1. Andhra Pradesh
2. Gujarat
3. Himachal Pradesh
4. Sikkim
81.x: Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim were listed as meeting the 50 per cent quota exactly. Gujarat was listed as short of 50 per cent, at 49.9 per cent.
81.tq: Separate the exact-50-per-cent group from the near-50-per-cent group.
xs: **AP, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim** meet 50% exactly — option **(1)**.
**Gujarat** is short, at **49.9%**.
xa: **Madhya Pradesh** also meets 50% exactly.
Others short: **Haryana 42.12%**, **Tripura 45.25%**, **DNH & DD 31.97%**.
Data: MoPR, **23 Apr 2026**.

81.s: Which of the following initiatives is intended to counter token representation of women in Panchayati Raj institutions?
o: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats
PESA and the Sixteenth Finance Commission grants
81.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan and Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to promote substantive women’s leadership and counter token representation.
81.tq: Match the initiative with its stated social-governance objective.
xs: **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** and **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats** counter token representation — option **(2)**.
**SabhaSaar** (on **Bhashini**) is an AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes; **OWMS** monitors AP water projects.
xa: Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan trains **women elected representatives**.
At least **one** Model Women-Friendly GP per district.
**Bokkasampalem** (Tirupati) won **1st** for women-friendly panchayat (**2026**).

81.s: According to Ministry of Panchayati Raj data (April 2026), women make up approximately what share of the elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
81.x: Of 24.41 lakh elected panchayat representatives, 12.14 lakh (49.75%) are women, well above the constitutional floor of one-third (33%). 40% and 60% do not match the data.
81.tq: One-third is the floor; actual share is near 50%.
xs: Women are **about 49.75 per cent** of elected panchayat representatives — option **(3)** (MoPR, **23 Apr 2026**).
Of **24.41 lakh** representatives, **12.14 lakh** are women — far above the **one-third** floor of **Art. 243D(4)**.
xa: Women increasingly win **unreserved** seats too.
**AP, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Sikkim** meet the **50%** quota exactly.
Short of 50%: **Gujarat 49.9%**, **Haryana 42.12%**, **Tripura 45.25%**.

81.s: In K. Krishna Murthy v. Union of India (2010), the Constitution Bench upheld the constitutional validity of provisions enabling reservation for backward classes in local bodies under:
81.x: K. Krishna Murthy upheld the provisions contained in Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), while distinguishing political backwardness from social and educational backwardness.
81.tq: Match the case with the precise constitutional provisions involved.
xs: **K. Krishna Murthy (2010)** upheld **Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6)** — option **(2)**.
It was a **Constitution Bench**; it held **political backwardness ≠ social/educational backwardness**.
xa: Total vertical reservation should normally stay within **50%**.
⚠ **Krishna Murthy 2010** = upheld OBC quota; **Gawali 2021** = **triple test**.
**Art. 280(3)(bb)** is about the Union Finance Commission and panchayats.

81.s:
The triple test laid down in Vikas Kishanrao Gawali v. State of Maharashtra (2021) includes which of the following?
1. A dedicated commission conducting rigorous empirical inquiry
2. Fixation of local-body-wise reservation based on the findings
3. Keeping the aggregate SC, ST and OBC reservation within 50 per cent
4. Automatic reservation of 50 per cent for OBCs in every local body
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 constitute the triple test. Statement 4 is false because the judgment does not provide for automatic 50 per cent OBC reservation in every local body.
81.tq: Use the three-part test and reject the absolute automatic-quota statement.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 3** form the **Gawali triple test** — option **(2)**.
(1) **Dedicated commission** for a rigorous empirical inquiry; (2) **local-body-wise** proportion fixed on its findings.
(3) **SC+ST+OBC** total not above **50%**.
4 is wrong: the test caps the total at **50%**; it gives no automatic OBC quota.
xa: AP: a **34%** BC quota plus SC/ST shares must pass Gawali's **50%** ceiling.
AP's **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** notified a **33.33%** BC quota for ULB polls.

81.s: The distinction emphasised in K. Krishna Murthy between political backwardness and social or educational backwardness is relevant to:
o: Reservation for backward classes in local bodies
The distribution of State taxes to Municipalities
The appointment of State Election Commissioners
81.x: K. Krishna Murthy (2010) upheld backward-class reservation in local bodies under Articles 243D(6) and 243T(6), holding that political backwardness is distinct from social and educational backwardness. It did not deal with tax distribution, SEC appointments or the term of Panchayats.
81.tq: Apply the judicial distinction to the subject area in which it operates.
xs: The political vs social/educational backwardness distinction concerns **reservation for backward classes in local bodies** — option **(1)**.
**K. Krishna Murthy (2010)** upheld **243D(6)/243T(6)** on this basis.
xa: BC reservation under **243D** is **optional** for states.
**Gawali (2021)** later laid down the **triple test**.
Normal cap on total vertical reservation: **50%**.

81.s: Which Government Order notified a 33.33 per cent BC quota for Urban Local Body elections in Andhra Pradesh?
81.x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 notified the 33.33 per cent BC quota for Urban Local Body polls in Andhra Pradesh.
81.tq: Recall the exact order number associated with the notified urban quota.
xs: **G.O. Rt. No. 1065** notified a **33.33%** BC quota for AP ULB polls — option **(1)**.
It was issued on **20 Aug 2026**.
xa: Such quotas must meet **Gawali's** triple test (**2021**).
AP ULB elections are due for **100 of 123** ULBs.
**16th Finance Commission** grants require duly constituted local bodies.

81.s: How many subjects are included in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
81.x: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects related to Panchayats. The figure 18 belongs to the Twelfth Schedule concerning municipalities.
81.tq: Discriminate between the closely associated figures 29 and 18.
xs: The **Eleventh Schedule** has **twenty-nine** subjects — option **(4)**.
⚠ **18** is the **Twelfth Schedule** (municipalities) — "18 functional items for Panchayats" is FALSE (APPSC 2023).
xa: It is linked to panchayats by **Art. 243G**.
It is a **menu, not a transfer** — the State "may" devolve.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Eleventh Schedule:
1. It contains 29 subjects.
2. It automatically transfers all the listed subjects to Panchayats.
3. The State may devolve powers and responsibilities relating to these subjects to Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Eleventh Schedule provides a menu of subjects; it does not itself automatically transfer every subject to Panchayats.
81.tq: Identify the trap created by converting a permissive constitutional provision into an automatic transfer.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: it has **29** subjects.
2 wrong: it is a **menu, not a transfer** — nothing is automatically transferred.
3: the **State "may" devolve** these subjects (**Art. 243G**).
xa: Devolving the **29** subjects is a **voluntary** provision.
Result: funds, functions and functionaries devolved **unevenly**.

81.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Land improvement — Eleventh Schedule
2. Minor irrigation — Eleventh Schedule
3. Public order — Eleventh Schedule
4. Fisheries — Eleventh Schedule
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
81.x: Land improvement, minor irrigation and fisheries are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Public order is not included in the Eleventh Schedule.
81.tq: Locate the wrong subject by distinguishing Panchayat functions from core State-list functions.
xs: **Land improvement**, **minor irrigation** and **fisheries** are Eleventh Schedule subjects — option **(2)**.
**Public order** (like **police**) is a typical distractor, not in the Eleventh Schedule.
xa: Other agri items: **animal husbandry, dairying, poultry**; **social and farm forestry**; **minor forest produce**.
Not in it: **defence**, **railways**.

81.s:
Which of the following is NOT an Eleventh Schedule subject?
1. Rural housing
2. Drinking water
3. Fire services
4. Rural electrification
81.x: Rural housing, drinking water and rural electrification are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Fire services is a Twelfth Schedule subject relating to municipalities.
81.tq: Find the municipal subject placed among Panchayat subjects.
xs: **Fire services** is not an Eleventh Schedule subject — option **(1)**: it is a **Twelfth Schedule** (municipal) item.
**Rural housing**, **drinking water** and **rural electrification** are Eleventh Schedule subjects.
xa: **Urban planning** is also Twelfth Schedule.
Infrastructure items: **roads, culverts, bridges, ferries, waterways**.

81.s:
Which of the following sets consists only of Eleventh Schedule subjects?
1. Fuel and fodder
2. Roads, culverts, bridges, ferries and waterways
3. Non-conventional energy
4. Urban planning
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
81.x: Fuel and fodder, rural roads and related infrastructure, and non-conventional energy are included in the Eleventh Schedule. Urban planning belongs to the Twelfth Schedule.
81.tq: Use one clearly misplaced municipal item to split the answer options.
xs: **Fuel and fodder**, **roads, culverts, bridges, ferries, waterways** and **non-conventional energy** — option **(1)**.
**Urban planning** is a **Twelfth Schedule** item.
xa: Industry and energy items: **small-scale industries**, **khadi, village and cottage industries**, **rural electrification**.
Twelfth Schedule also has **slaughterhouses**, **burial grounds**, **fire services**.

81.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Eleventh Schedule?
81.x: Poverty alleviation programme is an Eleventh Schedule subject. Slum improvement, cattle pounds, and burial or cremation grounds are associated with the Twelfth Schedule.
81.tq: Distinguish rural poverty and development functions from municipal service functions.
xs: **Poverty alleviation programme** is an Eleventh Schedule subject — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Slum improvement**, **cattle pounds**, **burial grounds** = **Twelfth Schedule** (municipal) items.
xa: Welfare items: **social welfare** (incl. handicapped); welfare of **weaker sections, SCs and STs**.
Also: **public distribution system**; maintenance of community assets.

81.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Primary and secondary education are included in the Eleventh Schedule.
2. Technical training and vocational education are included in the Eleventh Schedule.
3. Adult and non-formal education are included in the Eleventh Schedule.
4. Libraries are included in the Eleventh Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: All four statements correctly identify education-related subjects included in the Eleventh Schedule.
81.tq: Treat a complete thematic list as an all-correct statement set after checking each item.
xs: All four are Eleventh Schedule subjects — option **(4)**.
**Primary and secondary education**; **technical training and vocational education**; **adult and non-formal education**; **libraries**.
xa: Also: **cultural activities**; **markets and fairs**.
Health items: **health and sanitation** (hospitals, PHCs, dispensaries); **family welfare**.

81.s:
Which one of the following combinations is correctly associated with the final subjects of the Eleventh Schedule?
1. Public distribution system
2. Maintenance of community assets
3. Slaughterhouses
4. Burial grounds
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
81.x: Public distribution system and maintenance of community assets are Eleventh Schedule subjects. Slaughterhouses and burial grounds are Twelfth Schedule municipal subjects.
81.tq: Use the final entries of the list while excluding familiar municipal distractors.
xs: **PDS** and **maintenance of community assets** are Eleventh Schedule subjects — option **(1)**.
**Slaughterhouses** and **burial grounds** belong to the **Twelfth Schedule**.
xa: Other health and welfare items: **women and child development**, **family welfare**.
Twelfth Schedule = **18** subjects; Eleventh = **29**.

81.s:
With reference to the State Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. The Governor constitutes it every five years.
2. It reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities.
3. Its recommendations are binding on the State Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years, and it reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities. Its recommendations are advisory, not binding.
81.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking the constitutional role against the extreme claim that recommendations are binding.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: the **Governor** constitutes it every **five years**.
2: it reviews finances of **Panchayats** (**243I**) and **Municipalities** (**243Y**).
3 wrong: its recommendations are **advisory**, not binding.
xa: Its report goes to the Governor, who lays it before the Legislature with an **action taken report**.
APPSC-G1 2022: set up **once in five years**.

81.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional provisions relating to the State Finance Commission?
o: Article 243I concerns the Union Finance Commission and Article 243Y concerns State Budgets
Article 243I concerns Municipalities and Article 243Y concerns Panchayats
Article 243I concerns Panchayats and Article 243Y extends the role to Municipalities
Both Articles 243I and 243Y concern only the distribution of Union taxes
81.x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission to review Panchayat finances, while Article 243Y applies the corresponding review to Municipalities.
81.tq: Discriminate between the closely related Articles 243I and 243Y by matching each Article with its local-body level.
xs: **243I** = SFC for **Panchayats**; **243Y** = the same Commission for **Municipalities** — option **(3)**.
The Union Finance Commission is under **Art. 280**, not 243I.
xa: It recommends sharing **State taxes, duties, tolls and fees**, assigned taxes and **grants-in-aid**.
APPSC-G2 2025: it examines finances **and** reviews revenue distribution between state and local bodies.

81.s: The report of the State Finance Commission is submitted to the Governor, who is required to:
o: Reject it before placing it before the State Legislature
Place it only before the Legislative Council
Forward it directly to the Union Finance Commission for approval
Lay it before the State Legislature along with an action-taken memorandum
81.x: The Governor lays the State Finance Commission report before the State Legislature together with a memorandum explaining the action taken on its recommendations.
81.tq: Test the constitutional procedure by identifying the authority responsible for laying the report and the accompanying document.
xs: The Governor **lays it before the State Legislature with an action-taken memorandum** — option **(4)**.
The report is **advisory**, not sent to the Union Finance Commission for approval.
xa: The **Governor** constitutes the SFC every **five years**.
The Union FC acts **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.

81.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the composition and qualifications of a State Finance Commission is correct?
o: They are prescribed by the Governor through executive instructions alone
They are prescribed by the State Election Commission
They are prescribed exclusively by the Union Finance Commission
They are prescribed by State law
81.x: The composition of the State Finance Commission and the qualifications of its members are prescribed by State law.
81.tq: Apply the 'who makes the rule?' method to distinguish State legislation from neighbouring constitutional authorities.
xs: The SFC's composition and members' qualifications are set by **State law** — option **(4)**.
The **State Legislature** decides them; the Governor only constitutes the Commission.
xa: First SFC was due within **one year** of **24 April 1993**.
Karnataka's **5th SFC** asked for **5%** of urban **GST** revenue for ULBs.

81.s: Under Article 280(3)(bb) and Article 280(3)(c), the Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State for supplementing the resources of:
o: Panchayats under clause (bb) and municipalities under clause (c)
Municipalities under clause (bb) and Panchayats under clause (c)
State Legislatures under clause (bb) and municipalities under clause (c)
81.x: Article 280(3)(bb) concerns panchayats and was inserted through the 73rd Amendment. Article 280(3)(c) concerns municipalities and was inserted through the 74th Amendment.
81.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring constitutional clauses and the local bodies covered by them.
xs: **280(3)(bb)** = **panchayats** (73rd); **280(3)(c)** = **municipalities** (74th) — option **(1)**.
The **Central Finance Commission** recommends measures to augment a **State's Consolidated Fund** for these.
xa: It acts **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.
⚠ "Union FC has no role in LB assistance" is **false** (UPPSC 2011).

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the role of the Union Finance Commission in local-body finance:
1. It recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State.
2. Its recommendations concerning local bodies are made on the basis of the recommendations of the State Finance Commission.
3. Central tax devolution is paid directly to Panchayats rather than to the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: The Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for supplementing local-body resources, drawing on State Finance Commission recommendations. Central tax devolution goes to the States; Panchayats receive Central assistance through Finance Commission grants routed via the State.
81.tq: Identify the wrong channel of fund flow by asking which level first receives tax devolution.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: the Union FC recommends measures to augment a **State's Consolidated Fund**.
2: it does so **on the basis of the SFC's recommendations**.
3 wrong: **Central tax devolution goes to states**; panchayats get Central money only as **FC grants routed through the state**.
xa: Clause **(bb)** came with the 73rd; clause **(c)** with the 74th.
AP local bodies stand to lose **₹12,150 crore** of Central funds if elections are not held by October 2026.

81.s: The first State Finance Commission under Article 243I was required to be constituted within:
o: Two years of the first Panchayat election
Five years of the Constitution’s commencement
Six months of the commencement of the 73rd Amendment
81.x: The first State Finance Commission was required to be constituted within one year of 24 April 1993, the date on which the 73rd Amendment came into force.
81.tq: Separate the first-time limit from the normal five-year cycle.
xs: The first SFC had to be constituted within **one year of 24 April 1993** — option **(2)**.
24 April 1993 is when the **73rd Amendment** came into force.
xa: Thereafter, every **five years** (**Art. 243I**).
The same SFC also reviews **municipal** finances (**243Y**).

81.s:
Which of the following is NOT a function or recommendation associated with the State Finance Commission?
1. Distribution of net proceeds of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and local bodies
2. Grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of the State
3. Measures to improve the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities
4. Appointment of the State Election Commissioner
81.x: The State Finance Commission makes recommendations on fiscal distribution, assigned taxes, grants-in-aid and improvement of local finances. Appointment of the State Election Commissioner is not its function.
81.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional authority among closely connected local-government functions.
xs: **Appointing the State Election Commissioner** is not an SFC function — option **(1)**, "4 only".
SFC recommends: sharing **State taxes, duties, tolls and fees**; **grants-in-aid**; measures to improve local finances.
xa: The **State Election Commission** is under **Art. 243K**.
The SFC also handles any matter the **Governor** refers.

81.s: Which legislation gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2005
The Andhra Pradesh Land Revenue Act, 1990
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
The Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act, 1955
81.x: Part VI of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 gives effect to Article 243I for Panchayats.
81.tq: Match the constitutional provision with its State-level implementing law.
xs: **Part VI** of the **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** gives effect to **Art. 243I** — option **(3)**.
It is AP's conformity law — **Act No. 13 of 1994**.
xa: It has **278 sections** in **8 Parts**.
Enacted on **21 April 1994**.

81.s: The 13 Zilla Parishads of Andhra Pradesh are being reorganised into how many Zilla Parishads?
81.x: The cited reorganisation proposes increasing the number of Zilla Parishads from 13 to 28.
81.tq: Test the before-and-after figures in a current-affairs numerical comparison.
xs: AP's **13** Zilla Parishads are being reorganised into **28** — option **(3)**.
The **13** ZPPs date from the older district count (May 2026); **28** is the new figure (Sep 2026).
xa: AP has ~**15,000+** GPs and **588** mandals.
AP tiers: Gram Panchayat — **Mandal Parishad** — Zilla Parishad.
**2026** local body polls are under SEC **Punetha**.

81.s: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, which served as the State's conformity law, was enacted on
81.x: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, was enacted on 21 April 1994 as the State's conformity law.
81.tq: Distinguish the conformity-law date from the earlier Panchayati Raj commencement dates.
xs: The **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** was enacted on **21 April 1994** — option **(1)**.
**2 October 1959** = Rajasthan's PR launch; **1 November 1959** = AP's; **24 April 2020** = SVAMITVA.
xa: It is **Act No. 13 of 1994**, with **278 sections**, **8 Parts**.
**PESA 1996** also applies in AP's **Fifth Schedule** agency areas.

81.s: Which State was the first to launch Panchayati Raj Institutions, and when did Andhra Pradesh launch them?
o: Andhra Pradesh first on 1 November 1959; Rajasthan second on 2 October 1959
Rajasthan first on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 1 November 1959
Rajasthan first on 1 November 1959; Andhra Pradesh second on 2 October 1959
Andhra Pradesh first on 2 October 1959; Rajasthan second on 1 November 1959
81.x: Rajasthan was the first State to launch PRIs on 2 October 1959, while Andhra Pradesh was the second on 1 November 1959.
81.tq: Anchor the sequence with the first and second States and verify both dates.
xs: **Rajasthan** first (**2 October 1959**), **AP** second (**1 November 1959**) — option **(2)**.
The other options swap the states or the dates.
xa: ⚠ **First to implement the 73rd** = **Madhya Pradesh**, not Rajasthan.
**Bihar** was first to give women **50%**, in **2006**.
**West Bengal** = pioneer three-tier system (**1973** Act, **1978** polls).

81.s: Which State was the first to implement the 73rd Constitutional Amendment by holding panchayat elections under it?
81.x: Madhya Pradesh was the first State to implement the 73rd Amendment (MPPSC 2015 key). Rajasthan was first to adopt Panchayati Raj in 1959; Andhra Pradesh was second in 1959 and passed its conformity Act on 21 April 1994; Kerala is known for the 1996 People's Plan Campaign.
81.tq: Pre-1993 first = Rajasthan; post-73rd first = Madhya Pradesh.
xs: **Madhya Pradesh** was first to implement the 73rd Amendment — option **(1)** (MPPSC 2015 key).
**Rajasthan** was first to launch PRIs in **1959**; **AP** second; **Kerala** is known for the **1996** People's Plan Campaign.
xa: AP passed its conformity Act on **21 April 1994**.
MP also meets the **50%** women quota exactly.

81.s: Which of the following is the newer composite tool of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj for assessing Panchayat advancement?
81.x: The Panchayat Advancement Index is the newer composite, multi-domain index used to assess Panchayat performance against localised Sustainable Development Goals.
81.tq: Discriminate between an older general index label and the exact newer institutional term.
xs: The **Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI)** is MoPR's newer tool — option **(4)**.
It is a composite multi-domain index on **localised SDGs**.
xa: It scores **2.5 lakh+ GPs** (ES 2025-26).
It is also used to pick **National Panchayat Award** winners.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Panchayat Advancement Index:
1. It is a composite multi-domain index.
2. It assesses Panchayats against localised Sustainable Development Goals.
3. It covers more than 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: The Panchayat Advancement Index is composite and multi-domain, measures localised SDGs, and covers more than 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats.
81.tq: Treat scale, purpose and structure as separate factual components.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
PAI is **composite and multi-domain**, scores GPs on **localised SDGs**, and covers **2.5 lakh+ GPs**.
xa: National Panchayat Awards are judged on **9 LSDG themes** under **RGSA**, using the PAI.
Awards are given on **24 April**.

81.s: The People's Plan Campaign associated with Kerala was launched in
81.x: Kerala's People's Plan Campaign was launched in 1996.
81.tq: Use the year as the decisive discriminator among Panchayati Raj milestones.
xs: Kerala's **People's Plan Campaign** began in **1996** — option **(3)**.
⚠ Don't confuse it with the national "**Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas**" from **2 Oct 2018**.
xa: It devolved a large share of plan funds; plans were made **from Gram Sabhas up**.
**1973** = West Bengal Panchayat Act; **1978** = its first polls.

81.s: Which one of the following best describes Kerala's People's Plan Campaign?
o: Exclusive financing of urban infrastructure through municipal bonds
Centralisation of all plan funds at the State secretariat
Replacement of Gram Sabhas by municipal corporations
Devolution of a large share of plan funds and preparation of plans from Gram Sabhas upwards
81.x: The campaign devolved a large share of plan funds and encouraged planning from Gram Sabhas upwards.
81.tq: Identify the governance model from its functional characteristics rather than its name alone.
xs: Kerala's campaign = **large share of plan funds devolved** + plans made **from Gram Sabhas up** — option **(4)**.
**Municipal bonds** are used by only a few large cities — unrelated.
xa: Launched in **1996**.
The national version (**2 Oct 2018**) prepares **GPDPs** through Gram Sabhas.

81.s:
With reference to West Bengal's Panchayati Raj system, consider the following statements:
1. Its three-tier system was associated with a 1973 Act.
2. The first elections under that Act were held in 1978.
3. Pradhans traditionally had no financial powers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Pradhans held unusual financial powers; therefore, statement 3 is false.
81.tq: Find the reversed or negated institutional characteristic in the statement set.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1 and 2: West Bengal's pioneer three-tier system came from the **1973 Act**, with polls in **1978**.
3 wrong: **Pradhans** held **unusual financial powers** — curbed by a **2026** amendment.
xa: West Bengal is listed as a **model state** for PR.
**Rajasthan** (**2 Oct 1959**) was first to launch PRIs.

81.s: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project was introduced under
81.x: The e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project was undertaken under the National e-Governance Plan, launched in 2006.
81.tq: Match a digital governance project with its parent programme and year.
xs: The **e-Panchayat MMP** came under the **National e-Governance Plan** (NeGP, **2006**) — option **(2)**.
**AMRUT 2.0** (**2021**) is a MoHUA urban mission.
xa: Its apps: **PriaSoft**, **PlanPlus**, **AuditOnline**.
**e-GramSwaraj** came in **2020**.

81.s:
Which of the following applications are associated with the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project?
1. PRIASoft
2. PlanPlus
3. AuditOnline
4. SVAMITVA
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
81.x: PRIASoft, PlanPlus and AuditOnline are applications associated with the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project. SVAMITVA is a separate initiative involving drone mapping and property records.
81.tq: Separate applications within one platform from a related but distinct scheme.
xs: **PRIASoft**, **PlanPlus** and **AuditOnline** are e-Panchayat apps — option **(1)**.
**SVAMITVA** is separate: **drone mapping** for **Record of Rights** (**24 April 2020**).
xa: e-Panchayat MMP: under **NeGP (2006)**.
**Meri Panchayat** = MoPR's mobile app for citizens.

81.s: Which one of the following statements about e-GramSwaraj is correct?
o: It was launched in 2021 for municipal bonds.
It was launched in 2006 for urban municipalities only.
It was launched in 2020 as a single-window platform for Gram Panchayat profiles.
It was launched in 2023 exclusively for Gram Sabha minutes.
81.x: e-GramSwaraj was launched in 2020 and provides a single-window Gram Panchayat profile platform.
81.tq: Distinguish the launch year and function of closely related e-governance tools.
xs: **e-GramSwaraj** was launched in **2020** as a **single-window GP profile** — option **(3)**.
xa: **2.54 lakh GPs** uploaded GPDP on it for FY25.
⚠ **SVAMITVA** = **24 April 2020**; **e-GramSwaraj** = **2020**.

81.s: SVAMITVA primarily uses drone mapping for
81.x: SVAMITVA uses drone mapping to support the preparation of Records of Rights in rural inhabited areas.
81.tq: Identify the practical outcome of a technology-based governance scheme.
xs: SVAMITVA uses drone mapping for **Record of Rights** — option **(2)**.
Gram Sabha minutes are done by **SabhaSaar** (AI tool), not SVAMITVA.
xa: Launched **24 April 2020** (National Panchayati Raj Day).
Implemented with the **Survey of India** and **NICSI**.

81.s: Which organisations are associated with the implementation architecture of SVAMITVA?
81.x: SVAMITVA is associated with the Survey of India and NICSI.
81.tq: Use the implementing institutions to distinguish the scheme from urban and financial initiatives.
xs: SVAMITVA works with the **Survey of India and NICSI** — option **(1)**.
**NHB** is linked to **UIDF** (urban infrastructure), not SVAMITVA.
xa: It maps for **Record of Rights** using **drones**.
Launched **24 April 2020**.

81.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: GS NIRNAY — 2023 app on Gram Sabha decisions
SabhaSaar — mobile app for municipal bonds
Meri Panchayat — drone mapping for Records of Rights
81.x: GS NIRNAY is a 2023 application concerning Gram Sabha decisions. SabhaSaar uses AI for Gram Sabha minutes, Meri Panchayat is a citizen-facing mobile app, and SVAMITVA uses drone mapping for Records of Rights.
81.tq: Discriminate among similarly themed digital applications by their exact functions.
xs: **GS NIRNAY — 2023 app on Gram Sabha decisions** is correct — option **(1)**.
**SabhaSaar** = AI for **Gram Sabha minutes**; **Meri Panchayat** = citizen mobile app; **SVAMITVA** = drone mapping.
xa: SabhaSaar: piloted in **Tripura**, on **Bhashini**.
e-GramSwaraj (**2020**): single-window GP profile.

81.s: Which of the following statements about SabhaSaar is correct?
o: It is the first AI tool for preparing Gram Sabha minutes and was piloted in Tripura on Bhashini.
It is an urban governance tool piloted in Andhra Pradesh for municipal budgets.
It is a State Election Commission portal used only for voter registration.
It is a Finance Commission application used for distributing grants to Zilla Parishads.
81.x: SabhaSaar is described as the first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes; it was piloted in Tripura on the Bhashini platform.
81.tq: Identify the tool by its function, pilot location and platform together.
xs: **SabhaSaar** is MoPR's **first AI tool for Gram Sabha minutes**, piloted in **Tripura** on **Bhashini** — option **(1)**.
It is a **Gram Sabha** tool — not an urban, SEC or Finance Commission application.
xa: ~**1 lakh GPs** used it for **1.38 lakh Gram Sabhas** by Nov 2025.
**GS NIRNAY** (**2023**) is the app on Gram Sabha decisions.
**Meri Panchayat** is MoPR's citizen app.

81.s: The SVAMITVA scheme for drone-based mapping of rural inhabited areas was launched on:
81.x: SVAMITVA was launched on 24 April 2020, National Panchayati Raj Day, with the Survey of India and NICSI preparing Records of Rights through drone mapping. The other dates are distractors.
81.tq: 24 April = National PR Day: 73rd in force (1993), SVAMITVA (2020), Panchayat Awards.
xs: **SVAMITVA** was launched on **24 April 2020** — option **(1)** — National Panchayati Raj Day.
It uses **drone mapping** with the **Survey of India** and **NICSI**.
xa: Its output: **Record of Rights** for rural inhabited areas.
⚠ **e-GramSwaraj** was also launched in **2020**.

81.s: The National Panchayat Awards are given on
81.x: The National Panchayat Awards are given on 24 April.
81.tq: Separate the award date from other nationally significant dates used in governance schemes.
xs: National Panchayat Awards are given on **24 April** — option **(3)**.
**21 April** is when the **AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994** was enacted.
xa: 24 April is **National Panchayati Raj Day** (73rd in force **24 April 1993**).
Judged on **9 LSDG themes** under **RGSA**, using the **PAI**.

81.s: The National Panchayat Awards are judged on how many localised Sustainable Development Goal themes?
81.x: The awards are judged on nine localised Sustainable Development Goal themes.
81.tq: Use the exact count rather than assuming the total number of global SDGs.
xs: The awards are judged on **9 LSDG themes** — option **(2)**.
They run under **RGSA**, using the **Panchayat Advancement Index**.
xa: **Nanaji Deshmukh** award = holistic; **Deen Dayal Upadhyay** award = theme-wise.
Given on **24 April**.

81.s: Which one of the following awards is intended as the holistic category of the National Panchayat Awards?
o: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar
Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar
81.x: The Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar is the holistic category. The Deen Dayal Upadhyay award is theme-wise, while the others are special or institutional awards.
81.tq: Distinguish award categories by their scope rather than by names alone.
xs: The **Nanaji Deshmukh Sarvottam Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar** is the **holistic** award — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Deen Dayal Upadhyay** = **theme-wise**; Capacity Building and Atmanirbhar are **special** awards.
xa: **Kuppam** mandal: **3rd**, Nanaji Deshmukh Puraskar **2025** (₹**1.5** crore).
Special awards: **Climate Action**, **Atmanirbhar Panchayat**, **Capacity Building**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Panchayat Awards:
1. The Deen Dayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Puraskar is theme-wise.
2. Climate Action is one of the special award categories.
3. The awards use the Panchayat Advancement Index in their assessment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: All three statements are correct. The awards include theme-wise and special categories and use the Panchayat Advancement Index for assessment.
81.tq: Combine category, special-award and assessment-method facts in one coded question.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: **Deen Dayal Upadhyay** award = **theme-wise**.
2: **Climate Action** is a special award.
3: the awards use the **Panchayat Advancement Index**.

81.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?

Municipal bonds — introduced only for all Gram Panchayats

Municipal bonds can be issued only by Gram Panchayats.

81.s: Which one of the following is identified as a reason for the uneven devolution of funds, functions and functionaries to Panchayats?

The State Election Commission controls all Panchayat finances
Panchayats are excluded from the Constitution
The Eleventh Schedule contains no subjects

xs: Devolution is uneven because **the 29 subjects are voluntary for devolution** — option **(1)**.

xa: Uneven areas: **funds, functions and functionaries**.
Devolving the 29 subjects is listed among **voluntary** provisions of Part IX.
The **Panchayat Advancement Index** scores **2.5 lakh+ GPs**.

81.s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Part X, Articles 244–244A and Fifth Schedule with 29 subjects
Part IXB, Articles 243ZH–243ZT and Ninth Schedule with 18 subjects
Part IX, Articles 243A–243O and Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects

81.x: The 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA, comprising Articles 243P to 243ZG, and the Twelfth Schedule containing 18 subjects.
81.tq: Use the Part–Article range–Schedule combination to identify the correct constitutional amendment.
xs: 74th Amendment: **Part IXA**, **Art. 243P–243ZG**, **Twelfth Schedule** with **18** subjects — option **(4)**.
Option 3 is the **73rd**: Part IX, **243-243O**, Eleventh Schedule (**29**).
xa: 74th came into force on **1 June 1993**; 73rd on **24 April 1993**.
Part IXA has **18 Articles**; Part IX has **16**.
⚠ **243ZC** = Part IXA exemption.

81.s: The 30 years of which legislation or framework were marked in the context of recent Panchayati Raj developments?
o: The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
The Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996

xs: **30 years of PESA** — the **Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996** — were marked in **2026** — option **(4)**.
PESA came from the **Bhuria Committee, 1995**.
xa: It extends Part IX to **Fifth Schedule** areas in **ten States, including AP**.
Under PESA the **Gram Sabha is supreme**.
The AP Panchayat Raj Act is of **1994**; the 73rd Amendment of **1992**.

81.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 2026 urban local body elections in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Elections are proposed for 100 of the 123 urban local bodies.
2. Articles 243-U, 243-K and 243-ZA are relevant to the process.
3. The elections concern only Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
81.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the process concerns urban local bodies, not only Gram Panchayats.
81.tq: Reject the statement that changes the rural–urban scope of the election.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: polls for **100 of 123** ULBs.
2: held under **Arts 243-U, 243-K, 243-ZA**.
3 wrong: these are **urban local body** polls, not Gram Panchayat polls.
xa: **16th Finance Commission** grants require duly constituted local bodies.
YSRCP moved court to postpone polls until the **SIR** of rolls.

81.s: The issue concerning the 34 per cent BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh local bodies is that the BC quota together with SC/ST shares must remain within the:
o: Fifty per cent ceiling associated with the Gawali principle
81.x: Under the Vikas Kishanrao Gawali triple test (2021), total SC+ST+OBC reservation must not exceed 50 per cent, so the 34 per cent BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within that 50 per cent ceiling.
81.tq: Add the reservation components conceptually and identify the applicable ceiling.
xs: AP's **34%** BC quota plus SC/ST shares must stay within the **fifty per cent** ceiling of **Gawali** — option **(1)**.
Gawali (**2021**) triple test: dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportion, **SC+ST+OBC** not above **50%**.
xa: **K. Krishna Murthy (2010)** had set **50%** as the normal cap.
**G.O. Rt. No. 1065** notified a **33.33%** BC quota for AP ULB polls.

81.s: Which of the following is regarded as one of the clearest achievements of the 73rd and 74th Amendments in the stated assessment?
o: Complete uniformity in the devolution of all 29 subjects
Abolition of State Election Commissions and increased official appointments
Regular elections and near-50 per cent representation of women
Replacement of Gram Sabhas by urban local bodies

81.tq: Distinguish recognised achievements from unresolved criticism about devolution.
xs: **Regular elections** + **near-50% women representation** are the clearest achievements — option **(3)**.
Devolution of the **29** subjects is **uneven**, not uniform.
xa: Women = **49.75%** of elected panchayat representatives.
States are **constitutionally obliged** to hold elections.
2026 women-leadership drives aim to move from **numerical** reservation to **real** empowerment.

81.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following correctly represents the three Panchayati Raj tiers?
o: Gram Panchayat, Mandal Parishad and Zilla Parishad
Gram Sabha, Municipal Council and Zilla Parishad

Gram Panchayat, Nagar Panchayat and Zilla Parishad
81.x: The Andhra Pradesh structure comprises Gram Panchayats, Mandal Parishads or Mandal Praja Parishads, and Zilla Parishads.

xs: AP tiers: **Gram Panchayat**, **Mandal Parishad** (Mandal Praja Parishad), **Zilla Parishad** — option **(1)**.
**Municipal Council** and **Nagar Panchayat** are urban bodies, not PR tiers.
xa: AP has **588** mandals and ~**15,000+** GPs.
**13** ZPPs are being reorganised into **28**.
PESA applies in AP's **agency areas**.

82.s: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in:
82.x: The Municipal Corporations of Bombay and Calcutta were established in 1726.
82.tq: Use the distinct early-municipality dates to distinguish 1726 from the later decentralisation milestones.
xs: The Municipal Corporations of **Bombay** and **Calcutta** came in **1726** — option **(2)**.
**1688** = **Madras** (first corporation); **1870** = **Lord Mayo**; **1882** = **Lord Ripon**.
xa: Madras charter dated **30 Dec 1687**; corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.
⚠ **Mayo 1870** = financial decentralisation; **Ripon 1882** = "**Magna Carta**".
UP's **KAVAL towns** got corporations in **1953**.

82.s: The five KAVAL towns in which Uttar Pradesh set up corporations in 1953 were:
o: Kanpur, Agra, Bareilly, Allahabad and Lucknow
Kanpur, Aligarh, Varanasi, Agra and Lucknow

Kashi, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Meerut
82.x: The five KAVAL towns were Kanpur, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad and Lucknow. Uttar Pradesh set up corporations in these towns in 1953, followed by the UP Municipal Corporations Act, 1959.
82.tq: Expand the mnemonic by verifying every member of the named list.
xs: KAVAL = **Kanpur, Agra, Varanasi, Allahabad, Lucknow** — option **(3)**.
The other options slip in **Bareilly**, **Aligarh** or **Meerut**.
xa: UP set up these corporations in **1953**.
Followed by the **UP Municipal Corporations Act 1959**.
The first corporation in India: **Madras, 1688**.

82.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the constitutional history of urban local government?
1. The Municipalities Bill of 1989 lapsed.
2. P. V. Narasimha Rao’s Bill introduced in September 1991 became the 74th Constitutional Amendment.
3. The 74th Amendment incorporated urban local government provisions in Part IXA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: All three statements are correct. The 1989 Municipalities Bill lapsed, while the Bill introduced by P. V. Narasimha Rao in September 1991 resulted in the 74th Amendment and Part IXA.
82.tq: Trace the legislative sequence and identify the Amendment’s constitutional location.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
1: the **1989 Municipalities Bill lapsed**.
2: **P.V. Narasimha Rao's** bill (**Sep 1991**) became the **74th**.
3: the 74th inserted **Part IXA "The Municipalities"**.
xa: Passed by both Houses **December 1992**; in force **1 June 1993**.
Part IXA: **Art. 243P to 243ZG**, **18** Articles.

82.s: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at:
82.x: The first Municipal Corporation was set up at Madras in 1688 (charter dated 30 December 1687; it began on 29 September 1688). Bombay and Calcutta got corporations later, in 1726. 1882 is the year of Lord Ripon's resolution, not of a corporation, and Delhi is not the first.
82.tq: Madras 1688 first; Bombay and Calcutta 1726 next.
xs: The first Municipal Corporation was at **Madras in 1688** — option **(3)**.
Charter **30 Dec 1687**; corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.
**Bombay and Calcutta** came later, in **1726**; **1882** is **Lord Ripon's resolution**, not a corporation.
xa: Ripon's resolution is the "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government.
**Lord Mayo (1870)** = financial decentralisation.

82.s: Which resolution is described as the 'Magna Carta' of local self-government in India?
o: The UP Municipal Corporations Act of 1959
82.x: Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882 is called the Magna Carta of local self-government. Lord Mayo's 1870 resolution dealt with financial decentralisation. The 1687 charter created the Madras corporation, and the 1959 UP Act followed the KAVAL towns corporations; neither is the Magna Carta.
82.tq: Ripon 1882 = Magna Carta; Mayo 1870 = financial decentralisation.
xs: **Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882** is the "**Magna Carta**" of local self-government — option **(2)**.
**Lord Mayo's 1870** resolution was on **financial decentralisation**.
The **1687** charter set up the Madras corporation; the **1959** UP Act followed the KAVAL corporations.
xa: Madras corporation began **29 Sep 1688**.
**Bombay** and **Calcutta** corporations: **1726**.

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992:
1. It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 1992.
2. Presidential assent was given in April 1993.
3. It came into force on 24 April 1993.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the 74th Amendment came into force on 1 June 1993; 24 April 1993 was the commencement date of the 73rd Amendment.
82.tq: Separate the passage, assent and commencement dates instead of treating them as one event.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
1: passed by both Houses in **December 1992**; 2: Presidential assent in **April 1993**.
3 wrong: the 74th came into force on **1 June 1993**; ⚠ **24 April 1993** was the **73rd**.
xa: It is called the **Nagarpalika Act** (Municipalities).
States had **one year** to bring their municipal laws into conformity (**243ZF**).

82.s:
With reference to the Constitution (Seventy-Fourth Amendment) Act, 1992, consider the following statements:
1. It inserted Part IXA, 'The Municipalities', into the Constitution.
2. Part IXA comprises Articles 243P to 243ZG.
3. It inserted the Eleventh Schedule listing the functions of municipalities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
82.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 74th Amendment inserted Part IXA 'The Municipalities'. Statement 2 is correct: Part IXA runs from Article 243P to 243ZG (18 Articles). Statement 3 is wrong: the 74th inserted the Twelfth Schedule (18 items); the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) came with the 73rd for Panchayats. So (a) is incomplete and (c), (d) include the false statement; (b) is correct.
82.tq: 73rd = Part IX + Eleventh (29); 74th = Part IXA + Twelfth (18).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: it inserted **Part IXA "The Municipalities"**; 2: **Art. 243P to 243ZG** (**18** Articles).
3 wrong: the 74th added the **Twelfth Schedule** (**18** items); the **Eleventh** (**29**) came with the 73rd.
xa: The Twelfth Schedule is linked to **Art. 243W**.
In force **1 June 1993**.

82.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional effect of the 74th Amendment?
o: It abolished the distinction among municipal corporations, municipalities and Nagar Panchayats.
It made local government a Union List subject and municipalities optional for all States.
It transferred all municipal taxation powers exclusively to the Union Government.
It gave urban local bodies constitutional status and made a uniform municipal framework obligatory for States.
82.x: The 74th Amendment gave urban local bodies constitutional status and required States to establish a uniform municipal framework through conforming laws.
82.tq: Choose the option that combines the two distinct consequences without adding an extreme claim.
xs: The 74th gave **ULBs constitutional status** and made a **uniform municipal framework obligatory** for states — option **(4)**.
It kept the **three types** of municipalities (**243Q**); 'Local Government' stayed a **State List** subject.
xa: States had to conform their laws within **one year** (**243ZF**).
Taxing powers and grants (**243X**) are left to state legislatures.

82.s:
With reference to urban local government in India, consider the following statements:
1. Local Government continues to be a subject in the State List.
2. The 74th Amendment transferred Local Government to the Union List.
3. Municipal laws were required to be brought into conformity with the Constitution within one year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: Local Government remains in the State List, and Article 243ZF required municipal laws to be brought into conformity within one year. Statement 2 is false because the subject was not transferred to the Union List.
82.tq: Identify the wrong-list trap and connect Article 243ZF with the one-year compliance requirement.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
1: 'Local Government' remains a **State List** subject (Seventh Schedule).
2 wrong: the 74th did **not** move it to the Union List.
3: municipal laws had to conform within **one year** (**243ZF**).
xa: **243ZF** also lets existing laws continue for one year.
The 74th = **Nagarpalika Act**, in force **1 June 1993**.

82.s: Which one of the following is a compulsory provision to be incorporated in State municipal law under the 74th Amendment?
o: The manner of electing the Mayor
Direct election of all members from wards
Representation of Members of Parliament in municipalities
82.x: Direct election of all municipal members from wards is compulsory. Representation of MPs, reservation for backward classes and the manner of electing the Chairperson are left to State legislatures.
82.tq: Distinguish mandatory constitutional requirements from provisions left to State legislative choice.
xs: **Direct election of all members from wards** is compulsory (**243R**) — option **(2)**.
**Manner of electing the Mayor**, **BC reservation** and **MP representation** are **voluntary**.
xa: Other compulsory items: **three types** of municipalities, **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh+**), **5-year term**.
SC/ST reservation by population; not less than **one-third** for women (**243T**).

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT a compulsory provision under the 74th Amendment?
o: Reservation for backward classes in every municipality
Ward Committees in municipalities having a population of three lakh or more
Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to population
82.x: Reservation for backward classes is voluntary and is left to the State legislature. Ward Committees for municipalities with a population of three lakh or more, five-year terms, and SC/ST reservation are compulsory provisions.
82.tq: Find the provision expressly left to State legislative discretion among otherwise mandatory features.
xs: **Reservation for backward classes** is **voluntary** — option **(1)**.
Compulsory: **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh or more**), **SC/ST reservation** by population, **5-year** term.
xa: Other voluntary items: representation of **MPs, MLAs, MLCs**; manner of electing the **Chairperson**.
Devolving the Twelfth Schedule subjects (**243W**) is also voluntary.

82.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

(a) Article 243Q
(b) Article 243R
(c) Article 243S
(d) Article 243T

List-II (Provision)
(i) Ward Committees
(ii) Reservation of seats
(iii) Types of municipalities
(iv) Composition of municipalities
82.x: Article 243Q deals with types of municipalities, Article 243R with their composition, Article 243S with Ward Committees and Article 243T with reservation of seats.

xs: Correct code: **a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii** — option **(1)**.
**243Q** — types of municipalities; **243R** — composition; **243S** — **Ward Committees**; **243T** — **reservation**.

**243W** — powers and the **Twelfth Schedule**.

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding municipal tenure and elections:
1. A municipality has a five-year term.
2. An election must be held within six months of dissolution of a municipality.
3. The State Election Commission is responsible for municipal elections.
4. The State Finance Commission reviews the financial position of municipalities.

xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.

**SEC** runs municipal polls (**243ZA**); **SFC** reviews municipal finances (**243Y**).

82.s: Which one of the following matters is voluntary and may be decided by the State legislature under the 74th Amendment?
o: The five-year term of a municipality
The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson
Ward Committees in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more
State Election Commission supervision of municipal elections

xs: **The manner of electing the municipal Chairperson** is left to the state — option **(2)**.
The **5-year term**, **Ward Committees** (**3 lakh+**) and **SEC** supervision are compulsory.
xa: AP Cabinet (**18 Aug 2026**) approved **direct election of Mayors** and chairpersons, replacing the indirect system.

82.s: Under Part IXA of the Constitution, which Article contains the definitions relating to municipalities?
82.x: Article 243P contains the definitions for the purposes of Part IXA, while Article 243Q deals with the constitution of municipalities.
82.tq: Use precise Article–subject matching rather than relying on adjacent Article numbers.
xs: **Article 243P** has the definitions for Part IXA — option **(1)**.
**243Q** = three types of municipalities; **243R** = composition; **243S** = Ward Committees.
xa: A **metropolitan area** (population **10 lakh or more**) is defined in **Art. 243P**.
The **MPC** is under **243ZE**.

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three types of municipalities specifically recognised under Article 243Q?
82.x: Article 243Q recognises Nagar Panchayats for transitional areas, Municipal Councils for smaller urban areas and Municipal Corporations for larger urban areas. Cantonment Boards are other forms of urban local bodies outside this classification.
82.tq: Find the one institution outside the constitutional three-fold classification.
xs: The **Cantonment Board** is not one of the **243Q** types — option **(1)**.
243Q types: **Nagar Panchayat** (transitional), **Municipal Council** (smaller), **Municipal Corporation** (larger).
xa: Cantonment Boards come under the **Ministry of Defence**.
Also outside 243Q: notified area committee, town area committee, township, port trust, special purpose agency.

82.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Article 243R — Composition of municipalities
2. Article 243T — Reservation of seats
3. Article 243U — Duration of municipalities
4. Article 243X — Audit of municipal accounts
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
82.x: Articles 243R, 243T and 243U concern composition, reservation and duration respectively. Article 243X concerns taxes and funds; audit is dealt with by Article 243Z.
82.tq: Split the options by checking the closely placed Articles 243X and 243Z.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
**243R** — composition; **243T** — reservation; **243U** — duration.
Pair 4 is wrong: **243X** = **taxes and funds**; **audit** is **243Z**.
