the National Commission for Backward Classes Act and urban land rights
protection under the A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956 and habitat rights under Section 3(1)(e) of the Forest Rights Act
111.x: The Shompen area is protected by the A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation, 1956, while habitat rights are linked to Section 3(1)(e) of the Forest Rights Act.
111.tq: Connect the contemporary issue with the two specific protective legal provisions.
xs: The **Shompen** are protected by the **A&N (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation 1956** and **FRA habitat rights, Sec. 3(1)(e)** — option **(4)**.
The Tribal Council alleged pressure on them over the **Great Nicobar project**.
xa: The Shompen speak an **Austro-Asiatic** language.
First PVTG with habitat rights: **Bharia** (MP).

111.s: Which of the following comparisons between Andhra Pradesh and India is correct in respect of Scheduled Tribes?
o: AP ST literacy is 48.8% against India’s 59%, and AP ST sex ratio is 1009 against India’s 990.
AP ST literacy is 59% against India’s 48.8%, and AP ST sex ratio is 990 against India’s 1009.
AP ST literacy is 48.8% against India’s 59%, and AP ST sex ratio is 990 against India’s 1009.
AP ST literacy is 59% against India’s 48.8%, and AP ST sex ratio is 1009 against India’s 990.
111.x: Andhra Pradesh has an ST literacy rate of 48.8% compared with India’s 59%, while its ST sex ratio is 1009 compared with India’s 990.
111.tq: Check both comparison columns together; one reversed figure makes an option incorrect.
xs: ST literacy **48.8%** vs India's **59%**, and ST sex ratio **1009** vs India's **990** — option **(1)** (**Census 2011**).
Options (2) to (4) swap one or both pairs.
xa: **64.83%** of ST holders are **marginal holders**.
Lists are **State-specific**.

111.s: The Banchhada community, formerly described as a ‘criminal tribe’, is listed as a Scheduled Caste in
111.x: The Banchhada are listed as Scheduled Castes in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, despite their earlier description as a ‘criminal tribe’.
111.tq: Use the state-specific-list trap: community classification can differ across States.
xs: The **Banchhada**, once a "**criminal tribe**", are listed as **SC** in **Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan** — option **(1)**.
It shows that tribe/caste lists are **State-specific**.
xa: The **Criminal Tribes Act 1871** branded ~**200** communities; repealed **31 August 1952**.
After repeal such groups were called "**Denotified**".

112.s: Which of the following best defines an ethnic group?
o: People residing only within a constitutionally recognised State
People belonging exclusively to the same religious denomination
People identified solely by their common occupation
People who identify with one another through common language, history, society, culture or nation
112.x: An ethnic group consists of people who identify with one another through common language or dialect, history, society, culture or nation. Ethnicity is not confined to occupation, territory or religion alone.
112.tq: Choose the comprehensive definition rather than an exclusive single-marker definition.
xs: An **ethnic group** is people who **identify with one another** through common **language/dialect, history, society, culture or nation** — option **(4)**.
Ethnicity is not limited to one religion, one occupation or residence in one State.
xa: Ethnic **markers**: **language, religion, race, region, culture**.
**Intra-ethnic** conflict is within a group; **inter-ethnic** is between groups.
**T.K. Oommen** is India's foremost scholar on ethnicity.

112.s: Which of the following is NOT generally considered a marker of ethnicity?
112.x: Language, religion, race, region and culture are recognised markers of ethnicity. Annual income is not listed as an ethnic marker.
112.tq: Find the unrelated socioeconomic characteristic among recognised identity markers.
xs: **Annual income** is not an ethnic marker — option **(1)**.
The markers are **language, religion, race, region, culture** — so religion, region and language are all markers.
xa: An ethnic group shares **language/dialect, history, society, culture or nation**.
**Arnold Rose**: a minority is set apart by **race, nationality, religion or language**.
India: **121 languages**, **270 mother tongues**, **22** scheduled languages.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s linguistic diversity:

1. More than 19,500 languages and dialects were returned.
2. The 2011 Census recorded 121 languages and 270 mother tongues.
3. India has 22 Scheduled Languages.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: All three statements are correct. India’s linguistic diversity includes more than 19,500 returned languages and dialects, 121 languages, 270 mother tongues and 22 Scheduled Languages.
112.tq: Retain the distinction between returned languages and dialects, Census figures and Scheduled Languages.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **19,500+** languages and dialects were returned.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Census 2011** — **121 languages and 270 mother tongues**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **22** scheduled languages — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: ⚠ **121** languages vs **270** mother tongues vs **22** scheduled vs **19,500+** returned.
Linguistic stocks: **Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic, Tibeto-Burman**.

112.s: A conflict occurring within members of the same ethnic group is classified as which type?
112.x: An intra-ethnic conflict occurs within an ethnic group, whereas an inter-ethnic conflict occurs between different ethnic groups.
112.tq: Discriminate between the prefixes intra- and inter-.
xs: A conflict **within** one ethnic group is **intra-ethnic** — option **(1)**.
**Inter-ethnic** conflict is **between** groups, e.g. **Meitei vs Kuki** in Manipur.
xa: **Conflict approach**: groups as interest groups competing unequally (**South Africa**, **Sri Lankan Tamils**).
**Consensus approach**: groups coexist with separate identities.
Ethnic markers: language, religion, race, region, culture.

112.s: Which of the following correctly describes the conflict approach to ethnicity?
o: Groups coexist with separate identities without unequal competition.
Ethnic boundaries are irrelevant to political mobilisation.
Groups are interest groups competing unequally for power and resources.
Ethnic identity is fixed exclusively by biological inheritance.
112.x: The conflict approach views groups as interest groups competing unequally, with South Africa and Sri Lankan Tamils cited as examples. The coexistence of separate identities describes the consensus approach.
112.tq: Contrast the defining assumptions of the consensus and conflict approaches.
xs: The **conflict approach** sees groups as **interest groups competing unequally** — option **(3)**.
Peaceful coexistence with separate identities is the **consensus** approach (option 1).
Identity fixed by birth is the **primordialist** view, not the conflict approach.
xa: Examples cited: **South Africa** and **Sri Lankan Tamils**.
**Sri Lanka**: Tamil and Muslim parties formed a common platform (**Jul 2026**).
**Inter-ethnic** = between groups; **intra-ethnic** = within.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about views of ethnic identity:
1. Primordialists such as Clifford Geertz see identity as given by birth, rooted in deep primordial attachments.
2. Instrumentalists such as Paul Brass see identity as socially made and kept by boundaries.
3. Constructivists such as Fredrik Barth see identity as socially made and maintained through boundaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Statement 1 is correct: primordialism (Geertz, Shils) sees identity as given by birth. Statement 2 is wrong: instrumentalists (Paul Brass) hold that elites mobilise identity for power and resources; 'made and kept by boundaries' is the constructivist idea. Statement 3 is correct: constructivism (Barth, Anderson) sees identity as socially made and kept by boundaries. So B is right; A, C and D include statement 2.
112.tq: Birth = primordial; elites/resources = instrumental; boundaries/imagined = constructivist.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **primordialists** (**Clifford Geertz**, Edward Shils) see identity as **given by birth**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: **instrumentalists** (**Paul Brass**) say **elites mobilise identity** for power and resources; "made and kept by boundaries" is constructivist.
Statement 3 is **correct**: **constructivists** (**Fredrik Barth**) see identity as socially made and kept by **boundaries** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: ⚠ **Barth** = boundaries; **Geertz** = primordial attachments; **Kothari / Jaffrelot** = instrumentalist.
**Benedict Anderson** ("Imagined Communities") is also constructivist.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. Rajni Kothari discussed electoral mobilisation in Politics in India.
2. Christophe Jaffrelot wrote India’s Silent Revolution.
3. Fredrik Barth wrote Ethnic Groups and Boundaries.
4. Benedict Anderson wrote Imagined Communities.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: All four statements are correct. Rajni Kothari and Christophe Jaffrelot are associated with instrumentalist discussions, while Barth and Anderson are associated with constructivist perspectives.
112.tq: Verify author–work pairs directly and avoid swapping scholars across theories.
xs: All four are **correct**: **Kothari** — **Politics in India**; **Jaffrelot** — **India's Silent Revolution**; **Barth** — **Ethnic Groups and Boundaries**; **Anderson** — "**Imagined Communities**" — option **(4)**.
Kothari and Jaffrelot are **instrumentalist**; Barth and Anderson **constructivist**.
xa: **T.K. Oommen**: Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity.
**Primordialist**: Clifford Geertz, Edward Shils.

112.s: T.K. Oommen is particularly known for which contribution to the study of ethnicity?
o: Formulating the concept of Greater Nagalim
Separating nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship
Classifying Indian tribes exclusively by race
112.x: T.K. Oommen is regarded as a foremost Indian scholar on ethnicity and distinguished nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship in Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity.
112.tq: Identify the scholar through his distinctive conceptual contribution and work.
xs: **T.K. Oommen** separates **nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship** — option **(2)**.
**Greater Nagalim** is the Naga demand; racial classification follows **S.S. Sarkar**.
xa: Oommen's book: **Citizenship, Nationality and Ethnicity**.
He is India's **foremost scholar on ethnicity**.
**Barth**: Ethnic Groups and Boundaries.

112.s:

i. Longpi pottery

iii. Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival
iv. Wet rice cultivation without animals or machines
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Nyishi (largest tribe of Arunachal) hold the Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival; the Apatani of Ziro valley grow wet rice without animals or machines; the Idu Mishmi observe the 'iyu-ena' taboo on killing tigers; the Tangkhul Naga of Manipur make Longpi pottery. B swaps Nyishi and Apatani, C swaps Idu Mishmi and Tangkhul, D swaps Nyishi and Idu Mishmi.
112.tq: Tangkhul is the only Manipur group here, so Longpi pottery goes to it; Ziro = Apatani.
xs: **Nyishi** — **Pakke Paga Hornbill Festival** (a-iii); **Apatani** — **wet rice without animals or machines** (b-iv); **Idu Mishmi** — **'iyu-ena'** tiger taboo (c-ii); **Tangkhul Naga** — **Longpi pottery** (d-i) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps Nyishi and Apatani; (3) swaps Idu Mishmi and Tangkhul; (4) swaps Nyishi and Idu Mishmi.
xa: **Nyishi** = largest tribe of **Arunachal**; **Apatani** live in the **Ziro valley**.
**Tangkhul Naga** are of **Manipur**; two Tangkhul Nagas were killed in Ukhrul (**Apr 2026**).

112.s: Which of the following is the correct list of linguistic stocks mentioned in relation to India?
112.x: The linguistic stocks listed are Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Tibeto-Burman.
112.tq: Select the complete classification while rejecting unrelated linguistic families.
xs: India's linguistic stocks: **Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Tibeto-Burman** — option **(3)**.
Uralic, Semitic, Romance and Celtic are not among the listed stocks.
xa: ⚠ **Khasi** = Austro-Asiatic (**Mon-Khmer**); **Garo** = Sino-Tibetan (**Bodo group**).
**121 languages and 270 mother tongues** (Census **2011**).
**22** scheduled languages.

112.s: Racial classification in the cited framework is associated with which scholar?
112.x: The racial classification mentioned in relation to Indian ethnic groups follows S.S. Sarkar.
112.tq: Match the classification with its stated scholar.
xs: India's **racial classification** follows **S.S. Sarkar** — option **(1)**.
**Paul Brass** is an instrumentalist; **T.K. Oommen** separates nation, nationality, ethnicity and citizenship.
xa: Ethnic markers include **race**, along with language, religion, region, culture.
**Arnold Rose**: minority set apart by **race, nationality, religion or language**.

112.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the official languages of Meghalaya is correct?

1. Khasi and Garo were made official languages alongside English.
2. Khasi belongs to the Austro-Asiatic Mon-Khmer group.
3. Garo belongs to the Bodo group of the Sino-Tibetan family.
4. Khasi and Garo are included in the Eighth Schedule.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Khasi and Garo are official languages of Meghalaya alongside English, but neither is included in the Eighth Schedule.
112.tq: Look for the exception in the final statement and distinguish official status from Scheduled status.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Khasi** and **Garo** are official languages of **Meghalaya** alongside English (**2026**).
Statements 2 and 3 are **correct**: Khasi = **Austro-Asiatic (Mon-Khmer)**; Garo = **Bodo group, Sino-Tibetan**.
Statement 4 is **wrong**: **neither is in the Eighth Schedule** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: India has **22** scheduled languages.
**Sixth Schedule** autonomous district councils exist in **Meghalaya** too.

112.s: According to Arnold Rose, a minority is a group that is set apart by
o: economic class alone and is recognised only by the State
race, nationality, religion or language, and is regarded as different by itself and by others
territorial concentration alone, irrespective of identity
112.x: Arnold Rose describes a minority as a group set apart by race, nationality, religion or language that sees itself, and is seen by others, as different, with negative connotations.
112.tq: Select the option containing the complete definition rather than a partial attribute.
xs: **Arnold Rose**: a minority is set apart by **race, nationality, religion or language** and is **seen as different by itself and others** — option **(3)**.
The difference carries **negative connotations**.
xa: **Giddens**: minority marked by **disadvantage**, **group solidarity**, physical/social **isolation**.
**National minority**: a term from **European minority-rights law**.
NCM Act **1992** notifies India's minorities.

112.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the features associated with minorities in Giddens' formulation?
112.x: Giddens identifies disadvantage, group solidarity and physical or social isolation as features associated with minorities; constitutional sovereignty is not included.
112.tq: Identify the unrelated constitutional term among the three stated sociological features.
xs: **Constitutional sovereignty** is not a Giddens feature — option **(2)**.
**Giddens** lists **disadvantage**, **group solidarity** and **physical/social isolation** — options (3), (4), (1).
xa: **Arnold Rose**: minority set apart by race, nationality, religion or language.
**National minority**: non-dominant citizen group with its own ethnic, religious or linguistic identity.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about the term 'national minority':
1. The term comes from Indian constitutional law.
2. It denotes a non-dominant citizen group with its own ethnic, religious or linguistic identity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
112.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the term comes from European minority-rights law. Statement 2 is correct: a national minority is a non-dominant citizen group with its own ethnic, religious or linguistic identity. So B is right; A and C accept the false origin and D rejects the correct definition.
112.tq: 'National minority' is a European minority-rights term; India uses 'notified minorities' under the NCM Act.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: "**national minority**" comes from **European minority-rights law**, not Indian constitutional law.
Statement 2 is **correct**: a **non-dominant citizen group** with its own **ethnic, religious or linguistic identity** — so **2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: India's minorities are notified under the **NCM Act 1992**.
**Arnold Rose** and **Giddens** gave definitions of minority.

112.s:
Consider the following statements about minorities notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992:
1. Muslims, Christians, Buddhists and Parsis are notified minorities.
2. Jains were notified as a minority in 2014.
3. Sikhs were added to the list only in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Statement 1 is correct: Muslims, Christians, Buddhists and Parsis are notified (along with Sikhs). Statement 2 is correct: Jains were the 2014 addition. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2014 addition was the Jains, not the Sikhs. So A is right; B, C and D include the false statement 3.
112.tq: Six notified minorities; the late entry (2014) is the Jains.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Muslims, Christians, Buddhists, Parsis** are notified (with **Sikhs**) under the **NCM Act 1992**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Jains** were added in **2014**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the **2014** addition was the Jains, not Sikhs — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: "**National minority**" is a term from European minority-rights law.
**Giddens**: minority = disadvantage, group solidarity, isolation.

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. China’s law on “ethnic unity and progress” covers 55 minority groups.
2. Uyghurs, Hui and Tibetans are examples of groups covered by the law.
3. Critics argue that the law strengthens non-Han identity by reducing Han dominance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: The law covers 55 minority groups, including Uyghurs, Hui and Tibetans. Critics argue that it erodes non-Han identity, not that it strengthens it.
112.tq: Identify the reversed effect in the third statement while retaining the factual group and number statements.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: China's law on "**ethnic unity and progress**" (**Mar 2026**) covers **55** minority groups.
Statement 2 is **correct**: e.g. **Uyghurs, Hui, Tibetans**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: critics say it **erodes non-Han identity** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: **Han** are over **91%** of China's population.
**Sri Lanka**: Tamil and Muslim parties formed a common platform (**Jul 2026**).

112.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The States Reorganisation Commission was headed by Fazl Ali.
2. The States Reorganisation Commission was constituted in 1953.
3. The formation of Andhra Pradesh followed the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: Fazl Ali headed the States Reorganisation Commission, which was constituted in 1953; the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 led to the formation of Andhra Pradesh on 1 November 1956.
112.tq: Check the institution, year and consequence separately before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: the **SRC** was headed by **Fazl Ali**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the SRC dates to **1953**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: the **States Reorganisation Act 1956** formed **Andhra Pradesh** on **1 Nov 1956** — so **1, 2 and 3**, option **(4)**.
xa: **Andhra State (1953)** = first state on language lines, after **Potti Sriramulu**'s fast.

112.s: Which of the following groups correctly represents the States formed in 1987?
112.x: Goa, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram became States in 1987.
112.tq: Test a complete named list, with distractors formed by swapping neighbouring north-eastern States.
xs: **Goa, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram** became states in **1987** — option **(2)**.
**Nagaland** became a state in **1963**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Mizoram statehood followed the **Mizo Accord 1986**.
**1960**: Bombay split into **Maharashtra** and **Gujarat**; **1966**: **Punjab/Haryana**.
**2014**: **Telangana**; **2019**: J&K and Ladakh UTs.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Year)
 a. 1960
 b. 1963
 c. 1966
 d. 1975

List-II (Reorganisation)
 i. Sikkim became the 22nd State
 ii. Nagaland was formed
 iii. Bombay was divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat
 iv. Punjab and Haryana were formed and Chandigarh became a Union Territory

Select the correct answer using the code below.
112.x: The 1960 reorganisation divided Bombay into Maharashtra and Gujarat; 1963 saw Nagaland; 1966 saw Punjab and Haryana with Chandigarh as a Union Territory; and Sikkim became the 22nd State in 1975.
112.tq: Start with the sure year-event pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatched reorganisation.
xs: **1960** — Bombay split into **Maharashtra and Gujarat** (a–iii); **1963** — **Nagaland** (b–ii); **1966** — **Punjab/Haryana**, Chandigarh a UT (c–iv) — option **(1)**.
That leaves **1975** for **Sikkim** as the **22nd** State (d–i).
xa: **1987**: Goa, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram.
⚠ **371F** = Sikkim special provisions.
**2014**: Telangana.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs (Year — Reorganisation):
1. 2014 — Telangana formed
2. 2019 — Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories
3. 1966 — Nagaland formed
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
112.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct: Telangana was formed in 2014, and J&K and Ladakh became UTs in 2019. Pair 3 is wrong: Nagaland was formed in 1963; 1966 was the Punjab/Haryana reorganisation, with Chandigarh made a UT. So '1 only' leaves out a true pair, and the options with 3 include the false one.
112.tq: 1963 Nagaland, 1966 Punjab/Haryana, 2014 Telangana, 2019 J&K/Ladakh UTs.
xs: Pair 1 is **correct**: **2014** — **Telangana**.
Pair 2 is **correct**: **2019** — **J&K and Ladakh UTs**.
Pair 3 is **wrong**: **Nagaland** was formed in **1963**; **1966** was **Punjab/Haryana** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **AP** was formed **1 Nov 1956**.
Nagaland: Act **1962**, inaugurated **1 Dec 1963**.

112.s:
Match List-I (Movement) with List-II (Demand):
List-I
a. Naga movement
b. Bodo movement
c. ULFA
d. Khalistan movement
List-II
i. Sovereign Assam for ethnic Assamese
ii. Separate Sikh state
iii. Independence / 'Greater Nagalim'
iv. Bodoland state (after the earlier Udayachal demand)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Naga movement sought independence / Greater Nagalim; the Bodo movement moved from Udayachal to a Bodoland state; ULFA (April 1979) sought a sovereign Assam for ethnic Assamese; the Khalistan movement sought a separate Sikh state. Option B swaps Bodo and ULFA, C swaps Naga and Bodo, D swaps Naga and Khalistan.
112.tq: Both Bodo and ULFA are Assam-based: Bodo wants a state within India, ULFA wants sovereignty.
xs: **Naga** — **independence / "Greater Nagalim"** (a-iii); **Bodo** — **Bodoland** after **Udayachal** (b-iv); **ULFA** — **sovereign Assam** (c-i); **Khalistan** — **separate Sikh state** (d-ii) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps Bodo and ULFA; (3) swaps Naga and Bodo; (4) swaps Naga and Khalistan.
xa: **ULFA** was formed in **April 1979**; **ABSU** in **1967**.
Khalistan leader: **Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale**.

112.s:
The Naga movement is primarily associated with which of the following regions?

1. Nagaland
2. Naga areas of Manipur
3. Mizoram
4. Assam’s North bank of the Brahmaputra

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Naga movement is associated with Nagaland and Naga areas of Manipur. Mizoram and the North bank of the Brahmaputra are associated with other movements.
112.tq: Use regional separation to detect statements belonging to neighbouring movements.
xs: The Naga movement covers **Nagaland** and **Naga areas of Manipur** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(1)**.
**Mizoram** is the **Mizo** movement's area; the **north bank of the Brahmaputra** is the **Bodo** area.
xa: Outfits: **NNC** (A.Z. Phizo), **NSCN**.
State response: **Nagaland** state, talks, **AFSPA**.
**371A** = Nagaland.

112.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Naga movement — NNC and NSCN
2. Mizo movement — MNF
3. Bodo movement — ABSU and NDFB
4. Gorkhaland movement — GNLF

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
112.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The Naga movement involved NNC and NSCN, the Mizo movement MNF, the Bodo movement ABSU and NDFB, and the Gorkhaland movement GNLF.
112.tq: Verify each organisation against its movement before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All four are **correct**: **Naga — NNC, NSCN**; **Mizo — MNF**; **Bodo — ABSU, NDFB**; **Gorkhaland — GNLF** — option **(4)**.
Leaders: **A.Z. Phizo** (NNC), **Laldenga** (MNF), **Subhash Ghising** (GNLF).
xa: **ABSU** was formed in **1967**.
Gorkhaland responses: **DGHC 1988**; **Gorkhaland Territorial Administration 2012**.

112.s: With reference to the Naga movement, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1962 and Nagaland was inaugurated in 1963.
The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1963 and the State was inaugurated in 1962.
Both the Act and the inauguration took place in 1962.
Both the Act and the inauguration took place in 1963.
112.x: The State of Nagaland Act was enacted in 1962, while the State of Nagaland was inaugurated in 1963.
112.tq: Discriminate between two closely related years rather than treating them as the same event.
xs: The **State of Nagaland Act** was **1962**; the state was **inaugurated** on **1 Dec 1963** — option **(1)**.
CDI gives both **1962** and **1963** — this explains the two dates.
xa: Nagaland got special provisions under **Art. 371A**.
Naga outfits: **NNC**, **NSCN**; demand "**Greater Nagalim**".

112.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
112.x: Operation Blue Star was conducted in 1984 in the context of the Khalistan movement and the Golden Temple. The other operations or accords are associated with different movements.
112.tq: Use the operation–movement association to expose swapped organisations and events.
xs: **Operation Blue Star (1984)** at the **Golden Temple** was the response to the **Khalistan movement** — option **(2)**.
**All Clear (2003)** and **Rhino (1991)** were **ULFA** operations; the **Mizo Accord 1986** was with the **MNF**.
xa: ⚠ **Blue Star** = Punjab; **Bajrang / Rhino / All Clear** = ULFA (Assam).
Blue Star was asked in **APPSC 2025**.

112.s:
Which of the following operations were associated with ULFA-related counter-insurgency efforts?

1. Operation Bajrang
2. Operation Rhino
3. Operation All Clear in Bhutan
4. Operation Blue Star

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: Operations Bajrang in 1990, Rhino in 1991 and All Clear in Bhutan in 2003 were associated with ULFA-related operations. Operation Blue Star was associated with Khalistan militancy.
112.tq: Separate similarly named operations by their movement and location.
xs: **Bajrang (1990)**, **Rhino (1991)** and **All Clear in Bhutan (2003)** were against **ULFA** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
**Operation Blue Star (1984)** was against **Khalistan** militancy in Punjab.
xa: **ULFA** (April **1979**) sought a **sovereign Assam** for ethnic Assamese.
The pro-talks ULFA faction **disbanded** after the **Dec 2023** settlement.

112.s: The present ethnic conflict in Manipur, as described in relation to its principal demands, involves which of the following?
o: Meitei demand for ST status and Kuki demand for separate administration
Khasi demand for language rights and Garo demand for land reform
Bengali demand for autonomy and Mizo demand for statehood
Naga demand for statehood and Bodo demand for Udayachal
112.x: The Manipur conflict has involved the Meitei demand for Scheduled Tribe status and the Kuki demand for separate administration, with the conflict continuing since May 2023.
112.tq: Match each community with its specific demand instead of recalling only the conflict’s names.
xs: Manipur's conflict turns on the **Meitei demand for ST status** and the **Kuki demand for separate administration** — option **(1)**.
It has continued **since May 2023**.
xa: **Meitei vs Kuki** was asked in **APPSC 2024**.
Manipur shutdowns hit **12 of 16 districts** (**Apr 2026**).
**371C** = Manipur.

112.s: The Assam Movement was primarily associated with conflict between which communities and over which issue?
o: Meitei and Kuki communities over ST status
Mizo and Bru communities over the Eighth Schedule
Assamese and Bengali communities over illegal migration
Tribes and Bengali settlers over demographic change in Tripura
112.x: C is right: the Assam Movement (led by AASU) was an Assamese-Bengali conflict over illegal migration. A is the Manipur Meitei-Kuki conflict over ST status, B the Mizo-Bru conflict (not about the Eighth Schedule), and D the Tripura tribes-vs-Bengali-settlers conflict.
112.tq: Pair the conflict communities with the correct underlying cause.
xs: The **Assam Movement** (**AASU**) was an **Assamese-Bengali** conflict over **illegal migration** — option **(3)**.
(1) is the **Manipur** conflict; (2) refers to the **Mizo-Bru** clash; (4) is the **Tripura** conflict.
xa: It ended in the **Assam Accord 1985** — cut-off **24 March 1971**.
The **ABSU** revived the Bodoland demand after the Accord.

112.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Tripura ethnic conflict?
o: Conflict between Meitei and Kuki communities over separate administration
Conflict between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers following demographic change
Conflict between Nagas and Mizos over Greater Nagalim
Conflict between Assamese and Bengali communities over illegal migration
112.x: The Tripura conflict developed between indigenous tribes and Bengali settlers after demographic change. The Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council provides local self-rule.
112.tq: Distinguish the Tripura conflict from the similar ethnic conflicts of Manipur and Assam.
xs: **Tripura**: **indigenous tribes vs Bengali settlers** after **demographic change** — option **(2)**.
(1) is **Manipur**; (4) is **Assam**; Greater Nagalim is the **Naga** demand.
xa: The **Tripura Tribal Areas ADC** gives local self-rule.
Regionalism aids **democratisation** (Tripura ADC) but can feed secessionism.

112.s:
Match List-I (Accord) with List-II (Key outcome):
List-I
a. Assam Accord, 1985
b. Mizo Accord, 1986
c. Bru-Reang Agreement, 2020
d. ULFA settlement, December 2023
List-II
i. Brus displaced from Mizoram settled in Tripura
ii. 24 March 1971 cut-off for detecting foreigners
iii. Pro-talks faction disbanded
iv. End of insurgency, followed by statehood in 1987
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
112.x: The Assam Accord (1985, AASU/AAGSP) fixed 24 March 1971 as the cut-off; the Mizo Accord (1986, MNF) ended insurgency and led to statehood in 1987; the Bru-Reang Agreement (2020) settled Brus displaced from Mizoram in Tripura; the ULFA settlement (Dec 2023) saw the pro-talks faction disband. B swaps Assam and Mizo, C swaps Bru and ULFA, D swaps Assam and Bru.
112.tq: Anchor on the dates: 1971 cut-off can only be Assam; 1987 statehood can only be Mizoram.
xs: **Assam Accord 1985** — **24 March 1971** cut-off (a-ii); **Mizo Accord 1986** — end of insurgency, statehood **1987** (b-iv); **Bru-Reang 2020** — Brus settled in **Tripura** (c-i); **ULFA Dec 2023** — faction disbanded (d-iii) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps Assam and Mizo; (3) swaps Bru and ULFA; (4) swaps Assam and Bru.
xa: Assam Accord was with **AASU/AAGSP**; Mizo Accord with the **MNF**.

112.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bodo accords:

1. The 1993 accord was associated with the Bodoland Autonomous Council.
2. The 2003 accord was associated with the Bodoland Territorial Council.
3. The 2020 accord was associated with the Bodoland Territorial Region.
4. The accords involved organisations such as ABSU, BLT and NDFB.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
112.x: All four statements are correct. The Bodo settlement process included the 1993, 2003 and 2020 accords, leading respectively to the Bodoland Autonomous Council, BTC and BTR, with the listed organisations involved at different stages.
112.tq: Follow the chronological institutional changes and verify all named participants.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **1993** — **Bodoland Autonomous Council**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **2003** — **BTC**.
Statements 3 and 4 are **correct**: **2020** — **BTR**; parties **ABSU, BLT, NDFB** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
xa: **ABSU (1967)** first demanded **Udayachal**, then **Bodoland** (**1987**).
ABSU revived the Bodoland demand after the **Assam Accord (1985)**.

112.s: The ABSU revived the demand for Bodoland after which event?
112.x: The All Bodo Students’ Union revived the Bodoland demand after the Assam Accord of 1985.
112.tq: Connect the revival of a demand to the preceding regional political event.
xs: **ABSU** revived the **Bodoland** demand after the **Assam Accord** of **1985** — option **(1)**.
The **Mizo Accord 1986** dealt with the MNF; **Blue Star** with Punjab.
xa: ABSU (**1967**) earlier demanded **Udayachal** (**1960s**).

112.s: Autonomous district councils under the Sixth Schedule are related to which Article of the Constitution?
112.x: The Sixth Schedule, under Article 244(2), provides autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Article 244(1) relates to the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas elsewhere), and Article 371 contains special provisions for particular States.
112.tq: Distinguish the precise constitutional provision from nearby tribal-area and special-provision articles.
xs: The **Sixth Schedule** works through **Article 244(2)** — option **(4)**.
It provides **autonomous district councils** in **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**.
**Art. 371** is a separate set of special provisions for states.
xa: ⚠ **371A** = Nagaland; **371D** = AP; **371G** = Mizoram.
**Tripura Tribal Areas ADC** = local self-rule.

112.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Article)
 a. Article 371A
 b. Article 371B
 c. Article 371C
 d. Article 371D

List-II (State or subject)
 i. Assam
 ii. Nagaland
 iii. Manipur
 iv. Andhra Pradesh—public employment and education

Select the correct answer using the code below.
112.x: Article 371A concerns Nagaland, 371B Assam, 371C Manipur and 371D Andhra Pradesh in relation to public employment and education.
112.tq: Start with Article 371D and then match the north-eastern State provisions.
xs: **371A** — **Nagaland** (a–ii); **371B** — **Assam** (b–i); **371C** — **Manipur** (c–iii); **371D** — **AP**, public employment and education (d–iv) — option **(1)**.
Option (4) swaps Assam and Manipur.
xa: **371F** Sikkim; **371G** **Mizoram**; **371H** Arunachal.
⚠ **371A** = Nagaland; **371D** = AP; **371G** = Mizoram.

112.s: The Inner Line Permit system referred to in the context of north-eastern State responses dates from
112.x: The Inner Line Permit system dates from 1873.
112.tq: Test the specific historical year associated with an administrative mechanism.
xs: The **Inner Line Permit** dates from **1873** — option **(2)**.
It is one of the state's responses to ethnic and regional demands.
xa: Other responses: **statehood**, **AFSPA**, **peace accords**, **MDoNER**.
**Sixth Schedule** (**Art. 244(2)**): autonomous district councils.

112.s: Which of the following sets contains only measures or mechanisms mentioned as part of the State response to ethnic and regional demands?
o: Statehood, Inner Line Permit, AFSPA, peace accords and MDoNER
President’s Rule, Finance Commission, GST Council and AFSPA
Sixth Schedule, Election Commission, peace accords and Finance Commission
MDoNER, Supreme Court, GST Council and State Finance Commission
112.x: The stated response includes statehood, the Inner Line Permit, AFSPA, peace accords and MDoNER.
112.tq: Choose the option made entirely of items belonging to the same policy-response cluster.
xs: The listed responses are **statehood, Inner Line Permit, AFSPA, peace accords and MDoNER** — option **(1)**.
Finance Commission, GST Council and Election Commission are not listed responses.
xa: ILP dates from **1873**.
Accords: **Assam 1985**, **Mizo 1986**, **Bodo 2020**.

112.s: Which of the following correctly describes the democratic and political consequences attributed to regionalism?
o: It always produces secessionism and never supports democratic participation.
It is confined exclusively to linguistic state formation.
It eliminates vote-bank politics wherever autonomous councils exist.
It can aid democratisation, as in the Tripura ADC, but can also feed secessionism and vote-bank politics.
112.x: Regionalism may aid democratisation, illustrated by the Tripura ADC, but may also feed secessionism such as Greater Nagalim and vote-bank politics.
112.tq: Select the balanced option containing both the positive and negative consequences.
xs: Regionalism **aids democratisation** (**Tripura ADC**) but can **feed secessionism** (**Greater Nagalim**) and **vote-bank politics** — option **(4)**.
So options (1) and (3) overstate one side.
xa: NE insurgency: **over 50** ethnic rebel groups.
**Andhra State (1953)** = first state on language lines.

112.s: Which of the following is associated with the demand for a larger Naga homeland?
112.x: Greater Nagalim is associated with secessionist pressures connected with Naga aspirations.
112.tq: Match the political demand with its associated regional movement.
xs: **Greater Nagalim** is the demand for a larger Naga homeland — option **(2)**.
**MDoNER** and the **Tripura ADC** are state responses; **Andhra State** was the first linguistic state.
xa: Naga outfits: **NNC** (A.Z. Phizo), **NSCN**.
Naga areas extend into **Manipur**.

112.s: The shutdowns reported in Manipur after the Tronglaobi bomb attack and the killing of two Tangkhul Nagas affected how many of the State’s districts?
112.x: The shutdowns affected 12 of Manipur’s 16 districts.
112.tq: Retain both parts of the ratio instead of rounding it to all districts.
xs: Manipur shutdowns hit **12 of 16 districts** — option **(1)**.
They followed the **Tronglaobi** (Bishnupur) bomb attack and the killing of **two Tangkhul Nagas** in **Ukhrul** (**Apr 2026**).
xa: Manipur conflict: **Meitei vs Kuki** since **May 2023**.
The Centre gave **₹10 crore** of rice for refugees in **Mizoram** (**Jun 2026**).

112.s: Which was the first state in India formed on linguistic lines, following the fast of Potti Sriramulu?
112.x: Andhra State, formed in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's fast, was the first state formed on language lines. Andhra Pradesh was formed later, on 1 Nov 1956, under the States Reorganisation Act. Maharashtra was carved out of Bombay in 1960, and Nagaland (1963) was formed in response to Naga aspirations, not on language lines.
112.tq: First linguistic state: Andhra State 1953 (Potti Sriramulu).
xs: **Andhra State (1953)** was the **first state on language lines**, after **Potti Sriramulu**'s fast — option **(1)**.
**AP** was formed later, on **1 Nov 1956**; **Maharashtra (1960)** came from Bombay; **Nagaland (1963)** met Naga aspirations.
xa: **SRC (Fazl Ali, 1953)** → **States Reorganisation Act 1956**.
**371D** gives AP special provisions on public employment and education.

113.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Technology — Industrial Revolution and the inventions of Watt and Hargreaves
Media — migration of nomads in a particular season
113.x: The Industrial Revolution, associated here with Watt and Hargreaves, illustrates technology as a factor of social change. The other pairs wrongly associate examples with education, planning and media.
113.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate examples assigned to neighbouring factors.
xs: **Technology** — the **Industrial Revolution** with **Watt and Hargreaves** — is correctly matched, option **(1)**.
The **Green Revolution** is a **planning** example (**3rd Plan**), not education.
**Widow remarriage laws** illustrate **law**; **seasonal nomad migration** is a routine cycle, not social change.
xa: Technology today: **820 million+** internet users (LENS Dec **2025**).
**Media**: behaviour-change communication (Economic Survey **2025-26** SBCC); street plays in **Nasha Mukt Bharat**.
**Planning**: inclusive growth goal in the **11th Plan**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements regarding factors and sources of social change:
1. The spread of modern education is an example of education as a source of social change.
2. The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, illustrates the role of law.
3. Street plays under Nasha Mukt Bharat illustrate behaviour-change communication through media.
4. Reform and Dalit movements are examples of social movements.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All four statements are correct. Modern education, legislation, behaviour-change communication and social movements are all identified as sources or illustrations of social change.
113.tq: Test each statement against the factor-example relationship before selecting the coded combination.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **modern education** is a source of change (**APPSC 2019** source).
Statement 2 is **correct**: the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** shows the role of **law**.
Statements 3 and 4 are **correct**: **Nasha Mukt Bharat** street plays = **media**; **reform and Dalit movements** = **social movements** — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: Dalit change came through **state policy, reform movements, and Sanskritisation and Westernisation**.
⚠ **Seasonal nomad migration** = routine cycle, NOT social change.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about planning as a factor of social change:
1. Inclusive growth was the stated goal of the Seventh Plan.
2. The Green Revolution came under the Third Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is wrong: inclusive growth was the goal of the Eleventh Plan (the Seventh Plan is linked with technology-led modernisation). Statement 2 is correct: the Green Revolution came under the Third Plan. So B is right; A and C accept the wrong plan and D rejects the true statement.
113.tq: 3rd = Green Revolution, 7th = technology-led modernisation, 11th = inclusive growth.
xs: Statement 1 is **wrong**: **inclusive growth** was the **11th Plan** goal; the **7th Plan** prioritised technology-led modernisation.
Statement 2 is **correct**: the **Green Revolution** came under the **3rd Plan** — so **2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Other factors of change: **technology, education, law, media, migration/urbanisation, social movements**.
The **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** illustrates law as a factor.

113.s: Which one of the following is NOT a source of social change?
o: Migration of nomads in a particular season
Legislation such as the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955
113.x: Seasonal migration of nomads is a routine, recurring cycle and does not alter social structure, so it is not a source of social change (APPSC 2019). Modern education, legislation like the Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955, and industrialisation/urbanisation are all recognised sources of social change.
113.tq: Routine seasonal cycles = not social change.
xs: **Migration of nomads in a particular season** is **not** a source of social change — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2019**).
It is a **routine cycle** that recurs without altering society.
**Modern education**, the **Untouchability (Offences) Act 1955** and **industrialisation/urbanisation** are all recognised sources.
xa: ⚠ Seasonal nomad migration = routine cycle, NOT social change.
**Technology**: **820 million+** internet users.
**Planning**: Green Revolution (**3rd Plan**).

113.s:
With reference to the evolutionary or linear theory of social change, consider the following statements:
1. Auguste Comte is associated with the theory of three stages.
2. Herbert Spencer explained social evolution as a movement from simple to complex forms.
3. Durkheim explained social change in terms of the transition from mechanical to organic solidarity.
4. L. H. Morgan is associated with the evolutionary approach.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: All four statements are correct. Comte, Spencer, L. H. Morgan and Durkheim are associated with the evolutionary or linear theory of social change.
113.tq: Test the complete set of theorists and their distinctive formulations rather than relying on one familiar name.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Comte** — **three stages**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **Spencer** — **simple to complex**.
Statements 3 and 4 are **correct**: **Durkheim** — **mechanical to organic**; **L.H. Morgan** is also evolutionary — so all four, option **(4)**.
xa: **Cyclical** theory: **Spengler, Toynbee, Sorokin, Pareto**.
**Conflict**: **Karl Marx**, Dahrendorf, Coser.
**Technological**: Veblen, **Ogburn**.

113.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Thinker)
A. Oswald Spengler
B. Arnold Toynbee
C. Pitirim Sorokin
D. Vilfredo Pareto

List-II (Associated idea)
1. Challenge and response
2. Circulation of elites
3. Sensate and ideational cultures
4. Decline of the West

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
113.x: Spengler wrote about the decline of the West, Toynbee proposed challenge and response, Sorokin distinguished sensate and ideational cultures, and Pareto explained the circulation of elites.
113.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes by matching each thinker with his distinctive concept.
xs: **Spengler** — **Decline of the West** (A-4); **Toynbee** — **challenge and response** (B-1); **Sorokin** — **sensate/ideational** (C-3); **Pareto** — **circulation of elites** (D-2) — option **(1)**.
All four are **cyclical** theorists.
xa: **Evolutionary (linear)**: Comte, **Spencer**, L.H. Morgan, Durkheim.
**Conflict**: Karl Marx (class struggle), Dahrendorf, Coser.

113.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
113.x: Arnold Toynbee is associated with the cyclical theory through the concept of challenge and response. Class struggle is associated with Karl Marx, while Dahrendorf and Coser are associated with conflict theory.
113.tq: Find the mismatched proponent-concept pair among neighbouring theories.
xs: **Arnold Toynbee — Class struggle** is **wrongly matched** — option **(3)**.
Toynbee is a **cyclical** theorist (**challenge and response**); **class struggle** is **Karl Marx**.
**Dahrendorf** and **Coser** are rightly listed under **conflict** theory.
xa: Other cyclical theorists: **Spengler**, **Sorokin**, **Pareto**.
**Diffusion**: Elliot Smith, Perry, Boas.

113.s: The diffusion theory of social change is associated with which of the following group of thinkers?
113.x: Elliot Smith, Perry and Boas are identified with the diffusion theory of social change.
113.tq: Identify the complete thinker-group belonging to one theory instead of selecting an individual name.
xs: **Diffusion** theory: **Elliot Smith, Perry and Boas** — option **(4)**.
Comte, Spencer, Durkheim are **evolutionary**; Spengler, Toynbee, Pareto **cyclical**; Veblen, Ogburn **technological**.
xa: British school: **Elliot Smith, Perry** (**Egypt** as source).
German-Austrian: **Graebner, Schmidt** (**culture circles**); American: **Boas, Wissler** (**culture areas**).

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Thorstein Veblen is associated with the technological theory of social change.
2. William F. Ogburn is associated with the technological theory of social change.
3. Elliot Smith is identified with the technological theory of social change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Veblen and Ogburn are associated with the technological theory. Elliot Smith is associated with diffusion theory, not technological theory.
113.tq: Use a nearby-theory name as the false statement to test classification of proponents.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are **correct**: **Veblen** and **Ogburn** are **technological** theorists.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Elliot Smith** is a **diffusionist** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: **Ogburn** originated **cultural lag** in Social Change (**1922**).
Diffusion: Elliot Smith, Perry, **Boas**.

113.s: A minority community gradually merges into the wider society and loses its distinct identity. This process is known as:
113.x: Assimilation occurs when a minority merges fully into the wider society and loses its distinct identity.
113.tq: Apply the definition to the scenario instead of treating every cultural contact as acculturation.
xs: A minority that **merges fully and loses its distinct identity** undergoes **assimilation** — option **(2)**.
In **acculturation** the group is influenced by another culture but **stays distinct**.
xa: ⚠ Acculturation = influenced but distinct; assimilation = distinct identity lost.
**Sanskritisation**: a low caste or tribe adopts the customs of a higher caste.
**De-sanskritisation**: groups reject Sanskritic norms and assert their own identity.

113.s:
Match List-I (Diffusionist school) with List-II (Scholars and idea):
List-I
a. British school
b. German-Austrian school
c. American school
List-II
i. Boas and Wissler - culture areas
ii. Elliot Smith and Perry - Egypt as the source
iii. Graebner and Schmidt - culture circles
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: The British school (Elliot Smith, Perry) saw Egypt as the source of culture; the German-Austrian school (Graebner, Schmidt) developed culture circles; the American school (Boas, Wissler) developed culture areas. B swaps British and German-Austrian, C swaps German-Austrian and American, D swaps British and American.
113.tq: Circles = German (Kulturkreis); areas = American; Egypt = British.
xs: **British** — **Elliot Smith, Perry**, Egypt as source (a-ii); **German-Austrian** — **Graebner, Schmidt**, culture circles (b-iii); **American** — **Boas, Wissler**, culture areas (c-i) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) swaps British and German-Austrian; (3) swaps German-Austrian and American; (4) swaps British and American.
xa: ⚠ Culture **circles** = German-Austrian; culture **areas** = American.
Indus debate: **Mackay** (migration), **Wheeler** (diffusion of ideas).

113.s: In the diffusionist interpretation of the Indus civilisation, which scholar is associated with migration from Mesopotamia?
113.x: Mackay is associated with the interpretation that the Indus civilisation involved migration from Mesopotamia. Wheeler represented diffusion of ideas, while Marshall is associated with indigenous evolution.
113.tq: Use the scholar-debate association and distinguish migration from diffusion of ideas.
xs: **Mackay** saw **migration from Mesopotamia** behind the Indus civilisation — option **(4)**.
**Wheeler** argued **diffusion of ideas**; **Marshall** argued **indigenous evolution**.
**Milton Singer** studied Madras temple culture, not the Indus.
xa: Diffusionist schools: **British**, **German-Austrian**, **American**.
British school saw **Egypt** as the source of culture.

113.s: The process of cultural change that results from sustained contact between groups, in which one group is influenced by the imperatives of another culture, is called:
113.x: Acculturation is change through sustained contact, being influenced by another culture's imperatives (APPSC 2019). Assimilation goes further: a minority merges fully and loses its identity. De-sanskritisation is rejection of Sanskritic norms. Cultural lag is Ogburn's gap between material and non-material culture.
113.tq: Acculturation = influenced by contact; assimilation = identity lost.
xs: Change through **sustained contact**, being influenced by another culture's imperatives, is **acculturation** — option **(2)** (**APPSC 2019**).
**Assimilation** goes further: the group **loses its identity**.
**De-sanskritisation** rejects Sanskritic norms; **cultural lag** is Ogburn's gap between material and non-material culture.
xa: ⚠ Acculturation = influenced but distinct.
**Westernisation**: changes from **150+ years** of British rule.

113.s: Who propounded the concept of cultural lag?
113.x: W.F. Ogburn propounded the concept of cultural lag in Social Change, published in 1922.
113.tq: Match the concept with its originator, not with a scholar associated with another process of change.
xs: **W.F. Ogburn** originated **cultural lag** in **Social Change (1922)** — option **(2)**.
**Daniel Lerner** gave the modernisation sequence; **Weber** called secularisation the "disenchantment of the world".
xa: Ogburn is a **technological** theorist, with **Veblen**.
Lagging factors: **religion, law, tradition**; **politics is not** one (**UPPSC 2014**).

113.s: According to Ogburn, cultural lag occurs because:
o: Non-material culture changes faster than material culture
Material culture, especially technology, changes faster than non-material culture
Religion and law are entirely unaffected by technological change
Both material and non-material culture always change at the same rate
113.x: Ogburn held that material culture, particularly technology, changes faster, while beliefs, norms and other non-material elements lag behind.
113.tq: Check the direction of the comparison; the material–non-material order is the central trap.
xs: In Ogburn's **cultural lag**, **material culture** (technology) changes **faster** than **non-material culture** (beliefs, norms) — option **(2)**.
Option (1) reverses it; (3) and (4) contradict the idea of a lag.
xa: Lagging factors: **religion, law, tradition**.
Example: digital spread vs slow norms on children's online safety (**DPDP Act 2023**).
Ogburn: Social Change (**1922**).

113.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a lagging factor in cultural lag?
113.x: Religion, law and tradition are identified as lagging factors. Politics is not included in that list.
113.tq: Find the outsider in the short list rather than selecting a familiar social institution automatically.
xs: **Politics** is **not** a lagging factor — option **(3)** (**UPPSC 2014**).
**Religion, law and tradition** are the lagging factors.
xa: ⚠ Cultural lag: **politics** is NOT a lagging factor.
Material culture (technology) changes faster than non-material culture.
Concept by **W.F. Ogburn** (**1922**).

113.s: The rapid spread of digital technology accompanied by slower changes in norms concerning children's online safety illustrates:
113.x: The example illustrates cultural lag because technological change is faster than the adjustment of social norms. The reference also mentions parental consent for persons under 18 under the DPDP Act, 2023.
113.tq: Apply the material-versus-non-material distinction to a contemporary example.
xs: Fast **digital spread** with **slow change in norms** on children's online safety is **cultural lag** — option **(1)**.
Technology moves ahead; norms lag behind.
xa: The **DPDP Act 2023** requires **parental consent** for under-**18**s.
India has **820 million+** internet users.
Concept by **W.F. Ogburn**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about the term Sanskritisation:
1. M.N. Srinivas first called the process 'Brahminisation'.
2. He coined the term in Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India (1952).
3. He first coined the term in Social Change in Modern India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: Srinivas first called it Brahminisation. Statement 2 is correct: the term was coined in Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India (1952). Statement 3 is wrong: Social Change in Modern India only developed the concept later. So B is right; A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
113.tq: Coined in the Coorgs book (1952); developed in Social Change in Modern India.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: Srinivas first called it "**Brahminisation**".
Statement 2 is **correct**: he coined Sanskritisation in **Religion and Society among the Coorgs of South India (1952)**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **Social Change in Modern India** only **developed** it — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Coined by **M.N. Srinivas** (**APPSC 2019**).
Reference groups: **Brahmins**, **Kshatriya, Vaishya** and the local **dominant caste**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Sanskritisation:
1. A low caste or tribe adopts the customs, rituals and way of life of a higher, often twice-born, caste to claim higher rank.
2. It brings structural change in the caste system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: this is Srinivas's definition of Sanskritisation. Statement 2 is wrong: Sanskritisation brings positional change, not structural change; the hierarchy stays. So A is right; B and C accept the false statement and D rejects the definition.
113.tq: Sanskritisation moves a caste up the ladder; the ladder itself stays: positional, not structural.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: a **low caste or tribe** adopts the **customs, rituals and way of life** of a higher, often twice-born, caste.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: Sanskritisation brings **positional, not structural** change — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: Sanskritisation gives a caste mobility but **leaves the hierarchy intact**.
**De-sanskritisation**: rejection of Sanskritic norms (non-Brahmin/Dravidian movement).

113.s:
Which of the following may function as reference groups in Sanskritisation?
1. Brahmins
2. Kshatriyas
3. Vaishyas
4. The local dominant caste
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: Reference groups may include Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and the locally dominant caste.
113.tq: Check whether the list includes both the traditionally twice-born groups and the local dominant caste.
xs: Reference groups: **Brahmins**, **Kshatriya**, **Vaishya** and the local **dominant caste** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
Dominant caste is itself a **Srinivas** concept.
xa: Srinivas first called the process "**Brahminisation**".
Coined in the **Coorgs** study (**1952**).

113.s: De-sanskritisation refers to a process in which groups:
o: Reject Sanskritic norms and assert their own identity
Replace non-material culture with material culture
Adopt only Western technology and institutions
Merge completely with a dominant culture
113.x: De-sanskritisation involves rejecting Sanskritic norms and asserting one's own identity, as illustrated by the non-Brahmin or Dravidian movement.
113.tq: Use the reversal of Sanskritisation carefully; rejection and identity assertion are the key clues.
xs: **De-sanskritisation**: groups **reject Sanskritic norms** and **assert their own identity** — option **(1)**.
Example: the **non-Brahmin/Dravidian movement**.
Full merger with a dominant culture is **assimilation**.
xa: **Sanskritisation**: positional, not structural change.
**Acculturation**: influenced by another culture but distinct.

113.s: Who is associated with the sociological concept of Westernisation in the Indian context?
113.x: M.N. Srinivas associated Westernisation with changes produced by more than 150 years of British rule.
113.tq: Separate the originator of Westernisation from scholars associated with modernisation and cultural lag.
xs: **M.N. Srinivas** gave **Westernisation** — option **(4)**.
It means changes from **150+ years of British rule**.
**Ogburn** gave cultural lag.
xa: Levels: **technology, institutions, ideology and values**.
Srinivas's set: **Secularisation + Sanskritisation + Westernisation + Dominant Caste**.

113.s:
According to M.N. Srinivas, Westernisation operates at which levels?
1. Technology
2. Institutions
3. Ideology
4. Values
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: Srinivas identified technology, institutions, ideology and values as levels at which the effects of British rule produced Westernisation.
113.tq: Check all four dimensions instead of treating Westernisation as merely technological imitation.
xs: Srinivas's Westernisation works at **technology, institutions, ideology and values** — so **1, 2, 3 and 4**, option **(4)**.
It flows from **150+ years** of **British rule**.
xa: Srinivas treated Westernisation as **ethically neutral**.
Westernisation has a **specific source**; modernisation is **universal**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Westernisation and modernisation:
1. Westernisation has a specific source (the West/British), while modernisation is a universal process that may come from any source.
2. Srinivas treated Westernisation as value-loaded and modernisation as ethically neutral.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: Westernisation is source-specific, modernisation universal. Statement 2 is wrong: it is reversed; Srinivas preferred Westernisation as ethically neutral, while modernisation is value-loaded ('progress'). So A is right; B and C accept the reversed statement and D rejects the true one.
113.tq: Srinivas chose 'Westernisation' precisely because it is neutral; 'modernisation' implies progress.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Westernisation** has a **specific source** (the West/British); **modernisation** is **universal**.
Statement 2 is **wrong** — it is reversed: Westernisation is **ethically neutral**, modernisation **value-loaded** ("progress") — so **1 only**, option **(1)**.
xa: The **value-neutrality** debate is a criticism point (Srinivas).
Modernisation indicators include **rationality**, **scientific temper**, literacy, mass media.

113.s: Urbanisation and education may change authority patterns in families but do not necessarily end the:
113.x: Srinivas observed that urbanisation and education can alter authority patterns within families without necessarily ending the joint family.
113.tq: Distinguish change in internal authority from disappearance of the institution itself.
xs: Urbanisation and education change **authority patterns** but **do not end the joint family** (Srinivas) — option **(2)**.
So family change is partial: authority shifts, the joint form persists.
xa: **Westernisation**: from **150+ years of British rule**.
**Migration/urbanisation** is a factor of social change.

113.s:
According to Daniel Lerner's sequence, which of the following is the correct order associated with modernisation?
A. Urbanisation
B. Literacy
C. Media exposure
D. Participation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: Lerner's sequence is urbanisation, followed by literacy, media exposure and participation.
113.tq: Use the sequence clue and distinguish the order of the four indicators.
xs: **Lerner**'s sequence: **urbanisation → literacy → media exposure → participation** — option **(1)**.
The other orders scramble or reverse it.
xa: Lerner linked "**Empathy**" with **psychic mobility**.
His book: **The Passing of Traditional Society (1958)**.

113.s:
Consider the following statements about Daniel Lerner:
1. He wrote The Passing of Traditional Society (1958).
2. He linked 'empathy' with psychic mobility.
3. He wrote When a Great Tradition Modernizes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
113.x: Statement 1 is correct: Lerner wrote The Passing of Traditional Society (1958). Statement 2 is correct: he linked empathy with psychic mobility. Statement 3 is wrong: When a Great Tradition Modernizes is by Milton Singer. So B is right; A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
113.tq: Lerner = Passing of Traditional Society, empathy; Singer = Great Tradition, Madras temples.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Lerner** wrote **The Passing of Traditional Society (1958)**.
Statement 2 is **correct**: he linked "**Empathy**" with **psychic mobility**.
Statement 3 is **wrong**: **When a Great Tradition Modernizes** is by **Milton Singer** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Lerner's sequence: urbanisation → literacy → media exposure → participation.
**Singer** showed tradition and modernity continuing together in **Madras temple culture**.

113.s: Milton Singer's When a Great Tradition Modernizes argues that:
o: Tradition and modernity can continue together in Madras temple culture
Modernity always destroys every traditional institution
Caste groups can change only through legislation
113.x: Singer showed that tradition and modernity can coexist, using Madras temple culture as an example.
113.tq: Choose the precise coexistence argument and reject extreme claims about modernity destroying tradition.
xs: **Milton Singer** showed **tradition and modernity continue together** in **Madras temple culture** — option **(1)**.
So modernity need not destroy tradition (option 2 is the opposite).
xa: Book: **When a Great Tradition Modernizes**.
**Lerner**: The Passing of Traditional Society (**1958**).

113.s:
Which of the following are indicators of modernisation?
1. Rationality and scientific temper
2. Industrialisation and urbanisation
3. Literacy and mass media
4. Democratic participation
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: Rationality, scientific temper, industrialisation, urbanisation, literacy, mass media and democratic participation are all listed as indicators of modernisation.
113.tq: Verify each indicator and use the complete combination only when all four belong to the same framework.
xs: Modernisation indicators: **rationality, scientific temper, industrialisation, urbanisation, literacy, mass media, democratic participation** — option **(4)**.
All four listed pairs fall in this list.
xa: Modernisation is **universal**, from **any source**; it is **value-loaded** ("progress").
Planning prioritised technology-led modernisation from the **7th Plan**.

113.s: Planning gave priority to technology-led modernisation from which Five-Year Plan?
113.x: Technology-led modernisation received priority from the Seventh Plan.
113.tq: Distinguish the Seventh Plan reference from the Third Plan's Green Revolution and Eleventh Plan's inclusive growth.
xs: Planning prioritised **technology-led modernisation** from the **7th Plan** — option **(2)**.
The **3rd Plan** brought the **Green Revolution**; the **11th Plan** aimed at **inclusive growth**.
xa: Modernisation indicators: rationality, scientific temper, **industrialisation**, urbanisation.
**Planning** is itself listed as a factor of social change.

113.s: Which of the following constitutional provisions are associated with constitutional secularism in India?
113.x: Constitutional secularism is associated here with Articles 25 to 28, concerning freedom of religion and the state's relationship with religious practice.
113.tq: Use the Article-range association and avoid swapping it with other Fundamental Rights groups.
xs: Constitutional secularism lies in **Articles 25–28** — option **(1)**.
It means the **state's neutrality and equal respect** for religions.
xa: **Sociological secularisation** concerns **society's** belief and practice.
**Weber**: secularisation = "**disenchantment of the world**".

113.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sociological secularisation concerns changes in social beliefs and practices.
2. Constitutional secularism concerns state neutrality and equal respect.
3. The two concepts are identical because both exclusively require the removal of religion from public life.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because sociological secularisation and constitutional secularism are distinct, and constitutional secularism does not require the exclusive removal of religion from public life.
113.tq: Reject the extreme word exclusively and distinguish social change from constitutional neutrality.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **sociological secularisation** concerns **society's** belief and practice.
Statement 2 is **correct**: **constitutional secularism** = **state's neutrality and equal respect** (Arts. **25-28**).
Statement 3 is **wrong**: the two are **distinct** — so **1 and 2 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Sociological secularisation = **decline of religion's hold** on social life.
Srinivas: less "religious" meaning, differentiation, **rationalisation**.

113.s: Max Weber described secularisation as:
113.x: Max Weber used the expression “disenchantment of the world” in relation to secularisation.
113.tq: Match the distinctive phrase with the correct sociological thinker.
xs: **Weber** called secularisation the "**disenchantment of the world**" — option **(4)**.
**Psychic mobility** is **Lerner**'s; **culture circles** the German-Austrian school's; **great tradition** relates to **Singer**.
xa: Srinivas's secularisation: differentiation and **rationalisation**.
Sociological secularisation = decline of religion's hold on social life.

113.s:
Srinivas associated secularisation with which combination?
1. Sanskritisation
2. Westernisation
3. Dominant caste
4. Culture circles
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
113.x: Srinivas listed secularisation together with Sanskritisation, Westernisation and dominant caste. Culture circles belong to the German-Austrian diffusionist school.
113.tq: Identify the one concept belonging to another theoretical cluster and eliminate it.
xs: Srinivas grouped secularisation with **Sanskritisation**, **Westernisation** and **dominant caste** — so **1, 2 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
**Culture circles** belong to the **German-Austrian** diffusionists (**Graebner, Schmidt**).
xa: Srinivas also noted urbanisation changes **authority patterns** without ending the joint family.
Sanskritisation was first called "**Brahminisation**".

113.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in India's social protection coverage between 2015 and 2025?
113.x: The coverage increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025.
113.tq: Read the direction of change first, then verify the two paired percentages.
xs: India's social protection coverage **increased** from **19%** (**2015**) to **64.3%** (**2025**) (ILO) — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses it; **25** to **100** is the number of people in crore, not a percentage.
xa: People covered: **25 crore → 100 crore**.
**Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** uses community outreach and street plays.

113.s:
Consider the following statements regarding debates on social change:
1. Sanskritisation can provide mobility to a caste.
2. Sanskritisation necessarily abolishes the caste hierarchy.
3. The debate between Westernisation and modernisation includes the issue of value-neutrality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
113.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Sanskritisation may provide mobility to a caste but leaves the hierarchy intact; the Westernisation-modernisation debate concerns value-neutrality.
113.tq: Reject the absolute implication that mobility automatically destroys the existing hierarchy.
xs: Statement 1 is **correct**: **Sanskritisation** gives a caste **mobility**.
Statement 2 is **wrong**: it **leaves the hierarchy intact**.
Statement 3 is **correct**: Westernisation vs modernisation is a debate on **value-neutrality** — so **1 and 3 only**, option **(2)**.
xa: Sanskritisation = **positional, not structural** change.
Srinivas preferred Westernisation as **ethically neutral**.

113.s: The number of people covered by social protection increased from approximately 25 crore to what level?
113.x: The reported number of people covered by social protection increased from 25 crore to 100 crore.
113.tq: Distinguish the population figures from the percentage figures in a current-affairs comparison.
xs: People covered by social protection rose from **25 crore** to **100 crore** — option **(4)**.
**64.3** is the 2025 coverage percentage, not crore.
xa: **Nasha Mukt Bharat**: community outreach and street plays.

113.s: Which of the following methods is specifically used by the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan as a tool of behavioural change?
113.x: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan uses community outreach and street plays as tools of behavioural change.
113.tq: Identify the practical field-level intervention from among unrelated theoretical concepts.
xs: **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** uses **community outreach and street plays** — option **(2)**.
Mechanical/organic solidarity (Durkheim) and challenge-response (Toynbee) are theories, not tools.
xa: Media as a factor: **behaviour-change communication** (Economic Survey **2025-26** SBCC).
Social protection coverage: **64.3%** (**2025**).

113.s: Which of the following correctly describes the value orientation associated with Westernisation and modernisation in the Srinivas framework?
o: Westernisation is ethically neutral, whereas modernisation is value-loaded as progress.
Westernisation is value-loaded, whereas modernisation is ethically neutral.
113.x: Srinivas preferred to treat Westernisation as ethically neutral, whereas modernisation is commonly value-loaded through the idea of progress.
113.tq: Do not reverse the value-neutral and value-loaded descriptions.
xs: Srinivas held **Westernisation** **ethically neutral** and **modernisation** **value-loaded as progress** — option **(1)**.
Option (2) reverses the pair.
xa: Westernisation has a **specific source** (West/British); modernisation is **universal**.
Westernisation levels: **technology, institutions, ideology, values**.

114.s: Social stratification refers to the ranking of groups in a hierarchy based on unequal distribution of which of the following?
114.x: Social stratification is the hierarchical ranking of groups according to unequal wealth, prestige and power.
114.tq: Use the precise definition rather than selecting a related social characteristic.
xs: **Stratification** ranks groups in a hierarchy of unequal **wealth, prestige and power** — option **(1)**.
Language, religion, region or residence are not the unequal rewards in the definition.
xa: Bases: **caste, class, gender, age, race, ethnicity**.
⚠ **Language is NOT a basis** of stratification (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
**Melvin Tumin**: stratification is social, ancient, universal, diverse in form, consequential.

114.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally recognised as a basis of social stratification?
114.x: Caste, gender and ethnicity are recognised bases of social stratification. Language is not treated as a basis in this context.
114.tq: Find the odd term among the recognised bases of stratification.
xs: **Language** is **not** a basis of social stratification — option **(1)** (**APPSC-GS 2019**).
**Ethnicity**, **gender** and **caste** are all bases, along with class, age and race.
xa: Stratification = ranking by unequal **wealth, prestige and power**.
Caste has **vertical** (ranking by birth) and **horizontal** (separate groups) classification.
Among **Muslims**: **Ashraf, Ajlaf, Arzal**.

114.s: According to Melvin Tumin, which of the following is NOT a characteristic of social stratification?
o: It affects the life chances of individuals
It is social rather than biological
It is a recent phenomenon of industrial societies
114.x: Tumin regarded stratification as ancient and universal, not as a recent phenomenon limited to industrial societies.
114.tq: The extreme time claim in the option is the trap; compare it with the characteristic of being ancient.
xs: For **Tumin**, stratification is **ancient**, so "a **recent phenomenon of industrial societies**" is not a characteristic — option **(3)**.
His list: **social (not biological)**, **ancient**, **universal**, diverse in form, **consequential** (decides **life chances**).
xa: Tumin also **criticised Davis-Moore**: stratification **wastes talent** and passes inequality on.
In India, **Harappan** society showed differentiation (citadel vs lower town).

114.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Approach)
A. Functionalist
B. Conflict or Marxian
C. Multi-dimensional
D. Ideological caste approach

List-II (Theorist)
1. Karl Marx
2. Max Weber
3. Louis Dumont
4. Kingsley Davis and Wilbert Moore

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
114.x: Functionalism is associated with Davis and Moore; the conflict approach with Marx; the multi-dimensional approach with Weber; and the ideological caste approach with Dumont.
114.tq: Start with the sure pair of Marx and the conflict approach, then complete the remaining matches.
xs: **Functionalist** — **Davis and Moore** (A-4); **Conflict** — **Karl Marx** (B-1); **Multi-dimensional** — **Max Weber** (C-2); **Ideological caste** — **Louis Dumont** (D-3) — option **(1)**.
The other codes shuffle these four pairings.
xa: ⚠ Davis-Moore = functionalist; **Tumin** = its critic; Weber = **class, status, party**.
Dumont's book: **Homo Hierarchicus** (purity and pollution).

114.s: According to the functionalist theory of stratification developed by Kingsley Davis and Wilbert Moore, stratification is necessary because it:
o: Prevents all forms of social mobility
Draws scarce talent into functionally important positions through higher rewards
Makes ownership of the means of production irrelevant
114.x: Davis and Moore argued that unequal rewards help attract scarce talent to positions considered functionally important.
114.tq: Identify the function claimed for unequal rewards, not a general effect of inequality.
xs: **Davis and Moore**: higher rewards **draw scarce talent into functionally important positions** — option **(2)**.
They did not claim it prevents mobility or removes inequality; **means of production** is Marx's idea.
xa: The theory dates from **1945**.
**Melvin Tumin** countered that it **wastes talent** and passes inequality to the next generation.

114.s: Who criticised functionalism by arguing that stratification wastes talent and transmits inequality to the next generation?
114.x: Melvin Tumin criticised the functionalist view, arguing that stratification can waste talent and reproduce inequality across generations.
114.tq: Link the critique to the critic rather than to the original functionalist theorists.
xs: **Melvin Tumin** argued stratification **wastes talent** and **passes inequality to the next generation** — option **(4)**.
**Thorner** classified agrarian classes; **Beteille** studied Sripuram; **Sorokin** set out vertical and horizontal mobility.
xa: Tumin critiqued the **functionalist** theory of **Davis and Moore** (**1945**).
Tumin's characteristics: social, ancient, universal, diverse, consequential.

114.s: In Karl Marx’s theory, class is primarily determined by:
o: The ownership or non-ownership of the means of production
The number of political parties in a society
114.x: For Marx, class position depends fundamentally on whether a person owns or does not own the means of production.
114.tq: Use the ownership distinction as the defining Marxian criterion.
xs: For **Karl Marx**, class depends on **ownership or non-ownership of the means of production** — option **(3)**.
**Purity and pollution** is **Dumont**'s ideological reading of caste; education is a class feature in the caste-class comparison.
xa: **Weber**: three dimensions — **class, status, party (power)**.
Weber: class position and "**market situation**" decide **life chances**.

114.s:
