115.tq: Separate the post-reorganisation percentages from the old 13-district figures.
xs: In the **28-district** map, **Visakhapatnam 89.69%** is highest and **Polavaram 2.84%** lowest — so option **(2)** is correct (AP Survey 2025-26).
**47.45%** and **16.16%** are the old-district figures for Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam.
xa: AP reorganised into **28 districts** in **2025**; new districts include **Polavaram** and **Markapuram**.
⚠ Old 13 districts: least **Srikakulam**; 28 districts: lowest **Polavaram**.
Krishna's old-district share was **40.81%**.

115.s: Which district had the largest rural population in absolute numbers in Andhra Pradesh?
115.x: East Godavari had the largest rural population in absolute numbers.
115.tq: Separate absolute population from percentage share.
xs: **East Godavari** had the largest rural population in absolute numbers — so option **(4)** is correct (**APPSC-G2 2017** key).
**Srikakulam** is the least urbanised by share, while **Visakhapatnam** and **Krishna** are the most urbanised.
xa: AP is about **70.5% rural** (2011).
AP urban share **29.47%** (2011) vs India's **31.16%**.
Below India's 1991 level (**22.87%**): **Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, West Godavari**.

115.s: Which group of cities has been recommended as Tier-2 cities to absorb migration?
115.x: Kurnool, Ongole and Rajahmundry have been recommended as Tier-2 cities to help absorb migration.
115.tq: Recall the recommended urban-centre group and distinguish it from the capital-area cluster.
xs: **Kurnool, Ongole and Rajahmundry** are recommended (CDI) as Tier-2 cities to absorb migration — so option **(1)** is correct.
The aim is to correct AP's **spatial imbalance**: **Vizag about 47%** urban vs **Srikakulam 16%**.
xa: Old 13 districts: most urbanised **Visakhapatnam 47.45%**, then **Krishna 40.81%**.
Least urbanised: **Srikakulam 16.16%** and **Prakasam 19.56%**.
AP urban share **29.47%** (2011), below India's **31.16%**.
Main migrant **source States** in India: **UP and Bihar**.

115.s: The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh cover approximately how much geographical area?
115.x: The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh cover 16,267.63 sq km, about 10.15% of the State's area, with 3,512 villages; about 12.9 lakh tribals live in them.
115.tq: Compare the closely spaced numerical options carefully.
xs: AP's **Scheduled Areas** cover **16,267.63 square kilometres** — so option **(1)** is correct.
That is about **10.15%** of the State, with **3,512 villages**.
xa: About **12.9 lakh** tribals live in them (APSES 2024-25 p.251).
Districts: **Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Anakapalli, Eluru**.
AP STs: **27.39 lakh = 5.53%** (2011); **34 ST communities**.
⚠ Not all AP tribals live in Scheduled Areas — about **12.9 lakh** of **27.39 lakh**.

115.s: Which authority was reported to have told a parliamentary panel that the Census Town definition is outdated?
o: Office of the Registrar General of India
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
115.x: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs told the parliamentary panel headed by TDP MP Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy that the Census Town definition is outdated.
115.tq: Use the ‘who said what’ authority trap in an institutional context.
xs: The **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** told a parliamentary panel the **Census Town** definition is outdated — so option **(4)** is correct.
The panel was headed by TDP MP **Magunta Sreenivasulu Reddy**.
The **RGI** is the body keeping the definition for **Census 2027**; **KVIC** runs **PMEGP**.
xa: Census town tests: population **≥5,000**, **≥75%** of male workers non-farm, density **≥400/sq km**.
Criteria unchanged since **1981**.
**Statutory towns** are notified by States and run by **ULBs**.

115.s: What is the stated position of the Registrar General of India regarding the Census Town definition?
o: It has abolished the definition immediately for all purposes.
It is retaining the definition for Census 2027.
It is applying the definition only to Scheduled Areas.
It has transferred the definition to the Election Commission.
115.x: Although the Census Town definition was criticised as outdated, the Registrar General of India is retaining it for Census 2027.
115.tq: Distinguish criticism of a definition from the administrative decision to retain it temporarily.
xs: The **RGI** is **retaining the Census Town definition for Census 2027** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It does so although **MoHUA** told a parliamentary panel the definition is outdated (17 Sep 2026).
xa: Census towns are **administratively villages** meeting all three tests.
⚠ Census town = **5,000 – 75% – 400**; unchanged since **1981**.
"Hidden urbanisation": satellite data put India about **63%** urban (2015), vs Census **31%**.

115.s: Why is the rural-urban binary criticised in discussions of rapidly urbanising areas?
o: It prevents any rural area from receiving public funds.
It classifies every village as a statutory town.
It places such areas under panchayats that may have limited fiscal power.
It gives all rapidly urbanising areas complete municipal autonomy.
115.x: The rural-urban binary may leave rapidly urbanising areas under panchayats with limited fiscal power, creating a governance mismatch.
115.tq: Apply the classification problem to the institutional consequence for fast-urbanising areas.
xs: The rural-urban binary leaves fast-urbanising areas **under panchayats with little fiscal power** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Such areas have urban traits but no **ULB**-level finances.
xa: "Hidden urbanisation" (DEGURBA): about **63%** urban in **2015**, more than double the Census **31%** (EAC-PM).
**16th Finance Commission** raised the ULB share of local-body grants from **36% to 45%**.
ES 2025-26: cities lack fiscal autonomy due to **institutional fragmentation**.

116.s: Casteism is best described as:
o: A form of occupational specialisation without social hierarchy
A system of universal brotherhood cutting across caste groups
A hereditary social group with a traditional occupation
Discrimination and prejudice against people because of their caste
116.x: Casteism is the evil form of the caste system involving discrimination and prejudice based on caste, along with concentration of power, money and prestige in a few castes.
116.tq: Distinguish the attitude and practice of casteism from the institution of caste.
xs: **Casteism** is **discrimination and prejudice against people because of their caste** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It is the **evil form** of the caste system: power, money and prestige **concentrate in a few castes**.
A **hereditary group with a traditional occupation** (option 3) describes **caste** the institution, not casteism.
xa: ⚠ Caste = institution (may exist **without hostility**); casteism = **partisan attitude and practice**.
**Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty".
Casteism produces **discrimination, conflict and vote-bank politics**.

116.s: Kaka Kalelkar defined casteism as:
o: A division of labour based on hereditary occupation
A system of political representation for disadvantaged groups
A voluntary association based on economic interests
An overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty
116.x: Kaka Kalelkar described casteism as “an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty” that ignores justice, fair play and universal brotherhood.
116.tq: Use the exact wording of a thinker’s definition to avoid look-alike interpretations.
xs: **Kaka Kalelkar** defined casteism as "**an overriding, blind and supreme group loyalty**" — so option **(4)** is correct.
Such loyalty ignores **justice, fair play and universal brotherhood**.
xa: **Ambedkar**: caste is "not just a division of labour, but also a **division of labourers**".
**Rajni Kothari**: politics does not just use caste, it **politicises** it.
Casteism = **partisan loyalty** to one's own caste against others.

116.s: According to B.R. Ambedkar, caste is not merely a division of labour but also a:
116.x: Ambedkar stated that caste is “not just a division of labour, but also a division of labourers.” He argued that it splits the working class and blocks collective bargaining.
116.tq: Test the precise completion of a well-known quotation.
xs: **Ambedkar**: caste is "not just a division of labour, but also a **division of labourers**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It **splits the working class** and **blocks collective bargaining**.
xa: Ambedkar wrote **Annihilation of Caste (1936)**, Who Were the Shudras? and **Mooknayak**.
He founded the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**.
He embraced **Buddhism** on **14 Oct 1956** at **Nagpur**.

116.s:
With reference to G.S. Ghurye’s features of caste, consider the following statements:

1. Segmental division and hierarchy are features of caste.
2. Restrictions on feeding and social intercourse are associated with caste.
3. Civil and religious disabilities and privileges form part of the features of caste.
4. Caste permits unrestricted choice of occupation and exogamous marriage.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because caste involves restricted choice of occupation and endogamy, with hypergamy or anuloma as an exception.
116.tq: Find the statement that reverses the paired features of occupation and marriage.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statements 1-3 correct: **segmental division, hierarchy**, **restrictions on feeding and social intercourse**, **civil and religious disabilities and privileges** are Ghurye's features.
Statement 4 wrong: caste means **restricted choice of occupation** and **endogamy**.
xa: The exception to endogamy is **hypergamy (anuloma)**.
Only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste (Aug 2025).
⚠ Caste may exist without hostility; **casteism** is the partisan practice.

116.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes caste from casteism?
o: Caste is always hostile, whereas casteism may exist without hostility
Caste and casteism are identical terms for hereditary endogamy
Caste is a social structure, whereas casteism is partisan loyalty to one’s own caste against others
Caste is based only on political mobilisation, whereas casteism is based only on occupation
116.x: Caste is a social structure involving hereditary and endogamous identity, whereas casteism is an attitude and practice involving partisan loyalty and the use of caste for gain.
116.tq: Separate the institution from the attitude and practice built around it.
xs: **Caste is a social structure, whereas casteism is partisan loyalty to one's own caste against others** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Caste = **hereditary, endogamous group** with traditional occupation (Ghurye's features); it **may exist without hostility**.
Casteism uses caste for **political, economic or social gain**, producing discrimination and **vote-bank politics**.
xa: **Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "blind and supreme group loyalty".
Casteism hinders **national integration** and excludes castes from the economy.
**Rajni Kothari** (Caste in Indian Politics, **1970**): politics **politicises** caste.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about endogamy and casteism:
1. Endogamy keeps caste boundaries and the idea of caste 'purity' intact.
2. About a quarter of Indian marriages are now inter-caste.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only about 5% of Indian marriages are inter-caste. Hence '1 only'; 'Both' and '2 only' fail on statement 2, 'Neither' fails on statement 1.
116.tq: Inter-caste marriages: only about 5%.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **endogamy** keeps caste boundaries and "**purity**" intact.
Statement 2 wrong: only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste (Aug 2025), not a quarter.
xa: **Dr. Ambedkar Scheme** for inter-caste marriages gives **₹2.5 lakh** per couple to weaken endogamy.
Honour-killing paradox: **TN, Telangana, Maharashtra, Kerala** show more inter-caste unions and more honour killings.
**Lata Singh (2006)**: no bar on inter-caste marriage.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reproduction of caste consciousness:

1. Families reproduce caste through customs and rituals.
2. Marriage norms transmit caste identity across generations.
3. Children absorb caste consciousness at an early age.
4. Urban migration automatically eliminates caste prejudice from families.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Urban migration does not automatically eliminate caste prejudice; migrants may carry it into cities.
116.tq: Reject the absolute claim that urbanisation automatically removes a social practice.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Families** reproduce caste through **customs, rituals and marriage norms**; children **absorb it early**.
Statement 4 wrong: **migrants carry caste prejudice into cities** — urban anonymity has limits.
xa: In cities **caste networks** decide informal jobs; caste associations and **caste stickers** on vehicles persist (UPSC).
**Endogamy** keeps boundaries and "purity" intact.
Upper-caste **landlords refusing tenants** is an urban manifestation.

116.s: Which of the following has contributed to the persistence of casteism in electoral politics?
o: Prohibition of caste associations from acting as pressure groups
Complete separation of elections from social identities
Decline of caste-based vote banks and caste associations
Political mobilisation through caste-based vote banks and caste politics
116.x: Caste-based vote banks and caste politics have increased, and caste associations may act as pressure groups in electoral politics.
116.tq: Identify the causal factor rather than an absolute reversal of the trend.
xs: **Political mobilisation through caste-based vote banks and caste politics** keeps casteism alive — so option **(4)** is correct.
Caste-based vote banks have **increased**, and caste associations act as **pressure groups**.
xa: Origin of caste in electoral politics: **Minto-Morley Reforms, 1909** (separate electorates).
**Samajwadi Party** and **RJD** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.
**Rajni Kothari**: politics **politicises** caste.
TN: **Gounders, Mukkulathors and Vanniyars** used caste solidarity to enter the legislature.

116.s: Which of the following correctly describes the economic dimension of casteism?
o: Economic competition has no relationship with caste hierarchy
Dominant castes may use ritual status to monopolise land and resources, while lower castes remain dependent
SCs are predominantly large landowners and upper castes are largely landless labourers
Casteism eliminates differences in access to land and resources
116.x: Dominant castes may use ritual status to monopolise land and resources. Upper castes own land, whereas SCs are largely marginal farmers and landless labourers.
116.tq: Use the reversed comparison trap in statements about land ownership and dependence.
xs: **Dominant castes use ritual status to monopolise land and resources**, keeping lower castes dependent — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Upper castes own land**, so option (3) reverses the reality.
xa: Casteism **excludes castes from the economy** and hinders national integration.
Remedies: remove **socio-economic gaps** and give **economic-criteria welfare**.
Ambedkar: caste is a **division of labourers** — it blocks **collective bargaining**.

116.s: Which one of the following is NOT a manifestation of caste prejudice in urban areas?
o: Caste associations continuing to operate in cities
Complete disappearance of caste identity among migrants
Caste networks deciding access to informal jobs
116.x: Migrants may carry caste prejudice into cities. Caste networks, caste associations and caste stickers on vehicles may persist, so caste identity does not completely disappear.
116.tq: Find the option using an absolute claim that contradicts the limits of urban anonymity.
xs: **Complete disappearance of caste identity among migrants** is NOT a manifestation — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Migrants carry caste prejudice into cities**; caste networks decide **informal jobs**.
Caste associations and **caste stickers on vehicles** persist (UPSC).
xa: Housing: upper-caste **landlords refuse tenants**; workplace discrimination.
**Caste-based matrimonial sites** are another manifestation.
**UP** banned caste rallies and caste signboards after an **Allahabad HC** directive.

116.s: Which of the following is correctly associated with caste-based discrimination in housing and employment?
o: Exclusive access of lower castes to all urban housing
Absence of caste considerations from matrimonial platforms
Upper-caste landlords refusing tenants and discrimination at the workplace
Caste associations functioning only as religious institutions
116.x: Manifestations include refusal of tenants by upper-caste landlords, workplace discrimination and caste-based matrimonial sites.
116.tq: Combine the two settings—housing and employment—with the associated discriminatory practices.
xs: **Upper-caste landlords refusing tenants and discrimination at the workplace** is correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Caste-based matrimonial sites** are a further manifestation, so option (2) is wrong.
xa: Political manifestation: **caste-based voting** and caste associations as **pressure groups**.
Campus discrimination: **UGC (Promotion of Equity in HEIs) Regulations, 2026**.
Caste **networks** decide informal jobs in cities.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about the UGC Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions Regulations, 2026:

1. They defined caste-based discrimination as discrimination against SC, ST and OBC members.
2. The Supreme Court stayed the Regulations in the interim.
3. The case arose in the context of student suicides.
4. The case is titled Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All four statements are correct. The 2026 Regulations covered discrimination against SC, ST and OBC members, were stayed interim by the Supreme Court, and the case arose from student suicides in Abeda Salim Tadvi v. Union of India.
116.tq: Check each statement against the authority, affected groups, legal status and case name.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **UGC Regulations, 2026** defined caste-based discrimination as against **SC, ST and OBC** members.
Statement 2 correct: the **Supreme Court** stayed them in the interim.
Statements 3-4 correct: the case **Abeda Salim Tadvi v. UoI** arose from **student suicides** (8 Apr 2026).
xa: Criticism: the SC/ST/OBC-only definition **excluded general-category students**.
**Art. 15(1)**: no discrimination on grounds of caste.
National Helpline **14566** for FIRs under the Atrocities Act.

116.s: Which of the following pairs of States is associated with both more inter-caste unions and more honour killings in the indicated context?
o: Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Sikkim and Himachal Pradesh
Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala
116.x: Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala are identified as States where empowered Dalits show both more inter-caste unions and more honour killings.
116.tq: Test the complete membership of a closely related geographical list.
xs: **Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra and Kerala** show both more inter-caste unions and more honour killings — so option **(4)** is correct.
This is the **honour-killings paradox** in States with **empowered Dalits** (Aug 2025).
xa: Only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste.
**Shakti Vahini (2018)**: **safe houses** in every district + police protection for couples.
**TN** announced a safe house in each district "in line with" Shakti Vahini.

116.s: The casteist element in electoral politics in India is traced back to the:
116.x: The casteist element in electoral politics is traced to the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909, particularly their provision for separate electorates.
116.tq: Distinguish between closely associated constitutional and electoral milestones by year.
xs: The casteist element in electoral politics goes back to the **Minto-Morley Reforms, 1909** — so option **(1)** is correct.
They introduced **separate electorates**.
xa: ⚠ **Communal G.O.** = **1921** (Justice Party), not 1909.
Caste enumeration returns in **Census 2027**; **Bihar caste survey** (2022-23) cited as model.
**Samajwadi Party** and **RJD** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.

116.s: Rajni Kothari’s central observation in Caste in Indian Politics (1970) was that:
o: Politics does not just use caste; it politicises caste
Politics merely reflects caste without changing it
Caste has no role in electoral mobilisation
116.x: Rajni Kothari argued that politics does not merely use caste but also politicises it, thereby transforming caste into a political resource.
116.tq: Test the precise distinction between using a social identity and politicising it.
xs: **Rajni Kothari** held that politics **does not just use caste; it politicises caste** — so option **(1)** is correct.
His book **Caste in Indian Politics** appeared in **1970**.
xa: **Kaka Kalelkar**: casteism = "blind and supreme group loyalty".
Political manifestation: **caste-based voting** + caste associations as **pressure groups**.
Parties court caste leaders at every level (**caste arithmetic**).

116.s: Which pair of political parties grew out of backward-caste mobilisation?
o: Samajwadi Party and Rashtriya Janata Dal
Bahujan Samaj Party and Telugu Desam Party
Justice Party and Communist Party of India
Indian National Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party
116.x: The Samajwadi Party and the Rashtriya Janata Dal grew out of backward-caste mobilisation.
116.tq: Match the political parties with the social mobilisation from which they emerged.
xs: The **Samajwadi Party** and **RJD (Rashtriya Janata Dal)** grew out of backward-caste mobilisation — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Justice Party** mobilised Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas against Brahmin dominance in Andhra.
xa: TN: **Gounders, Mukkulathors and Vanniyars** used caste solidarity to enter the legislature.
Origin of caste in elections: **Minto-Morley, 1909**.
Post-**Karamchedu**, Dalits formed independent **Dalit Mahasabhas**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice Party era in Andhra:
1. It mobilised Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas against Brahmin dominance.
2. It won the Communal G.O. in 1909.
3. It laid the ground for these castes' dominance in post-independence Andhra politics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Communal G.O. was won in 1921 (1909 is the Minto-Morley Reforms). Hence '1 and 3 only'.
116.tq: Communal G.O. = 1921; separate electorates = 1909.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Justice Party** mobilised **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas** against Brahmin dominance.
Statement 2 wrong: the **Communal G.O.** was won in **1921**; **1909** is Minto-Morley.
Statement 3 correct: it laid the ground for their dominance in **post-independence Andhra politics**.
xa: AP angle: intermediate-caste (**Reddy/Kamma/Kapu**) political dominance.
**Karamchedu** massacre led Dalits to form independent **Dalit Mahasabhas**.
⚠ **Minto-Morley 1909** = separate electorates; **Communal G.O. 1921** = Justice Party.

116.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the political response of Dalits in Andhra Pradesh after the Karamchedu massacre?

1. Dalits broke from the Congress and the Communists.
2. Independent Dalit Mahasabhas were formed.
3. Katti Padma Rao and Manda Krishna Madiga were associated with this mobilisation.
4. The movement was led by the Justice Party against Brahmin dominance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
116.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the post-Karamchedu Dalit mobilisation was associated with independent Dalit Mahasabhas, not the Justice Party’s anti-Brahmin mobilisation.
116.tq: Separate two distinct Andhra political developments by identifying the correct actors and context.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
After **Karamchedu**, Dalits **broke from Congress and the Communists** and formed independent **Dalit Mahasabhas**.
Leaders: **Katti Padmarao** and **Manda Krishna Madiga**.
Statement 4 wrong: the **Justice Party** mobilised intermediate castes against **Brahmin dominance**, a different movement.
xa: Justice Party won the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
AP angle: **Reddy/Kamma/Kapu** dominance; Dalit assertion after Karamchedu.
**Gurram Jashuva** (Vinukonda, Guntur) — pioneer of **Telugu Dalit literature**.

116.s: Caste enumeration is scheduled to return in which Census?
116.x: Caste enumeration is scheduled to return in Census 2027. The 2022–23 Bihar caste survey is cited as a model for this exercise.
116.tq: Test the exact year of a current constitutional-administrative development.
xs: Caste enumeration returns in **Census 2027** — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **2022-23 Bihar caste survey** is cited as a model (9 Jul 2026).
xa: Debate: counting caste **ossifies it** or **exposes inequity**?
Census 2027 will also keep the **Census Town** definition (RGI).
Caste in electoral politics dates to **Minto-Morley, 1909**.

116.s: Under the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages, the incentive provided per couple is:
116.x: The scheme provides an incentive of ₹2.5 lakh per couple. It seeks to weaken the practice of endogamy through inter-caste marriages.
116.tq: Use direct numerical recall and distinguish closely spaced monetary figures.
xs: The **Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages** gives **₹2.5 lakh** per couple — so option **(3)** is correct.
Its aim is to **weaken endogamy**.
xa: Only about **5%** of Indian marriages are inter-caste.
**PM-DAKSH** = skilling; **Venture Capital Fund for SCs** (2 Sep 2026).
National Helpline **14566** — FIRs under the Atrocities Act.

116.s: The Supreme Court has held that choosing a spouse, including across caste lines, is protected under:
116.x: The choice of a spouse, including the choice to marry across caste, is protected as part of personal liberty under Article 21.
116.tq: Match the constitutional protection with the precise Article rather than a neighbouring fundamental right.
xs: The Supreme Court held that **choosing a spouse**, including across caste, is protected by **Article 21** — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006)**: no bar on inter-caste marriage; police must protect such couples.
xa: **Shakti Vahini (2018)**: khap interference in marriage of consenting adults is **illegal**.
**Art. 17** abolishes untouchability; **Art. 15(2)** bars denial of access to shops and public places.
⚠ **Lata Singh** = **2006**; **Shakti Vahini** = **2018**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018):
1. Khap or caste-panchayat interference in the marriage of consenting adults is illegal.
2. The Court laid down preventive, remedial and punitive measures.
3. Safe houses were directed only in metropolitan cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: safe houses were to be set up in every district, with police protection for couples. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
116.tq: Shakti Vahini: safe house in every district.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **khap/caste-panchayat** interference in marriage of consenting adults is **illegal**.
Statement 2 correct: the Court laid down **preventive, remedial and punitive** measures.
Statement 3 wrong: **safe houses** were directed in **every district**, with police protection.
xa: **Tamil Nadu** announced a safe house in each district "in line with" Shakti Vahini.
⚠ **Lata Singh** = **2006**; **Shakti Vahini** = **2018**.
Spouse choice is protected by **Art. 21**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding judicial protection of inter-caste couples:
1. Lata Singh v. State of UP was decided in 2006.
2. The Supreme Court held that there is no bar on inter-caste marriage in that case.
3. Police were directed to protect such couples.
4. The case authorised caste panchayats to settle disputes involving consenting adults.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because caste panchayats were not authorised to interfere in marriages of consenting adults.
116.tq: Locate the single reversed legal proposition among otherwise accurate case facts.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006)**: **no bar on inter-caste marriage**; **police must protect** such couples.
Statement 4 wrong: caste panchayat interference is **illegal** (**Shakti Vahini**, 2018).
xa: Shakti Vahini directed **safe houses** in every district.
Choosing a spouse is protected by **Art. 21**.
Inter-caste marriage incentive: **₹2.5 lakh** per couple.

116.s: Tamil Nadu's announcement of a safe house in each district for inter-caste couples was stated to be in line with:
o: Lata Singh v. State of UP
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India
The Protection of Civil Rights Act alone
116.x: Tamil Nadu announced a safe house in each district for inter-caste couples in line with the directions associated with Shakti Vahini v. Union of India.
116.tq: Connect a later administrative measure with the judicial precedent it follows.
xs: TN's **safe house in each district** for inter-caste couples is "in line with" **Shakti Vahini v. Union of India** — so option **(3)** is correct (30 Aug 2026).
**Shakti Vahini (2018)** directed **safe houses** in every district + police protection; **Lata Singh (2006)** only held there is no bar on inter-caste marriage.
**Satyashodhak Samaj** was Phule's 1873 body, not a court direction.
xa: Shakti Vahini laid down **preventive, remedial and punitive** measures.
TN is among States with more inter-caste unions and more **honour killings**.
**PCR Act 1955** and **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** penalise untouchability and atrocities.

116.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the suggested measures for reducing casteism?
o: Using education to change social mindsets
Encouraging politicians to use caste-based vote-bank politics
Providing welfare on economic criteria to move towards a caste-free approach
116.x: Politicians are expected to shun caste vote-bank politics, not encourage it. Removing socio-economic gaps, education and economic-criteria welfare are suggested remedial measures.
116.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated remedial measure.
xs: **Encouraging caste-based vote-bank politics** is NOT a measure — politicians should **shun** it — so option **(2)** is correct.
Measures: **remove socio-economic gaps**, use **education** to change mindsets, **economic-criteria welfare**.
xa: Support: **₹2.5 lakh** inter-caste marriage incentive; helpline **14566**.
Casteism hinders **national integration**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional safeguards against caste discrimination:
1. Article 14 embodies equality before law.
2. Article 15(1) prohibits discrimination on grounds including caste.
3. Article 15(2) prohibits denial of access to shops and public places on grounds of caste.
4. Article 17 abolishes untouchability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All four statements are correct. Articles 14, 15(1), 15(2) and 17 respectively provide the safeguards described.
116.tq: Test several closely related constitutional provisions together and select the complete combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Art. 14** = equality; **Art. 15(1)** = no discrimination on grounds of caste.
**Art. 15(2)** = no denial of access to **shops and public places**; **Art. 17** = **untouchability abolished**.
xa: **PCR Act 1955** and **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** penalise untouchability and atrocities.
Spouse choice across caste is protected by **Art. 21**.
Haldwani "**purification**" ritual after Kharge's rally was attacked as **untouchability**.

116.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 primarily provide for:
o: Promotion of inter-caste marriages through financial incentives
116.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 provide penal safeguards against untouchability and atrocities.
116.tq: Link each statute to its central legal purpose rather than its year alone.
xs: The **PCR Act 1955** and **SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** **penalise untouchability and atrocities** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Inter-caste marriage incentives come from the **Dr. Ambedkar Scheme** (**₹2.5 lakh**), not these Acts.
xa: National Helpline **14566** handles FIRs under the **Atrocities Act**.
**Art. 17** abolished untouchability.
UP's caste-rally ban **exempted PoA cases**.

116.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a support measure for Scheduled Castes?
o: National Helpline 14566 — Assistance relating to FIRs under the Atrocities Act
Venture Capital Fund for SCs — Safe houses in every district
Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi — Police protection for khap victims
116.x: National Helpline 14566 relates to FIRs under the Atrocities Act. PM-DAKSH is associated with skilling, the Venture Capital Fund supports SC entrepreneurs, and Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi supports SC students studying abroad.
116.tq: Start with the sure scheme-function pair and eliminate swapped institutional roles.
xs: **National Helpline 14566** — FIRs under the **Atrocities Act** — is correctly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
**PM-DAKSH** is for **skilling**; **Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi** is for SC students abroad.
**Safe houses** come from **Shakti Vahini (2018)**, not the Venture Capital Fund.
xa: **Venture Capital Fund for SCs** (2 Sep 2026).
AP's Vidya Nidhi: **₹36 crore** (2024-25).
Inter-caste marriage incentive: **₹2.5 lakh** per couple.

116.s: The Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi of Andhra Pradesh is meant for:
o: Training elected representatives in social justice
All students preparing for civil services
116.x: The Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi supports SC students studying abroad. The allocation mentioned for 2024–25 was ₹36 crore.
116.tq: Identify the target beneficiary before considering the financial figure.
xs: AP's **Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi** is for **SC students pursuing education abroad** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Allocation: **₹36 crore** (2024-25).
xa: **PM-DAKSH**: skilling; **Venture Capital Fund for SCs**.
Helpline **14566**: FIRs under the Atrocities Act.
AP reformer **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu** organised **Saha Pankti Bhojanam**.

116.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gulamgiri by Jyotiba Phule?
o: It compared caste with American slavery
It described the life of Telugu Dalit communities
It was a constitutional critique published in 1936
116.x: Phule's Gulamgiri compared the caste system with American slavery. It is distinct from Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste and Periyar's Self-Respect Movement.
116.tq: Use work–author–theme matching and avoid assigning a famous work to a neighbouring thinker.
xs: Phule's **Gulamgiri** **compared caste with American slavery** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Self-Respect Movement** was **Periyar**'s; **Annihilation of Caste (1936)** is Ambedkar's; Telugu Dalit literature is **Gurram Jashuva**'s field.
xa: Phule founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** and the **first girls' school (1848)**.
Born **11 Apr 1827**, Pune (Mali caste); title '**Mahatma**' in **1888**.
⚠ **1888** = Phule's 'Mahatma' title AND Narayana Guru's **Aruvippuram** consecration.

116.s:
Arrange the following events associated with Jyotiba Phule in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the first girls' school
B. Formation of the Satyashodhak Samaj
C. Conferment of the title 'Mahatma'
D. 200th birth anniversary
116.x: The correct sequence is 1848, 1873, 1888 and 2026: first girls' school, Satyashodhak Samaj, title 'Mahatma' and 200th birth anniversary.
116.tq: Arrange by the four stated years, using the first and last events as anchors.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**First girls' school (1848)** → **Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)** → title '**Mahatma' (1888)** → **200th birth anniversary (11 Apr 2026)**.
xa: Phule was born **11 Apr 1827** at **Pune** (Mali caste).
His **Gulamgiri** compared caste with **American slavery**.
⚠ **1888** is also Narayana Guru's **Aruvippuram** Shiva consecration.

116.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with B.R. Ambedkar?
116.x: Annihilation of Caste was associated with B.R. Ambedkar and was published in 1936. The other works or organisations belong to Phule, Jashuva and Periyar respectively.
116.tq: Separate the works and dates of four anti-caste thinkers instead of relying on the common theme.
xs: **Annihilation of Caste — 1936** is Ambedkar's — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Satyashodhak Samaj** is Phule's (**1873**); **Gabbilam (1941)** is Jashuva's; **Self-Respect Movement (1925)** is Periyar's.
xa: Ambedkar also wrote **Who Were the Shudras?** and **Mooknayak**.
He founded the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**.
Embraced **Buddhism**, **14 Oct 1956**, **Nagpur**.

116.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with B.R. Ambedkar?
116.x: B.R. Ambedkar established the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924. Mooknayak is also associated with Ambedkar, but the stated pairing with 1956 is incorrect; Gabbilam belongs to Jashuva and Satyashodhak Samaj to Phule.
116.tq: Catch the wrong year attached to a familiar organisation or publication.
xs: **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — 1924** is Ambedkar's — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1956** is his conversion to Buddhism, not Mooknayak; **Gabbilam** is Jashuva's (**1941**); **Satyashodhak Samaj** is Phule's (**1873**).
xa: Ambedkar's **Annihilation of Caste** = **1936**.
⚠ **1924** is also **Vaikom Satyagraha** (Periyar jailed).
Ambedkar: caste is a "**division of labourers**".

116.s: B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism on 14 October 1956 at:
116.x: Ambedkar embraced Buddhism on 14 October 1956 at Nagpur. The other places are associated with different reformers or events.
116.tq: Test a date–place pair and reject locations belonging to other thinkers.
xs: Ambedkar embraced **Buddhism** on **14 Oct 1956** at **Nagpur** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Pune** is Phule's birthplace; **Aruvippuram** is Narayana Guru's consecration site; **Vinukonda** is Jashuva's birthplace.
xa: Ambedkar founded the **Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)**.
**Annihilation of Caste (1936)**; Who Were the Shudras?; **Mooknayak**.
Caste splits the working class and **blocks collective bargaining**.

116.s:
Periyar E.V. Ramasamy is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Self-Respect Movement
2. Self-respect marriages without Brahmin priests
3. Participation in the Vaikom Satyagraha
4. Jailed in 1924 in connection with the Vaikom Satyagraha
Which of the statements given above are correct?
116.x: All four statements are correct. Periyar led the Self-Respect Movement from 1925, supported self-respect marriages without Brahmin priests and was jailed during the Vaikom Satyagraha in 1924.
116.tq: Combine movement, social practice, event and date to distinguish Periyar from other reformers.
xs: All four statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement (1925)** and promoted **self-respect marriages without Brahmin priests**.
He took part in the **Vaikom Satyagraha** and was **jailed in 1924**.
xa: ⚠ **Vaikom (1924)** = Periyar jailed; **Self-Respect Movement** = **1925**.
**Jyotiba Phule**'s **Satyashodhak Samaj** dates to **1873**.
**Sree Narayana Guru**: "**One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man**".

116.s:
Consider the following statements about Gurram Jashuva:
1. He was born in 1895 at Vinukonda, Guntur.
2. He wrote Gulamgiri, comparing caste with American slavery.
3. He was called 'Ubhaya Bhasha Praveena' and is a pioneer of Telugu Dalit literature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Gulamgiri is Jyotiba Phule's work; Jashuva wrote Gabbilam (1941), Firadausi and Kristu Charitra. Hence '1 and 3 only'.
116.tq: Gabbilam = Jashuva; Gulamgiri = Phule.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Gurram Jashuva** was born in **1895** at **Vinukonda, Guntur**.
Statement 2 wrong: **Gulamgiri** is **Jyotiba Phule**'s work.
Statement 3 correct: he was "**Ubhaya Bhasha Praveena**", pioneer of **Telugu Dalit literature**.
xa: Jashuva's works: **Gabbilam (1941)**, **Firadausi**, **Kristu Charitra**.
AP reformer **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu**: **Saha Pankti Bhojanam**.
Post-Karamchedu Dalit leaders: **Katti Padmarao**, **Manda Krishna Madiga**.

116.s: Which of the following is NOT a work associated with Gurram Jashuva?
116.x: Annihilation of Caste is associated with B.R. Ambedkar. Gabbilam, Firadausi and Kristu Charitra are works associated with Gurram Jashuva.
116.tq: Find the work belonging to another thinker in a list of familiar titles.
xs: **Annihilation of Caste** is **B.R. Ambedkar**'s (**1936**), not Jashuva's — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Gabbilam (1941)**, **Kristu Charitra** and **Firadausi** are Jashuva's works.
xa: Jashuva: born **1895**, **Vinukonda** (Guntur); "**Ubhaya Bhasha Praveena**".
He is a pioneer of **Telugu Dalit literature**.
**Gulamgiri** = **Phule**.

116.s:
Consider the following statements about Sree Narayana Guru:
1. He launched the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.
2. He performed the Aruvippuram Shiva consecration in 1888.
3. He gave the message 'One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
116.x: Statement 1 is wrong: the Self-Respect Movement (1925) was Periyar's. Statements 2 and 3 are correct; he is also linked with the SNDP Yogam. Hence '2 and 3 only'.
116.tq: Self-Respect Movement = Periyar, not Narayana Guru.
xs: Statements **2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 wrong: the **Self-Respect Movement (1925)** was **Periyar**'s.
Statement 2 correct: **Aruvippuram Shiva consecration** in **1888**.
Statement 3 correct: "**One Caste, One Religion, One God for Man**".
xa: He is linked with the **SNDP Yogam**.
⚠ **1888** is also Phule's '**Mahatma**' title.
**Periyar** was jailed in the **Vaikom Satyagraha (1924)**.

116.s: Saha Pankti Bhojanam, meaning inter-caste dining, was organised in Andhra Pradesh by:
116.x: AP reformer Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu organised Saha Pankti Bhojanam as an initiative promoting inter-caste dining.
116.tq: Identify the regional reformer by the specific social reform activity.
xs: **Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu** organised **Saha Pankti Bhojanam** (inter-caste dining) in AP — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Sree Narayana Guru** worked in Kerala (**Aruvippuram**); **Periyar** led the **Self-Respect Movement**; **Gurram Jashuva** was a poet (**Gabbilam**).
xa: Jashuva is a pioneer of **Telugu Dalit literature**.
Justice Party won the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
AP: **Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi** (**₹36 crore**, 2024-25).

116.s: With reference to the reported ban on caste rallies and caste signboards in Uttar Pradesh, which statement is correct?
o: Only inter-caste marriage rallies were banned, while caste signboards were permitted.
The ban was issued by the Supreme Court and covered PoA cases without exception.
The ban was introduced by Tamil Nadu as part of its safe-house policy.
The ban followed an Allahabad High Court directive, while PoA cases were exempt.
116.x: Uttar Pradesh banned caste rallies and caste signboards after an Allahabad High Court directive. Cases under the Prevention of Atrocities Act were exempt.
116.tq: Separate the issuing context, geographical jurisdiction and statutory exception.
xs: **UP** banned caste rallies and caste signboards after an **Allahabad HC directive**, with **PoA cases exempt** — so option **(4)** is correct (Sep 2025).
Tamil Nadu's policy is **safe houses** for inter-caste couples, not a rally ban.
xa: Haldwani (**Uttarakhand**) "**purification**" ritual after Kharge's rally was attacked as **untouchability**.
**SC/ST (PoA) Act 1989** penalises atrocities.
Caste **stickers on vehicles** persist in cities.

116.s: Which of the following best expresses the stated significance of casteism for Indian society and the economy?
o: It eliminates socio-economic gaps through hereditary occupations.
It affects only electoral representation and not economic participation.
It hinders national integration and excludes castes from the economy.
It strengthens national integration by preserving social identities.
116.x: Casteism is significant because it hinders national integration and excludes castes from participation in the economy.
116.tq: Choose the option that captures both the social and economic consequences.
xs: Casteism **hinders national integration and excludes castes from the economy** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Dominant castes **monopolise land and resources**, keeping lower castes dependent.
xa: It produces **discrimination, conflict and vote-bank politics**.
Remedies: **remove socio-economic gaps**; **economic-criteria welfare**.
Ambedkar: caste **blocks collective bargaining**.

116.s: The debate over counting caste in the Census centres on whether it would:
o: Abolish caste distinctions immediately or create reservations automatically
End all caste-based political mobilisation or prohibit caste associations
Replace the Constitution or remove Article 17
Ossify caste identities or expose existing inequity
116.x: The debate is whether caste enumeration would ossify caste identities or instead expose existing inequities for corrective policy.
116.tq: Identify both sides of a policy debate rather than selecting an extreme consequence.
xs: The debate is whether counting caste in the Census would **ossify caste or expose inequity** — so option **(4)** is correct (9 Jul 2026).
Caste enumeration returns in **Census 2027**.
xa: The **2022-23 Bihar caste survey** is cited as a model.
**Rajni Kothari**: politics **politicises** caste.
Article **17** abolished untouchability.

116.s: The criticism of the UGC's definition restricted to SC, ST and OBC categories was that it:
116.x: The UGC's SC/ST/OBC-only definition was criticised for excluding students belonging to the general category.
116.tq: Match the criticised classification with the group left outside it.
xs: The UGC's **SC/ST/OBC-only** definition was criticised for **excluding general-category students** — so option **(3)** is correct (8 Apr 2026).
The **UGC (Promotion of Equity in HEIs) Regulations, 2026** were **stayed** by the Supreme Court in the interim.
xa: Case: **Abeda Salim Tadvi v. UoI**, arising from **student suicides**.
**Art. 15(1)**: no discrimination on grounds of caste.
Counting caste in the Census: **ossify** or **expose inequity**?

116.s: Which of the following correctly reflects the Andhra Pradesh angle concerning caste politics?
o: Caste politics being confined to urban local bodies without social movements
Dominance exclusively of Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh politics
Complete disappearance of intermediate-caste political influence after Karamchedu
Political dominance of intermediate castes such as Reddy, Kamma and Kapu, and Dalit assertion after Karamchedu
116.x: The AP angle includes the political dominance of intermediate castes such as Reddy, Kamma and Kapu, along with Dalit assertion after Karamchedu.
116.tq: Select the option containing both linked regional dimensions rather than an absolute claim.
xs: AP angle: **intermediate-caste (Reddy, Kamma, Kapu) political dominance** and **Dalit assertion after Karamchedu** — so option **(4)** is correct.
After **Karamchedu**, Dalits broke from Congress and Communists to form **Dalit Mahasabhas**.
xa: The **Justice Party** mobilised **Reddys, Kammas, Kapus and Velamas** against Brahmin dominance.
It won the **Communal G.O. (1921)**.
Leaders: **Katti Padmarao**, **Manda Krishna Madiga**.

117.s: Which scholar defined communalism as the belief that a group following a particular religion also has common social, political and economic interests?
117.x: Bipan Chandra defined communalism as the belief that followers of a particular religion have common social, political and economic interests.
117.tq: Use scholar-definition matching and distinguish closely related formulations.
xs: **Bipan Chandra** defined communalism as the belief that a religious group also has **common social, political and economic interests** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Ram Ahuja** saw interests that **differ and often oppose**; **T.K. Oommen** gave **six dimensions**; **Asghar Ali Engineer** is a scholar of communal harmony.
xa: Bipan Chandra also gave the **three stages**: communal nationalism → liberal → extreme communalism.
⚠ **T.K. Oommen** = six dimensions; **Bipan Chandra** = three stages.
**Melson and Wolpe**: "political assertiveness of a community" (APPSC-G2 2025).

117.s: Ram Ahuja described communalism as which of the following?
o: An ideology that society is divided into religious communities whose interests differ and often oppose each other
A movement for the complete separation of religion from politics
A constitutional arrangement providing separate electorates to minorities
A process through which all religious communities assimilate into one nation
117.x: Ram Ahuja viewed communalism as an ideology in which religious communities are considered to have differing and often opposing interests. He also associated communal persons with practising politics through religion.
117.tq: Match the precise definition with its scholar rather than selecting a related institutional concept.
xs: **Ram Ahuja**: communalism is an **ideology that society is divided into religious communities whose interests differ and often oppose** each other — so option **(1)** is correct.
"**Communal persons**" practise **politics through religion**.
Separate electorates are a colonial device (**1909** Act), not Ahuja's definition.
xa: **Bipan Chandra**: a religious group has **common social, political and economic interests**.
**Melson and Wolpe**: political assertiveness of a community in a **plural society undergoing modernisation**.
**Asghar Ali Engineer** wrote **Communalism in India**.

117.s:
With reference to communalism, consider the following statements:
1. T.K. Oommen identified six dimensions of communalism.
2. The dimensions range from assimilationist to secessionist.
3. Asghar Ali Engineer is associated with the study of communal harmony.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements are correct. T.K. Oommen identified six dimensions ranging from assimilationist to secessionist, while Asghar Ali Engineer is a leading scholar of communalism and communal harmony.
117.tq: Check each scholar-feature pair independently before choosing the coded combination.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
Statements 1-2 correct: **T.K. Oommen** gave **six dimensions**, from **assimilationist to secessionist**.
Statement 3 correct: **Asghar Ali Engineer** is a leading scholar of **communalism and communal harmony**.
xa: Six dimensions: assimilationist, welfarist, retreatist, **retaliatory**, **separatist**, **secessionist**.
⚠ **Separatist** = state **within** India (Gorkhaland, Bodoland); **secessionist** = state **outside** India (Khalistan).
⚠ **Bipan Chandra** = three stages, not six dimensions.

117.s: In the Indian context, communalism is most commonly perceived as
o: the peaceful coexistence of religious communities within a nation
religious differences between groups leading to tension and rioting
economic competition between regions without religious implications
the constitutional recognition of linguistic minorities
117.x: In India, communalism is commonly understood as religious differences between groups that generate tension and rioting, often when one group promotes its interests at the expense of others.
117.tq: Identify the central meaning rather than confusing communalism with diversity or minority protection.
xs: In India communalism is most often seen as **religious differences between groups leading to tension and rioting** — so option **(2)** is correct.
A group promotes its interests **at the expense of others**.
xa: Communalism is **always relational** — "us vs them".
Hindu-Muslim communalism = **single largest threat** to secular ideals.
**1906** = first communal party (**Muslim League**); **1909** Act = first legal separate electorate.

117.s: Communalism has been defined as "the political assertiveness of a community to maintain its identity in a plural society undergoing modernisation". This definition is given by:
117.x: The definition is by Robert Melson and Howard Wolpe (asked in APPSC-G2 2025). Bipan Chandra defined communalism as the belief that followers of one religion share common social, political and economic interests. Ram Ahuja saw it as an ideology of religious communities with differing, often opposing, interests. T.K. Oommen gave its six dimensions.
117.tq: 'Political assertiveness... plural society' = Melson & Wolpe.
xs: "**Political assertiveness of a community** to maintain its identity in a plural society undergoing modernisation" is by **Robert Melson and Howard Wolpe** — so option **(2)** is correct (**APPSC-G2 2025**).
**Bipan Chandra**: a religious group has **common social, political and economic interests**.
**Ram Ahuja**: communities with interests that **differ and often oppose**; **T.K. Oommen**: **six dimensions**.
xa: Bipan Chandra also gave **three stages** of communalism.
**Asghar Ali Engineer**: leading scholar of communal harmony.
Exam angle: **definition → scholar** matching.

117.s: Which one of the following best distinguishes religious fundamentalism from communalism?
o: Fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal and seeks a return to literal scripture, whereas communalism politically mobilises religious identity against other communities.
Fundamentalism is always directed against another community, whereas communalism reforms one's own community.
Communalism is concerned only with religious doctrine and is unrelated to power or resources.
Fundamentalism and communalism both necessarily involve inter-group conflict.
117.x: Religious fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal, emphasising a return to fundamentals and literal scripture. Communalism is political mobilisation of religious identity against other communities to seek power and resources.
117.tq: Discriminate between look-alike concepts by comparing their direction, objective and method.
xs: **Fundamentalism** is mainly **doctrinal** (return to literal scripture); **communalism** is **political mobilisation of religious identity against other communities** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Fundamentalism is aimed at **reforming one's own community**; communalism at **other communities**, seeking power and resources.
Fundamentalism **can exist without inter-group conflict**, so option (4) is wrong.
xa: Communalism is **always relational** — "us vs them".
Fundamentalism is often **anti-modern**.
**Political** communalism uses religion for **votes**.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding religious fundamentalism and communalism:
1. Religious fundamentalism is often directed at reforming one's own community.
2. Communalism is always relational and constructs an “us versus them” relationship.
3. Religious fundamentalism cannot exist without inter-group conflict.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Fundamentalism can exist without inter-group conflict; therefore, statement 3 is false.
117.tq: Find the statement that reverses the essential distinction, especially the absolute word “cannot”.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: fundamentalism is directed at **reforming one's own community** (often anti-modern).
Statement 2 correct: communalism is **always relational** — "**us vs them**".
Statement 3 wrong: fundamentalism **can exist without inter-group conflict**.
xa: Fundamentalism = return to "**fundamentals**" and literal scripture.
Communalism seeks **power and resources**.
**Ram Ahuja**: "communal persons" practise politics through religion.

117.s:
Assertion (A): Communalism is always relational in character.
Reason (R): Communalism mobilises the identity of one religious community against other communities in the pursuit of power and resources.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
117.x: Both statements are true, and the mobilisation of one community against others explains why communalism necessarily has an “us versus them” or relational character.
117.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the defining relational feature in the assertion.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A true: communalism is **always relational** ("us vs them").
R true and the reason: it **mobilises religious identity against other communities** to seek **power and resources**.
xa: Fundamentalism, by contrast, **can exist without inter-group conflict**.
**Retaliatory** communalism attempts to **harm members of other communities** (riots, revenge cycles).
Indian perception: religious differences → **tension and rioting**.

117.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the assimilationist dimension of communalism?
o: A community works exclusively for the welfare of its own members
A community keeps away from political activity
A small religious group seeks an independent state outside India
A small religious group is absorbed into a larger religious community
117.x: Assimilationist communalism involves the absorption of smaller religious groups into a larger one, as illustrated by claims that STs, Jains, Sikhs and Buddhists are Hindus.
117.tq: Match the exact definition with the dimension instead of being distracted by neighbouring forms.
xs: **Assimilationist** communalism = **a small religious group absorbed into a larger one** — so option **(4)** is correct.
Example: claiming **STs, Jains, Sikhs, Buddhists** are Hindus.
Own-welfare = **welfarist**; keeping away from politics = **retreatist**; independent state outside India = **secessionist**.
xa: Six dimensions by **T.K. Oommen** (CDX prints "T.R. Oommen").
**Retaliatory** = attempts to harm other communities (riots).
**Separatist** = state **within** India (Gorkhaland, Bodoland).

117.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Dimension of communalism — Illustration
1. Welfarist — Christian or Parsi associations
2. Retreatist — Bahai community
3. Separatist — Gorkhaland or Bodoland
4. Secessionist — Khalistan or “Azad Kashmir”

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
117.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Welfarist communalism serves one community, retreatist groups avoid politics, separatists seek a territorial state within India, and secessionists seek an independent state outside India.
117.tq: Check each definition–example pair independently; the comprehensive combination is valid when no pair is reversed.
xs: All four pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Welfarist** — Christian or Parsi associations; **retreatist** — **Bahai** community.
**Separatist** — **Gorkhaland, Bodoland** (state **within** India); **secessionist** — **Khalistan**, "Azad Kashmir" (state **outside** India).
xa: **Assimilationist** = small groups absorbed into a larger one.
**Retaliatory** = riots, revenge cycles.
Dimensions given by **T.K. Oommen** (source: CDX pp.38-39; UPSC p.79).

117.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Welfarist communalism — using religion for votes
Retaliatory communalism — attempts to harm members of other communities
Separatist communalism — keeping away from politics
Retreatist communalism — seeking an independent state outside India
117.x: B is right: retaliatory communalism attempts to harm members of other communities (riots, revenge cycles). A is wrong: welfarist communalism works for one community's welfare; using religion for votes is political communalism. C is wrong: keeping away from politics is retreatist. D is wrong: seeking an independent state outside India is secessionist.
117.tq: Use the wrong-person/wrong-definition trap by distinguishing closely related dimensions.
xs: **Retaliatory communalism — attempts to harm members of other communities** is correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Using religion for votes is **political** communalism, not welfarist.
Keeping away from politics is **retreatist**; an independent state outside India is **secessionist**.
xa: **Welfarist** = welfare of one community only (Christian or Parsi associations).
**Retreatist** example: **Bahai** community.
**Separatist** = state within India (Gorkhaland, Bodoland).

117.s:
With reference to the forms of communalism, consider the following statements:
1. Political communalism uses religion for securing votes.
2. Economic communalism grows from competition for jobs and resources.
3. Social communalism builds prejudice and social distance.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: All three statements are correct. The political, economic and social forms respectively concern electoral mobilisation, competition over opportunities and resources, and prejudice or social distance.
117.tq: Separate the political, economic and social dimensions by identifying their distinct causes and effects.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Political** form uses religion for **votes**; **economic** form grows from **competition for jobs and resources**.
**Social** form builds **prejudice and social distance**.
xa: Economic causes: **poverty, unemployment, lopsided development**, relative deprivation.
Social/media causes: **fake news** and hate messages on social media.
Political causes: **vote-bank** and identity politics; religion-based parties.

117.s:
Arrange the following stages of communalism identified by Bipan Chandra in the correct order:
A. Extreme communalism
B. Communal nationalism
C. Liberal communalism
117.x: Bipan Chandra’s sequence is communal nationalism, liberal communalism and extreme communalism.
117.tq: Use the progression from a nationalist outlook to antagonism and violence.
xs: Order **B, C, A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Communal nationalism** → **liberal communalism** → **extreme communalism** (Bipan Chandra).
xa: Stage 1: common **secular** interests, still nationalist.
Stage 2: interests **different** but reconcilable within one nation.
Stage 3: **mutually antagonistic** — politics of **fear, hatred and violence**.
After the **1937** elections the Muslim League turned to extreme communalism.

117.s:
Consider the following statements about Bipan Chandra's stages of communalism:
1. In communal nationalism, followers of one religion are believed to share common secular interests while remaining nationalist in outlook.
2. In liberal communalism, the interests of different communities are seen as mutually antagonistic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
117.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: in liberal communalism interests are different but reconcilable within one nation; 'mutually antagonistic' marks extreme communalism. Hence '1 only'.
117.tq: Different but reconcilable = liberal; antagonistic = extreme.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: in **communal nationalism**, believers share common **secular** interests and stay **nationalist** in outlook.
Statement 2 wrong: in **liberal communalism** interests are **different but reconcilable**; "**mutually antagonistic**" marks **extreme** communalism.
xa: Extreme communalism = politics of **fear, hatred and violence**.
Muslim League turned extreme after the **1937** elections; echoed by **Hindu Mahasabha** and **RSS**.
⚠ **Bipan Chandra** = three stages; **Oommen** = six dimensions.

117.s:
Consider the following statements regarding extreme communalism:
1. It views the interests of religious communities as mutually antagonistic.
2. It is associated with politics of fear, hatred and violence.
3. It necessarily preserves a common nationalist outlook among all communities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
117.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Extreme communalism treats community interests as mutually antagonistic and is expressed through fear, hatred and violence; statement 3 is incorrect.
117.tq: Find the statement that reverses the defining feature of the extreme stage.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
Extreme communalism sees interests as **mutually antagonistic** and works through **fear, hatred and violence**.
Statement 3 wrong: a **nationalist outlook** belongs to stage 1, **communal nationalism**.
xa: After **1937**, the **Muslim League** turned to extreme communalism.
This was echoed by the **Hindu Mahasabha and RSS** (UPSC Modern History p.300).
Liberal communalism: interests **different** but reconcilable.

117.s: After the elections of 1937, the Muslim League turned towards extreme communalism based mainly on
o: cooperation with the Congress on joint electorates
117.x: After the 1937 elections, the Muslim League adopted extreme communalism based on fear, hatred and violence. This approach was echoed by the Hindu Mahasabha and the RSS.
117.tq: Link the political turning point with its stated ideological characteristics.
xs: After the **1937** elections the Muslim League turned to extreme communalism "based on **fear, hatred and violence**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was echoed by the **Hindu Mahasabha and RSS**.
xa: Extreme communalism sees interests as **mutually antagonistic** (Bipan Chandra's stage 3).
**Lahore ("Pakistan") Resolution** followed on **24 Mar 1940**.
**Allama Iqbal** proposed a consolidated Muslim state in **1930**.

117.s: Which one of the following is NOT a historical or colonial cause of communalism listed in the context of India?
o: Recording caste and religion in the first census
117.x: Relative deprivation is an economic cause. British divide-and-rule policies, separate electorates, the recording of caste and religion in the first census, and revivalist movements are historical or colonial causes.
117.tq: Classify each option by cause-category and identify the misplaced item.
xs: **Relative deprivation** is an **economic** cause, not historical/colonial — so option **(4)** is correct.
Historical/colonial causes: **divide and rule**, **separate electorates**, caste and religion in the **first census (1871-72)**, **revivalist movements**.
xa: Economic causes: **poverty, unemployment, lopsided development**, relative deprivation.
Legal/administrative: **delayed justice**, lenient punishment, police inaction, biased intelligence.
1920s: **Shuddhi and Sangathan** (Arya Samaj) vs **Tabligh and Tanzim** (Muslim).

117.s: The first census in which caste and religion were recorded, contributing to communal consciousness, was conducted in
117.x: The recording of caste and religion in the first census of 1871-72 is identified as a historical or colonial factor contributing to communalism.
117.tq: Retain the exact census range and reject nearby-looking dates.
xs: Caste and religion were recorded in the **first census (1871-72)** — so option **(2)** is correct.
It is listed among the **historical/colonial** causes of communalism.
xa: Other colonial causes: British **divide and rule**, **separate electorates**, **revivalist movements**.
**1909** Act = first legal separate electorate.
**1905 Partition of Bengal**: Muslim-majority East, Hindu-majority West.

117.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Legal-administrative causes — biased intelligence
2. Social and media causes — media amplification of communal narratives
3. Psychological and international causes — foreign funding
4. Political causes — revivalist movements
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
117.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Revivalist movements are listed under historical or colonial causes, not political causes, so pair 4 is incorrect.
117.tq: Use category boundaries to detect the single misplaced cause.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Biased intelligence** = legal/administrative; **media amplification** = social/media; **foreign funding** = psychological/international.
Pair 4 wrong: **revivalist movements** are a **historical/colonial** cause; political causes are **vote-bank** politics and religion-based parties.
xa: Revivalist movements fed communal sentiment in the **19th century**.
Economic causes: **poverty, unemployment, lopsided development**.
Psychological causes include **prejudices and rumours**.

117.s: In the 1920s, which pair of movements represented contrasting mobilisation efforts among Hindus and Muslims respectively?
o: Swadeshi and Home Rule; Khilafat and Non-Cooperation
Shuddhi and Sangathan; Tabligh and Tanzim
Tabligh and Tanzim; Shuddhi and Sangathan
Brahmo and Arya Samaj; Aligarh and Deoband
117.x: The Arya Samaj promoted Shuddhi and Sangathan, while Muslim organisations promoted Tabligh and Tanzim in the 1920s.
117.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed religious mobilisation movements by community association.
xs: **Shuddhi and Sangathan** (Arya Samaj, Hindu) vs **Tabligh and Tanzim** (Muslim) — so option **(2)** is correct.
Option (3) reverses the two.
xa: ⚠ **Shuddhi and Sangathan** = Arya Samaj; **Tabligh and Tanzim** = Muslim.
**Hindu Mahasabha** founded **1915** (Maharaja of **Kasim Bazar**).
Revivalist movements are a **historical/colonial** cause.

117.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Cause category)
 a. Historical/colonial
 b. Political
 c. Economic
 d. Legal/administrative

List-II (Example)
 i. Vote-bank politics
 ii. Poverty
 iii. Separate electorates
 iv. Delayed justice

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
117.x: Separate electorates are historical or colonial; vote-bank politics is political; poverty is economic; and delayed justice is legal-administrative.
117.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing category swaps.
xs: **a–iii, b–i, c–ii, d–iv** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**Separate electorates** = historical/colonial; **vote-bank politics** = political.
**Poverty** = economic; **delayed justice** = legal/administrative.
xa: Social/media causes: **fake news** and hate messages on social media.
Psychological/international: prejudices, rumours, **foreign funding**.
Caste and religion first recorded in the **1871-72** census.

117.s: The All-India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dacca primarily to:
117.x: The Muslim League was founded at Dacca in 1906 to safeguard Muslim political interests.
117.tq: Link an organisation with its stated political objective.
xs: The **Muslim League** was founded at **Dacca** in **1906** to **guard Muslim political interests** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was founded under the **Aga Khan** and **Nawab Salimullah of Dacca**.
xa: It is the **first communal political party** (**1906**).
The **Simla Deputation** (Oct 1906) to **Lord Minto** demanded **separate electorates**.
**1909** Act = first legal separate electorate.

117.s: Who among the following were associated with the founding of the All-India Muslim League at Dacca in 1906?
o: Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca
117.x: The Muslim League was founded at Dacca under the leadership of Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca.
117.tq: Use the founder–organisation association rather than the later reform association.
xs: The Muslim League was founded under the **Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah of Dacca** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Minto** received the Simla Deputation; he did not found the League.
xa: The **Aga Khan** led the **Simla Deputation** (Oct 1906).
Lord **Minto** = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**".
⚠ **1906** = Muslim League; **1909** = first legal separate electorate.

117.s: The Simla Deputation to Lord Minto, which preceded the formation of the Muslim League, took place in:
117.x: The Simla Deputation to Minto took place in October 1906, before the Muslim League was founded later in 1906.
117.tq: Separate closely related events by their month and year.
xs: The **Simla Deputation** to **Lord Minto** was in **October 1906** — so option **(2)** is correct.
Led by the **Aga Khan**, it demanded **separate electorates**.
xa: The **Muslim League** was founded later in **1906** at **Dacca**.
**1905**: Partition of Bengal; **1909** Act: first legal separate electorate.
Minto = "**Father of the Communal Electorate**".

117.s: Who is known as the “Father of the Communal Electorate” in British India?
117.x: Lord Minto is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate because the reforms associated with him introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
117.tq: Use the person–policy association and distinguish Minto from other Viceroys.
xs: **Lord Minto** is the "**Father of the Communal Electorate**" — so option **(3)** is correct.
He received the **Simla Deputation (1906)** demanding separate electorates; the **1909** Act gave the first legal separate electorate.
xa: ⚠ Ideological father of the two-nation theory = **Syed Ahmad Khan**.
**Ramsay MacDonald** gave the **Communal Award (1932)**.
**Lord Dufferin** used Syed Ahmad Khan in **1887** to keep Muslims from Congress.

117.s: Who used Syed Ahmad Khan to keep Muslims away from the Congress in 1887?
117.x: Lord Dufferin used Syed Ahmad Khan in 1887 to keep Muslims away from the Congress.
117.tq: Match the colonial official with the specific political action and year.
xs: **Lord Dufferin** used **Syed Ahmad Khan** in **1887** to keep Muslims away from Congress — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Lord Minto** is linked with the **Simla Deputation (1906)** and separate electorates.
xa: Syed Ahmad Khan = **ideological father** of the **two-nation theory** (Hindi-Urdu controversy).
He advised Muslims to **stay out of Congress**.
**Allama Iqbal** proposed a consolidated Muslim state (**1930**).

117.s: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 created which of the following demographic arrangements?
o: A Muslim-majority West Bengal and Hindu-majority East Bengal
Two Hindu-majority provinces with no communal distinction
A Muslim-majority East Bengal and Hindu-majority West Bengal
Two Muslim-majority provinces under a single legislature
117.x: The 1905 Partition of Bengal created a Muslim-majority East Bengal and a Hindu-majority West Bengal.
117.tq: Use the location and majority-community pair together to avoid reversal.
xs: The **1905 Partition of Bengal** created a **Muslim-majority East Bengal and Hindu-majority West Bengal** — so option **(3)** is correct.
Option (1) reverses the two halves.
xa: Next year (**1906**): Simla Deputation and founding of the **Muslim League** at **Dacca**.
**1909** Act: first legal separate electorate.
British **divide and rule** is a historical/colonial cause of communalism.

117.s: The All India Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 under the aegis of the
117.x: The All India Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 under the aegis of the Maharaja of Kasim Bazar. It was also associated with Madan Mohan Malaviya.
117.tq: Use the founder-patron association rather than a prominent associated leader.
xs: The **All India Hindu Mahasabha** was founded in **1915** under the aegis of the **Maharaja of Kasim Bazar** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **Aga Khan** and the **Nawab of Dacca** are linked with the **Muslim League (1906)**.
xa: The Mahasabha is associated with **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
After **1937**, Hindu Mahasabha and RSS echoed the League's extreme communalism.
1920s: Arya Samaj **Shuddhi and Sangathan**.

117.s: Which one of the following is the principal criticism of the Lucknow Pact?
o: It legitimised communal electorates despite producing short-term unity.
It abolished the demand for self-government.
It ended all cooperation between Congress and the Muslim League.
It prevented the reunion of Moderates and Extremists.
117.x: Although the Pact promoted short-term Hindu-Muslim and Congress-League unity, it also legitimised communal electorates.
117.tq: Select the critical assessment that contains both the immediate benefit and the long-term drawback.
xs: The **Lucknow Pact** gave short-term unity but **legitimised communal electorates** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Congress **accepted separate electorates and weightage**, which laid **groundwork for Partition**.
xa: **1909** Act = first legal separate electorate.
**Communal Award (1932)**: separate electorates for Muslims, Sikhs, Christians + **Depressed Classes**.
**Lahore Resolution**: **24 Mar 1940**.

117.s: The Communal Award was based on the recommendations of the
117.x: The Communal Award of 1932 was based on the recommendations of the Lothian Committee.
117.tq: Match the constitutional award with the committee behind its recommendations.
xs: The **Communal Award** was based on the **Lothian Committee** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It was given by British PM **Ramsay MacDonald** on **16 Aug 1932**.
xa: It gave separate electorates to **Muslims, Sikhs, Christians + Depressed Classes** (for **20 years**).
The **Poona Pact (1932)** replaced Dalit separate electorates with reserved seats (**71 → 148**).
Poona Pact was signed at **Yerwada Jail**.

117.s: The Poona Pact of 1932 was concluded between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar at
117.x: The Poona Pact was concluded in 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar at Yerwada Jail.
117.tq: Distinguish the exact venue from other locations associated with the freedom movement.
xs: The **Poona Pact (1932)** between **Gandhi and Ambedkar** was concluded at **Yerwada Jail** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It replaced Dalit separate electorates with **reserved seats in joint electorates** (**71 → 148**).
xa: It followed the **Communal Award** (**16 Aug 1932**) of **Ramsay MacDonald**.
The Award was based on the **Lothian Committee**.
⚠ Communal Award separate electorates were for **20 years**.

117.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 1932 — Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award
1930 — Allama Iqbal proposed a consolidated Muslim state
117.x: A is the wrongly matched pair: Jinnah issued his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report (1928); 1940 is the year of the Lahore ('Pakistan') Resolution (24 March 1940). The Communal Award (1932, Ramsay MacDonald) and Iqbal's 1930 proposal for a consolidated Muslim state are correctly dated.
117.tq: Check the person-event-year combination and identify the swapped event.
xs: **1940 — Jinnah's Fourteen Points** is wrongly matched — so option **(1)** is correct.
