Statement 2 correct: the **Assam Movement (1979-85)** targeted **illegal immigrants**.
Statement 3 correct: it was later followed by clashes between **Bodos and Bengali-speaking Muslims**.
xa: ⚠ **Shiv Sena** = South Indians (1960s); **MNS** = North Indians (2008).
**Mulki rules** — local-residence preference in **Hyderabad/Telangana** jobs.
Anti-Hindi agitations → **two-language formula**.

119.s: The Mulki rules were primarily associated with which demand?
o: Reservation of all Central Government jobs for migrants
Preference for local residents in jobs in Hyderabad/Telangana
Separate statehood for Tamil Nadu outside the Union
119.x: The Mulki rules provided a preference for local residents in jobs in Hyderabad/Telangana and contributed to the agitations of 1969 and 1972–73.
119.tq: Connect the rule to its practical employment preference rather than to a broader secessionist claim.
xs: The **Mulki rules** gave **local-residence preference in jobs in Hyderabad/Telangana** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They led to the **1969** and **1972-73** agitations.
xa: **Telangana movements**: **1969** agitation and **2009-14** phase → statehood in **2014**.
Only **Parliament** can prescribe a residence requirement (**Art. 16(3)**).
Sons-of-the-soil doctrine: state belongs to its **main linguistic group**.

119.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Telangana movements mentioned in relation to regionalism?
o: The 1969 agitation and the 2009–14 phase eventually led to statehood in 2014.
The 1937 agitation led directly to statehood in 1965.
The movement was confined entirely to the 1960s and had no later phase.
The movement concerned only inter-State river disputes and not statehood.
119.x: The Telangana movement included the 1969 agitation and the 2009–14 phase, culminating in statehood in 2014.
119.tq: Track the two phases and the final outcome rather than treating the movement as a single-year event.
xs: The **1969** agitation and the **2009-14** phase led to **statehood in 2014** — so option **(1)** is correct.
**1937** and **1965** are anti-Hindi agitation years in **Tamil Nadu**, not Telangana.
xa: The **Mulki rules** led to the **1969** and **1972-73** agitations.
Telangana is a **separatism** case (new state inside the Union).
Women's roles in the **Telangana** and **Jharkhand** movements often go unrecognised.

119.s: The Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu are associated with which outcome?
119.x: The Anti-Hindi agitations of 1937, 1965 and 1986 in Tamil Nadu led to the two-language formula.
119.tq: Distinguish the policy outcome of the language movement from outcomes of other regional movements.
xs: TN's **anti-Hindi agitations** led to the **two-language formula** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They took place in **1937, 1965, 1986**.
The **Mulki rules** are Hyderabad's; **Chandigarh** is a capital dispute; **Greater Nagaland** is secessionist.
xa: **Dravida Nadu** (**1960s**) was a secessionist demand from the same region.
**Autonomy** demands came from TN, Punjab, AP, WB (since the 1960s).
**M.G. Ramachandran** — regional party leader of TN.

119.s:
Which of the following constitutional provisions are commonly invoked in arguing that domicile-based reservations in private employment may violate constitutional guarantees?
1. Article 14
2. Article 15
3. Article 16
4. Article 19
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19 are relevant to equality, non-discrimination, public employment and freedom of movement or occupation, respectively.
119.tq: Test the complete constitutional cluster rather than recalling only the employment-related article.
xs: All four — **Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19** — are cited against local job reservation — so option **(4)** is correct.
They protect **equality**, **non-discrimination on place of birth**, and **freedom of movement/occupation** across India.
xa: **Art. 16(2)** bars discrimination in public employment incl. **place of birth and residence**.
**Art. 16(3)**: only **Parliament** can prescribe a residence requirement.
Haryana's **75%** quota law (**2020**) was **struck down** in **Nov 2023**.

119.s: The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act was enacted in which year?
119.x: The Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act was enacted in 1957.
119.tq: Distinguish the specific statutory year from nearby constitutional and post-Constitution dates.
xs: The **Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act** was passed in **1957** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It was made under **Art. 16(3)**, which lets only **Parliament** prescribe a residence requirement.
xa: **Art. 16(2)** bars discrimination in public employment on **place of birth and residence**.
AP's **2019** Act was the **first** 75% private-job local-quota law.
**SR Act** came a year earlier, in **1956**.

119.s:
Consider the following pairs:

State law — Provision or status
1. AP Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019 — 75% reservation of private industrial jobs for locals
2. Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020 — 75% reservation of private jobs up to a salary ceiling
3. Jharkhand State Employment of Local Candidates in Private Sector Act, 2021 — 75% reservation of lower-salary private jobs

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
119.x: All three pairs are correct: AP's 2019 Act reserved 75% of private industrial jobs for locals (the first such law), Haryana's 2020 Act 75% of private jobs up to a salary ceiling (struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in Nov 2023), and Jharkhand's 2021 Act 75% of lower-salary private jobs.
119.tq: Match each law with its quota and scope before selecting the coded combination.
xs: All three pairs are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**AP 2019** — **75%** of private **industrial** jobs (first such law); **Haryana 2020** — **75%** of private jobs **up to a salary ceiling**.
**Jharkhand 2021** — **75%** of **lower-salary** private jobs.
xa: Haryana's Act was **struck down by the Punjab & Haryana High Court (Nov 2023)**.
AP's Act was **challenged in the AP High Court**.
⚠ First 75% law = **AP (2019)**; struck down = **Haryana**.

119.s: The Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020 was struck down in November 2023 by which court?
119.x: The Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down the Haryana law in November 2023 as unconstitutional.
119.tq: Discriminate between the State concerned and the court that delivered the ruling.
xs: The **Punjab and Haryana High Court** struck down Haryana's **2020** Act in **Nov 2023** — so option **(3)** is correct.
It held the law **unconstitutional**.
xa: **APPSC-G2 2025** asked which state's 75% quota was struck down — **Haryana**.
Objection: it contradicts **Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19**.

119.s: Under Article 16(3) of the Constitution, a residence requirement for employment under a State may be prescribed only by:
119.x: Article 16(3) allows only Parliament to prescribe a residence requirement (it did so through the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957). The State Legislature, Governor and State PSC have no such power; Article 16(2) otherwise bars discrimination by place of birth or residence.
119.tq: Residence requirement = Parliament only (Art. 16(3)).
xs: Under **Art. 16(3)**, only **Parliament** can prescribe a residence requirement — so option **(3)** is correct.
Parliament did so via the **Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957**.
xa: **Art. 16(2)** bars discrimination in public employment on **place of birth and residence**.
States' 75% laws: **AP 2019**, **Haryana 2020**, **Jharkhand 2021**.
**Mulki rules** were a local-residence preference in **Hyderabad/Telangana**.

119.s:
Consider the following statements about regional parties in India:
1. They rose prominently in the late 20th century.
2. They commonly demand more powers and funds for states.
3. They reduce the political diversity of Indian federalism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: regional parties rose in the late 20th century and demand more powers and funds for states. Statement 3 is wrong: they represent state interests and add political diversity to Indian federalism. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
119.tq: Regional parties add diversity; they do not reduce it.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: regional parties rose in the **late 20th century**.
Statement 2 correct: they demand **more powers and funds** for states.
Statement 3 wrong: they **add political diversity** to Indian federalism.
xa: Leaders: **M.G. Ramachandran** (TN), **N.T. Rama Rao** (AP), **Jyoti Basu** (WB).
Positive: **backward regions get represented**; negative: regional sentiment **exploited for votes**.
Steps to contain regionalism include the **National Integration Council**.

119.s:
Which of the following leaders is correctly associated with a regional party and the state mentioned?
1. M.G. Ramachandran — Tamil Nadu
2. N.T. Rama Rao — Andhra Pradesh
3. Jyoti Basu — West Bengal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: M.G. Ramachandran is associated with Tamil Nadu, N.T. Rama Rao with Andhra Pradesh and Jyoti Basu with West Bengal.
119.tq: Verify each leader-state association before choosing the all-inclusive code.
xs: All three are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
**M.G. Ramachandran** — **TN**; **N.T. Rama Rao** — **AP**; **Jyoti Basu** — **WB**.
xa: Regional parties rose in the **late 20th century**.
They demand **more powers and funds** for states.
**AP** also demanded **autonomy** (since the 1960s).

119.s: Which one of the following represents a positive aspect of regional parties?
o: They always prevent the exploitation of regional sentiment.
They enable backward regions to receive political representation.
They transfer all policy-making powers to the Union.
They reduce the representation of marginal regions.
119.x: A positive aspect of regional parties is that backward regions get represented in the political process.
119.tq: Separate the stated positive role from the stated criticism of regional parties.
xs: Regional parties let **backward regions receive political representation** — so option **(2)** is correct.
They do not always prevent exploitation — regional sentiment can be **exploited for votes**.
xa: They **represent state interests** and add **political diversity** to federalism.
Positive consequences also include **cultural pride, balanced development, accountability**.
Demand: **more powers and funds** for states.

119.s:
Assertion (A): Regional sentiment can become a negative feature of regional-party politics.
Reason (R): Regional sentiment may be exploited for electoral votes.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
119.x: Both statements are true, and the exploitation of regional sentiment for votes explains why it can become a negative feature of regional-party politics.
119.tq: Test whether the stated political motive directly explains the identified negative consequence.
xs: **Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A** — so option **(1)** is correct.
A true: regional sentiment can be a **negative** of regional-party politics.
R true and the reason: it may be **exploited for votes**.
xa: Positive side: **backward regions get represented**.
Negatives of regionalism: **parochialism**, **political exploitation**, openings for **extremists**.
Hostility to migrants: **Shiv Sena, MNS**.

119.s:
Which of the following are mentioned as government steps to contain regionalism?
1. National Integration Council
2. Articles 44 and 51A
3. Eleventh Schedule
4. Fifth and Sixth Schedules
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: The listed measures are the SR Act 1956, the National Integration Council, Articles 44 and 51A, the Fifth and Sixth Schedules and the Eighth Schedule. The Eleventh Schedule (panchayats) is not listed. So '1, 2 and 4 only'; '1 and 2 only' misses item 4 and options with 3 are wrong.
119.tq: Schedules named: Fifth, Sixth, Eighth; not Eleventh.
xs: Items **1, 2 and 4** are listed — so option **(2)** is correct.
Steps: **SR Act 1956**, **National Integration Council**, **Art. 44 and Art. 51A**, **Fifth and Sixth Schedules**, **Eighth Schedule**.
The **Eleventh Schedule** is not listed.
xa: Regionalism's negatives include **inter-state disputes** and **new linguistic minorities**.
India has **22** official languages.
SR Act 1956: **14 states + 6 UTs**.

119.s:
With reference to the current Gorkhaland issue, consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Home Affairs set up a panel under former Deputy NSA Pankaj Kumar Singh.
2. The panel was intended to draft a permanent solution to the Gorkhaland statehood demand.
3. Concerns regarding the Siliguri Corridor are connected with the issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
119.x: All three statements are correct: the MHA panel was set up under former Deputy NSA Pankaj Kumar Singh to draft a permanent solution, with concerns centred on the Siliguri Corridor.
119.tq: Check the authority, chairperson, purpose and strategic concern together in a current-affairs statement question.
xs: All three statements are correct — so option **(4)** is correct.
The **MHA** set up a panel under former Deputy NSA **Pankaj Kumar Singh** to draft a **permanent solution** for Gorkhaland.
Concerns over the **Siliguri Corridor** are linked (27 Aug 2026).
xa: Gorkhas in Bengal illustrate **marginalisation of minority linguistic groups**.
**Separatism** = new state inside the Union.
⚠ Separatist ≠ secessionist (state outside India, e.g. **Khalistan**).

119.s: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha revived debate primarily concerning:
o: The North-South relationship in federal politics
The creation of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council
The replacement of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956
The abolition of the Eighth Schedule
119.x: The defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 revived the North-South debate in the context of representation and fiscal federalism.
119.tq: Identify the central political debate linked to a current constitutional development.
xs: The defeat of the **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** in the Lok Sabha revived the **North-South debate** — so option **(1)** is correct (20 May 2026).
Southern states fear lifting the **1971-census seat freeze**.
xa: Industrialised states resent acting as **net fiscal donors**.
Regional parties demand **more powers and funds** for states.
Uneven industrialisation: **Bombay and West Bengal** held **59%** of capital in **1948**.

119.s:
Which of the following concerns was associated with the North-South debate after the defeat of the 131st Amendment Bill, 2026?
1. Southern states feared lifting the seat freeze based on the 1971 Census.
2. Industrialised states resented acting as net fiscal donors.
3. States demanded the complete abolition of Lok Sabha elections.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
119.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The complete abolition of Lok Sabha elections was not part of the stated debate.
119.tq: Reject an extreme invented consequence while retaining the two stated federal concerns.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: southern states fear lifting the **1971-census seat freeze**.
Statement 2 correct: industrialised states resent acting as **net fiscal donors**.
Statement 3 wrong: abolition of **Lok Sabha** elections was no part of the debate.
xa: The debate followed the **131st Amendment Bill, 2026**'s defeat in the **Lok Sabha**.
**Autonomy** demands from TN, Punjab, AP, WB date from the **1960s**.
Regional parties add **political diversity** to federalism.

119.s: Which aspect of regional movements is identified as often remaining unrecognised?
o: The role of foreign governments in linguistic reorganisation
The role of Governors in appointing regional parties
The role of women in movements such as Telangana and Jharkhand
The role of courts in delimitation alone
119.x: The roles played by women in regional movements, including those in Telangana and Jharkhand, are often left unrecognised.
119.tq: Identify the neglected social dimension rather than the institutional dimensions of regionalism.
xs: **Women's roles** in regional movements such as **Telangana and Jharkhand** often go unrecognised — so option **(3)** is correct.
Both Telangana and Jharkhand are **separatism** cases (new states inside the Union).
xa: **Telangana**: **1969** agitation and **2009-14** phase → statehood **2014**.
Neglected sub-regions demanded **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Telangana**.
**Jharkhand**'s **2021** Act: **75%** of lower-salary private jobs for locals.

119.s: Which State passed the first law reserving 75% of private industrial jobs for local candidates, in 2019?
119.x: Andhra Pradesh's Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019 was the first such law. Haryana (2020) and Jharkhand (2021) followed with their own 75% laws; Maharashtra is linked with the Shiv Sena's sons-of-the-soil politics, not this law.
119.tq: First 75% local quota = AP 2019; struck down = Haryana.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** passed the first **75%** private-job local-quota law (**2019**) — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Haryana (2020)** and **Jharkhand (2021)** followed; **Maharashtra** is linked with **Shiv Sena** sons-of-the-soil politics.
xa: AP's Act was **challenged in the AP High Court**.
Haryana's Act was **struck down** by the **Punjab & Haryana HC (Nov 2023)**.
AP angle: **Andhra State (1953)** triggered linguistic reorganisation.

120.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with its pre-2022, 13-district regional grouping?
o: North Andhra — Srikakulam, Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam
North Andhra — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
Coastal Andhra — East Godavari, West Godavari, Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore
Rayalaseema — Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
120.x: Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore were placed in Coastal Andhra, not North Andhra. The other three pairings are correct; Kadapa is also known as YSR district.
120.tq: Find the wrong regional grouping by checking the complete membership list.
xs: **North Andhra — Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore** is wrongly matched — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore** formed **Zone III** of **Coastal Andhra**; **North Andhra** was **Zone I**.
Coastal Andhra = **Zone II (EG, WG, Krishna)** + **Zone III (Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore)**; **Rayalaseema** = **Zone IV**.
xa: **Zones V and VI** went to **Telangana**.
Public-employment zones follow the **same regional grouping**.
Backward districts package: **7 districts** = **4 of Rayalaseema + 3 of North Andhra**.

120.s: In the public-employment zonal grouping described for the pre-2022 regional structure, Zone II comprised:
o: East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna
120.x: Zone II comprised East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna. Zone I covered North Andhra, Zone III covered Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore, and Zone IV covered Rayalaseema.
120.tq: Distinguish regional grouping from the similarly numbered employment zone.
xs: **Zone II** = **East Godavari, West Godavari and Krishna** — so option **(2)** is correct.
**Zone I** = North Andhra; **Zone III** = **Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore**; **Zone IV** = **Rayalaseema**.

120.s:

120.tq: Use the full list to avoid confusing the regional and zonal classifications.
xs: All four statements are accepted — so option **(4)** is correct.
**Zone I** = **North Andhra**; **Zone IV** = **Rayalaseema**.
**Zones V and VI** were the Telangana zones and **went to Telangana**; the key places **Hyderabad** in **Zone VI**.
xa: **Zone II** = EG, WG, Krishna; **Zone III** = Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore.
Hyderabad was the **common capital** for up to **10 years** under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
AP Reorganisation Act appointed day: **2 June 2014**.

120.s: Under the public-employment zonal grouping of the residuary Andhra Pradesh, the districts of Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore formed:

**Zone I** = North Andhra; **Zone II** = EG, WG, Krishna; **Zone IV** = Rayalaseema.
xa: **Zones V and VI** went to **Telangana**.
The zones follow the **regional grouping** of AP.

120.s: Which of the following regions has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema, particularly in the case of Krishna-Guntur?
120.x: Coastal Andhra, especially the Krishna-Guntur region, has historically been more developed than North Andhra and Rayalaseema.

xs: **Coastal Andhra**, esp. **Krishna-Guntur**, was historically more developed than **North Andhra and Rayalaseema** — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Kalyana Karnataka** is a region of Karnataka with **Art. 371J** status.
xa: AP Cabinet tracked **₹8.55 lakh crore** investment aimed at jobs in **North Andhra and Rayalaseema** (Jan 2026).

Backward districts package: **₹50 crore per district per year**.

120.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change in the approach to addressing regional disparities in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The BRGF continues as the sole state incentive mechanism.

The AP Industrial Policy 2023 has been replaced by the defunct BRGF.

xs: The **defunct BRGF** has given way to **state incentives such as AP Industrial Policy 2023** — so option **(3)** is correct.
The BRGF is no longer the mechanism, and **SCS** is not the only route.
xa: NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts (Jan 2026).
**₹8.55 lakh crore** investment tracked for **North Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
**Sec. 94** of the AP Reorganisation Act gives **tax incentives**.

xs: NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts — so option **(2)** is correct (Jan 2026).

xa: AP Cabinet tracked **₹8.55 lakh crore** of investment for North Andhra and Rayalaseema.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Rayalaseema's emergence as an industrial hub:

2. Royal Enfield has a facility in Tirupati.

120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: JSW steel (Kadapa) and Royal Enfield (Tirupati) are cited. Statement 3 is wrong: the proposed Space City is near Sriharikota, not Visakhapatnam. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.

xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **JSW steel plant** — **Kadapa**.

**₹8.55 lakh crore** investment aimed at jobs in **North Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
JSP MP sought an **AIIMS** in **Rayalaseema** and one in the north coastal districts.

120.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bhargava Committee — Legal safeguards for Mulki employment
Wanchoo Committee — Assessment of Telangana surplus funds
Srikrishna Committee — Consultation on the Telangana/united Andhra Pradesh question
Sivaramakrishnan Committee — Investigation of literacy disparities
120.x: The Srikrishna Committee, headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna, was appointed in 2010 to consult on the Telangana or united Andhra Pradesh question. The Bhargava Committee dealt with surplus funds, the Wanchoo Committee with Mulki safeguards, and the Sivaramakrishnan Committee with locating the new capital.
120.tq: Start from the sure committee–mandate pair and eliminate swapped mandates.
xs: **Srikrishna Committee — Telangana/united-AP question** is correct — so option **(3)** is correct.
**Bhargava** assessed **Telangana surplus funds**; **Wanchoo** examined **Mulki safeguards** — options (1) and (2) are swapped.
**Sivaramakrishnan** dealt with locating the **new capital**, not literacy.
xa: Srikrishna (Justice **B.N. Srikrishna**, **2010**) reported in **Dec 2010** with **six options**.

Sivaramakrishnan Committee: **2014**, under the AP Reorganisation Act.

120.s:
With reference to the Wanchoo Committee, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted in 1969.
2. It examined legal and constitutional methods for retaining Mulki employment safeguards.
3. It was headed by Justice B.N. Srikrishna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Justice B.N. Srikrishna headed the Srikrishna Committee constituted in 2010.
120.tq: Separate the committee’s year and mandate from the swapped chairperson trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **Wanchoo Committee** (**1969**) examined **legal and constitutional ways** to keep **Mulki (employment) safeguards**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Justice B.N. Srikrishna** headed the **Srikrishna Committee (2010)**.
xa: The **Bhargava Committee (1969)** assessed **Telangana surplus funds**.
**8-Point Formula (1969)** set up a high-level committee under a judge.
⚠ **Srikrishna** (2010) = Telangana question; **Sivaramakrishnan** (2014) = new capital.

120.s: Which committee was constituted under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 as an expert committee for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh?
120.x: The Sivaramakrishnan Committee, headed by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan, was the expert committee under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh.
120.tq: Who would perform this specific statutory task?
xs: The **Sivaramakrishnan Committee** (**K.C. Sivaramakrishnan**, **2014**) located AP's **new capital** — so option **(4)** is correct.
It was an expert committee under the **AP Reorganisation Act**.
**Srikrishna** = Telangana question (**2010**); **Bhargava** = surplus funds; **Wanchoo** = Mulki safeguards (both **1969**).
xa: Three-capitals plan (**2020**): **Visakhapatnam** executive, **Amaravati** legislative, **Kurnool** judicial.
Both 2020 laws were withdrawn in **Nov 2021**.
Hyderabad was common capital for up to **10 years**.

120.s:
The 8-Point Formula of 1969 provided for which of the following institutional arrangements?
1. A high-level committee under a judge
2. A special committee on Telangana surpluses
3. An expert committee for locating the new capital of Andhra Pradesh
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: The 8-Point Formula of 1969 itself set up a high-level committee under a judge and a special committee on Telangana surpluses. The capital-location committee was constituted much later under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
120.tq: Use chronology to reject the later capital-location committee.
xs: Items **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
The **8-Point Formula (1969)** set up a **high-level committee under a judge** and a **special committee on Telangana surpluses**.
Item 3 wrong: the capital-location committee (**Sivaramakrishnan**) came in **2014**.
xa: **Bhargava Committee (1969)**: Telangana surplus funds.
**Wanchoo Committee (1969)**: Mulki safeguards.
**Srikrishna Committee (2010)**: report with **six options**.

120.s: The appointed day under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 was:
120.x: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 took effect on the appointed day, 2 June 2014.
120.tq: Direct date recall with close-date distractors.
xs: The **appointed day** of the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** was **2 June 2014** — so option **(2)** is correct.
From that day **Hyderabad** became the common capital for up to **10 years**.
xa: PM promised **SCS** in the Rajya Sabha in **Feb 2014**.
**Sections 46(2)-(3)**: backward-areas package; **Section 94**: tax incentives.
**Sivaramakrishnan Committee** under the Act located the **new capital**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014:
1. Hyderabad was made the common capital for up to ten years.
2. Sections 46(2)-(3) provide a special development package for backward areas.
3. Section 94 provides for the common-capital arrangement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Hyderabad was the common capital for up to 10 years, and Sections 46(2)-(3) give the backward-areas package. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 94 provides tax incentives. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
120.tq: 46 = backward-area package; 94 = tax incentives.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: **Hyderabad** was common capital for up to **10 years**.
Statement 2 correct: **Sections 46(2)-(3)** = special package for **backward areas**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Section 94** provides **tax incentives**.
xa: ⚠ **Sec. 46(2)-(3)** = backward areas; **Sec. 94** = tax incentives.
Package: **7 districts**, **₹50 crore per district per year** (KBK/Bundelkhand model).
Appointed day: **2 June 2014**.

120.s: The backward districts package for Andhra Pradesh covered:
o: Six districts—three in Rayalaseema and three in Coastal Andhra—with ₹100 crore per district per year
Seven districts—four in Rayalaseema and three in North Andhra—with ₹50 crore per district per year
Seven districts—three in Rayalaseema and four in North Andhra—with ₹50 crore per district in total
Eight districts—four in Rayalaseema and four in North Andhra—with ₹50 crore per district per year
120.x: The package covered seven districts: four in Rayalaseema and three in North Andhra. It provided ₹50 crore per district per year and was based on the KBK/Bundelkhand model.
120.tq: Break the quantitative option into number, regional composition and annual amount.
xs: **Seven districts — four in Rayalaseema and three in North Andhra — ₹50 crore per district per year** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The package follows the **KBK/Bundelkhand model**.
xa: It flows from **Sections 46(2)-(3)** of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
**Section 94**: tax incentives.
NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about the Special Category Status debate concerning Andhra Pradesh:

2. The Fourteenth Finance Commission ended the general-versus-special distinction for devolution.
3. A special assistance measure was offered instead.
4. The demand has ceased to be a political issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
120.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the demand remains a political issue.

xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **PM promised SCS** in the **Rajya Sabha** in **Feb 2014**.
The **14th Finance Commission** ended the general/special distinction; a "**special assistance measure**" was offered instead.
Statement 4 wrong: the demand **remains a political issue**.
xa: Backward districts package: **₹50 crore per district per year**.
**Section 94**: tax incentives.
Comparison: **Kalyana Karnataka** has **Art. 371J** status (since **2013**).

120.s: Which of the following pairs of Acts constituted the three-capitals legislative framework of Andhra Pradesh in 2020?
o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020
AP Regional Balance Act, 2020 and Kurnool Judicial Capital Act, 2020
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and Six-Point Formula Act, 1973
AP Capital Development Act, 2019 and Amaravati Protection Act, 2021
120.x: The framework consisted of the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020.
120.tq: Identify the exact official names of paired enactments.
xs: The **AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020** and the **APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020** made up the three-capitals framework — so option **(1)** is correct.
They made **Visakhapatnam** executive, **Amaravati** legislative and **Kurnool** judicial capital.
xa: Both were withdrawn in **2021** (Nov 2021).
**APPSC-GS 2023** asked the bill behind three capitals: **APCRDA (Repeal) Bill, 2020**.
**APPSC-GS 2022** asked when the Decentralisation Act was dropped: **2021**.

120.s: Both the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020 were withdrawn in:
120.x: Both laws were withdrawn in November 2021.
120.tq: Discriminate between the year of enactment and the year of withdrawal.
xs: Both three-capitals laws were withdrawn in **2021** (**Nov 2021**) — so option **(2)** is correct.
**APPSC-GS 2022** asked exactly this.
xa: The laws: **AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020** + **APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020**.
After **2024**, the coalition is pushing a **central law** to protect **Amaravati**.
Coalition fear: three-capital plan revived in **2029**.

120.s:
Consider the following statements about Amaravati after 2024:
1. The coalition government is committed to completing Amaravati within three years.
2. It is pushing for a central law, through a Bill in Parliament, to protect Amaravati as the capital.
3. FICCI Andhra Pradesh sought a special central package for Amaravati in Union Budget 2026-27.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct as reported (TH, 7 Jan 2026). Statement 3 is wrong: it was CII Andhra Pradesh, not FICCI, that sought the special package. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
120.tq: Amaravati package demand came from CII AP.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the coalition is committed to completing **Amaravati within three years**.
Statement 2 correct: it seeks a **central law (Bill in Parliament)** to protect it as capital (TH, 7 Jan 2026).
Statement 3 wrong: it was **CII AP**, not FICCI, that sought a special central package in **Union Budget 2026-27**.
xa: **YSRCP view**: big Amaravati spending hurts **north coastal districts** and drought-prone **Rayalaseema**.
Coalition fears a three-capital revival in **2029**.
The 2020 three-capitals laws were withdrawn in **2021**.

120.s: Which of the following correctly represents the political positions concerning the three-capitals proposal?
o: YSRCP argued that Amaravati spending hurts north coastal districts and drought-prone Rayalaseema, while the coalition feared revival of the three-capitals plan in 2029.
YSRCP supported Amaravati spending, while the coalition opposed its revival in 2029.
The coalition argued that Amaravati spending harms Telangana, while YSRCP favoured three capitals after 2029.
Both YSRCP and the coalition demanded that Kurnool be made the permanent capital.
120.x: YSRCP criticised large spending on Amaravati as harmful to north coastal districts and drought-prone Rayalaseema; the coalition feared that the three-capitals plan could be revived in 2029.
120.tq: Separate the positions of competing political actors rather than matching only one issue.
xs: **YSRCP** said Amaravati spending hurts **north coastal districts and drought-prone Rayalaseema**; the **coalition** fears a **three-capitals revival in 2029** — so option **(1)** is correct.
Neither side demanded **Kurnool** as the permanent capital; Kurnool was only the proposed **judicial** capital.
xa: Three capitals (2020): **Visakhapatnam** executive, **Amaravati** legislative, **Kurnool** judicial.
**CII AP** sought a special central package for Amaravati (1 Feb 2026).
The coalition is pushing for a **central law** to protect Amaravati.

120.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the Andhra Pradesh Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020?
o: Visakhapatnam—legislative capital, Amaravati—executive capital, Kurnool—judicial capital
Visakhapatnam—executive capital, Amaravati—legislative capital, Kurnool—judicial capital
Visakhapatnam—judicial capital, Amaravati—executive capital, Kurnool—legislative capital
Visakhapatnam—executive capital, Amaravati—judicial capital, Kurnool—legislative capital
120.x: The 2020 Act proposed Visakhapatnam as the executive capital, Amaravati as the legislative capital and Kurnool as the judicial capital.
120.tq: Test the precise capital–function pairing and avoid reversing the three roles.
xs: **Visakhapatnam — executive**, **Amaravati — legislative**, **Kurnool — judicial** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The other options shuffle the three roles.
xa: ⚠ Three capitals: **Visakhapatnam** = executive; **Amaravati** = legislative; **Kurnool** = judicial.
Repealed in **Nov 2021** along with the **APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020**.
After 2024 the coalition aims to complete **Amaravati within three years**.

120.s: A proposal to establish two additional AIIMS—one in Rayalaseema and another in the north coastal districts—was intended primarily to address:
o: The devolution formula of the Finance Commission
120.x: The proposal for two additional AIIMS was aimed at reducing regional healthcare gaps in Rayalaseema and the north coastal districts.
120.tq: Identify the policy objective from the regions and institutional intervention described.
xs: Two more **AIIMS** — one in **Rayalaseema**, one **north coastal** — were sought to remove **regional healthcare gaps** — so option **(1)** is correct (7 Aug 2026).
The demand came from a **JSP Rajya Sabha MP**.
xa: Coastal Andhra (Krishna-Guntur) is historically more developed than **North Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
**₹8.55 lakh crore** investment tracked for jobs in these regions.
Backward districts package: **4 of Rayalaseema + 3 of North Andhra**.

120.s: With reference to regional disparity and special constitutional arrangements, which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Kalyana Karnataka — Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act
North Andhra — Article 46(2)-(3) of the AP Reorganisation Act
120.x: Kalyana Karnataka has special status under Article 371J since 2013, although disparities continue. The other pairs wrongly combine unrelated constitutional or statutory provisions.
120.tq: Match the region with the correct constitutional provision, not a nearby AP provision.
xs: **Kalyana Karnataka — Article 371J** is correct — so option **(1)** is correct.
It has had special status **since 2013**, yet **disparities persist** (13 Apr 2026).
**Section 94** (tax incentives) and **Sections 46(2)-(3)** (backward areas) belong to the **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014**, not the Constitution or Karnataka.
xa: AP's backward districts package: **7 districts**, **₹50 crore per district per year**.
AP's **SCS** demand remains a political issue.
NITI Aayog monitors **112** Aspirational Districts.

120.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sri Bagh Pact (1937) was the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord.
2. Its agreement template was reused in the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1969.
3. Agreement-based safeguards such as these are criticised for institutionalising sub-regional fault lines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
120.x: Statement 1 is correct: Sri Bagh (1937) was the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gentlemen's Agreement was in 1956, not 1969. Statement 3 is correct: such safeguards institutionalised sub-regional fault lines and poor implementation fed agitations. So '1 and 3 only'.
120.tq: Sri Bagh 1937 -> Gentlemen's Agreement 1956.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — so option **(2)** is correct.
Statement 1 correct: the **Sri Bagh Pact (1937)** was the **first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord**.
Statement 2 wrong: its template was reused in the **Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956**, not 1969.
Statement 3 correct: such safeguards **institutionalised sub-regional fault lines**; poor implementation fed agitations.
xa: **1969** is the year of the **8-Point Formula**, **Bhargava** and **Wanchoo** Committees.
**Srikrishna Committee (2010)** reported with **six options**.
Public-employment **Zones V and VI** went to **Telangana**.

121.s: Which of the following best describes youth unrest?
o: Collective frustration among young people when social norms appear ineffective or harmful
Organised violence undertaken exclusively by political parties
A temporary disagreement between students and teachers over examinations
Individual dissatisfaction among elderly persons caused by economic decline
121.x: Youth unrest refers to collective frustration among young people when society's norms seem ineffective or harmful.
121.tq: Use the precise definition rather than a broad description of protest.
xs: **Youth unrest** is the **collective frustration among young people** when society's **norms seem ineffective or harmful** — so option **(1)** is correct.
It is **collective**, not individual, and concerns **young people**, not the elderly; nor is it limited to political parties or a passing student-teacher dispute.
Its signs: **shared dissatisfaction**, **public attention** and a **desire for change**.
xa: Types: **Persuasive** (exam postponement), **Resistance** (against attendance rules), **Revolutionary** (overthrow the system — **AASU, Bodo**).
Life cycle: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Theories: discontent, **personal maladjustment**, **relative deprivation (Stouffer)** and **resource mobilisation**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of youth unrest:
1. About 9.7 million people join the working-age group each year (2021-31).
2. Education mismatch and capitation fees add to it.
3. The identity crisis and generation gap are linked to families becoming more joint.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct causes. Statement 3 is wrong: the identity crisis and generation gap grow as families become nuclear, not joint. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
121.tq: Generation gap = nuclear families.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: about **9.7 million** join the working-age group each year (**2021-31**) — the "**jobless growth**" problem.
Statement 2 correct: **education mismatch** and **capitation fees** feed unrest.
Statement 3 wrong: the identity crisis and **generation gap** grow as families become **nuclear**, not joint.
xa: **Political interference** is another listed cause.
Campus causes: **exams, fees, hostels, teacher tensions**; off-campus: **sympathetic strikes**, political interference, wider issues (**CAA/NRC**).
Deviance form of unrest: **drug abuse**.

121.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Campus causes — wider issues such as CAA/NRC
Off-campus causes — examinations and hostel problems
Campus causes — examinations, fees, hostels and teacher tensions
121.x: Examinations, fees, hostels and teacher tensions are campus causes. Sympathetic strikes, political interference and wider issues such as CAA/NRC are off-campus causes.
121.tq: Separate campus causes from off-campus causes using the location clue.
xs: **Campus causes** are **examinations, fees, hostels and teacher tensions** — option **(4)**.
**Off-campus causes** are **sympathetic strikes**, **political interference** and wider issues such as **CAA/NRC** — so options (2) and (3) swap the two lists.
**Personal maladjustment** is a **theory** of youth unrest, not an off-campus cause — option (1) is wrong.
xa: Root causes: **unemployment / jobless growth**, **education mismatch + capitation fees**, **identity crisis + generation gap**.
About **9.7 million** join the working-age group every year (**2021-31**).
Forms: regional/secessionist agitations (**Naga, Assam, Khalistan**), militancy (**Dalit Panthers**, 1972), deviance (**drug abuse**).

121.s:
Consider the following statements about theories of youth unrest:
1. The relative deprivation theory is associated with Stouffer.
2. Resource mobilisation theory holds that grievances matter more than tactics and leadership.
3. Personal maladjustment is one of the theories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: relative deprivation is Stouffer's. Statement 2 is wrong: resource mobilisation says tactics and leadership matter more than grievances. Statement 3 is correct: personal maladjustment is listed with discontent. So '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: Resource mobilisation = resources and leaders, not grievances.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **relative deprivation** theory is associated with **Stouffer**.
Statement 2 wrong: **resource mobilisation** holds that **tactics and leadership** matter **more than grievances** — the reverse of the statement.
Statement 3 correct: **personal maladjustment** is listed alongside **discontent** theory.
xa: ⚠ **Relative deprivation = Stouffer** — a favourite matching trap.
Life cycle of an agitation: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Revolutionary unrest aims to **overthrow the system** — e.g. **AASU, Bodo**.

121.s: According to MoSPI 2022, the youth unemployment rate was:
121.x: For youth aged 15–29 years, the reported unemployment rates were 13.0% for males and 12.5% for females.
121.tq: Keep the sex-wise percentages in their correct order.
xs: Option (1) reverses the two figures; **17.5% / 22.7%** are AP's overall and urban youth rates (**PLFS 2023-24**).
**13.1% vs 27.4%** are the ILO 2026 global rates for **men vs women**.
xa: AP youth unemployment **17.5%** — well **above the national rate**; rural **15.5%**, urban **22.7%**.
AP **urban female youth**: **29.1%** — the highest figure in the table.
**ILO 2026**: global youth unemployment **12.4%** (**67 M**); **NEET 20%**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh in 2023–24:
1. The overall youth unemployment rate was 17.5%.
2. The rural youth unemployment rate was 15.5%.
3. The urban youth unemployment rate was 22.7%.
4. Urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: All four are correct as per PLFS 2023-24: AP youth unemployment was 17.5% (well above the national rate), rural 15.5%, urban 22.7%, and urban female youth 29.1%.
121.tq: Check the overall, rural, urban and urban-female figures separately.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)** (**PLFS 2023-24**, Andhra Pradesh).
Overall AP youth unemployment **17.5%**, well **above the national rate**.
**Urban female youth 29.1%** — the most affected group.
xa: Global (**ILO 2026**): youth unemployment **12.4%** (**67 M**), **NEET 20%**; women **27.4%** vs men **13.1%**.
AP skilling: **APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.

121.s: According to ILO 2026, which of the following correctly states the global youth labour-market figures?
121.x: The ILO 2026 figures cited are a 12.4% youth unemployment rate, about 67 million unemployed youth and a 20% NEET rate.
121.tq: Keep the rate, absolute number and NEET percentage distinct.
xs: **ILO 2026**: global youth unemployment **12.4%** (about **67 million**) and **NEET 20%** — option **(4)**.
The other options jumble these numbers; **29.1%** is AP's urban female youth rate and **13.1%** the ILO rate for **men**.
xa: ILO gender gap: **women 27.4% vs men 13.1%**.
**NEET** = young people **not in employment, education or training** — one in five globally (**20%**).

121.s: With reference to Andhra Pradesh, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is 15.7%, which is above the national rate.
Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is 17.5%, which is below the national rate.
Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is 17.5%, which is above the national rate.
Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is 7.5%, which is equal to the national rate.
121.x: Youth unemployment in Andhra Pradesh is reported as 17.5%, and this is higher than the national rate.
121.tq: Read the figure together with the direction of comparison instead of treating the percentage in isolation.
xs: AP youth unemployment is **17.5%**, **above the national rate** — option **(3)**.
The figure is from **PLFS 2023-24**; options citing **15.7%** or **7.5%**, or "below/equal" to the national rate, are wrong.
xa: AP break-up: **rural 15.5%**, **urban 22.7%**, **urban female youth 29.1%**.
AP skilling: **APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.

121.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Persuasive agitation — overthrow of the existing system
Revolutionary agitation — overthrow of the system
Revolutionary agitation — opposition to attendance rules
121.x: Revolutionary agitation seeks to overthrow the system. Examination postponement is persuasive, while opposition to attendance rules is resistance.
121.tq: Use the objective of each agitation to eliminate swapped classifications.
xs: **Revolutionary** agitation aims to **overthrow the system** — option **(3)**; examples **AASU** and **Bodo**.
**Persuasive** agitation seeks a change such as **exam postponement** — not overthrow.
**Resistance** agitation opposes things like **attendance rules** — so options (2) and (4) swap the types.
xa: Youth unrest = **collective frustration** when norms seem ineffective or harmful.
Life cycle: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Theories: **relative deprivation (Stouffer)**; **resource mobilisation** (tactics and leadership over grievances).

121.s:
Arrange the stages in the life cycle of a youth agitation in the correct order:
A. Public support
B. Initiation
C. Official action
D. Discontent
E. Formalisation
121.x: The sequence is discontent, initiation, formalisation, public support and official action.
121.tq: Fix the first stage as discontent and then follow the development of the movement.
xs: The life cycle is **Discontent → Initiation → Formalisation → Public support → Official action** — **D, B, E, A, C**, option **(1)**.
It begins with **discontent**, not initiation, and ends with **official action** by the state.
xa: Signs of youth unrest: **shared dissatisfaction**, **public attention**, **desire for change**.
Types: **Persuasive**, **Resistance**, **Revolutionary**.
**Resource mobilisation** theory: **tactics and leadership** matter more than grievances.

121.s: Which of the following is an example of a regional or secessionist youth agitation?
121.x: Naga, Assam and Khalistan agitations are cited as regional or secessionist youth agitations.
121.tq: Identify the movement belonging to the specified category.
xs: The **Naga agitation** is a **regional/secessionist** youth agitation — option **(3)**; the notes also list **Assam** and **Khalistan**.
**NSS**, **Skill India** and the **Youth Parliament** are government youth **programmes / remedies**, not agitations.
xa: Militancy form: **Dalit Panthers** (**1972**, **Maharashtra**).
Deviance form: **drug abuse**.
New pattern: **leaderless, digital** protests on **encrypted apps** — **Bangladesh 2024** (job quota), **Nepal Gen Z 2025**.

121.s: The Dalit Panthers emerged as a militant movement in:
121.x: The Dalit Panthers emerged in 1972 in Maharashtra and are associated with militancy.
121.tq: Link the movement with its year and location.
xs: The **Dalit Panthers** emerged in **1972** in **Maharashtra** as a **militant** form of youth unrest — option **(2)**.
**1974 Gujarat** is the **Nav Nirman** movement; **1979 Assam** is **AASU**; **1990 North India** is the **Anti-Mandal** agitation.
xa: Regional/secessionist forms: **Naga, Assam, Khalistan**.
Deviance form: **drug abuse**.
New pattern: **leaderless, digital** protests — Bangladesh **2024**, **Nepal Gen Z 2025**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the new pattern of youth protest:
1. Protests are increasingly leaderless and digital, organised on encrypted apps.
2. The Bangladesh 2024 protests were over job quotas.
3. Such protests are typically led by a formally constituted central committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the new pattern is leaderless, digital protest on encrypted apps, e.g. Bangladesh 2024 over job quotas. Statement 3 is wrong because it contradicts 'leaderless'. So '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: Leaderless rules out a central committee.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the new pattern is **leaderless, digital** protest organised on **encrypted apps**.
Statement 2 correct: **Bangladesh 2024** protests were over the **job quota**.
Statement 3 wrong: a **formal central committee** contradicts the **leaderless** pattern.
xa: Another example: **Nepal Gen Z 2025**.
A wave of youth-led protests also hit **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.
Older forms: regional/secessionist (**Naga, Assam, Khalistan**), militancy (**Dalit Panthers**, 1972), deviance (**drug abuse**).

121.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Nav Nirman movement — Gujarat — corruption and prices
121.x: The Nav Nirman movement of Gujarat involved students protesting corruption and prices. The other pairs interchange the states or issues of different movements.
121.tq: Start with the sure movement–state–issue combination and eliminate swapped pairs.
xs: **Nav Nirman** (**1974**) — **Gujarat** — students against **corruption and prices** is correct, option **(1)**.
**JP movement** was in **Bihar** (not Assam) and fed into the **Emergency**; **AASU** was in **Assam** against illegal migrants.
**Anti-Mandal** (1990, North India) opposed **27% OBC reservation**; separate statehood was the **Telangana students'** issue.
xa: Nav Nirman forced CM **Chimanbhai Patel** to resign (**Feb 1974**).
⚠ **Nav Nirman = Gujarat**; **JP movement = Bihar** — both **1974**.
**AASU** (1979-85) ended with the **Assam Accord 1985**.

121.s: The JP movement of 1974 was primarily associated with student agitations in:
121.x: The JP movement of 1974 was associated with student agitations in Bihar and was led by Jayaprakash Narayan.
121.tq: Test the state associated with the movement rather than its later consequence.
xs: The **JP movement (1974)** was based on student agitations in **Bihar** — option **(1)**.
It was led by **Jayaprakash Narayan** and fed into the **Emergency (June 1975)**.
**Gujarat** was the **Nav Nirman** movement; **Assam** the **AASU**; **North India** the **Anti-Mandal** agitation.
xa: ⚠ **Nav Nirman = Gujarat**, **JP = Bihar** — both **1974**.
Nav Nirman: students against **corruption and prices**; CM **Chimanbhai Patel** resigned (**Feb 1974**).
Others: **Anna Hazare** movement, **Nirbhaya** protests, **Patidar (2015)**, **Jallikattu (2016-17)**.

121.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. AASU movement - against illegal migrants - Assam Accord 1985
2. Anti-Mandal movement (1990) - against 10% EWS reservation
3. Telangana students' movement - Osmania University - separate statehood
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
121.x: Pair 1 is correct: AASU (1979-85) opposed illegal migrants, ending in the Assam Accord 1985. Pair 2 is wrong: the Anti-Mandal movement opposed 27% OBC reservation. Pair 3 is correct: Osmania University students led the statehood agitation. So '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: Mandal = 27% OBC quota.
xs: Pairs **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Pair 1 correct: **AASU** (**1979-85**) fought **illegal migrants**, ending in the **Assam Accord 1985**.
Pair 2 wrong: the **Anti-Mandal** movement (**1990**) opposed **27% OBC reservation**, not EWS reservation.
Pair 3 correct: **Osmania University** students led the **separate statehood** agitation (**1969; 2009-14**).
xa: **AASU** is also cited as a **revolutionary** type of agitation, with the **Bodo**.
**Nav Nirman** (Gujarat) and **JP movement** (Bihar) — both **1974**.
**Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) followed the SC upholding the **Mulki Rules**; ended by the **Six-Point Formula (1973)**.

121.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Patidar movement — 2015
2. Jallikattu movement — 2016–17
3. Nirbhaya protests — 1974
4. Anna Hazare movement — included among other student and youth movements
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
121.x: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Patidar agitation 2015, Jallikattu 2016-17, and the Anna Hazare movement is listed among other youth movements. Pair 3 is wrong: the Nirbhaya protests followed the December 2012 Delhi gang-rape; 1974 is the year of the Nav Nirman and JP movements.
121.tq: Detect the false date while retaining the correctly identified movements.
xs: Pairs **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Patidar** movement — **2015**; **Jallikattu** — **2016-17**; the **Anna Hazare** movement is listed among other youth movements.
Pair 3 wrong: **1974** is the year of the **Nav Nirman** and **JP** movements, not the **Nirbhaya** protests.
xa: **Nav Nirman** (Gujarat) forced CM **Chimanbhai Patel** to resign (**Feb 1974**).
**JP movement** (Bihar) fed into the **Emergency (June 1975)**.
**Anti-Mandal** (**1990**) opposed **27% OBC reservation**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about student movements of 1974:
1. The Nav Nirman movement in Gujarat led to the resignation of Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel.
2. The JP movement in Bihar fed into the Emergency of June 1975.
3. The Nav Nirman movement was led by Jayaprakash Narayan in Bihar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Nav Nirman (Gujarat) forced Chimanbhai Patel's resignation in February 1974, and the JP movement (Bihar) fed into the June 1975 Emergency. Statement 3 is wrong: JP led the Bihar movement; Nav Nirman was a Gujarat student agitation. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.
121.tq: Nav Nirman = Gujarat, Chimanbhai; JP = Bihar, Emergency.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **Nav Nirman** (Gujarat) students against corruption and prices forced CM **Chimanbhai Patel** to resign (**Feb 1974**).
Statement 2 correct: the **JP movement** (Bihar) fed into the **Emergency (June 1975)**.
Statement 3 wrong: **Jayaprakash Narayan** led the **Bihar** movement; Nav Nirman was in **Gujarat**.
xa: ⚠ **Nav Nirman = Gujarat**; **JP = Bihar** — both **1974**.
**AASU** (**1979-85**, Assam) against illegal migrants → **Assam Accord 1985**.
**Telangana students** (**1969; 2009-14**) — **Osmania University** — separate statehood.

121.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Andhra Pradesh agitations?
o: Jai Andhra — 1972–73 — separate Andhra demand after the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules
Special Category Status — 1966 — steel plant for Visakhapatnam
Visakha Ukku — after 2014 — SCS promised at bifurcation
121.x: The Jai Andhra agitation occurred in 1972–73 after the Supreme Court upheld the Mulki Rules and demanded a separate Andhra; it ended with the Six-Point Formula in 1973.
121.tq: Use the year and immediate trigger to distinguish the three Andhra issues.
xs: **Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) demanded a separate Andhra after the SC upheld the **Mulki Rules** — option **(2)**.
**Visakha Ukku - Andhrula Hakku** (**1966**) demanded a **steel plant** for Visakhapatnam — not a separate Andhra.
The **Special Category Status** agitation came **after 2014**, over the SCS promised at **bifurcation**.
xa: Jai Andhra was ended by the **Six-Point Formula (1973)**.
Visakha Ukku: **T. Amrutha Rao's** fast; deaths in police firing.
Latest: YSRCP student and youth wings protested over alleged **Mega DSC** recruitment irregularities (**29 Jul 2026**).

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Visakha Ukku - Andhrula Hakku' agitation:
1. It took place in 1966 and demanded a steel plant for Visakhapatnam.
2. T. Amrutha Rao undertook a fast during it.
3. It was ended by the Six-Point Formula of 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 1966 agitation sought a steel plant and T. Amrutha Rao fasted. Statement 3 is wrong: the Six-Point Formula (1973) ended the Jai Andhra agitation, not Visakha Ukku. So '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: Six-Point Formula closes Jai Andhra (1972-73).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: the agitation (**1966**) demanded a **steel plant** for **Visakhapatnam**.
Statement 2 correct: **T. Amrutha Rao** undertook a **fast**; there were deaths in police firing.
Statement 3 wrong: the **Six-Point Formula (1973)** ended the **Jai Andhra** agitation.
xa: **Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) followed the SC upholding the **Mulki Rules**.
**Special Category Status** agitation — **after 2014** — for the SCS promised at bifurcation.
**Mega DSC** recruitment protests by YSRCP youth wings (**29 Jul 2026**).

121.s: The latest agitation mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh youth and student wings concerned alleged irregularities in:
121.x: YSRCP student and youth wings protested statewide over alleged Mega DSC recruitment irregularities on 29 July 2026.
121.tq: Identify the specific immediate issue rather than the broader political context.
xs: The latest AP agitation was over alleged **Mega DSC recruitment** irregularities — option **(3)**.
**YSRCP student and youth wings** protested statewide (**29 Jul 2026**).
The **Mulki Rules** relate to **Jai Andhra**; the **steel plant** to **Visakha Ukku (1966)**; the **Assam Accord** to **AASU**.
xa: **Jai Andhra** (**1972-73**) was ended by the **Six-Point Formula (1973)**.
**Visakha Ukku - Andhrula Hakku**: **T. Amrutha Rao's** fast.
**Special Category Status** agitation — students and youth, **after 2014**.

121.s: Under the National Youth Policy 2014, the term ‘youth’ refers to persons in which age group?
121.x: The National Youth Policy 2014 defines youth as persons aged 15–29 years. The National Youth Policy 2003 used the age group 13–35 years.
121.tq: Separate the age group in NYP 2014 from the earlier NYP 2003 definition.
xs: **NYP 2014** defines youth as **15-29 years** — option **(1)**.
**13-35 years** was the age group of the earlier **NYP 2003** — a classic trap.
xa: NYP 2014 has **5 objectives** and **11 priority areas**.
The same **15-29** band is used for **MoSPI 2022** youth unemployment data.

121.s: Which one of the following correctly states the vision of the National Youth Policy 2014?
o: To provide compulsory military training to all youth
To help youth reach their full potential and help India find its rightful place among nations
To restrict youth participation to educational institutions
To make all youth government employees by 2030
121.x: The vision of NYP 2014 is to help youth reach their full potential and thereby help India find its rightful place among nations.
121.tq: Select the precise official vision statement.
xs: The **NYP 2014** vision: help youth **reach their full potential** and through them help **India find its rightful place among nations** — option **(2)**.
Compulsory military training, restricting youth to campuses or making all youth government employees are not part of the policy.
xa: **5 objectives**, **11 priority areas** — education, employment and skills, entrepreneurship, health, sports and more.
Priority areas also include **participation in politics and governance**, **inclusion** and **social justice**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Youth Policy 2014:
1. It has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas.
2. Participation in politics and governance is one of its priority areas.
3. Sports is not among its priority areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NYP 2014 has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas, including participation in politics and governance. Statement 3 is wrong: sports is one of the 11 priority areas. So '1 and 2 only'.
121.tq: 5 objectives, 11 priority areas; sports is in.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: NYP 2014 has **5 objectives** and **11 priority areas**.
Statement 2 correct: **participation in politics and governance** is a priority area.
Statement 3 wrong: **sports** is one of the priority areas.
xa: Other priority areas: **education**, **employment and skills**, **entrepreneurship**, **health**, **social values**, **community engagement**, **inclusion**, **social justice**.
Youth = **15-29 years** under NYP 2014.
A Bill seeks a constitutional **National Commission for Youth**; the last, non-statutory one ran **2002-04**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Service Scheme (NSS):
1. It was started in 1969.
2. Its motto is 'Service Before Self'.
3. It is based on the idea of 'Education through Service'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
121.x: Statement 1 is correct: NSS began in 1969. Statement 2 is wrong: its motto is 'Not Me But You'. Statement 3 is correct: it rests on 'Education through Service'. So '1 and 3 only'.
121.tq: NSS motto: Not Me But You.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **NSS** began in **1969**.
Statement 2 wrong: the NSS motto is **"Not Me But You"**.
Statement 3 correct: NSS rests on **"Education through Service"**.
xa: **MY Bharat** (**31 Oct 2023**) replaced **NYKS** under **MoYAS**.
**National Young Leaders Programme** (**Dec 2014**) includes the **Neighbourhood Youth Parliament**.
**PMKVY (Skill India)** — **2015** — skill training for new entrants to the job market.

121.s: MY Bharat, launched on 31 October 2023, replaced which organisation?
121.x: MY Bharat was launched on 31 October 2023 and replaced NYKS under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
121.tq: Identify the predecessor organisation from the institutional relationship.
xs: **MY Bharat** (**31 Oct 2023**) replaced **NYKS** — option **(3)**; it is under the **MoYAS**.
**NSS** (1969) continues; **PMKVY** is a Skill India scheme; the **National Youth Advisory Council** is part of the National Young Leaders Programme.
xa: **NSS** motto: **"Not Me But You"**; idea: **"Education through Service"**.
**National Young Leaders Programme** — **Dec 2014**.
**PMKVY** — **2015** — skill training for new job-market entrants.

121.s: The National Young Leaders Programme, launched in December 2014, included:
o: Neighbourhood Youth Parliament and National Youth Advisory Council
Only the Prime Minister's Kaushal Vikas Yojana
The Assam Accord and the Six-Point Formula
121.x: The National Young Leaders Programme included the Neighbourhood Youth Parliament and the National Youth Advisory Council.
121.tq: Recall the two component initiatives rather than selecting a related but separate programme.
xs: The **National Young Leaders Programme** (**Dec 2014**) includes the **Neighbourhood Youth Parliament** and the **National Youth Advisory Council** — option **(1)**.
**PMKVY** and **NSS** are separate programmes; the **Assam Accord** and **Six-Point Formula** ended agitations.
xa: **NSS** — **1969** — motto **"Not Me But You"**.
**MY Bharat** — **31 Oct 2023** — replaced **NYKS**.
**PMKVY (Skill India)** — **2015**.

121.s: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana under Skill India was launched in:
121.x: PMKVY under Skill India was launched in 2015 and provides skill training for new entrants to the job market.
121.tq: Distinguish the launch year from the year of the National Young Leaders Programme.
xs: **PMKVY** under **Skill India** began in **2015** — option **(4)**; it gives skill training to new entrants to the job market.
**1969** is **NSS**; **2003** the earlier **NYP**; **2014** the current **NYP** and the National Young Leaders Programme.
xa: AP skilling: **APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.
**MY Bharat** — **31 Oct 2023** — replaced **NYKS**.
Unemployment backdrop: about **9.7 million** join the working-age group each year (**2021-31**).

121.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a remedy for youth unrest?
121.x: Anger-management education, guidance from parents and teachers, and responsive administration are identified remedies. Permanent suppression of peaceful expression is not.
121.tq: Reject the extreme response and select constructive remedies.
xs: **Permanent suppression of peaceful expression** is not a remedy — option **(4)**.
The notes list **anger-management education**, **guidance from parents and teachers** and **responsive administration** as remedies.
xa: Programmes: **NSS (1969)**, **MY Bharat (2023)**, **National Young Leaders Programme (2014)**, **PMKVY (2015)**.
**APSSDC** trained **2,57,575** people in **2024-25**.
A Bill seeks a constitutional **National Commission for Youth**; the last non-statutory one ran **2002-04**.

121.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the protests over the NEET paper leak:
1. The protests began at Jantar Mantar.
2. The protests subsequently became nationwide.
3. SFI and AISF demanded the resignation of the Education Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
121.x: All three statements are correct. The protests started at Jantar Mantar, spread nationwide, and SFI, AISF and other organisations demanded the Education Minister's resignation.
121.tq: Check each statement separately, especially the sequence from a local protest to a nationwide agitation.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **NEET paper leak** protests began at **Jantar Mantar** and then turned **nationwide**.
**SFI, AISF** and others demanded the **Education Minister's resignation** (**24 Jul 2026**).
xa: A **ministerial resignation** followed (**5 Aug 2026**).
Comparative note: youth-led protests in **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.
New pattern: **leaderless, digital** protests on encrypted apps.

121.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of developments associated with the NEET paper leak protests?
o: Ministerial resignation, nationwide protests, protests at Jantar Mantar
Protests at Jantar Mantar, nationwide protests, ministerial resignation
Nationwide protests, ministerial resignation, protests at Jantar Mantar
Protests at Jantar Mantar, ministerial resignation, nationwide protests
121.x: The protests began at Jantar Mantar, turned nationwide, and were followed by the ministerial resignation.
121.tq: Arrange the events by identifying the initial protest, its expansion and the subsequent consequence.
xs: The sequence was **Jantar Mantar → nationwide protests → ministerial resignation** — option **(2)**.
**SFI, AISF** and others demanded the Education Minister's resignation (**24 Jul 2026**); a **resignation followed (5 Aug 2026)**.
xa: The trigger was the **NEET paper leak**.
Life cycle of agitation: **Discontent → initiation → formalisation → public support → official action**.
Wave of youth-led protests in **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya**.

121.s: A wave of youth-led protests was reported in which of the following combination of countries?
121.x: The comparative account refers to youth-led protests in Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya.
121.tq: Match the complete set of countries and reject options containing a substituted country.
xs: The wave of youth-led protests hit **Bangladesh, Nepal and Kenya** — option **(1)** (**10 Jun 2026**).
India, Sri Lanka and Bhutan are not in the list cited.
xa: **Bangladesh 2024** — over the **job quota**.
**Nepal Gen Z 2025** protests.
These follow the new pattern of **leaderless, digital** protests on **encrypted apps**.

122.s: The National Institute of Social Defence functions under the
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
122.x: NISD works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
122.tq: Apply the ministry-organisation matching method.
xs: The **National Institute of Social Defence (NISD)** works under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE)** — option **(1)**.
NISD implements the **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan** and trains officials (e.g. on **children who beg**).
**MoYAS** runs the 2026 **Nasha Mukt Yuva** campaign through **MY Bharat**; the **NCB** is under the **MHA**.
xa: **NMBA** — launched **15 Aug 2020** by **MoSJE**; first in **272** vulnerable districts, now in all.
**SMILE** (MoSJE, **2022**) — sub-scheme for **comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging**.
Social defence scope: **drug and alcohol abuse**, **beggary**, **destitute elderly**, **transgender persons**.

122.s: Which of the following is NOT included within the stated scope of social defence?
o: Support for destitute elderly and transgender persons
Prevention and rehabilitation relating to drug abuse
Prevention and rehabilitation relating to alcohol abuse
122.x: Social defence covers drug and alcohol abuse, beggary, destitute elderly persons and transgender persons; regulation of foreign exchange markets is unrelated.
122.tq: Find the odd policy area outside the defined social-defence group.
xs: **Regulation of foreign exchange markets** is not part of social defence — option **(2)**.
Social defence covers **prevention and rehabilitation** for **drug and alcohol abuse**, **beggary**, **destitute elderly** and **transgender persons**.
xa: The nodal body is **NISD**, under **MoSJE**.
⚠ India lies between the **Golden Crescent** and the **Golden Triangle** — the two major drug-producing regions.
**Indore** was declared the **first beggar-free city** (**2025**).

122.s: Article 47 of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to prohibit
o: Only the sale of alcohol to minors
All forms of tobacco and medicines
Intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes
122.x: Article 47, a Directive Principle, refers to prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health, except for medicinal purposes.
122.tq: Use the exact constitutional wording and retain its medicinal-use exception.
xs: **Art. 47** (a **DPSP**) directs the State to try to **prohibit intoxicating drinks and harmful drugs, except for medicinal use** — option **(4)**.
It is not limited to sale to minors, and does not cover all medicines or tobacco.
xa: **NDPS Act, 1985** — **Sec. 71** provides for **treatment centres**.
Drug enforcement: **Police**, **NCB (1986, MHA)**, **Customs**, **DRI**.
Temperance precedent: **R. Venkataratnam Naidu's Social Purity Association (1891)**.

122.s: The Anti-Arrack Movement was led by
122.x: Dubagunta Rosamma led the Anti-Arrack Movement among neo-literate women of the literacy campaign.
122.tq: Avoid the wrong-person-for-the-deed trap by linking the leader to the movement.
xs: **Dubagunta Rosamma** led the **Anti-Arrack Movement** — option **(3)**.
**R. Venkataratnam Naidu** founded the **Social Purity Association (1891)**, an earlier temperance campaign; **Harsh Mander** is linked to the Delhi HC begging case (**2018**).
xa: The movement began in **1992** in **Dubagunta** village, **Nellore** district.

o: A drug treatment centre under the NDPS Act
A campaign for compulsory beggary registration

122.x: The movement began in 1992 in Dubagunta village of Nellore district, led by Dubagunta Rosamma. Chittoor, Kurnool and Prakasam are other AP districts not linked to its origin.

122.s: Section 71 of the NDPS Act, 1985 provides for

122.s:
Consider the following statements about enforcement of the NDPS Act, 1985:
1. It is enforced by the police, the NCB, Customs and the DRI.
2. The Narcotics Control Bureau was set up in 1986 under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
122.x: Statement 1 is correct: police, NCB, Customs and DRI enforce the NDPS Act. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCB (1986) is under the Ministry of Home Affairs; MoSJE runs the demand-side campaigns. So '1 only'; '2 only', 'Both' and 'Neither' are all wrong.
122.tq: NCB = MHA (enforcement); MoSJE = rehabilitation side.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 correct: drugs law is enforced by the **Police**, **NCB**, **Customs** and **DRI**.
Statement 2 wrong: the **NCB** was set up in **1986** under the **MHA**, not MoSJE.
xa: **MoSJE** handles the rehabilitation side — **NMBA** via **NISD**.
**NDPS Act, 1985** — **Sec. 71** provides for **treatment centres**.
⚠ India lies between the **Golden Crescent** and **Golden Triangle**.

122.s:

122.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NMBA was launched on 15 Aug 2020 by MoSJE, first in 272 districts and now in all. Statement 3 is wrong: it is implemented by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD). So '1 and 2 only'.
122.tq: NMBA: MoSJE + NISD, 272 districts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 correct: **NMBA** was launched on **15 Aug 2020** by **MoSJE**.
Statement 2 correct: it began in **272** vulnerable districts and now covers **all** districts.
Statement 3 wrong: it is implemented by **NISD**, not the NCB.
xa: NMBA focuses on **campuses**.
⚠ **NMBA = MoSJE (2020)**; **Nasha Mukt Yuva = MoYAS through MY Bharat (2026)**.
**Anti-drug day**: **26 June**.

122.s: The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan, launched in August 2026, is implemented through
122.x: The August 2026 youth campaign is being taken forward by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through MY Bharat.
122.tq: Match the campaign with its correct ministry and platform.
xs: The **Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan** runs through **MoYAS** via **MY Bharat** — option **(4)**.
**NCB (MHA)** is an enforcement agency; **AIIMS-NDDTC** worked with MoSJE on the **2019** survey; **DRI** is enforcement.
xa: It is a **100-week Jan Bhagidari** plan guided by the **Kashi Declaration** (July **2025**).
⚠ Distinguish from **NMBA** — **MoSJE**, **15 Aug 2020**, implemented by **NISD**.
**Tele-MANAS** — **10 Oct 2022** — toll-free **14416**.

122.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use (2019):
1. It was conducted by MoSJE with AIIMS-NDDTC.
2. Alcohol was the most-used substance.
