128.tq: Match each law with its subject and reject cross-subject substitutions.
xs: **Special Marriage Act 1954 — civil marriage irrespective of religion** — option **(1)**.
**Hindu Marriage Act 1955** = **monogamy, divorce grounds**, not equal pay.
**Equal pay** is the **Equal Remuneration Act 1976**; night shifts come under the **OSH Code 2020**.
xa: **HSA 1956**: equal inheritance, limited estate abolished.
**Muslim Women (Divorce) Act 1986** was passed after **Shah Bano**.
**Sarla Mudgal (1995)** stressed the **UCC**.

128.s: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is primarily associated with
128.x: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides for monogamy and specifies grounds of divorce under Hindu personal law.
128.tq: Identify the subject matter of the personal law statute without confusing it with succession law.
xs: The **Hindu Marriage Act 1955** provides for **monogamy and divorce grounds** — option **(1)**.
Local-body reservation is under **Arts. 243D/243T**; statutory **floor wage** is in the **Code on Wages, 2019**.
xa: **Special Marriage Act 1954**: civil marriage irrespective of religion.
**Sarla Mudgal (1995)**: a Hindu man's **conversion** cannot validate his second marriage.
**HSA 1956**: equal inheritance for women.

128.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Hindu Succession Act enacted
B. Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act under NTR
C. Central amendment making daughters coparceners by birth
D. *Vineeta Sharma* judgment
128.x: The correct sequence is 1956, 1985, 2005 and 2020. Andhra Pradesh passed its amendment on 24 September 1985 under N.T. Rama Rao.
128.tq: Anchor the sequence to the four supplied years and check the middle events.
xs: Order **A, B, C, D** — option **(1)**.
**HSA** (**1956**) → AP Assembly's amendment under **NTR** (**24 Sept 1985**) → central **2005 amendment** → **Vineeta Sharma** (**2020**).
xa: The AP amendment is dated **1986** — unmarried daughters made coparceners well before 2005.
Vineeta Sharma: the right holds **whether or not the father was alive** on **9 Sept 2005**.
AP angle: daughters' property law (**1985**) + **50%** quotas.

128.s: Which State had already made unmarried daughters coparceners through its amendment before the national Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005?
128.x: Andhra Pradesh made unmarried daughters coparceners through an earlier amendment. The Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the relevant Act on 24 September 1985 under NTR.
128.tq: Identify the State-level precursor to the later central reform.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** made **unmarried daughters coparceners** well before **2005** — option **(1)**.
The AP Assembly passed its Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act on **24 Sept 1985** under **NTR**.
xa: The AP amendment is dated **1986**.
Central **2005 amendment**: daughters = **equal coparceners**.
**Vineeta Sharma (2020)**: daughter a **coparcener by birth**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 was passed after the Shah Bano judgment.
2. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 was Parliament's response to the Shamim Ara judgment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
128.x: Statement 1 is correct: the 1986 Act followed Shah Bano (1985). Statement 2 is wrong: the 2019 Act was Parliament's response to Shayara Bano (2017); Shamim Ara (2002) was an earlier SC ruling on triple talaq. Hence 1 only (A); B, C and D are wrong.
128.tq: Pair each Act with its case: 1986 - Shah Bano; 2019 - Shayara Bano.
xs: Only statement **1** is correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the **1986** Act was passed after **Shah Bano** — correct.
Statement 2: the **2019** Act answered **Shayara Bano**, not **Shamim Ara (2002)** — wrong.
xa: ⚠ Case → law: **Shah Bano** → **1986** Act; **Shayara Bano** → **2019** Act.
**Allahabad High Court** had held triple talaq illegal (PYQ BPSC **1994**).
The **2019** Act: **cognisable, non-bailable**, up to **3 years** jail.

128.s: The judgment in Shah Bano (1985) is associated with which of the following issues?
o: Entry of women aged 10–50 into the Sabarimala temple
Permanent commission for women Army officers
Maintenance of a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 of the CrPC
128.x: The Shah Bano judgment recognised the entitlement of a divorced Muslim woman to maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC and also urged the adoption of a Uniform Civil Code.
128.tq: Match the landmark case with its distinctive legal issue.
xs: **Shah Bano (1985)**: a divorced Muslim wife is entitled to **maintenance under s.125 CrPC** — option **(4)**.
**Sabarimala** dealt with women aged **10-50**; **Babita Puniya** with **permanent commission** for women Army officers.
xa: The Court also **urged a UCC**.
The **Muslim Women (Divorce) Act, 1986** followed.
Today's secular route: **Sec. 144 BNSS**, replacing **Sec. 125 CrPC**.

128.s: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) primarily dealt with which of the following?
o: Conversion to Islam to contract a second Hindu marriage
Adultery under Section 497 of the IPC
128.x: Sarla Mudgal held that conversion to Islam cannot be used to validate a second marriage by a Hindu man and stressed the need for a Uniform Civil Code.
128.tq: Use the wrong-person or wrong-issue trap in landmark-judgment questions.
xs: **Sarla Mudgal (1995)**: a Hindu man **converting to Islam to remarry** — option **(2)**.
**Conversion cannot validate his second marriage**; the Court stressed the **UCC**.
Workplace harassment is the **2013 Act**; adultery (**s.497 IPC**) was **Joseph Shine (2018)**.
xa: **Hindu Marriage Act 1955**: **monogamy**.
**Shah Bano (1985)** also urged a UCC.
UCC vs **Art. 25/29** remains a debate.

128.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Joseph Shine — Entry of women into Sabarimala
Seema v. Ashwani Kumar — Compulsory registration of all marriages
Shayara Bano — Instant triple talaq unconstitutional
Babita Puniya — Permanent commission for women Army officers
128.x: Joseph Shine (2018) struck down adultery under Section 497 of the IPC. Entry of women aged 10–50 into Sabarimala was the issue in the Sabarimala case.
128.tq: Find the swapped issue among closely related landmark judgments.
xs: **Joseph Shine — Sabarimala** is wrongly matched — option **(1)**: Joseph Shine (**2018**) struck down **adultery** (**s.497 IPC**).
**Shayara Bano**: instant triple talaq unconstitutional; **Babita Puniya**: permanent commission — both correct.
xa: **Sabarimala (2018)**: bar on women aged **10-50** struck down **4:1**.
Shayara Bano was decided **3:2** (Aug **2017**).
**Babita Puniya** was a **2020** case.

128.s: The Sabarimala judgment concerning women's rights dealt with the entry of women belonging to which age group into the temple?
128.x: The Sabarimala judgment concerned the entry of women aged 10–50 into the temple.
128.tq: Focus on the exact age range rather than the general subject of the case.
xs: Sabarimala concerned women of **menstruating age, 10-50 years** — option **(1)**.
The case: **Indian Young Lawyers Assn. v. Kerala** (**2018**).
xa: The bar was struck down **4:1**; **Justice Indu Malhotra** dissented.
A **larger-bench review** is pending.
**Haji Ali Dargah** (Bombay HC, **2016**): women allowed into the inner sanctum.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019:
1. It makes instant triple talaq void.
2. The offence is cognisable and non-bailable.
3. It provides for imprisonment up to three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: The 2019 Act declares instant triple talaq void, makes the offence cognisable and non-bailable, and provides for imprisonment up to three years.
128.tq: Test the legal status, procedural character and punishment together.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **MWPRMA 2019** makes **instant triple talaq void**; offence **cognisable, non-bailable**; up to **3 years** jail.
xa: Passed on **30 July 2019**, as Parliament's response to **Shayara Bano**.
**Shayara Bano (Aug 2017)**: held unconstitutional **3:2**.
Earlier: **Shamim Ara (2002)** in the SC.

128.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Sabarimala judgment?
o: The entry restriction was upheld unanimously.
The restriction was struck down by 3:2 in the Shayara Bano case.
The restriction was struck down by 4:1, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting.
The matter was decided by the Bombay High Court in 2016.
128.x: The Sabarimala entry restriction was struck down by a 4:1 majority, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting. Review by a larger bench is pending.
128.tq: Separate the court, case ratio and dissenting judge from neighbouring religious-rights cases.
xs: The Sabarimala bar was **struck down 4:1**, with **Justice Indu Malhotra** dissenting — option **(3)**.
It was not upheld; **3:2** was **Shayara Bano**; the **Bombay HC, 2016** case was **Haji Ali Dargah**.
xa: Women of **10-50** had been barred.
A **larger-bench review** is pending (APPCA **2026**).
**Joseph Shine (2018)** struck down adultery.

128.s: The Supreme Court held instant triple talaq unconstitutional in Shayara Bano v. Union of India by a majority of
128.x: Instant triple talaq was held unconstitutional by a 3:2 majority in 2017. The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act was enacted in 2019.
128.tq: Distinguish the numerical ratio in Shayara Bano from the 4:1 ratio in Sabarimala.
xs: **Shayara Bano (Aug 2017)** held **instant triple talaq** unconstitutional by **3:2** — option **(1)**.
**4:1** was the **Sabarimala** majority.
xa: The **MWPRMA 2019** followed (passed **30 July 2019**).
**Allahabad High Court** had earlier held triple talaq illegal; SC in **Shamim Ara (2002)**.
⚠ **Shah Bano** → **1986** Act; **Shayara Bano** → **2019** Act.

128.s: The Haji Ali Dargah case decided by the Bombay High Court in 2016 concerned
o: women’s exclusion from the inner sanctum
the constitutional status of the Commission on the Status of Women
the age of marriage under the Sarda Act
128.x: The case concerned the prohibition on women entering the inner sanctum of Haji Ali Dargah; entry was ultimately allowed.
128.tq: Identify the precise issue and court associated with a religion-related women’s rights case.
xs: **Haji Ali Dargah** (Bombay HC, **2016**): women **barred from the inner sanctum** — option **(1)**; entry was allowed.
Triple talaq was **Shayara Bano**; marriage age was the **Sarda Act (1929)**.
xa: Petition by **Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan** (**Zakia Soman**, **Noorjehan Safia Niaz**).
**Sabarimala (2018)**: temple entry bar struck down **4:1**.
**Commission on the Status of Women (1946)** is under **ECOSOC**.

128.s: The petition concerning women’s entry into the inner sanctum of Haji Ali Dargah was filed by the
o: National Council of Women in India
128.x: The petition was filed by the Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan, associated with Zakia Soman and Noorjehan Safia Niaz.
128.tq: Match a legal intervention with the organisation that brought it.
xs: The **Bharatiya Muslim Mahila Andolan** filed the Haji Ali petition — option **(3)**.
Its leaders: **Zakia Soman** and **Noorjehan Safia Niaz**.
**NCWI (1925)**, **AIWC (1927)** and **WIA (1917)** are pre-Independence women's bodies.
xa: The **Bombay HC (2016)** allowed entry to the inner sanctum.
**Sabarimala**: **Justice Indu Malhotra** dissented.

128.s: The secular maintenance remedy for wives that was earlier under Section 125 of the CrPC (applied in Shah Bano) is now found in:
o: Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act
128.x: Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita replaced CrPC Section 125 as the secular maintenance route. BNS is a penal code, Section 17 of the PWDVA is the right to residence, and BNSS Section 479 concerns release of undertrials.
128.tq: CrPC 125 → BNSS 144.
xs: The secular maintenance route is now **Sec. 144 BNSS**, replacing **Sec. 125 CrPC** — option **(1)**.
**Sec. 17** of the **DV Act 2005** is the **Right to Residence**, not maintenance.
xa: **Shah Bano (1985)** granted maintenance under **s.125 CrPC**.
The **1986** Muslim Women (Divorce) Act followed.
Marital rape exception now under **BNS s.63** is being challenged (**10 Sep 2026**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding surrogacy under the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act, 2021:
1. Commercial surrogacy is prohibited.
2. A woman can be a surrogate only once.
3. Sex selection is permitted if the surrogate gives written consent.
4. The couple requires certificates of essentiality and eligibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Sex selection is prohibited and cannot be permitted merely through the surrogate’s consent.
128.tq: Use one reversed prohibition to eliminate an otherwise attractive combination.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 4** are correct — option **(2)**.
**Commercial** surrogacy is banned; a woman can be a surrogate only **once**.
The couple needs **certificates of essentiality and eligibility**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **sex selection is prohibited**.
xa: **Altruistic** surrogacy allowed (medical costs, insurance only).
**Abandoning the child** is also prohibited.
⚠ "Abortion of surrogate child prohibited" was **NOT** in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).

128.s: A foetus carried through surrogacy may be aborted under the applicable law only when
o: the intending couple alone gives consent
the ART clinic recommends it without further approval
the surrogate gives written consent and authorisation is obtained under the MTP Act
the surrogate’s consent is specifically excluded
128.x: Abortion of a surrogate foetus is not prohibited outright. It requires the surrogate’s written consent and authorisation under the MTP Act.
128.tq: Apply the exception to a general prohibition instead of treating abortion as absolutely banned.
xs: A surrogate foetus may be aborted with the **surrogate's written consent** + **authorisation under the MTP Act** — option **(3)**.
It is **not banned outright**, and the couple's or clinic's say alone is not enough.
xa: ⚠ Trap: "abortion of the surrogate child is prohibited" was NOT in the **2019 Bill** (APPSC **2018**).
**MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021**: up to **20 weeks** on one doctor's opinion.
A woman can be a surrogate only **once**.

128.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the ART (Regulation) Act, 2021?
o: National registry — Regulatory record of ART institutions
Sale of gametes or embryos — Prohibited
128.x: Sex-selective ART is prohibited under the ART Act, 2021. Registered clinics and banks and a national registry are permitted regulatory arrangements.
128.tq: Locate the option that reverses a statutory prohibition.
xs: **Sex-selective ART — Permitted** is wrong — option **(2)**: the **ART Act 2021** **prohibits** it.
**Registered ART clinics and banks** and a **national registry** are permitted; **sale of gametes/embryos** is prohibited.
xa: **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
The **Surrogacy Act 2021** also prohibits **sex selection**.
Commercial surrogacy is banned.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021:
1. Termination up to 20 weeks may be undertaken on one doctor’s opinion.
2. Termination up to 24 weeks is available for special categories.
3. Beyond 24 weeks, a State Medical Board may permit termination for substantial foetal abnormality.
4. The woman’s identity may be disclosed without restriction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Act prohibits disclosure of the woman’s identity, so statement 4 is false.
128.tq: Combine statutory limits with the confidentiality safeguard and reject the reversed statement.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Up to **20 weeks**: one doctor's opinion; **24 weeks**: special categories.
Beyond **24 weeks**: only for **substantial foetal abnormality**, decided by a State **Medical Board**.
Statement 4 is wrong: **disclosing the woman's identity** is prohibited.
xa: Beyond 24 weeks **no gestation limit** applies.
**SC (2022)** removed **marital-status distinctions** for abortion access (**Art. 14**).
Surrogate foetus abortion needs consent + MTP Act approval.

128.s: The PCPNDT Act, 1994 prohibits
o: Sex selection and prenatal sex determination
Termination of pregnancy up to 20 weeks
128.x: The PCPNDT Act bans sex selection and prenatal sex determination. Tests are allowed for detecting genetic abnormalities.
128.tq: Distinguish the prohibited diagnostic purpose from permitted testing for genetic abnormality.
xs: The **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans **sex selection and pre-natal sex determination** — option **(2)**.
Tests are allowed **for genetic abnormality**, so not all tests are banned; termination up to **20 weeks** is under the **MTP Act**.
xa: Sex ratio at birth rose from **904 (2017-19)** to **917 (2021-23)**.
Most male-skewed: **Haryana, Punjab**; best SRB: **Kerala** and the **North-East**.
The **ART Act 2021** also prohibits sex-selective ART.

128.s: The Supreme Court’s 2022 ruling on abortion access removed distinctions based on
o: The State in which the woman resides
128.x: The Supreme Court in 2022 removed marital-status distinctions in access to abortion, invoking Article 14.
128.tq: Identify the exact discriminatory distinction removed by the judgment.
xs: The **SC (2022)** removed distinctions based on **marital status** for abortion access — option **(3)**, under **Art. 14**.
Doctor's age, State of residence or ART use were never the issue.
xa: **MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021**: **20 weeks** one doctor; **24 weeks** special categories.
Beyond 24 weeks: **substantial foetal abnormality** → State **Medical Board**.
The woman's identity cannot be disclosed.

128.s: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 was enacted to provide for
o: equal pay for equal work and absence of sex bias in recruitment and promotion
128.x: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 addressed equal pay for equal work and prohibited gender bias in recruitment and promotion.
128.tq: Separate the employment-equality statute from maternity and marriage laws.
xs: The **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976** gives **equal pay for equal work** and **no sex bias in recruitment or promotion** — option **(4)**.
**26 weeks** leave is the **Maternity Benefit (Amendment) 2017**; civil marriage is the **Special Marriage Act 1954**.
xa: It flows from **Art. 39(d)**.
It is now subsumed in the **Code on Wages, 2019**.
Code on Wages (Central) Rules notified **8 May 2026**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Code on Wages, 2019:
1. It subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976.
2. It bans wage and recruitment discrimination on gender, including against transgender persons.
3. It does not provide for a statutory floor wage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Code subsumes the Equal Remuneration Act (with the Minimum Wages, Payment of Wages and Payment of Bonus Acts) and bans gender discrimination including against transgender persons. Statement 3 is wrong: the Code provides a statutory floor wage. Hence A; B, C and D include statement 3.
128.tq: Code on Wages = subsumes ERA + bans gender bias incl. transgender + floor wage.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: the **Code on Wages, 2019** subsumes the **Equal Remuneration Act 1976** — correct.
Statement 2: it bans gender discrimination **including transgender persons** — correct.
Statement 3: it **does** provide a statutory **floor wage** — wrong.
xa: It also subsumes the **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Payment of Wages Act 1936**, **Payment of Bonus Act 1965**.
**Code on Wages (Central) Rules** notified **8 May 2026**.
**OSH Code 2020** governs women's **night shifts**.

128.s: Which of the following enactments was NOT absorbed into the Code on Wages, 2019?
128.x: The Code on Wages, 2019 absorbed the Equal Remuneration Act, Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act and Payment of Bonus Act. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 was not among these four enactments.
128.tq: Find the statute outside the specific group of laws subsumed by the Code.
xs: The **Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017** was not absorbed — option **(4)**.
The Code subsumes the **Minimum Wages Act 1948**, **Payment of Wages Act 1936**, **Payment of Bonus Act 1965** and the **Equal Remuneration Act 1976**.
xa: The 2017 amendment raised leave to **26 weeks**.
The Code bans discrimination **including against transgender persons**.
It sets a statutory **floor wage**.

128.s: Under the OSH Code, 2020, women may work before 6 a.m. or after 7 p.m. when
o: the work is performed only in government offices
the employer gives permission without any further condition
they consent and prescribed safety safeguards are provided
the worker has completed ten years of service
128.x: The OSH Code, 2020 permits women to work during these hours with their consent and subject to safety safeguards.
128.tq: Identify the conditional permission instead of treating it as an unrestricted power of the employer.
xs: Under the **OSH Code 2020**, women may work before **6 a.m.** or after **7 p.m.** **with consent and safety safeguards** — option **(3)**.
Not unconditional employer permission, nor limited to government offices.
xa: The **Code on Wages, 2019** subsumes four wage laws.
The **Equal Remuneration Act 1976** flows from **Art. 39(d)**.
**Art. 42**: just and humane work conditions, **maternity relief**.

128.s: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 provides for paid maternity leave of
128.x: The 2017 amendment raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks for women with fewer than two surviving children (at most 8 weeks before delivery); from the third child it stays 12 weeks.
128.tq: Recall the exact statutory duration and distinguish it from other leave periods.
xs: The **2017 amendment** gives **26 weeks** paid leave (from **12**) — option **(2)**.
It applies to women with fewer than **two surviving children**; at most **8 weeks before delivery**.
xa: **Third child**: **12 weeks**.
**Adopting / commissioning mothers**: **12 weeks** from handing over.
⚠ "**3 months pre + 3 months post-delivery**" is wrong (UPSC **2019**).

128.s: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, the paid maternity leave was:
o: 26 weeks for all establishments irrespective of size
8 weeks for establishments with 20 or more employees
16 weeks for establishments with 50 or more employees
12 weeks for establishments with 10 or more employees
128.x: The 1961 Act provided 12 weeks of paid maternity leave and applied to establishments employing 10 or more persons.
128.tq: Keep the leave duration and establishment threshold together; both are required for the correct option.
xs: The **1961 Act** gave **12 weeks** paid leave in establishments with **10+** employees — option **(4)**.
**26 weeks** came only with the **2017 amendment**.
xa: The 2017 amendment: **creche** where **50+ employees**, with **4 visits** a day.
**Work-from-home** after leave **by mutual agreement**.
Contract/fellowship researchers often fall outside the Act (**19 May 2026**).

128.s: In Rakhi Bisht v. Union of India, the Delhi High Court held that maternity protection also covers:
o: Only salary and leave, excluding the post held
Appointment to a higher post irrespective of eligibility
Only promotion, but not status or posting
Post, status and promotion, with entitlement to the same or an equivalent post on return
128.x: The Delhi High Court held that maternity protection extends to post, status and promotion. A returning woman is entitled to the same or an equivalent post, not automatically to a higher post.
128.tq: Reject the narrowed or exaggerated versions of a judicial protection principle.
xs: **Rakhi Bisht v Union of India (Delhi HC)** held maternity protection covers **post, status and promotion** — the returning woman gets the **same or an equivalent post** — option **(4)**.
It does not give a higher post irrespective of eligibility, nor is it limited to salary or promotion.
xa: Ruling dated **2 Sep 2026**.
**Maternity Benefit (Amendment) 2017**: **26 weeks** for the first two children.
**Art. 42**: **maternity relief**.

128.s: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, the maternity benefit for the third child onwards is:
128.x: The 2017 position provides 12 weeks of maternity benefit for the third child onwards. The longer period applies to the first two children.
128.tq: Distinguish the benefit applicable to later children from the first-two-children provision.
xs: From the **third child**, the benefit is **12 weeks** — option **(2)**.
**26 weeks** applies only to women with fewer than **two surviving children**.
xa: The **1961 Act** gave **12 weeks** to all.
Adopting (child under **3 months**) and commissioning mothers: **12 weeks**.
Up to **8 weeks before delivery**.

128.s: A woman adopting a child below three months of age is entitled under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 to maternity benefit for:
o: Six weeks from the date of adoption
Twelve weeks from the date the child is handed over to her
Twenty-six weeks from the date of adoption in every case
Eight weeks before the adoption and four weeks after it
128.x: An adopting mother of a child below three months is entitled to 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to her. The same 12-week period applies to a commissioning mother.
128.tq: Focus on both the eligibility condition and the statutory starting point.
xs: An adopting mother (child under **3 months**) gets **twelve weeks** from the date the child is **handed over** — option **(2)**.
The same **12 weeks** applies to a **commissioning mother**.
xa: ⚠ Some notes wrongly say **26** for adopting mothers.
**26 weeks** is for biological mothers with fewer than **two surviving children**.
**Creche**: **50+ employees**, **4 visits** a day.

128.s: A crèche facility is mandatory under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 in an establishment having:
o: 20 or more employees, with two visits a day
100 or more employees, with one visit a day
30 or more employees, with three visits a day
50 or more employees, with four visits a day
128.x: The amendment requires a crèche in establishments having 50 or more employees. The woman is to be allowed four visits a day to the crèche.
128.tq: Combine the threshold number with the associated statutory frequency.
xs: A **creche** is compulsory where there are **50+ employees**, with **4 visits** a day — option **(4)**.
Other thresholds in the options are not in the Act.
xa: **Work-from-home** after leave if work allows, **by mutual agreement**.
The **1961 Act** covered establishments with **10+** employees.
**26 weeks** leave for the first two children.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding work from home under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017:
1. It may be allowed after the period of maternity leave.
2. It is available where the nature of work permits it.
3. It requires mutual agreement between the woman and the employer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Work from home may be permitted after maternity leave where the nature of work allows it and where there is mutual agreement between the woman and the employer. Thus all three statements are correct.
128.tq: Check the cumulative conditions rather than treating work from home as an automatic right.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**Work-from-home** comes **after leave**, **if the nature of work allows**, and **by mutual agreement**.
xa: **Creche**: **50+ employees**, **4 visits** a day.
**26 weeks** for the first two children; **12 weeks** from the third.
**Rakhi Bisht (Delhi HC)**: a returning woman gets the same or an equivalent post.

128.s:
With reference to the National Commission for Women, consider the following statements:
1. It is a statutory body.
2. It was created under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
3. It was constituted in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: All three statements are correct. The NCW is statutory, derives its authority from the 1990 Act and was constituted in 1992.
128.tq: Check whether the question distinguishes the year of the Act from the year of constitution.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The NCW is **statutory**, set up under the **NCW Act 1990**, and constituted in **Jan 1992**.
xa: Composition: Chairperson + **5 members** (at least one **SC**, one **ST**) + Member-Secretary.
Functions: review laws, complaints and **suo motu** notice, inspect jails/remand homes, police gender sensitisation.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990** but **set up Jan 1992**.
First women's court: **West Bengal**, **Malda, 2013** (APPSC **2019**).

128.s: India's first exclusive women's court was set up in which State?
128.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal, at Malda in 2013 (APPSC 2019). Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are distractors.
128.tq: First women's court: Malda, West Bengal, 2013.
xs: India's first women's court was set up in **West Bengal**, at **Malda** in **2013** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2019**).
Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra are not linked with the first women's court in the notes.
xa: **Family Courts Act 1984**: **953** Family Courts in **29** States/UTs (as of **31 Jul 2025**).
**NCW Act 1990**; NCW set up **Jan 1992**.
Kerala instead stands out for the **best sex ratio at birth**, with the North-East.

128.s: Under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, the Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Member-Secretary and:
o: three members, at least one from the Scheduled Castes
five members, at least one each from the SCs and the STs
seven members, all nominated by the Chief Justice of India
five members, all of whom must be retired judges
128.x: The NCW has a Chairperson, five members (at least one SC and one ST) and a Member-Secretary. The counts of three and seven are wrong, and there is no requirement that members be retired judges or nominated by the CJI.
128.tq: NCW = Chair + 5 (≥1 SC, ≥1 ST) + Member-Secretary.
xs: The NCW has a Chairperson, **five members (at least one SC, one ST)** and a Member-Secretary — option **(2)**.
Three or seven members, CJI nomination or retired judges are not in the **NCW Act 1990**.
xa: NCW functions: review safeguards and laws, take complaints and **suo motu** notice.
It inspects **jails/remand homes**, does research and **police gender sensitisation**.
⚠ NCW **Act 1990**, but **set up Jan 1992**.

128.s: Which of the following correctly represents the sex ratio figures reported by NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 respectively?
128.x: The sex ratio was 991 in NFHS-4 and increased to 1020 in NFHS-5.
128.tq: Read the direction of change and distinguish survey figures from census figures.
xs: Sex ratio: **NFHS-4: 991**, **NFHS-5: 1020** — option **(3)**.
Option (1) reverses them; **904 and 917** are **sex ratio at birth** figures from MoSPI.
xa: Sex ratio at birth rose from **904 (2017-19)** to **917 (2021-23)** (**Women and Men in India 2025**, **27th edition**).
NFHS-5 also records **32%** spousal violence.
Causes of low ratio: **son preference**, female foeticide/infanticide, dowry, neglect of girls.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated cause of a low sex ratio?
128.x: Son preference, female foeticide or infanticide, dowry and neglect of girls are stated causes of a low sex ratio. Equal inheritance and universal schooling are not listed as causes.
128.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the causal group.
xs: **Equal inheritance and universal schooling** are not causes of a low sex ratio — option **(2)**.
The stated causes are **son preference**, **female foeticide/infanticide**, **dowry** and **neglect of girls**.
xa: **PCPNDT Act 1994** bans sex selection and pre-natal sex determination.
Most male-skewed: **Haryana, Punjab**; best SRB: **Kerala** and the **North-East**.
**Female Infanticide Prevention Act**: **1870**.

128.s: The Gender Development Index primarily compares females and males with respect to
o: population density, rainfall and literacy alone
health, education and command over resources
128.x: The GDI makes a female-to-male comparison in health, education and command over resources.
128.tq: Identify the exact dimensions of a composite gender index.
xs: The **GDI** is a female-to-male comparison on **health, education and command over resources** — option **(4)**.
Density, military strength or judicial appointments are not its dimensions.
xa: The **GII** was proposed to fix the GDI's gaps.
⚠ The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale belongs to the **GII**, not the GDI.
**Global Gender Gap Index (WEF)**: economic participation, education, health and survival, political empowerment.

128.s: Which statement regarding the Gender Inequality Index is correct?
o: It measures only sex ratio at birth.
It was proposed to address gaps in the GDI.
It is identical to the Global Gender Gap Index.
It was created by the World Economic Forum to measure political empowerment alone.
128.x: The GII was proposed to address limitations or gaps in the GDI. It is distinct from the WEF’s Global Gender Gap Index.
128.tq: Separate similar-sounding indices by their purpose and institutional association.
xs: The **GII** was **proposed to fix the GDI's gaps** — option **(2)**.
It is not the **Global Gender Gap Index**, which is the **WEF's**; nor does it measure only sex ratio at birth.
xa: ⚠ The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale is the GII's.
**GDI**: health, education and command over resources.
Women, Peace and Security Index **2023**: India **131/177**.

128.s: The 0 to 1 scale in which 0 denotes equality and 1 denotes the worst outcome belongs to the
128.x: The 0-to-1 scale, where 0 represents equality and 1 the worst outcome, belongs to the Gender Inequality Index, not the GDI.
128.tq: Correct a commonly confused index-scale association.
xs: The **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)** scale belongs to the **Gender Inequality Index** — option **(2)**.
⚠ Notes that give this scale for the **GDI** are wrong.
xa: The GII was **proposed to fix GDI's gaps**.
**GDI**: female-to-male comparison on health, education, command over resources.
**Global Gender Gap Index** is the **WEF's**.

128.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the dimensions of the Global Gender Gap Index?
128.x: The Global Gender Gap Index covers economic participation, education, health and survival, and political empowerment. Military expenditure is not one of its dimensions.
128.tq: Find the unrelated dimension in a list of index components.
xs: **Military expenditure** is not a Global Gender Gap Index dimension — option **(3)**.
Its dimensions: **economic participation**, **education**, **health and survival**, **political empowerment**.
xa: The index is published by the **WEF**.
**GII** fixes GDI gaps; scale **0 (equal) to 1 (worst)**.
**Women, Peace and Security Index 2023**: India **131/177**.

128.s: India’s female labour force participation rate increased from 23.3% in 2017–18 to _____ in 2022–23.
128.x: Women’s labour force participation rate rose from 23.3% in 2017–18 to 37% in 2022–23.
128.tq: Identify the later value in a two-period percentage comparison.
xs: That is a jump of well over half; **27%**, **31%** and **47%** are not the recorded figures.
xa: **APSES 2024-25 (SDG 5)** names **women in the labour force** as a gap for AP.
**Code on Wages, 2019** bans wage and recruitment discrimination on gender.
**OSH Code 2020** allows women night shifts with **consent and safety safeguards**.

128.s: Which of the following correctly describes the regional pattern of sex ratio in India?
o: Kerala and the North-East are the most male-skewed, while Punjab has the best sex ratio
Haryana and Punjab are the most male-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East have the best sex-ratio balance
Haryana and Punjab are the most female-skewed, while Kerala and the North-East are male-skewed
There is no marked regional variation in the sex ratio between northern and southern India
128.x: Haryana and Punjab are identified as the most male-skewed region, whereas Kerala and the North-East, including Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Mizoram, have the best sex-ratio balance.
128.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap by distinguishing the north-western pattern from the southern and north-eastern pattern.
xs: **Haryana and Punjab** are most **male-skewed**; **Kerala and the North-East** have the **best** sex ratio at birth — option **(2)**.
Options (1) and (3) reverse the pattern; (4) denies a pattern that the data show.
xa: North-East best: **Arunachal, Meghalaya, Mizoram** (CRS **2024**).
NFHS-5 sex ratio: **1020** (NFHS-4: **991**).

128.s: According to Women and Men in India 2025, the SRS-based sex ratio at birth changed from 2017–19 to 2021–23 as follows:
128.x: The SRS-based figure increased from 904 during 2017–19 to 917 during 2021–23.
128.tq: Read the direction of change and retain the correct time sequence.
xs: Option (2) reverses it.
xa: Source: **Women and Men in India 2025** (**MoSPI**, **27th edition**).
NFHS-5 overall sex ratio: **1020**; NFHS-4: **991**.
Main cause of low ratio: **son preference**.

128.s: The statement that “the world's welfare is impossible unless women's condition improves; a bird cannot fly on one wing” is associated with
128.x: This observation is associated with Swami Vivekananda.
128.tq: Discriminate among leaders linked with statements on women’s progress.
xs: "A bird cannot fly on one wing" — **Swami Vivekananda** — option **(1)**.
**Ambedkar**: "progress of a **community**"; **Nehru**: "condition of a **nation**"; **Gandhi**: "weaker sex is a libel".
xa: ⚠ "**community**" = Ambedkar (APPSC-G2 **2025**); "**nation**" = Nehru (APPSC **2019**).
Vivekananda's point: the world's welfare is impossible unless women's condition improves.
**Gandhi**: calling woman the weaker sex is man's injustice to woman.

128.s: Who stated, “To call woman the weaker sex is a libel; it is man's injustice to woman”?
128.x: The statement was made by Mahatma Gandhi.
128.tq: Direct quotation-based recall with closely related leader options.
xs: "To call woman the weaker sex is a libel" — **Mahatma Gandhi** — option **(4)**.
**Vivekananda**: bird on one wing; **Nehru**: condition of a nation; **Ambedkar**: progress of a community.
xa: ⚠ "**community**" = **Ambedkar**; "**nation**" = **Nehru**.
Ambedkar's quote was asked in APPSC-G2 **2025**; Nehru's in APPSC **2019**.

128.s:
Match List-I (Statement) with List-II (Leader):

List-I
a. "I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved"
b. "You can tell the condition of a nation by looking at the status of its women"
c. A bird cannot fly on one wing
d. "To call woman the weaker sex is a libel"

List-II
i. Swami Vivekananda
ii. Jawaharlal Nehru
iii. B.R. Ambedkar
iv. Mahatma Gandhi
128.x: Ambedkar measured a community's progress by the progress of its women (APPSC-G2 2025); Nehru said a nation's condition can be told from the status of its women (APPSC 2019); Vivekananda used the one-wing image; Gandhi called the 'weaker sex' label a libel. The other codes swap Ambedkar with Nehru or Gandhi, or Vivekananda with Gandhi.
128.tq: Ambedkar - community; Nehru - nation.
xs: **a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv** — option **(1)**.
Progress of a **community** – **Ambedkar**; condition of a **nation** – **Nehru**.
Bird on one wing – **Vivekananda**; weaker sex a libel – **Gandhi**.
xa: ⚠ Swapping **Ambedkar** and **Nehru** is the usual trap.
Ambedkar quote: APPSC-G2 **2025**; Nehru quote: APPSC **2019**.

128.s: ‘Nirbhay Raho’, associated with the Nirbhaya Fund, works through which institutional channel?
128.x: Nirbhay Raho works through Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).
128.tq: Match the programme with its implementation channel rather than with the fund alone.
xs: **Nirbhay Raho** (**Nirbhaya Fund**) works through **Panchayati Raj Institutions** — option **(1)** (Jun **2026**).
It is not routed through parliamentary committees, urban bodies only, or State Election Commissions.
xa: About **46%** of PRI representatives are women.
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** trains women elected representatives.
Crimes against women: **4,41,534** in **2024**.

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the current constitutional and legal debate on gender justice:
1. Challenges to the marital rape exception under BNS Section 63 have reached the Supreme Court.
2. The debate on a Uniform Civil Code involves questions relating to Articles 25 and 29.
3. A gender-justice approach necessarily requires religious exemptions in every matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 2 correctly identify the current debates. Statement 3 is false because the criticism is that gender justice should not be made subject to religious exemption.
128.tq: Find the statement that reverses the central criticism by using an absolute claim such as ‘necessarily’ and ‘every’.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: the SC is hearing challenges to the **marital rape exception** under **BNS s.63** — correct.
Statement 2: the **UCC** debate involves **Art. 25/29** — correct.
Statement 3: the critique is that **gender justice needs no religious exemption** — wrong.
xa: **Art. 44**: **Uniform Civil Code**.
**Shah Bano** and **Sarla Mudgal** both urged a UCC.
**Joseph Shine (2018)** struck down **adultery** (**s.497 IPC**).

128.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill, 2026:
1. It sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats to speed up the 33% women's quota of the 2023 Act.
2. It was passed by Parliament on 17 April 2026.
3. The 33% quota still waits for the Census and delimitation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Bill aimed to redistribute Lok Sabha seats to speed up the quota, which still waits for Census and delimitation. Statement 2 is wrong: the Opposition defeated the Bill on 17 April 2026. Hence C; A, B and D include statement 2.
128.tq: 131st Bill = defeated; quota tied to Census + delimitation.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(3)**.
Statement 1: the **131st Amendment Bill** sought to **redistribute Lok Sabha seats** to speed up the **33%** quota (**2023** Act) — correct.
Statement 2: it was **defeated** by the Opposition on **17 Apr 2026**, not passed — wrong.
Statement 3: the quota still waits for **Census and delimitation** — correct.
xa: The same day, the quota took effect in the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies.
Women's groups want the Census/delimitation link removed (**20 Apr 2026**).
**Arts. 330A / 332A**: **1/3** seats in Lok Sabha / State Assemblies.

128.s: According to the National Family Health Survey-5 figure cited in the context of women's rights, what proportion of women reported spousal violence?
128.x: The cited NFHS-5 figure for spousal violence is 32%.
128.tq: Distinguish the percentage figure from the separate absolute figure for crimes against women.
xs: **NFHS-5** records **32%** spousal violence — option **(3)**.
The figure was cited in the crime-data debate on women's rights (**22 Jun 2026**).
xa: **4,41,534** crimes against women in **2024**.
**DV Act 2005**: **Right to Residence (Sec. 17)**; decide within **60 days**.
NFHS-5 sex ratio: **1020**.

128.s: Which criticism has been raised against the women's movement in relation to social stratification?
o: It has removed the need for legal reform.
It has focused exclusively on rural women.
It has opposed all forms of local representation.
128.x: One criticism is that the women's movement has neglected women belonging to lower social strata.
128.tq: Identify the specific criticism instead of selecting an extreme statement about the entire movement.
xs: The movement has been criticised for **neglecting lower-strata women** — option **(4)** (UPSC Mains **2018**).
It did not abandon legal reform or local representation; the charge concerns **social stratification**.
xa: **Uma Chakravarti**: **Brahmanical patriarchy** vs Dalit patriarchy.
**Gail Omvedt**: **Dalit/Bahujan feminism**.
Another critique: **"proxy" women heads** in panchayats.

128.s:
According to the APSES 2024–25 assessment under Sustainable Development Goal 5, which of the following were identified as gaps in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Women's participation in the labour force
2. Institution building
3. Crime against women
Which of the statements given above are correct?
128.x: APSES 2024–25 identifies all three—women's participation in the labour force, institution building and crime against women—as gaps under SDG 5.
128.tq: Check whether all listed dimensions belong to the same assessment rather than treating crime and development indicators separately.
xs: All three are gaps — option **(4)**.
**APSES 2024-25 (SDG 5)** lists **women in the labour force**, **institution building** and **crime against women**.
xa: AP gives **50%** quotas in local bodies and nominated posts.
AP's daughters' property law: **1985**.
National women's LFPR: **37%** (**2022-23**).

128.s: Which one of the following is associated with the criticism of ‘proxy’ representation in Panchayati Raj institutions?
o: Transfer of all Panchayat powers to Parliament
Women elected as representatives but effectively controlled by others
Removal of the marital rape exception
Redistribution of Lok Sabha seats after delimitation
128.x: The expression ‘proxy’ women heads refers to situations in which elected women representatives are effectively controlled by others in local governance.
128.tq: Apply the institutional term to a short governance scenario rather than recalling it in isolation.
xs: **"Proxy" women heads** = women elected but **effectively controlled by others** — option **(2)**.
It is a panchayat-level critique, unrelated to marital rape or Lok Sabha delimitation.
xa: About **46%** of PRI representatives are women (**26 Jan 2026**).
**Art. 243D**: at least **one-third** seats and chairpersons' offices in Panchayats.
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** trains women representatives.

129.s: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act was originally known as SITA and was amended in:
129.x: The law was enacted in 1956 as the Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA) and was renamed the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act by the 1986 amendment. 1986 is the amendment year, not the enactment year; 1961, 1994 and 2003 relate to the Dowry Act, PNDT Act and its renaming.
129.tq: Distinguish the original enactment year from the amendment year.
xs: The law was **renamed ITPA by the 1986 amendment** — option **(2)**; it began in **1956** as the **Suppression of Immoral Traffic Act (SITA)**.
**1961** = **Dowry Prohibition Act**; **1994** = **PCPNDT (PNDT) Act**; **2003** = PNDT's renaming.
xa: ⚠ ITPA is a **1956** law; "ITPA 1986" refers only to its **amendment year**.
It gives effect to the **1950 UN Convention**.
It does **not criminalise prostitution itself**; **protective homes** are run by states.

129.s: The PCPNDT Act is associated with which of the following pairs of years?
o: 1994; the PNDT law was renamed in 2003
129.x: The law was enacted in 1994 as the PNDT Act and was renamed the PCPNDT Act in 2003.
129.tq: Test the enactment year separately from the later renaming year.
xs: The **PCPNDT Act** dates from **1994**; the PNDT law was **renamed in 2003** — option **(4)**.
**1987** is the **Sati Act**; **2006** the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act**; **2019** the triple talaq Act.
xa: ⚠ Don't confuse with **1986** (ITPA renamed) and **1987** (Sati Act).
**Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act**: **1987**, in force **1988**.
**Dowry Prohibition Act**: **1961**.

129.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act — 2006
Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987; came into force in 1988
129.x: The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act was enacted in 1987 and came into force in 1988. The Indecent Representation Act dates to 1986, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act to 2006 and the Muslim Women Act concerning triple talaq to 2019.
129.tq: Use neighbouring enactment years to expose swapped law-year pairs.
xs: **Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act — 1987**, in force **1988** — option **(2)**.
**Muslim Women (Marriage) Act** = **2019**, not 2006; **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act** = **2006**, not 2019.
The **Indecent Representation Act** is not of **1994** — that is the **PCPNDT Act**.
xa: The Sati Act punishes **attempt, abetment and glorification**.
The **DM** may seize property used for glorification.
The triple talaq Act was passed on **30 July 2019**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act bans denigrating depiction of women in advertisements and publications.
2. Monitoring under the law has been extended to digital and AI-generated content.
3. The Commission of Sati (Prevention) Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification of sati.
4. A District Magistrate may seize property used for glorification of sati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The Indecent Representation law covers denigrating depiction and, as of 2025, monitoring extends to digital and AI-generated content. The Sati Act punishes attempt, abetment and glorification, and permits the District Magistrate to seize property used for glorification.
129.tq: Combine provisions from two related women-protection laws while checking each statement independently.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
The **Indecent Representation Act** bans denigrating depiction in ads and publications; monitoring extended to **digital and AI-generated content (2025)**.
The **Sati Act** punishes **attempt, abetment and glorification**; the **DM** may seize property used for glorification.
xa: Sati Act: **1987**, in force **1988**.
**ITPA 1956** began as **SITA**.
**PCPNDT Act 1994** (renamed **2003**).

129.s: Under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, the term ‘dowry’ refers to:
o: Only property demanded by the bride’s family before marriage
Property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage
Any gift exchanged between the spouses after marriage, including mahr
Only cash or movable property given after marriage
129.x: Dowry includes property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage, in connection with the marriage. Dower or mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded.
129.tq: Test the exact statutory definition and distinguish the excluded term.
xs: **Dowry (s.2)** = property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, **directly or indirectly**, in connection with marriage — option **(2)**.
It covers **before, at or any time after marriage**, not just one stage or only cash.
**Dower/mahr** under Muslim personal law is **excluded**.
xa: The Act came into force on **1 July 1961** (APPSC **2025**).
It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Amendments of **1984 and 1986**.

129.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961?
o: Section 3 — Giving, taking or abetting dowry
Section 8A — Burden of proof on the accused
Section 8B — Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the Central Government
129.x: Section 8B provides for Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Government, not the Central Government. Sections 3, 4 and 8A are correctly matched.
129.tq: Find the wrong authority attached to a statutory power.
xs: **s.8B — officers appointed by the Central Government** is wrong — option **(3)**: **Dowry Prohibition Officers** are appointed by the **State Govt**.
**s.3**: giving, taking or abetting; **s.4**: demanding; **s.8A**: **burden of proof on the accused** — all correct.
xa: s.3 penalty: **not less than 5 years** + fine **not less than ₹15,000** or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
s.4 penalty: **6 months to 2 years** + fine up to **Rs 10,000**.
Offences are **cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961:
1. Giving or taking dowry (s.3) is punishable with imprisonment of up to five years at most.
2. Demanding dowry (s.4) is punishable with imprisonment of six months to two years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
129.x: Statement 1 is wrong: s.3 fixes five years as the minimum (not less than 5 years) plus a fine of not less than Rs 15,000 or the dowry's value, whichever is more. Statement 2 is correct: demanding dowry attracts 6 months to 2 years. Hence 2 only (B); A, C and D are wrong.
129.tq: Trap: five years is the MINIMUM for giving/taking, not the maximum.
xs: Only statement **2** is correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1: **s.3** fixes **5 years** as the **minimum**, not the maximum — wrong.
Statement 2: **demanding** dowry (**s.4**) = **6 months to 2 years** — correct.
xa: ⚠ Notes saying "up to five years" are wrong.
s.3 fine: at least **₹15,000** or the dowry's value, whichever is more.
s.4 fine: up to **Rs 10,000**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961:
1. The offences are cognisable.
2. The offences are non-bailable.
3. The offences are non-compoundable.
4. The burden of proof lies on the accused.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. Section 8A places the burden of proof on the accused; therefore all four statements are correct.
129.tq: Check each legal characteristic separately before selecting the comprehensive combination.
xs: All four statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Dowry offences are **cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable**.
**s.8A** puts the **burden of proof on the accused**.
xa: Courts may act on their **own knowledge** or on complaints by **recognised welfare bodies**.
**s.8B**: **Dowry Prohibition Officers** appointed by the State Govt.
~**20** dowry deaths a day, **6,000+** a year.

129.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to dowry-related criminal law after the transition from the IPC to the BNS?
o: Dowry death — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 304B
Cruelty — BNS Section 80; corresponding IPC Section 498A
Presumption of dowry death — BNS Section 85; corresponding Evidence Act Section 113B
Dowry death — BNS Section 86; corresponding IPC Section 304B
129.x: Dowry death is covered by BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B. Cruelty is covered by BNS Sections 85 and 86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A, while the presumption is under BSA Section 118, corresponding to Evidence Act Section 113B.
129.tq: Match the new BNS provision with its former IPC counterpart.
xs: **Dowry death — BNS s.80** (IPC **304B**) — option **(1)**.
**Cruelty** is **BNS 85-86** (IPC **498A**), not s.80; dowry death is not s.86.
**Presumption of dowry death** is **BSA s.118** (Evidence Act **113B**), not BNS 85.
xa: Dowry death = death within **7 years** of marriage.
IPC → BNS from **1 July 2024**.

129.s: For the purpose of the offence of dowry death, death occurring within what period from the date of marriage is specifically relevant?
129.x: BNS Section 80, corresponding to IPC Section 304B, concerns dowry death where the death occurs within seven years of marriage, subject to the other legal requirements.
129.tq: Use the statutory time-limit as the decisive numerical clue.
xs: Dowry death covers death **within seven years** (**7 years**) of marriage — option **(2)**.
It is **BNS s.80**, the old IPC **304B**.
xa: Presumption: **BSA s.118** (Evidence Act **113B**).
The **1986** amendment brought in dowry death.
**Guntur** special court gave **life imprisonment** in a **2020** dowry-death case (**2026**).

129.s:
The amendments of 1984 and 1986 to the dowry-related legal framework are significant because the 1986 changes brought in:
1. The offence of dowry death under Section 304B of the IPC.
2. The presumption relating to dowry death under Section 113B of the Evidence Act.
3. The exclusion of mahr from the definition of dowry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: The 1986 changes introduced dowry death under IPC Section 304B and the presumption under Evidence Act Section 113B. The exclusion of mahr forms part of the statutory definition and was not the stated significance of the 1986 changes.
129.tq: Separate the amendment-specific developments from an independent definitional provision.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
The **1986** changes brought in **dowry death (Sec. 304B IPC)** and the presumption in **Sec. 113B** of the Evidence Act.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **mahr exclusion** belongs to the **s.2 definition**, not the 1986 change.
xa: Presumption now in **BSA s.118**.
Cruelty: **BNS s.85/86** (IPC **498A**).
Amendments were in **1984 and 1986**.

129.s: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 came into force on:
129.x: The Dowry Prohibition Act came into force on 1 July 1961 (APPSC-G2 2025). The other dates are distractors; 26 October is the date the Domestic Violence Act came into force, in 2006.
129.tq: Dowry Act in force 1 July 1961.
xs: The **Dowry Prohibition Act** came into force on **1 July 1961** — option **(2)** (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
**26 October** is the **DV Act's** commencement, in **2006**.
xa: It penalises **giving, taking or abetting** dowry.
Offences: **cognisable, non-bailable, non-compoundable**.
IPC → BNS also took effect on **1 July** (**2024**).

129.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is primarily classified as a:
129.x: The Act is a civil law protecting women from domestic violence, although other criminal provisions may also apply to related conduct.
129.tq: Discriminate between the civil character of the Act and criminal provisions dealing with particular offences.
xs: The **DV Act 2005** is a **civil law** (only civil) — option **(4)**.
⚠ CDI's list of criminal laws wrongly includes it.
xa: It protects women **irrespective of the relationship's status** with the respondent.
In force **26 October 2006** (UPPSC **2015**).
Reliefs: protection (**s.18**), residence (**s.19**), monetary (**s.20**), custody (**s.21**), compensation (**s.22**).

129.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the forms of domestic violence covered under Section 3 of the Domestic Violence Act?
o: Physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse
129.x: Section 3 covers physical, sexual, verbal or emotional, and economic abuse.
129.tq: Recall the complete statutory classification rather than selecting a partial list.
xs: **s.3** covers **physical, sexual, verbal/emotional and economic** abuse — option **(1)**.
It is not limited to two forms, and "political/electoral" abuse is not in it.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
Authorities: **Protection Officers**, registered **Service Providers**, the **Magistrate**.
Disposal within **60 days**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements about the scope of the Domestic Violence Act:
1. It protects a woman irrespective of the nature of her relationship with the respondent.
2. It applies only when the relationship has been formally registered.
3. Protection Officers and registered Service Providers assist the aggrieved woman.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because protection is not restricted to formally registered relationships.
129.tq: Spot the formal-registration limitation, which improperly narrows the Act's relationship-based protection.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: protects women **irrespective of the relationship's status** — correct.
Statement 2: no formal registration is needed — wrong.
Statement 3: **Protection Officers** and registered **Service Providers** assist the woman — correct.
xa: Protection Officers are appointed by the **State Govt**.
In AP: **DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs** as Protection Officers; **55 NGOs** as Service Providers.
The Act is purely **civil**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Protection Officers under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005:
1. They are appointed by the State Government.
2. In Andhra Pradesh, DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs act as Protection Officers.
3. In Andhra Pradesh, 55 NGOs act as Protection Officers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Protection Officers are appointed by the State Govt, and in AP they are DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs. Statement 3 is wrong: the 55 NGOs in AP are registered Service Providers, not Protection Officers. Hence A; B, C and D include statement 3.
129.tq: Protection Officers = State-appointed (AP: PDs, RDOs); NGOs = Service Providers.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1: Protection Officers are appointed by the **State Govt** — correct.
Statement 2: in AP, **DWCDA Project Directors and RDOs** serve as Protection Officers — correct.
Statement 3: the **55 NGOs** are **Service Providers**, not Protection Officers — wrong.
xa: AP SES 2025-26: **51,581** cases addressed; **₹9 crore** relief to **2,207** victims.
APSES 2024-25: **47,734** petitions; **23,644** Domestic Incident Reports; **7,307** final orders.

129.s:
Match the relief under the Domestic Violence Act with its section:

List-I (Relief)
 a. Protection order
 b. Residence order
 c. Monetary relief
 d. Compensation order

List-II (Section)
 i. Section 20
 ii. Section 22
 iii. Section 18
 iv. Section 19

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Protection orders are under Section 18, residence orders under Section 19, monetary relief under Section 20 and compensation orders under Section 22.
129.tq: Start with the familiar protection-order provision and verify the sequential relief sections.
xs: **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**Protection** – **s.18**; **Residence** – **s.19**; **Monetary relief** – **s.20**; **Compensation** – **s.22**.
xa: **s.21**: temporary **custody** of children.
**Sec. 17**: **right to reside**.
Multiple reliefs in one case; disposal within **60 days**.

129.s: Which of the following statements regarding reliefs under the Domestic Violence Act is correct?
o: Several forms of relief may be sought in one case and the matter is to be disposed of within 60 days.
Relief is limited to compensation and does not include residence rights.
Only one form of relief can be sought in a case.
Temporary custody cannot be granted under the Act.
129.x: Multiple reliefs may be sought in one case, including residence, protection, monetary relief, temporary custody and compensation; disposal is contemplated within 60 days.
129.tq: Reject absolute restrictions by applying the Act's cumulative-relief structure and time limit.
xs: **Multiple reliefs** can be sought in one case, disposed of within **60 days** — option **(1)**.
Reliefs include **residence** (**s.19**) and temporary **custody** (**s.21**), so the other options are wrong.
xa: **s.18**: protection; **s.20**: monetary relief; **s.22**: compensation.
**Sec. 17**: right to residence.
Domestic violence (**s.3**): physical, sexual, verbal/emotional, economic.

129.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 came into force on:
129.x: The PWDVA, though enacted in 2005, came into force on 26 October 2006 (UPPSC 2015). 1 July is the Dowry Act's commencement date (1961), December 2013 is when the POSH Act came into force, and 26 January 2006 is a distractor.
129.tq: PWDVA: enacted 2005, in force 26 Oct 2006.
xs: The **PWDVA** came into force on **26 October 2006** — option **(2)** (UPPSC **2015**).
**1 July** is the **Dowry Act's** date (**1961**); **Dec 2013** is when the **POSH Act** came into force.
xa: The Act is a **civil law**.
**Protection Officers** are appointed by the State Govt.
AP: **51,581** PWDVA cases (AP SES 2025-26).

129.s: The Prevention of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 primarily addresses which of the following?
o: Domestic violence against women in private households
Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
129.x: The POSH Act, 2013 addresses sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
129.tq: Directly identify the principal subject of the legislation.
xs: The **POSH Act 2013** addresses **sexual harassment of women at the workplace** — option **(3)** (APPSC **2018**).
Domestic violence is the **PWDVA 2005**; trafficking falls under **ITPA** and **BNS s.143**.
xa: It grew out of the **Vishaka guidelines (1997)**.
In force **Dec 2013**.
**Internal Committee** in workplaces with **10 or more employees**.

129.s: The guidelines laid down in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) were primarily concerned with:
o: Sexual harassment of women at the workplace
129.x: In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, the Supreme Court laid down guidelines concerning sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
129.tq: Use the case-name and subject association to distinguish closely related women-centric laws.
xs: **Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)** laid down guidelines on **sexual harassment of women at the workplace** — option **(2)**.
They stood until a law was enacted, leading to the **POSH Act, 2013**.
xa: **Laxmi v Union of India (2013)**: acid sale regulation, compensation, free treatment.
POSH **Local Committee** is set up by the **District Officer**.
Complaint within **3 months**; inquiry within **90 days**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sexual harassment under the POSH Act:
1. Unwelcome physical contact or advances may constitute sexual harassment.
2. A demand for sexual favours may constitute sexual harassment.
3. Showing pornography is excluded from the definition unless accompanied by physical contact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because showing pornography is itself included among the forms of sexual harassment.
129.tq: Find the excluded-looking statement that reverses an express part of the definition.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Unwelcome physical contact/advances** and **demands for sexual favours** are sexual harassment.
Statement 3 is wrong: **showing pornography** is itself in the definition.
xa: **Sexually coloured remarks** are also covered.
Internal Committee: **1 external NGO member**; half the members women.
Employer's penalty for non-compliance: up to **₹50,000**.

129.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
 a. Internal Committee
 b. Local Committee
 c. Internal Committee Presiding Officer
 d. Local Committee establishing authority

List-II (Feature)
 i. District Officer
 ii. Senior woman employee
 iii. Workplace with fewer than 10 employees
 iv. Workplace with 10 or more employees

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: The Internal Committee is set up in workplaces with 10 or more employees (a-iv) and is presided over by a senior woman employee (c-ii); the Local Committee serves workplaces with fewer than 10 employees (b-iii) and is constituted at district level by the District Officer (d-i). Hence A.
129.tq: Start with the sure pair of the senior woman Presiding Officer and eliminate mismatched codes.
xs: **a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i** — option **(1)**.
**IC**: workplace with **10 or more**; **LC**: fewer than **10** employees.
IC **Presiding Officer**: **senior woman employee**; LC set up by the **District Officer**.
xa: LC also hears **complaints against the employer**.
IC: **2+** employees, **1 external NGO member**, half women.

129.s: Which of the following correctly states the time limits under the POSH Act?
o: Complaint within 6 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 90 days
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 90 days and employer action within 60 days
Complaint within 90 days, inquiry within 3 months and employer action within 6 months
Complaint within 3 months, inquiry within 60 days and employer action within 30 days
129.x: The complaint is ordinarily filed within three months, the inquiry is to be completed within 90 days, and the employer is to act within 60 days.
129.tq: Keep the three separate statutory periods distinct instead of swapping their order.
xs: Complaint within **3 months**, inquiry within **90 days**, employer acts within **60 days** — option **(2)**.
The other options jumble these limits.
xa: The complaint period is **extendable by 3** months.
AP: **86 of 88** POSH cases resolved.
**SHe-Box 2.0** tracks ICs/LCs online.

129.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated duty of an employer under the POSH Act?
o: Displaying the policy relating to prevention of sexual harassment
Transferring every complainant to another workplace
129.x: Employer duties include constituting the Internal Committee, displaying the policy, conducting awareness programmes and acting on reports. Mandatory transfer of every complainant is not stated as a general duty.
129.tq: Find the option that imposes an absolute duty not included among the listed employer responsibilities.
xs: **Transferring every complainant** is not an employer duty — option **(2)**.
Duties: **set up the IC**, **display the policy**, run **awareness programmes**, act on reports.
xa: Failure attracts a fine up to **₹50,000**.
IC is required with **10 or more employees**.
**Kerala film chamber** requires an **ICC report** from film sets before publicity clearance (**2026**).

129.s: SHe-Box 2.0, under Mission Shakti, is best described as:
o: A fund exclusively providing maternity benefits
An employment exchange for women in rural areas
A single-window online system for complaint and tracking of Internal and Local Committees
A criminal investigation portal for dowry deaths
129.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a single-window online complaint and tracking system for Internal and Local Committees under Mission Shakti.
129.tq: Match the digital platform with its operational function rather than its broad women-welfare context.
xs: **SHe-Box 2.0** (MWCD, **Mission Shakti**) is a **single-window online complaint** and **tracking** system for **ICs/LCs** — option **(3)**.
It covers **public, private, organised and unorganised** sectors.
xa: **SHINE app**: launched by **Railways** for staff.
**One Stop Centres (Sakhi)**: medical, legal, counselling, shelter under one roof.
**Women Helpline 181**: emergency help and counselling.

129.s: Under the POSH Act, 2013, an employer who fails to constitute an Internal Committee or carry out other duties under the Act is liable to a fine of up to:
129.x: An employer who does not set up the Internal Committee, display the policy, run awareness programmes or act on reports can be fined up to ₹50,000. ₹10,000, ₹15,000 and ₹25,000 are wrong; ₹15,000 is the minimum fine under s.3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
129.tq: POSH employer default: up to ₹50,000.
xs: An employer failing its POSH duties can be fined up to **₹50,000** — option **(4)**.
⚠ **₹15,000** is the **minimum fine** under **s.3** of the Dowry Act; **Rs 10,000** is the s.4 maximum.
xa: Duties: set up the IC, display the policy, awareness programmes, act on reports.
IC for **10 or more** employees; LC for fewer than **10**.
**Laxmi case**: acid victims get at least **₹3 lakh** compensation.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:
1. Voyeurism is dealt with under Section 77.
2. Stalking is dealt with under Section 78.
3. Sexual harassment (old IPC 354A) is dealt with under Section 74.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: voyeurism is BNS 77 (IPC 354C) and stalking is BNS 78 (IPC 354D). Statement 3 is wrong: sexual harassment (354A) is BNS 75; BNS 74 is outraging modesty (354). Hence A; B, C and D include statement 3.
129.tq: 74 modesty, 75 harassment, 77 voyeurism, 78 stalking.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**BNS 77** = **voyeurism** (IPC 354C); **BNS 78** = **stalking** (IPC 354D).
Statement 3 is wrong: sexual harassment (**354A**) is **BNS 75**; **BNS 74** is outraging modesty (**354**).
xa: **BNS 80**: dowry death; **85-86**: cruelty.
IPC → BNS from **1 July 2024**.

129.s: Cruelty by a husband or his relatives is covered under which provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
129.x: Cruelty by a husband or relatives is covered under BNS Sections 85-86, corresponding to IPC Section 498A.
129.tq: Distinguish the cruelty provision from the nearby dowry-death provision by section number.
xs: **Cruelty by husband or relatives** = **BNS sections 85-86** (IPC **498A**) — option **(4)**.
**80** is dowry death; **77-78** voyeurism and stalking; **143** trafficking.
xa: Debate: **misuse claims against 498A** vs heavy under-reporting.
The **1986** amendment linked this framework with **dowry death** (304B).

129.s:
Match the offence with the corresponding BNS provision:

List-I (Offence)
 a. Rape
 b. Trafficking of persons
 c. Selling or buying minors for prostitution
 d. Acid attack

List-II (BNS provision)
 i. Sections 98-99
 ii. Sections 63-64
 iii. Section 124
 iv. Section 143

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
129.x: Rape is covered by Sections 63-64, trafficking by Section 143, selling or buying minors for prostitution by Sections 98-99, and acid attack by Section 124.
129.tq: Begin with the sure rape pair and use elimination to place the remaining BNS provisions.
xs: **a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii** — option **(1)**.
**Selling/buying minors** – **98/99**; **acid attack** – **124**.
xa: Acid attack: minimum **10 years**, extendable to life; attempt **5-7 years**.
Old IPC: trafficking **370**; minors **372/373**; acid **326A/326B**.
**RPwD Act 2016** lists acid-attack injuries as a **disability**.

129.s:
Consider the following statements regarding selected provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:
1. Sections 74 and 75 deal respectively with outraging the modesty of a woman and sexual harassment.
2. Section 67 concerns intercourse with a separated wife and prescribes imprisonment of two to seven years.
3. Section 124 concerns trafficking of persons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because Section 124 concerns acid attack; trafficking of persons is covered under Section 143.
129.tq: Catch the swapped-offence trap between the acid-attack and trafficking provisions.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**74 / 75** = **outraging modesty / sexual harassment** — correct.
**67** = intercourse with a **separated wife**, **2-7 years** — correct.
Statement 3 is wrong: **s.124** is **acid attack**; trafficking is **s.143**.
xa: **77**: voyeurism; **78**: stalking.
**98/99**: selling/buying minors for prostitution.
Acid attack came via **CLA 2013**.

129.s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, rape is dealt with under Sections 63-64, corresponding to which IPC provisions?
129.x: BNS Sections 63-64 correspond to IPC Sections 375-376. The stated exception excludes a wife aged 18 years or above from the rape provision.
129.tq: Match the new section pair with the correct old-code pair rather than a neighbouring offence pair.
xs: **BNS 63-64** correspond to **IPC 375-376** (**sections 375 and 376**) — option **(1)**.
**354/354A** = outraging modesty / sexual harassment; **370/372** trafficking and minors; **304B/498A** dowry death and cruelty.
xa: **Exception 2**: a wife **18+** is excluded — the **marital rape exception**.
The SC is examining this exception (**2026**).
**BNS 67**: intercourse with a separated wife, **2-7 years**.

129.s: Under BNSS Section 144, maintenance of wives is available:
o: Only to wives belonging to a specified religion
Only when domestic violence has been proved
Only when the marriage is less than seven years old
129.x: BNSS Section 144 provides for maintenance of wives regardless of religion; it corresponds to old CrPC Section 125.
129.tq: Reject the religion-based limitation and apply the express universal qualification.
xs: **BNSS s.144** gives maintenance to wives **regardless of religion** — option **(1)**.
It replaces old **CrPC 125**; no proof of domestic violence or marriage-length condition applies.
xa: It is the secular route for **maintenance of wives** in criminal procedure.
**DV Act s.20** separately gives **monetary relief**.
IPC/CrPC → BNS/BNSS from **1 July 2024**.

129.s: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception in relation to which of the following provisions?
o: The domestic-violence relief provisions under Sections 17-22
The rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64
The maintenance provision under BNSS Section 144
The trafficking provision under BNS Section 143
129.x: The Supreme Court is examining the marital rape exception associated with the rape provisions under BNS Sections 63-64.
129.tq: Connect the constitutional-legal issue with the relevant offence provision rather than a related women-protection law.
xs: The **marital rape exception** sits in the **rape provisions, BNS 63-64** — option **(2)**.
**Exception 2** excludes a wife aged **18+**.
**s.144 BNSS** is maintenance; **s.143 BNS** is trafficking; **17-22** are DV Act reliefs.
xa: Rape: old IPC **375-376**.
The SC is hearing challenges to the exception (**2026**).

129.s:
With reference to Fast Track Special Courts, consider the following statements:
1. There were 743 functional courts.
2. Of these, 394 were exclusive POCSO courts.
3. They had disposed of 3,39,644 cases as on 31 July 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
129.x: All three statements are correct: 743 Fast Track Special Courts were functional, including 394 exclusive POCSO courts, and 3,39,644 cases had been disposed of by 31 July 2025.
129.tq: Treat the court total, the exclusive POCSO subset and the disposal figure as separate numerical facts.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4)**.
**743** Fast Track Special Courts functional, incl. **394 exclusive POCSO** courts.
xa: **One Stop Centres (Sakhi)**: medical, legal, counselling, shelter.
**Nirbhaya Fund** finances safety projects.
**Women Help Desks** in police stations.

129.s: Free legal aid for women and other eligible persons is provided through which institutional mechanism?
129.x: Free legal aid is provided through the Legal Services Authorities. Courts and police desks may support access to justice but are not the institution identified for providing free legal aid.
129.tq: Distinguish the institution providing legal aid from institutions providing emergency, police or judicial support.
xs: **Free legal aid** comes through **Legal Services Authorities** — option **(1)**.
**Cri-MAC** gives real-time trafficking alerts; **FTSCs** try cases; **Women Help Desks** sit in police stations.
xa: **Victim Protection Plan**: common protocol for legal aid, education, skills, livelihood.
**Nirbhaya Fund** for safety projects.
**Women Helpline 181**: **3 lakh+** calls in AP.

129.s: Which institution provides medical, legal, counselling and shelter support to women under one roof?
o: Women Help Desk in police stations
129.x: One Stop Centres (Sakhi) bring medical, legal, counselling and shelter support under one roof, and they exist in every AP district. Women Helpline 181 gives emergency help and counselling by phone, Fast Track Special Courts try cases, and Women Help Desks sit in police stations.
129.tq: Sakhi = One Stop Centre; 181 = helpline.
