xs: The **CLA 2013** inserted **Section 376E IPC** — **death penalty for repeat rape offenders** — option **(4)**.
**NDSO** dates from **2018**; **Safe City** is a Nirbhaya Fund project; POCSO courts come from the **POCSO Act**.
xa: 376E is now **BNS 71**.
The CLA 2013 also created **acid attack (326A)** and **stalking (354D)**.

130.s: In which State was India's first women's court set up?
130.x: The first women's court was set up in West Bengal (APPSC-GS 2019). Kerala had the first all-women police station (Kozhikode, 1973), Odisha announced 45 fast-track courts in 2019, and Andhra Pradesh is linked to the Disha model, so those options are traps.
130.tq: First women's court = West Bengal; first all-women police station = Kozhikode.
xs: The first women's court was set up in **West Bengal** — option **(3)** (APPSC-GS **2019**).
**Kerala** had the first **all-women police station** (**Kozhikode, 1973**); **Odisha** announced **45** fast-track courts (Dec **2019**).
xa: **AP** is linked with the **Disha** model.
AP's **Disha police stations**: **18** dedicated women's police stations.

130.s: In 2025, Fast Track Special Courts disposed of 87,754 POCSO cases against 80,320 cases registered. What disposal rate does this give?
130.x: 87,754 disposals against 80,320 registrations is a disposal rate of about 109%, meaning FTSCs disposed of more cases than were newly registered. The other figures do not match this ratio.
130.tq: FTSC 2025: 109% disposal rate (87,754 vs 80,320).
xs: **87,754** disposed vs **80,320** registered = **109%** — option **(3)**.
FTSCs disposed of more POCSO cases than were registered.
xa: **743 FTSCs** incl. **394 exclusive POCSO** (**31 Jul 2025**).
Sanctioned under extension: **790 courts**.

130.s: What percentage of India’s police force was reported to be women?
130.x: Women constituted only 11.7% of India’s police force according to the cited figure.
130.tq: Distinguish the police representation figure from the violence-related survey percentages.
xs: Only **11.7%** of India's police are women — option **(2)**.
**5.4%** is NFHS-4 marital rape; **32%** spousal violence.
xa: **Women Help Desks** in police stations.
**Mahila Police Volunteers** (MWCD-MHA).

130.s: The first all-women police station in India was established at:
130.x: The first all-women police station was established at Kozhikode in Kerala in 1973.
130.tq: Use the exact place and year rather than substituting a prominent State capital.
xs: The first all-women police station: **Kozhikode, Kerala (1973)** — option **(3)**.
Not New Delhi, Vijayawada or Hyderabad.
xa: First women's court: **West Bengal**.
AP's **Disha police stations**: **18**.
Women are only **11.7%** of the police.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding gender sensitisation of the police:
1. Women Help Desks are established in police stations.
2. Mahila Police Volunteers are a measure associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development and the Ministry of Home Affairs.
3. Mahila Police Volunteers are funded exclusively through the Union Budget, 2013 Nirbhaya corpus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Women Help Desks are set up in police stations, and Mahila Police Volunteers are a joint MWCD-MHA measure. Statement 3 is wrong because MPVs only drew on the Nirbhaya Fund; they were not funded 'exclusively' from it.
130.tq: Reject the unsupported exclusive funding claim while retaining the stated institutional measures.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Women Help Desks** are in police stations; **Mahila Police Volunteers** are an **MWCD-MHA** measure.
Statement 3 is wrong as framed: MPVs draw on the **Nirbhaya Fund**, but nothing makes it their **exclusive** source.
xa: The Nirbhaya Fund itself came from the Union Budget, **2013**.
Only **11.7%** of police are women.

130.s: The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 is enforced under Article 141 until:
o: All States adopt separate constitutional amendments
The Supreme Court withdraws every protection order
130.x: The Witness Protection Scheme, 2018 operates under Article 141 until Parliament enacts a law on the subject.
130.tq: Identify the stated constitutional interim basis and its legislative endpoint.
xs: The **Witness Protection Scheme 2018** is enforced under **Art. 141** until **Parliament enacts a law** — option **(1)**.
No State amendments or Nirbhaya Fund condition is involved.
xa: **Prajwala** (Jun **2026**): SC's Victim Protection Plan.
**K.P. Kiran Kumar** (Jan **2026**): child-trafficking guidelines.

130.s: The Disha Bill of Andhra Pradesh was introduced primarily as a response to:
130.x: The Disha Bill was Andhra Pradesh’s legislative response to the 2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder case.
130.tq: Match the legislation with the immediate triggering event.
xs: The **AP Disha Bill** answered the **2019 Hyderabad veterinarian rape-murder** — option **(2)**.
The **2012 Delhi** case led to the **CLA 2013**; **Kathua** (**2018**) to the **CLA 2018**.
xa: Passed by the AP Assembly in **December 2019** (APPSC **2018**).
**Death sentence** for rape and gang rape.
Verdict within **21 days**.

130.s: Under the Disha Act, the prescribed time structure for investigation and trial of rape cases is:
o: Investigation in 14 days and trial in 7 days
Investigation in 14 days and trial in 21 days
Investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days
Investigation in 21 days and trial in 14 days
130.x: The Disha Act specifies seven days for investigation and fourteen days for trial, making a total of twenty-one days.
130.tq: Separate the two components of the total time limit.
xs: **Investigation 7 days + trial 14 days** = verdict in **21 days** — option **(3)**.
The other options swap or inflate these periods.
xa: ⚠ Disha model (**21-day** verdict) vs Nirbhaya Act (**2-month** probe).
CLA 2018: investigation **2 months** + trial **2 months** + appeals **6 months**.
Disha mandates **forensic evidence**.

130.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the provisions of the Disha Act?
o: Mandatory forensic evidence in relevant cases
Death sentence for rape and gang rape
Penalties for cyber-stalking and deepfake misuse
A special court only at the State capital
130.x: The Disha Act provides for a special court in every district, not merely one special court at the State capital.
130.tq: Find the option that reverses the scope of a stated institutional provision.
xs: **A special court only at the State capital** is wrong — option **(4)**: Disha makes **special courts mandatory in every district**.
**Forensic evidence**, **death sentence** and penalties for **cyber-stalking and deepfake misuse** are Disha provisions.
xa: It needs **President's assent**; not in force as passed.
**Guntur** has a **special court for crimes against women**.
**Disha App**: SOS alerts for women.

130.s: Why does the Disha Act require the assent of the President of India?
o: It seeks to amend the Constitution.
It deals with subjects exclusively placed in the Union List.
It creates a new High Court in Andhra Pradesh.
Criminal law is included in the Concurrent List.
130.x: The Disha Act requires Presidential assent because criminal law falls in the Concurrent List. It has not come into force as passed.
130.tq: Ask which constitutional distribution of legislative power explains the requirement.
xs: Disha needs **President's assent** because **criminal law is in the Concurrent List** — option **(4)**.
It does not amend the Constitution, touch the Union List, or create a High Court.
xa: So it is **not in force as passed**.
Passed in **December 2019**.
**Disha police stations**: **18** dedicated women's police stations.

130.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Disha App — SOS alerts for women in distress or danger
2. Abhayam — Chittoor police awareness campaign for the safety of women and children
3. Abhay pilot — Free pick-up and drop for women stranded between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
4. Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi — Women-protection functionaries in village and ward secretariats
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
130.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Abhayam was associated with Chittoor, while the Abhay pilot was implemented by Prakasam police at Ongole.
130.tq: Verify the purpose and location attached to each similarly named initiative.
xs: All four pairs are correct — option **(4)**.
**Disha App**: **SOS alerts**; **Abhayam**: **Chittoor** police awareness campaign.
**Abhay** pilot: **Prakasam (Ongole)** free pick-up/drop for women stranded **9 pm to 5 am**.
**Mahila Samrakshana Karyadarsi**: women-protection functionaries in **village/ward secretariats**.
xa: ⚠ **Abhayam** = Chittoor awareness; **Abhay** = Ongole pick-up (APPSC-GS **2018**).
The SOS app is **Disha** (APPSC-G1 **2022**).
Both Abhayam and Abhay date from Dec **2019**.

130.s: Which of the following statements about recent Andhra Pradesh measures is correct?
o: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets of repeat offenders.
Sexual Offender Sheets are maintained only for first-time offenders.
Shakti Teams are special courts under the Disha Act.
Trishul committees deal exclusively with cybercrime.
130.x: Shakti Teams are used along with Sexual Offender Sheets for repeat offenders. Trishul committees have a broader three-part zero-tolerance mandate.
130.tq: Use the institutional-function distinction to reject swapped roles.
xs: **Shakti Teams** work along with **Sexual Offender Sheets (SOS)** of **repeat offenders** — option **(1)**.
SOS are for repeat offenders, not first-timers; Shakti Teams are not courts; **Trishul** is broader than cybercrime.
xa: ⚠ **SOS** = Disha **SOS app** and also **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
Crimes against women **fell 4.4%** (**2026**).
Current model: **Shakti Teams + SOS + Trishul**.

130.s:
The Trishul committees in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which of the following objectives?
1. Zero drugs
2. Zero tolerance to atrocities against women
3. Zero road accidents
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: Trishul committees are described as state and district panels pursuing zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women and zero road accidents.
130.tq: Treat a three-part slogan as three separate testable components.
xs: All three — option **(4)**.
**Trishul** committees: State and district panels for **"zero drugs, zero tolerance to atrocities against women, zero road accidents"**.
xa: Ordered by **CM Naidu**, with police response time of **30 minutes** (Sep **2026**).
Push for better **conviction rates**.

130.s:
The further 4.4% decline in crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh was credited to which of the following?
1. Shakti Teams
2. Women’s Safety Week rallies
3. Sexual Offender Sheets
4. Replacement of all police stations by women police stations
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women’s Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets. There is no record that all police stations were replaced by women police stations.
130.tq: Reject the absolute institutional claim and retain the three specifically cited measures.
xs: Statements **1, 2 and 3** — option **(2)**.
The further **4.4%** decline was credited to **Shakti Teams**, **Women's Safety Week rallies** and **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
Replacing all police stations with women's stations is not mentioned.
xa: Chargesheets: **94.4%**.

130.s: The APSES 2024–25 objective concerning crimes against women is to achieve:
o: A uniform conviction rate of 100% in every district
The highest crime rate in the country with ordinary courts only
One of the lowest crime rates and special courts for atrocity cases
130.x: APSES 2024–25 aims for one of the lowest crime rates and provides for special courts for atrocity cases.
130.tq: Select the measured policy objective and avoid an absolute numerical claim not stated.
xs: **APSES 2024-25** aims for **"one of the lowest crime rates"** + **special courts for atrocity cases** — option **(3)**.
It does not seek a uniform 100% conviction rate, the highest crime rate, or abolition of monitoring.
xa: **SDG-16**: **5.52** trafficking victims per **10** lakh population.
Largest AP head: **cruelty** (**9,165**).

130.s: The number of crimes against women reported in Andhra Pradesh declined from 25,503 in 2022 to 22,418 in 2023 and to how many in 2024?
130.x: Crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh fell to 19,952 in 2024, from 22,418 in 2023 and 25,503 in 2022. 17,149 is the number of arrests, not cases.
130.tq: Follow the year-wise sequence and avoid confusing cases with arrests.
xs: AP crimes against women fell to **19,952** in **2024** — option **(2)**.
⚠ **17,149** is the number of **arrests**.
xa: Chargesheets: **94.4%**.
AP heads: cruelty **9,165**, assault **2,389**, stalking **977**, rape **441**.

130.s: According to Crime in India 2024, which one of the following statements is correct regarding overall crime and cybercrime in India?
o: Total crime declined by 6%, while cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
Total crime increased by 6%, while cybercrime declined by 17.9%.
Both total crime and cybercrime declined by 6%.
Both total crime and cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
130.x: Crime in India 2024 recorded a 6% fall in total crime, whereas cybercrime increased by 17.9%.
130.tq: Use the reversed-trend trap by separately checking the direction of change for total crime and cybercrime.
xs: **Total crime fell 6%** while **cybercrime rose 17.9%** — option **(1)**.
The other options reverse or merge the two trends.
xa: Crime rate **418.9** per lakh, lowest since **2019**.
Cybercrime: **1,01,928** cases, first time over **1 lakh**.
Total: **58.86 lakh** cognisable crimes.

130.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023 is correct?
130.x: The comparative position cited for the Women, Peace and Security Index 2023 was 128 out of 177. A later publication printed 131, creating a reported variation in the cited figure.
130.tq: Resolve a close-number confusion by matching the rank with the correct total number of countries.
xs: India ranked **128th of 177** in the **Women, Peace and Security Index 2023** — option **(2)**.
Options (3) and (4) garble the totals.
xa: ⚠ LENS (Jun **2026**) prints **131** — option (1) reflects that variant.
Opposition claim: crimes against women **+42.6% since 2013**.

130.s:
Consider the following statements about crimes against women in India:
1. Cases involving crimes against women have been reported to have more than 90% pendency.
2. The opposition, citing Crime in India 2024, stated that crimes against women had risen by 42.6% since 2013.
3. The reported 42.6% increase refers to cybercrime alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the 42.6% claim concerned crimes against women overall, not cybercrime alone.
130.tq: Separate an overall crime-against-women claim from the distinct cybercrime trend.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Pendency is **>90%**; the Opposition claimed crimes against women rose **42.6% since 2013**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **42.6%** claim is about crimes against women, not cybercrime.
xa: Cybercrime rose **17.9%** in **2024**.
Rape conviction rate: **22.7%** (2023).

130.s: Which one of the following is a major criticism of the death penalty in cases involving sexual offences?
o: It makes rape laws completely gender-neutral.
It may discourage victims from reporting offences.
It necessarily eliminates delays in criminal trials.
It prevents all cases from reaching fast-track courts.
130.x: A stated criticism is that the death penalty may discourage reporting by victims or affected families. It does not automatically eliminate trial delays or make rape law gender-neutral.
130.tq: Identify the policy criticism rather than assuming that a severe punishment solves every procedural problem.
xs: The **death penalty** may **discourage reporting** — option **(2)**.
It does not make rape law gender-neutral or end trial delays.
xa: Disha prescribed **death sentence** for rape and gang rape.
**Justice Verma Committee** recommended **no death penalty for rape**.

130.s: With reference to debates on rape law in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Rape law has been criticised for not being gender-neutral.
Gender neutrality has eliminated all criticism of rape law.
The debate concerns only the speed of investigation and not the scope of the law.
Rape law is universally regarded as gender-neutral.
130.x: The non-gender-neutral character of rape law is a criticism. The debate is not confined only to investigation speed.
130.tq: Avoid the absolute-word trap in statements claiming that a legal debate has been completely settled.
xs: Rape law is criticised for **not being gender-neutral** — option **(1)**.
The debate is about the law's **scope**, not just investigation speed.
xa: The **marital rape exception** remains.
CLA **2013** widened rape to **penetration by objects/body parts + oral acts**.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fast-track justice and related concerns:
1. Trials may remain prolonged despite the existence of fast-track courts.
2. Rising disposals can coexist with falling POCSO conviction rates.
3. Fast-track courts, by themselves, guarantee a 100% conviction rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because fast-track courts do not guarantee a 100% conviction rate.
130.tq: Reject the absolute claim that an institutional mechanism automatically guarantees a particular outcome.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
**Trials stay long despite fast-track courts**; **disposals rise while POCSO conviction rates fall**.
Statement 3 is wrong: FTSCs guarantee no conviction rate.
xa: FTSC disposal rate: **109%** (**2025**).
**773 FTSCs** functioning (**2026**).

130.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Model or initiative)
 a. Disha model
 b. Nirbhaya Act
 c. Shakti Teams
 d. SHe-Box 2.0

List-II (Associated feature)
 i. Single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints
 ii. Two-month probe
 iii. Twenty-one-day verdict model
 iv. Current Andhra Pradesh policing model

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
130.x: The Disha model is associated with a 21-day verdict, the Nirbhaya Act with a two-month probe, Shakti Teams with the current Andhra Pradesh policing model, and SHe-Box 2.0 with the workplace-harassment complaint portal.
130.tq: Start with the sure pair and then eliminate codes using the distinctive time limits and institutional roles.
xs: **a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i** — option **(1)**.
**Disha**: **21-day** verdict; **Nirbhaya Act**: **2-month** probe.
**Shakti Teams**: current AP model; **SHe-Box 2.0**: workplace harassment single window.
xa: Disha (**2019**) is the earlier model; now Shakti Teams + SOS + **Trishul**.
SHe-Box 2.0 is available in **22** languages.

130.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sex-ratio figures:
1. Andhra Pradesh has a higher adult sex ratio than India.
2. Andhra Pradesh has a higher child sex ratio than India.
3. India’s adult sex ratio and child sex ratio are 996 and 944, respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
130.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh records 996 and 944 against India’s 943 and 918. Statement 3 reverses the State and national figures.
130.tq: Compare both rows of a paired State–India table before selecting the coded option.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
AP adult **996** > India **943**; AP CSR **944** > India **918**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **996 / 944** are **AP's** figures.
xa: India's CSR fell from **927** (2001).
NFHS-5 overall sex ratio: **1,020**.

130.s: Which of the following measures was ordered by Chief Minister Naidu in relation to crimes against women in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Replacement of Shakti Teams by a two-month investigation period
A uniform 21-day verdict for every criminal case in the State
Formation of Trishul committees and a police response time of 30 minutes
Abolition of Sexual Offender Sheets and withdrawal of conviction targets
130.x: The measures included Trishul committees, a police response time of 30 minutes, and an emphasis on improving conviction rates.
130.tq: Match the executive direction with the correct State-level institutional measures, not with unrelated time limits.
xs: **CM Naidu** ordered **Trishul** committees and a **30-minute** police response time — option **(3)** (Sep **2026**).
He kept **conviction rates** as a priority; SOS and Shakti Teams were not abolished.
xa: Trishul: **zero drugs**, **zero tolerance to atrocities against women**, **zero road accidents**.
Crimes against women fell **4.4%**.

130.s: SHe-Box 2.0, associated with the Ministry of Women and Child Development, is primarily:
o: A police database containing Sexual Offender Sheets in 22 States
A judicial platform for issuing 21-day verdicts in sexual-offence cases
A single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints available in 22 languages
A portal exclusively for reporting cybercrime against children in 30 languages
130.x: SHe-Box 2.0 is a Ministry of Women and Child Development single-window portal for workplace harassment complaints and is available in 22 languages.
130.tq: Use the body-function-language combination to distinguish the portal from policing and judicial mechanisms.
xs: **SHe-Box 2.0** (MWCD) is a **single window for workplace harassment complaints**, in **22** languages — option **(3)**.
**Sexual Offender Sheets** are AP police records; **21-day verdicts** belong to **Disha**.
xa: Cybercrime reporting is via **cybercrime.gov.in** and **1930** under **I4C**.
NCRB keeps **NDSO**, a police-only database of convicted offenders.

131.s: Which Articles of the Constitution provide for equal franchise in the context of women voters?
131.x: Articles 325 and 326 provide the constitutional basis for equal electoral franchise.
131.tq: Distinguish voting rights provisions from provisions concerning eligibility to contest elections.
xs: **Articles 325 and 326** provide **equal franchise** for women voters — option **(1)** is correct.
**Articles 84 and 173** only allow women to **contest** elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
**Articles 330A and 332A** are the women's seat quotas inserted by the **106th Amendment**.
xa: The reservation Bill was needed because women were historically **under-represented in legislatures**.
**Art. 330A** = Lok Sabha quota; **Art. 332A** = State Assemblies quota.
⚠ Women's turnout exceeded men's first in **2019** and again in **2024**.

131.s: Articles 84 and 173 are relevant to women in elections because they concern:
o: The ability of women to contest elections
The delimitation of constituencies for women voters
The reservation of seats for women in local bodies
The appointment of women as Election Commissioners
131.x: Articles 84 and 173 relate to qualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures, respectively, and thereby permit women to contest elections when the qualifications are met.
131.tq: Separate contesting eligibility from the constitutional provisions governing the franchise.
xs: **Articles 84 and 173** concern the **ability of women to contest elections** — option **(1)** is correct.
Equal franchise (right to vote) comes from **Articles 325 and 326**, not 84/173.
Reservation of seats for women in local bodies comes from **Art. 243D(3)** and **Art. 243T(3)**, not 84/173.
xa: Art. **84** relates to Parliament; Art. **173** to State Legislatures.
Key measure (APPSC **2007** key): **reserving seats in local bodies** came first; NCW, SHGs and the reservation Bill came after.
The legislature quota came only with the **106th Amendment** (**2023**).

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women's electoral participation:
1. Women's turnout exceeded men's for the first time in 2019.
2. Women's turnout again exceeded men's in 2024.
3. The ECI's SVEEP programme targets women voters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Women's turnout first exceeded men's in 2019, did so again in 2024, and women voters are among the targets of the ECI's SVEEP programme.
131.tq: Combine the trend, repetition of the trend and the relevant voter-awareness programme.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: women's turnout exceeded men's for the first time in **2019** (about **67.2%** vs **67.0%**).
Statement 2: it did so again in **2024**.
Statement 3: the **ECI** outreach programme **SVEEP** targets women voters.
xa: Nearly **10 crore women** in over **90 lakh SHGs** drive grassroots leadership.
**NCW** was set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**.
First woman **President**: **Pratibha Patil** (**2007**); first woman **Lok Sabha Speaker**: **Meira Kumar** (**2009**).

131.s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is associated with the
131.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, receiving assent in 2023.
131.tq: Match the popular name of the amendment with its constitutional number and assent year.
xs: The **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** is the **106th Constitutional Amendment** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was passed as the **128th Amendment Bill** on **21 Sept 2023** and received **Presidential assent** in **2023**.
The **104th Amendment** is the one that extended the **Art. 334** period to **2030** (SC/ST reservation).
xa: ⚠ **128th** Bill = **106th** Amendment Act; the **108th** Bill (**2008**) only passed the Rajya Sabha (**2010**).
It reserves **one-third** of seats in the **Lok Sabha**, **State Assemblies** and the **Delhi Assembly**.
Duration: **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.

131.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to women's reservation in chronological order:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) Act enacted
B. 108th Amendment Bill passed by the Rajya Sabha
C. 81st Amendment Bill introduced
D. 108th Amendment Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha
131.x: The 81st Amendment Bill was introduced in 1996, the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010, it lapsed in 2014, and the 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023.
131.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest Bill and the final enacted amendment.
xs: Correct order is **C, B, D, A** — option **(1)**.
C: **81st Amendment Bill** introduced in **1996** (Deve Gowda govt).
B: **108th Amendment Bill** passed by the **Rajya Sabha** on **9 March 2010**.
D: the 108th Bill **lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha** in **2014**; A: **106th Amendment** enacted in **2023**.
xa: The 81st Bill **lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha**; it was reintroduced in **1998, 1999, 2002-03** (Vajpayee govts) and lapsed again.
The 108th Bill was **introduced in the Rajya Sabha** in **2008**.
The 2023 measure was the **128th Amendment Bill**, passed on **21 Sept 2023**.

131.s: The Women's Reservation Bill introduced in 1996 was known as the:
131.x: The Bill introduced in 1996 during the Deve Gowda government was the 81st Amendment Bill.
131.tq: Use the year-Bill number association to distinguish earlier attempts from later versions.
xs: The **1996** Bill was the **81st Amendment Bill** (Deve Gowda govt) — option **(3)** is correct.
The **108th** Amendment Bill came in **2008**; the **128th** Amendment Bill in **2023**.
The 81st Bill **lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha**.
xa: Reintroduced in **1998, 1999, 2002-03** under the Vajpayee governments; lapsed each time.
The **108th** Bill passed the Rajya Sabha on **9 March 2010** but lapsed with the **15th Lok Sabha** in **2014**.
The **128th** Bill was enacted as the **106th Amendment** (**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**).

131.s:
Consider the following statements about the 108th Amendment Bill:
1. It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2008.
2. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 9 March 2010.
3. It lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha in 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The 108th Amendment Bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha in 2008, passed there on 9 March 2010, and lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha in 2014.
131.tq: Verify the legislative history as a sequence of introduction, passage and lapse.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: the **108th Amendment Bill** was introduced in the **Rajya Sabha** in **2008**.
Statement 2: it **passed the Rajya Sabha** on **9 March 2010**.
Statement 3: it **lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha** in **2014**.
xa: ⚠ The **108th** Bill only passed the Rajya Sabha; the **128th** Bill (**2023**) became the **106th Amendment**.
The first attempt was the **81st Amendment Bill** of **1996**.
**Presidential assent** to the 106th Amendment: **2023** (APPSC-GS **2024** key).

131.s: Which of the following correctly states the relationship between the 2023 Women's Reservation Bill and the Constitution?
o: The 108th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act in 2023.
The 106th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 128th Amendment Act.
The 81st Amendment Bill was revived and enacted without modification.
The 128th Amendment Bill was enacted as the 106th Amendment Act.
131.x: The 2023 Bill was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill and was enacted as the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.
131.tq: Keep the Bill number and enacted Amendment number distinct.
xs: The **128th Amendment Bill** was enacted as the **106th Amendment Act** — option **(4)** is correct.
It passed on **21 Sept 2023** and got assent in **2023**.
The **108th** Bill (**2008**) only passed the Rajya Sabha and **lapsed** in **2014**; the **81st** Bill (**1996**) lapsed with the 11th Lok Sabha.
xa: The 106th Amendment is called the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.
Articles inserted: **330A** (Lok Sabha), **332A** (State Assemblies), **239AA(2)(ba)** (Delhi), **334A** (commencement and duration).
Commencement only after the **first Census after the Act** and the delimitation that follows.

131.s: Which of the following measures came first in empowering women politically in India?
o: Setting up the National Commission for Women
Reserving seats for women in local bodies
Introducing the Women's Reservation Bill for legislatures
131.x: Reserving seats for women in local bodies came first (73rd/74th Amendments) and is the APPSC 2007 key. The NCW, SHGs and a Reservation Bill for legislatures came after, so they are not the answer.
131.tq: Local-body reservation first; legislature quota (106th) came much later.
xs: **Reserving seats for women in local bodies** came first — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2007** key).
The **NCW**, women's **SHGs** and the **Reservation Bill** for legislatures came after it.
Local-body reservation came through **Art. 243D(3)** (panchayats) and **Art. 243T(3)** (municipalities).
xa: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993**.
**NCW** was set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies (**2006**).

131.s: Which one of the following statements about the 106th Constitutional Amendment is NOT correct?
o: It came into operation immediately upon assent without any delimitation condition.
It covers the Delhi Legislative Assembly through an amendment to Article 239AA.
131.x: The Amendment does not operate immediately upon assent; commencement depends on delimitation based on the first Census after the Act. The other three statements are correct.
131.tq: Identify the false immediate-effect claim by checking the commencement condition.
xs: The NOT-correct statement is that it **came into operation immediately upon assent** — option **(2)**.
Commencement comes only after the **first Census after the Act** plus the **delimitation** that follows.
It does cover the **Lok Sabha** (**Art. 330A**), **State Assemblies** (**Art. 332A**) and the **Delhi Assembly** (**Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**).
xa: Linked to the **2027 Census**, so not enforceable before **2034** under current law.
**Art. 334A** deals with commencement, duration (**15 years**) and rotation.
In force for the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from **17 April 2026**.

131.s: Under Article 334A, the reservation of seats for women is to be rotated:
o: Every five years irrespective of delimitation
131.x: Article 334A provides for rotation of the reserved seats after each delimitation.
131.tq: Distinguish the constitutional trigger for rotation from the ordinary election cycle.
xs: Under **Art. 334A**, reserved seats **rotate after each delimitation** — option **(4)** is correct.
Rotation is tied to delimitation, not to every general election, a fixed five-year cycle or a referendum.
**Art. 334A** also covers the **commencement and duration** of the quota.
xa: Duration: **15 years**, **extendable by Parliament**.
⚠ **Art. 334A** = rotation + duration of the 106th quota; **Art. 368** = the special majority the **131st Bill** missed.
In panchayats, reserved seats and chairperson offices are also allotted **by rotation**.

131.s: Under the current law described for the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, the quota is linked to the 2027 Census and is therefore not enforceable before approximately:
131.x: Because commencement depends on the Census and subsequent delimitation, the quota is linked to the 2027 Census and is not expected to be enforceable before 2034 under the current law.
131.tq: Track the sequence of Census, delimitation and implementation rather than selecting the first relevant year.
xs: The quota is **not enforceable before 2034** under current law — option **(4)** is correct.
Commencement depends on the **first Census after the Act** (the **2027 Census**) and the **delimitation** that follows.
**2027** is only the Census year; the 131st Bill's aim of a quota **from 2029** was **defeated**.
xa: The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** tried to fast-track the quota using the **2011 Census**.
It was defeated on **17 April 2026**: **298 for, 230 against**, short of **352**.
Women's groups demand removing the **Census-delimitation condition**.

131.s: Implementation of the women’s reservation under the 106th Amendment is linked to delimitation based on:
o: The first Census conducted after the Act, namely the 2027 Census
131.x: The reservation is to commence only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.
131.tq: Connect commencement with the specified future Census and delimitation condition.
xs: The quota is linked to delimitation based on the **first Census after the Act**, namely the **2027 Census** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **2011 Census** was the basis only in the **131st Amendment Bill, 2026**, which was **defeated**.
Because of this condition, it is **not enforceable before 2034**.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
Duration: **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.
Critics see bundling the quota with delimitation as **political cover** for reallocating seats.

131.s: The Constitution (106th Amendment) Act provides reservation for women of:
o: One-third of the seats in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly, including within SC/ST seats
One-fourth of the seats in the Lok Sabha only
One-third of seats only in State Assemblies and municipalities
One-half of the seats in all legislatures, excluding SC/ST seats
131.x: The amendment provides reservation of one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including one-third within the seats reserved for SCs and STs.
131.tq: Check the institutions covered and whether sub-reservation within SC/ST seats is included.
xs: The Act reserves **one-third** of seats in the **Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and Delhi Assembly**, incl. **one-third of SC/ST seats** — option **(1)**.
It is not one-fourth, not one-half, and does not cover **municipalities** (those come under **Art. 243T(3)**).
**Exclusions:** no reservation in the **Rajya Sabha** or **State Legislative Councils**.
xa: **No OBC/BC sub-quota** is provided.
Articles inserted: **330A**, **332A**, **239AA(2)(ba)** and **334A**.
Local bodies give one-third as a floor (**one-half** in **19 States/UTs**) vs legislatures one-third only after delimitation.

131.s: From 17 April 2026, the women's reservation under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act was stated to be in force for the Assemblies of:
131.x: The reservation was stated to be in force for the Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry Assemblies from 17 April 2026.
131.tq: Match the effective date with the exact pair of Assemblies named.
xs: The quota was in force for the **J&K and Puducherry** Assemblies from **17 April 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
For the Delhi Assembly the quota comes through **Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**, but the notes list only **J&K and Puducherry** as in force.
xa: Nationally, commencement waits for the **2027 Census** and delimitation (not before **2034**).
The same day, **17 April 2026**, the **131st Amendment Bill** was defeated in the Lok Sabha.
The quota includes **one-third of SC/ST reserved seats**.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reservation provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023:
1. It provides one-third reservation in the Lok Sabha.
2. It provides one-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies.
3. It includes one-third of the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
4. It provides reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The Act provides one-third reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, including one-third of SC/ST-reserved seats. It does not provide reservation in the Rajya Sabha.
131.tq: Find the excluded chamber while retaining the correct scope of the quota.
xs: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct — option **(1) 1, 2 and 3 only**.
Statements 1 and 2: **one-third** reservation in the **Lok Sabha** (**Art. 330A**) and **State Assemblies** (**Art. 332A**).
Statement 3: it includes **one-third of SC/ST reserved seats**.
Statement 4 is wrong: there is **no reservation in the Rajya Sabha** or **State Legislative Councils**.
xa: **No OBC/BC sub-quota**.
The **Delhi Assembly** is covered via **Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**.
Duration **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.

131.s: Which of the following is NOT provided under the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023?
o: An OBC or BC sub-quota within the women's reservation
One-third reservation in the Delhi Legislative Assembly
Rotation of reserved seats after delimitation
One-third reservation in State Legislative Assemblies
131.x: The Act does not provide an OBC or BC sub-quota. It provides reservation in the specified legislatures and provides for rotation after delimitation.
131.tq: Look for the specific exclusion among otherwise correct features of the amendment.
xs: The Act provides **no OBC/BC sub-quota** — option **(1)** is the one NOT provided.
It does provide one-third in the **Delhi Assembly** (**Art. 239AA(2)(ba)**) and in **State Assemblies** (**Art. 332A**).
It does provide **rotation** after each delimitation (**Art. 334A**).
xa: It also excludes the **Rajya Sabha** and **State Legislative Councils**.
**AP angle:** AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.
In local bodies, reservation for **backward classes** is **voluntary** for States.

131.s: The duration of reservation under the 106th Amendment is:
o: 20 years, extendable only by the Election Commission
131.x: The reservation is provided for 15 years and may be extended by Parliament.
131.tq: Distinguish a fixed constitutional duration from permanent or election-cycle arrangements.
xs: The reservation lasts **15 years, extendable by Parliament** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not permanent, not 10 years, and extension is not done by the Election Commission.
**Art. 334A** covers commencement and duration.
xa: Seats **rotate** after each delimitation.
⚠ In panchayats, **SC/ST reservation** ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**), but **women's reservation has no such sunset**.
Commencement only after the **next Census and delimitation**.

131.s:
Match the Article inserted by the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 with its subject:
a. Article 330A
b. Article 332A
c. Article 239AA(2)(ba)
d. Article 334A
i. Delhi Legislative Assembly
ii. Commencement and duration of the reservation
iii. Lok Sabha
iv. State Legislative Assemblies
131.x: Article 330A is the Lok Sabha quota, 332A the State Assemblies quota, 239AA(2)(ba) the Delhi Assembly quota, and 334A deals with commencement, duration and rotation. The other codes swap these pairs.
131.tq: 330A LS, 332A States, 239AA Delhi, 334A commencement/duration.
xs: Correct code is **a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii** — option **(1)**.
**330A** = Lok Sabha; **332A** = State Assemblies.
**239AA(2)(ba)** = Delhi Assembly; **334A** = commencement and duration.
xa: **Art. 334A** also provides **rotation** after each delimitation.
⚠ **Art. 368** = the special majority that the **131st Bill** missed.
The Act is the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**, passed as the **128th Amendment Bill**.

131.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the proposed 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026 is correct?
o: It proposed increasing the Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 on the basis of the 2011 Census.
It introduced the GST Council into Article 279A.
It restored the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.
It proposed increasing the Rajya Sabha strength from 250 to 550 on the basis of the 2021 Census.
131.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, sought to expand the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats using the 2011 Census as the basis for delimitation.
131.tq: Use the paired numerical figures and the stated Census basis to identify the proposal.
xs: The **131st Bill** proposed raising the **Lok Sabha** maximum from **550 to 850**, delimitation on the **2011 Census** — option **(1)** is correct.
Of the **850**, **815** seats were for States and **35** for UTs.
Its aim was to **fast-track the women's quota from 2029**.
xa: It was **defeated** on **17 Apr 2026** in the special session of **16-18 April**.
Vote: **298 for, 230 against** of **528** present and voting; **352** needed under **Art. 368**.
Expansion would take southern seats from **129** to **195**, keeping their **23.8%** share.

131.s: The 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2026, was
o: referred to the JPC on 17 December 2024
131.x: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026 was defeated (negatived) in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026. It got 298 votes for and 230 against, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority. It was not enacted.
131.tq: Separate the fate and date of the amendment proposal from the separately withdrawn delimitation Bill.
xs: The **131st Amendment Bill, 2026** was **defeated** (negatived) in the Lok Sabha on **17 April 2026** — option **(2)** is correct.
It got **298 for, 230 against** — short of the **352** needed for the **Art. 368** special majority.
It was not enacted; the women's quota stays tied to the **next Census and delimitation**.
xa: It sought to raise the Lok Sabha from **550 to 850** seats using the **2011 Census**.
The vote came in the special session of **16-18 April**.
LENS (**28 Aug 2026**) still discusses the expansion proposal.

131.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 because:
o: It got fewer votes in favour than against
It got 298 votes in favour against 230, short of the 352 needed for the Article 368 special majority
The Rajya Sabha had rejected it first
It needed ratification by half the States, which was refused
131.x: It won a simple majority (298 for, 230 against, of 528 present and voting) but fell short of the 352 votes needed for the special majority under Article 368. It was not defeated on a simple vote, the Rajya Sabha did not vote first, and State ratification was not the reason.
131.tq: 131st Bill: 298-230, needed 352 (Art 368) -> defeated 17 Apr 2026.
xs: It got **298 for and 230 against**, short of the **352** needed for the **Art. 368** special majority — option **(2)** is correct.
It actually had **more votes in favour** than against, so option (1) is wrong.
**528** members were present and voting.
xa: ⚠ **Art. 368** = special majority; **Art. 334A** = rotation and duration of the 106th quota.
The Bill aimed at a quota **from 2029** with a Lok Sabha of **850** (**815** States, **35** UTs).
Defeated on **17 April 2026**.

131.s: Which State is exempt from reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats because it has no Scheduled Caste population?
131.x: Arunachal Pradesh is exempt from SC reservation because it has no Scheduled Caste population.
131.tq: Test the specific constitutional exception rather than the general reservation rule.
xs: **Arunachal Pradesh** is exempt because it has **no SC population** — option **(4)** is correct.
Elsewhere, SC/ST seats are reserved at every level **in proportion to population**.
**Bihar** is known instead as the first State with **50%** for women in local bodies (**2006**).
xa: **73rd Amendment** in force: **24 April 1993**.
**243D(2)**: one-third of SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).

131.s: The constitutional provision corresponding to the one-third reservation of seats for women in Municipalities is:
131.x: Article 243T(3) provides for reservation of not less than one-third of directly elected seats in Municipalities for women.
131.tq: Use the D–T distinction to separate Panchayat and Municipality provisions.
xs: **Article 243T(3)** gives women one-third of seats in **Municipalities** — option **(3)** is correct.
**243D(3)** is the same rule for **Panchayats**; **243D(4)** is women chairpersons in Panchayats.
**243T(4)** covers women chairpersons in municipalities.
xa: ⚠ **243D(3)** = women's seats; **243D(4)** = women chairpersons; **243T** = the same for municipalities.
**ST seats in municipalities:** **Art. 243T(1)** (MPPSC **2020**).
The one-third is a **floor, not a ceiling**.

131.s:
Which of the following statements regarding reservation in local bodies is correct?
1. Reservation of seats and chairperson offices for SCs and STs is proportionate to population.
2. Chairperson offices are reserved as provided by State law and allotted by rotation.
3. Reservation of seats for backward classes is constitutionally compulsory in every State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: SC/ST reservation is proportionate to population, and chairperson offices are arranged under State law and rotation. Reservation for backward classes is voluntary, not compulsory in every State.
131.tq: Spot the reversal of a compulsory SC/ST rule and a voluntary backward-class provision.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: SC/ST seats are reserved **in proportion to population** at every level.
Statement 2: reserved seats and chairperson offices are allotted **by rotation**, as **State law** provides.
Statement 3 is wrong: reservation for **backward classes** is **voluntary/optional** for States.
xa: **Women's one-third** is **compulsory**, a **floor, not a ceiling**.
**AP 2026:** Cabinet approved **34% BC** reservation in rural and **33.33%** in urban local bodies.
**Arunachal Pradesh** has no SC reservation (no SC population).

131.s: Reservation of seats and chairperson offices for SCs and STs in Panchayats is linked to the sunset provision contained in:
131.x: Article 243D(5) links the duration of SC/ST reservation in Panchayats to the period specified under Article 334. The current period is stated as extending to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.
131.tq: Match the local-government reservation rule with the constitutional sunset article.
xs: SC/ST reservation in Panchayats ends with the **Article 334** period — option **(4)** is correct.
The link is made by **Art. 243D(5)**; the period now runs to **2030** under the **104th Amendment**.
**Art. 330** relates to Lok Sabha seats; the 106th Amendment added **330A** for women.
xa: ⚠ **Women's reservation has no such sunset**.
Women's seats: **243D(3)**; women chairpersons: **243D(4)**.
**73rd Amendment** in force: **24 April 1993**.

131.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the duration of reservations in local bodies?
o: Women's reservation has no such sunset provision, whereas SC/ST reservation is linked to the Article 334 period.
All local-body reservations are permanently fixed by the 73rd Amendment.
SC/ST reservation has no constitutional time limit, but women's reservation ends in 2030.
Women's reservation and SC/ST reservation both automatically end in 2030.
131.x: Women's reservation in local bodies has no equivalent sunset provision. SC/ST reservation is linked to Article 334, whose current period extends to 2030 under the 104th Amendment.
131.tq: Compare the duration clauses instead of assuming that all reservation categories have the same limit.
xs: **Women's reservation has no sunset**, whereas **SC/ST reservation** ends with the **Art. 334** period — option **(1)** is correct.
The SC/ST period now runs to **2030** under the **104th Amendment** (via **Art. 243D(5)**).
So neither "both end in 2030" nor "women's ends in 2030" is right.
xa: The women's one-third is **compulsory** and a **floor, not a ceiling**.
By contrast, the **106th Amendment** quota lasts **15 years**, extendable by Parliament.
Reserved seats and chairperson offices rotate.

131.s: Under Article 243D(3) of the Constitution, the minimum reservation for women in seats of Panchayats is:
o: One-half of the total seats, excluding SC/ST seats
One-third of the total seats, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs
131.x: Article 243D(3) provides that not less than one-third of the total seats in every Panchayat, including one-third of the seats reserved for SCs and STs, shall be reserved for women.
131.tq: Test the constitutional minimum against the higher reservation adopted by some States.
xs: **Art. 243D(3)**: not less than **one-third** of total seats, **including one-third of SC/ST seats** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not one-half or one-fourth, and it is not limited to unreserved seats.
**243D(2)**: one-third of the SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.
xa: **243D(4)** = one-third of **chairperson offices** for women.
**19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** first (**2006**).
The same rule for municipalities is **Art. 243T(3)**.

131.s: Which provision of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of the offices of chairpersons in Panchayats at each level for women?
131.x: Article 243D(4) reserves at least one-third of chairperson offices in Panchayats for women. Article 243D(3) covers seats (not chairpersons), 243T(3) covers seats in Municipalities, and 243D(5) links SC/ST reservation to the Article 334 period.
131.tq: Seats 243D(3); chairpersons 243D(4); municipal = 243T.
xs: **Article 243D(4)** reserves at least **one-third of chairperson offices** in Panchayats for women — option **(2)** is correct.
**243D(3)** covers **seats**, not chairpersons; **243T(3)** covers seats in **Municipalities**.
**243D(5)** links SC/ST reservation to the **Art. 334** period.
xa: The municipal counterpart for chairpersons is **Art. 243T(4)**.
Chairperson offices are allotted **by rotation** as State law provides.
⚠ Statement 2 in **UPPSC 2017** on this topic is a known false-statement trap.

131.s: The Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, which introduced one-third reservation for women in Panchayats, came into force on:
131.x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day. The other dates are not its commencement date.
131.tq: 73rd in force 24 April 1993 (Panchayati Raj Day).
xs: The **73rd Amendment** came into force on **24 April 1993** — option **(2)** is correct.
It introduced not less than **one-third** of seats for women in Panchayats (**Art. 243D(3)**).
xa: The municipal counterpart is the **74th Amendment** (**Art. 243T(3)**).
Not applicable to **Arunachal Pradesh** for SC reservation (no SC population).
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period (**2030**); women's has no sunset.

131.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the constitutional position regarding reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities?
o: The Constitution leaves women's reservation entirely to State legislatures.
The Constitution prescribes a ceiling of one-third and prohibits States from increasing it.
The Constitution prescribes a floor of one-third, and States may provide a higher proportion such as one-half.
The Constitution provides one-half reservation in every local body throughout India.
131.x: The constitutional one-third requirement is a floor, not a ceiling. States may increase women's reservation, and several States provide one-half reservation.
131.tq: Apply the floor-versus-ceiling distinction to a State reservation policy.
xs: The Constitution sets a **floor of one-third**; States may give more, such as **one-half** — option **(3)** is correct.
The one-third is **compulsory**, so it is not left entirely to States and is **not a ceiling**.
Not every local body has one-half: **19 States/UTs** give **50%** (**2026**).
xa: APPSC **2019** key: "**1/2** of the seats" in PRIs.
**Bihar** was first with **50%** (**2006**); **Andhra Pradesh** has legislated **50%** for panchayats and municipalities.
Women are **over 49.7%** of elected panchayat representatives nationally.

131.s: Bokkasam Palem, located in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati, is associated with which achievement?
o: It received the first national award for tribal self-governance
It became the first girls’ Panchayat in India
It was ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats
It was the first Panchayat to introduce a BC-women sub-quota
131.x: Bokkasam Palem in Srikalahasti mandal of Tirupati ranked first nationally among women-friendly Panchayats under the Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards.
131.tq: Link the place, administrative location and award-related achievement precisely.
xs: **Bokkasam Palem** (Srikalahasti mandal, Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among **women-friendly panchayats** — option **(3)** is correct.
The ranking was under the **Deendayal Upadhyay Panchayat Satat Vikas Awards, 2026**.
India's first girls' panchayat (**Balika Panchayat**) was in **Kutch, Gujarat**, not here.
xa: MoPR's **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats**: at least **one per district**, with **SHG alignment**.
**AP** gives **50%** reservation to women in local bodies.
First woman **AP Assembly Speaker**: **Pratibha Bharati** (**2004**, undivided AP).

131.s: What percentage of seats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh local bodies, as specified in the context of women-led Panchayats?
131.x: Andhra Pradesh provides 50 per cent reservation for women in local bodies.
131.tq: Distinguish the State-level local-body figure from the constitutional one-third floor.
xs: **Andhra Pradesh** has legislated **50%** reservation for women in local bodies — option **(3)** is correct.
It covers both **panchayats and municipalities**.
**33** per cent would only be the constitutional **one-third floor**.
xa: **19 States/UTs** give women **50%** (**2026**); **Bihar** was first (**2006**).
**AP 2026:** Cabinet approved **34% BC** reservation in rural and **33.33%** in urban local bodies.
AP Congress and BC groups demand a **BC-women sub-quota**.

131.s: Which was the first State to raise the reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions to 50%, and in which year?
131.x: Bihar was the first State to give women 50% in PRIs, in 2006. Many States followed, and 19 States/UTs now give 50%, including Andhra Pradesh. The other pairs are not the first.
131.tq: 50% for women in PRIs: Bihar first (2006).
xs: **Bihar** was the first State to give women **50%** in local bodies, in **2006** — option **(3)** is correct.
Many States followed; **19 States/UTs** now give **50%** (**2026**), including **Andhra Pradesh**.
xa: Women are **~46%** of PRI representatives (Republic Day address, **2026**).
Only **10** States/UTs exceed the quota; **4** fall short (Centre, **23 Apr 2026**).
APPSC **2019** key: "**1/2** of the seats" in PRIs.

131.s: The Balika Panchayat initiative, India's first of its kind, was launched in June 2022 in which of the following places?
131.x: The first Balika Panchayat was established in villages of Kutch, Gujarat, in June 2022.
131.tq: Use the state-location association to distinguish the initiative from other grassroots programmes.
xs: India's first **Balika Panchayat** was set up in villages of **Kutch, Gujarat**, in **June 2022** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is a **girls' panchayat** that trains girls in local governance (APPSC **2021** key).
xa: **Mahila Sabha**: a women-only meeting before the Gram Sabha (e.g. **Maharashtra**).
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** builds the capacity of **Women Elected Representatives**.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st** among women-friendly panchayats.

131.s: The primary purpose of the Balika Panchayat is to:
o: Provide vocational training exclusively to adolescent boys
Conduct elections to State Legislative Assemblies
Monitor implementation of central taxation schemes
131.x: Balika Panchayat is a girls' panchayat intended to train girls in local governance.
131.tq: Match the named initiative with its precise purpose rather than its broad social objective.
xs: The **Balika Panchayat** is a girls' panchayat to **train girls in local governance** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is for girls, not boys, and has nothing to do with Assembly elections or taxation.
India's first was in **Kutch, Gujarat** (**June 2022**).
xa: APPSC **2021** key names it India's first in villages of **Gujarat**.
**Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** gender-sensitises **male** representatives.
**Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats**: at least **one per district**.

131.s: Mahila Sabha is best described as:
o: A meeting of women officers of the Election Commission
A statutory committee of the National Commission for Women
A meeting of women members of Parliament before a joint sitting
A women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha
131.x: Mahila Sabha refers to a women-only meeting conducted before the Gram Sabha, as exemplified in Maharashtra.
131.tq: Discriminate between a grassroots women-only forum and statutory or parliamentary bodies.
xs: **Mahila Sabha** is a **women-only meeting held before the Gram Sabha** — option **(4)** is correct.
It brings **women's issues to the Gram Sabha**; **Maharashtra** is an example.
It is not an ECI body, an NCW committee or a meeting of MPs.
xa: **Balika Panchayat** (Kutch, Gujarat, **June 2022**) trains girls in local governance.
**NCW** is a statutory body (**1992**) under the **NCW Act 1990**.
**ECI's SVEEP** targets women voters.

131.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the ministry associated with the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
131.x: The Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan is associated with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
131.tq: Apply the 'which ministry' test, using neighbouring ministries as distractors.
xs: The **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** belongs to the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** — option **(2)** is correct.
It builds capacity of **Women Elected Representatives (EWRs)**.
xa: Its training covers **leadership**, **legal awareness**, **gender justice** and **gender-based violence**.
⚠ **Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** (also MoPR) trains **male** representatives.
MoPR also runs **Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats** (at least **one per district**).

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan:
1. It provides leadership training to Women Elected Representatives.
2. It includes legal-awareness and gender-justice modules.
3. It includes modules on gender-based violence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: The Abhiyan provides leadership, legal-awareness and gender-justice training, including modules on gender-based violence, for Women Elected Representatives.
131.tq: Check whether all listed components belong to the same capacity-building programme.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: it gives **leadership** training to **Women Elected Representatives**.
Statement 2: it includes **legal-awareness** and **gender-justice** training.
Statement 3: it includes modules on **gender-based violence**.
xa: It is run by the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
⚠ It trains women; **Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** trains **male** panchayat representatives.
**NCW** held an all-India workshop on **gender-responsive governance** (Faridabad, Sep **2026**).

131.s:
With reference to Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats, consider the following statements:
1. At least one such panchayat is envisaged per district.
2. They are intended to provide safe spaces and gender-responsive governance.
3. Their approach includes alignment with Self-Help Groups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats are intended to be established at least one per district, promote safe spaces and gender-responsive governance, and align with SHGs.
131.tq: Use a three-part programme-description question and verify each stated feature.
xs: All three statements are correct — option **(4) 1, 2 and 3**.
Statement 1: at least **one per district**.
Statement 2: they provide **safe spaces** and **gender-responsive governance**.
Statement 3: they include **SHG alignment**.
xa: They are an initiative of the **Ministry of Panchayati Raj**.
**Bokkasam Palem** (Tirupati) ranked **1st nationally** among women-friendly panchayats.
Nearly **10 crore women** are in over **90 lakh SHGs**.

131.s: The initiative 'Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna' is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Training girls exclusively for urban municipal administration
Providing legal aid only to women prisoners
Increasing women's turnout through electronic voting
131.x: Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives.
131.tq: Identify the programme from its target group and objective.
xs: **Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** **gender-sensitises male panchayat representatives** — option **(2)** is correct.
It covers **~17.5 lakh male** representatives through **~28,500 master trainers**.
It is a **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** initiative.
xa: ⚠ **Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** trains women (**EWRs**).
**Proxy representation** ("sarpanch-pati") is a key barrier; it **declines markedly in a second term**.
**Balika Panchayat** trains girls (Kutch, Gujarat).

131.s: Self-Help Groups have been described as involving approximately:
o: Nearly 1 crore women in over 9 lakh SHGs
Nearly 90 lakh women in 10 crore SHGs
Nearly 10 crore women in over 90 lakh SHGs
131.x: Nearly 10 crore women are associated with more than 90 lakh Self-Help Groups, which contribute to grassroots leadership.
131.tq: Match each numerical magnitude with the correct unit: women and SHGs.
xs: **Nearly 10 crore women** in **over 90 lakh SHGs** — option **(4)** is correct.
SHGs **drive grassroots leadership**.
**17.5 lakh** and **28,500** are the figures for **Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** (male representatives, master trainers).
xa: Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats include **SHG alignment**.
APPSC **2007** key: SHGs came **after** local-body reservation.
Women are **over 49.7%** of elected panchayat representatives.

131.s: Which one of the following statements about the National Commission for Women is correct?
o: It is a constitutional body set up under Article 338
It is a statutory body set up in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990
It was created by an executive resolution in 2001
It is a statutory body under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
131.x: The NCW was set up in 1992 as a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990. It reviews safeguards, recommends measures and handles grievances. It is not a constitutional body (Article 338 is the SC Commission), not an executive creation, and not set up under the DV Act.
131.tq: NCW: Act 1990, set up 1992, statutory.
xs: The **NCW** is a **statutory body** set up in **1992** under the **NCW Act, 1990** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is not a constitutional body, not an executive creation and not formed under the Domestic Violence Act.
xa: Functions: **reviews safeguards**, **recommends measures**, **handles grievances**.
⚠ Set up **1992**, Act of **1990** — a common date trap.
**NCW** held an all-India workshop on **gender-responsive governance** (Faridabad, Sep **2026**).

131.s: The study by Chattopadhyay and Duflo (2004) examined the effect of women’s leadership in village governance by using which method?
o: Random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan
Rotation of Lok Sabha constituencies reserved for women
Census-based selection of women sarpanches in Andhra Pradesh
Nomination of women pradhans by the Union Government in all States
131.x: Chattopadhyay and Duflo used the random reservation of pradhan posts in West Bengal and Rajasthan to study the effects of women’s political leadership.
131.tq: Identify the distinctive research design and the two States attached to it.
xs: **Chattopadhyay & Duflo (2004)** used the **random reservation of pradhan posts** in **West Bengal and Rajasthan** — option **(1)** is correct.
It was about panchayat pradhans, not Lok Sabha seats or nominations by the Union.
xa: Finding: women leaders invested more in goods women asked for — **drinking water**, roads.
**Proxy representation** ("sarpanch-pati") = a male relative exercises the elected woman's office.
Proxy representation **declines markedly in a second term**.

131.s: According to the findings associated with the Chattopadhyay-Duflo study, women leaders invested more in which of the following?
o: Military infrastructure and border roads exclusively
Goods and facilities requested by women, including drinking water and roads
Only administrative buildings and police infrastructure
131.x: Women leaders invested more in public goods that women specifically requested, notably drinking water and roads.
131.tq: Apply the study’s finding to the type of public goods selected by women leaders.
xs: Women leaders invested more in **goods women asked for**, such as **drinking water** and **roads** — option **(2)** is correct.
The study was **Chattopadhyay & Duflo (2004)**, using random reservation in **West Bengal and Rajasthan**.
xa: Barriers to women leaders: **proxies**, **intimidation**, **online trolling**.
Legal shield for Dalit and tribal representatives: **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989** and **Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955**.
Women are **over 49.7%** of elected panchayat representatives nationally.

131.s: The term “sarpanch-pati” refers to a situation in which:
o: A male relative exercises the office elected to a woman representative
The husband of a male sarpanch receives a reserved Panchayat post
A woman sarpanch is appointed by the District Collector instead of being elected
A former sarpanch automatically becomes the adviser to every woman sarpanch
131.x: “Sarpanch-pati” denotes proxy representation in which a male relative exercises the office formally held by an elected woman.
131.tq: Discriminate between the elected office-holder and the person informally exercising the office.
xs: **"Sarpanch-pati"** means a **male relative exercises the office** of an elected woman — option **(1)** is correct.
This is called **proxy representation**; the woman is elected, not appointed by the Collector.
xa: Evaluation studies: proxy representation **declines markedly in a second term**.
Barriers: **proxies**, **intimidation**, **online trolling**.
**Nirbhay Raho - Nirbhay Chetna** gender-sensitises **~17.5 lakh male** panchayat representatives.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding proxy representation in women-led Panchayats:

1. Evaluation studies find that proxy representation declines markedly in a second term.
2. Proxies, intimidation and online trolling continue to be barriers.
3. Proxy representation means that the elected woman is legally replaced by a male relative.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because proxy representation is an informal exercise of the office by a male relative; it does not legally replace the elected woman.
131.tq: Separate the empirical finding from the legally incorrect extreme claim.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: proxy representation **declines markedly in a second term** (evaluation studies).
Statement 2: **proxies, intimidation and online trolling** remain barriers.
Statement 3 is wrong: a **male relative exercises** the office; the elected woman is not legally replaced.
xa: Proxy representation is popularly called **"sarpanch-pati"**.
**Sashakt Panchayat Netri Abhiyan** builds leadership of **Women Elected Representatives**.
**Chattopadhyay & Duflo (2004)**: women leaders invested more in **drinking water** and roads.

131.s: Which of the following pairs of laws constitutes the principal legal shield specifically mentioned for protection against atrocities and discrimination involving Dalit and tribal communities?
o: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 and the Panchayats Act, 1992
The National Commission for Women Act, 1990 and the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
131.x: The relevant legal safeguards identified are the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
131.tq: Match each law with the rights-protection issue it directly addresses.
xs: The legal shield is the **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989** and the **Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955** — option **(1)** is correct.
These protect **Dalit and tribal** panchayat representatives.
The **NCW Act, 1990** created the National Commission for Women — not an atrocities law.
xa: SC/ST seats in panchayats are reserved **in proportion to population**.
SC/ST reservation ends with the **Art. 334** period, now **2030** (**104th Amendment**).
**243D(2)**: one-third of SC/ST seats go to **SC/ST women**.

131.s: Which organisation publishes the Gender Development Index (GDI) as part of its Human Development Report?
o: Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security
131.x: The Gender Development Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme through its Human Development Report.
131.tq: Match the index with its publisher rather than with a similar global gender report.
xs: The **GDI** is published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** in its **Human Development Report** — option **(3)** is correct.
The **World Economic Forum** publishes the **GGGI**; the **Georgetown Institute** (with PRIO) publishes the **WPS Index**.
xa: ⚠ **GDI** and **GII** = **UNDP**; **GGGI** = **World Economic Forum**.
GDI = **ratio of female to male HDI**; parity near **1**.
The **GII** was introduced by UNDP in **2010**.

131.s: The Gender Development Index primarily measures the ratio of female to male achievement in which of the following dimensions?
o: Economic participation, educational attainment, health and political empowerment
Reproductive health, political empowerment and labour market participation
Health, education and command over economic resources
131.x: GDI compares female and male HDI achievements in life expectancy, education and earned income or command over economic resources.
131.tq: Distinguish the dimensions of GDI from the sub-indices of GII and GGGI.
xs: GDI compares women and men in **health**, **education** and **command over economic resources** — option **(3)** is correct.
Indicators: **life expectancy**, **expected and mean years of schooling**, **earned income**.
Option 1 lists the **GGGI** sub-indices; option 2 is the **GII**; option 4 is the **WPS Index**.
xa: GDI is the **ratio of female to male HDI**, published by **UNDP**.
GDI parity is near **1**.
⚠ The 0-to-1 "loss" scale (1 = women fare worst) is the **GII**'s.

131.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gender Development Index:
1. It is read in terms of parity between female and male human development.
2. A value close to 1 indicates near parity between women and men.
3. A scale in which 1 represents the worst position for women is the defining scale of the GDI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
131.x: GDI is interpreted through female-to-male parity, with a value near 1 indicating parity. The 0-to-1 loss scale in which 1 denotes the worst position belongs to the GII, not the GDI.
131.tq: Separate two closely related indices by identifying the reversed scale and its meaning.
xs: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — option **(1) 1 and 2 only**.
Statement 1: GDI is the **ratio of female to male HDI**, i.e. read as parity.
Statement 2: a value near **1** means **parity**.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **0-to-1 "loss" scale** (1 = women fare worst) belongs to the **GII**, not the GDI.
xa: Both GDI and GII are published by **UNDP**.
GII dimensions: **reproductive health**, **empowerment**, **labour market**.
India's GII lags its overall HDI rank.

131.s: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) was introduced by the United Nations Development Programme in which year?
131.x: The GII was introduced by UNDP in 2010.
131.tq: Use the year-specific numerical clue to distinguish GII from the other gender indices.
xs: The **GII** was introduced by **UNDP** in **2010** — option **(3)** is correct.
**2006** is when the **WEF** began the **Global Gender Gap Index**.
xa: GII dimensions: **reproductive health** (MMR, adolescent birth rate), **empowerment** (parliamentary seats, secondary education), **labour market** (female LFPR).
GII uses a **0-to-1 "loss" scale**, where **1** = women fare worst.
India's GII lags its HDI rank due to low **female labour-force participation** and **political representation**.

131.s: Which of the following indicators is included under the reproductive health dimension of the Gender Inequality Index?
o: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Mean years of schooling and earned income
Share of women in parliamentary seats only
131.x: The reproductive health dimension of GII includes maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate.
131.tq: Link each indicator to the correct index dimension.
xs: GII's **reproductive health** dimension = **maternal mortality ratio (MMR)** and **adolescent birth rate** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Parliamentary seats** belong to the **empowerment** dimension; **female LFPR** to the **labour market** dimension.
Mean years of schooling and earned income are **GDI** indicators.
xa: GII was introduced by **UNDP** in **2010**.
Empowerment also includes **secondary education**.
⚠ **GDI** and **GII** = **UNDP**; **GGGI** = **WEF**.

131.s: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the:
131.x: The Global Gender Gap Index is published by the World Economic Forum.
131.tq: Use publisher-index matching to avoid confusing GGGI with UNDP indices.
xs: The **GGGI** is published by the **World Economic Forum** — option **(3)** is correct.
**UNDP** publishes the GDI and GII; the **Georgetown Institute with PRIO** publishes the WPS Index.
xa: GGGI has existed **since 2006**.
Four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.

131.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four sub-indices of the Global Gender Gap Index?
131.x: The four GGGI sub-indices are Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Reproductive Health is associated with GII.
131.tq: Eliminate the GII dimension inserted into the GGGI list.
xs: **Reproductive Health** is NOT a GGGI sub-index — option **(1)**; it is a **GII** dimension.
GGGI's four sub-indices: **Economic Participation & Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health & Survival**, **Political Empowerment**.
xa: GGGI is published by the **World Economic Forum** (since **2006**).
GII reproductive health = **MMR** and **adolescent birth rate**.
India's economic participation parity was only **36.7%** (**2023**).

131.s: The Women, Peace and Security Index is associated with which of the following organisations?
o: Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security with PRIO
UN Women and International Labour Organization
131.x: The Women, Peace and Security Index is associated with the Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security and PRIO.
131.tq: Identify the less familiar publisher rather than choosing the better-known gender-index institution.
xs: The **WPS Index** is by the **Georgetown Institute for Women, Peace and Security** with **PRIO** — option **(1)** is correct.
It measures **inclusion, justice and security** of women.
The **WEF** publishes the GGGI; **UNDP** the GDI and GII.
xa: ⚠ **GDI** and **GII** = **UNDP**; **GGGI** = **World Economic Forum**.
Exam angle: **publisher-index matching** is a common question.

131.s: India's rank in the Global Gender Gap Index was 135th in 2022 and 127th out of 146 countries in 2023. Which conclusion follows from these figures?
o: India was ranked first among the 146 countries in 2023.
India remained at the same rank in both years.
131.x: A lower numerical rank represents a better position; therefore, India improved from 135th in 2022 to 127th of 146 in 2023.
131.tq: Read ranking changes in the correct direction instead of treating a larger number as improvement.
xs: India **improved**, from **135th** (**2022**) to **127th of 146** (**2023**) — option **(2)** is correct.
A lower numerical rank means a better position.
xa: In **2018** India was **108th of 149** (APPSC **2019** key).
**Economic participation parity:** only **36.7%** (**2023**).
Parity in **enrolment** achieved at all education levels.

131.s: India's Global Gender Gap Index rank in 2018 was:
131.x: India was ranked 108th among 149 countries in the 2018 Global Gender Gap Index.
131.tq: Match the rank with the correct year and denominator.
xs: India ranked **108th out of 149 countries** in the **2018** GGGI — option **(2)** is correct (APPSC **2019** key).
xa: GGGI is published by the **World Economic Forum**.
Four sub-indices include **Political Empowerment** and **Health & Survival**.
Economic participation parity: only **36.7%** (**2023**).

131.s: Which one of the following statements about India's performance in the 2023 Global Gender Gap Index is correct?
o: Political empowerment parity was 36.7%, while economic participation parity was complete.
Economic participation parity exceeded 75%, while enrolment parity was absent at all levels.
Economic participation parity was 36.7%, while enrolment parity had been achieved at all educational levels.
India ranked 108th out of 149 countries in 2023.
131.x: In 2023, India's economic participation parity was only 36.7%, whereas parity in enrolment had been achieved at all education levels.
131.tq: Separate the education achievement from the continuing economic participation gap.
