138.x: A Child in Need of Care and Protection is dealt with by the Child Welfare Committee, while a Child in Conflict with Law is dealt with by the Juvenile Justice Board.
138.tq: Start with the institutional pair and distinguish the two statutory child categories.
xs: A **Child in Need of Care and Protection** goes to the **Child Welfare Committee** — option **(3)** is correct.
A **Child in Conflict with Law** goes to the **Juvenile Justice Board**, so options (1) and (2) swap the bodies.
The **District Magistrate** is not the body for children in conflict with law.
xa: ⚠ CCL → **JJB**; CNCP → **CWC**; transferred 16-18 heinous cases → **Children's Court**.
JJB = Magistrate + **2** social workers; CWC = Chairperson + **4** members.
The **2021** amendment made the DM the focal point for implementation and gave him adoption cases.

138.s: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with which term?
138.x: The Act replaced the term ‘juvenile’ with ‘child’, reflecting a child-centred approach.
138.tq: Directly distinguish the exact statutory terminology from nearby legal terms.
xs: The **JJ Act 2015** replaced "juvenile" with **"child"** — option **(3)** is correct.
It created two categories: **Children in Conflict with Law** and **Children in Need of Care and Protection**.
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum punishment of **7 years or more**.
**CARA** was made a **statutory body** by the 2015 Act.
The Act was amended in **2021**.

138.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a ‘heinous offence’ is one for which the minimum punishment is:
138.x: A heinous offence is defined by a minimum punishment of seven years or more.
138.tq: Focus on the statutory minimum threshold rather than the maximum sentence.
xs: A **heinous offence** carries a minimum punishment of **seven years or more** — option **(3)** is correct.
A child aged **16-18** accused of a heinous offence faces a **preliminary assessment** by the JJB.
xa: After assessment the case may go to the **Children's Court** — the "**transfer system**".
Critics say the **transfer system** erodes rehabilitation.
The punitive turn followed the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Juvenile Justice Board may conduct a preliminary assessment in cases involving 16–18-year-olds accused of heinous offences.
2. Such assessment automatically establishes guilt.
3. The case may be transferred to the Children’s Court after the assessment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: The JJB conducts a preliminary assessment and may transfer the matter to the Children’s Court. The assessment does not itself establish guilt.
138.tq: Reject the extreme inference that a preliminary assessment is equivalent to a finding of guilt.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **JJB** conducts a **preliminary assessment** for **16-18**-year-olds accused of heinous offences.
Statement 2 is wrong: the assessment only decides on a possible **transfer**; it does not establish guilt.
Statement 3 is correct: the case may be transferred to the **Children's Court** (a **Sessions Court**).
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum punishment of **7 years or more**.
The transfer system came after the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)**.
Criticism: the **transfer system** erodes rehabilitation.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the Juvenile Justice (Amendment) Act, 2021:
1. It made the District Magistrate the focal point for implementation of the Act.
2. It gave the District Magistrate the power to decide adoption cases.
3. It introduced eligibility conditions for members of Juvenile Justice Boards, not Child Welfare Committees.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
138.x: Statement 1 is correct: the DM became the focal point for implementation. Statement 2 is correct: the DM decides adoption cases after 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: the eligibility conditions were for CWC members. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with statement 3 are wrong.
138.tq: 2021 amendment = DM strengthened (implementation + adoption) and CWC member eligibility.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the **District Magistrate** became the **focal point** for implementation.
Statement 2 is correct: the DM now **decides adoption** cases.
Statement 3 is wrong: the eligibility conditions are for **CWC members**, not JJB members.
xa: The amendment came with the **JJ Amendment Rules** and **Adoption Regulations 2022**.
**CWC** = Chairperson + **4 members**.
**CARA** was made statutory by the **2015** Act.

138.s:
Arrange the following laws in chronological order:
A. Juvenile Justice Act, 2015
B. Children Act, 1960
C. Juvenile Justice Act, 1986
D. Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000
138.x: The correct sequence is Children Act 1960, Juvenile Justice Act 1986, JJ Act 2000 and JJ Act 2015.
138.tq: Fix the earliest and latest laws first, then place the 1986 and 2000 Acts between them.
xs: The order is **B, C, D, A** — option **(1)** is correct.
**Children Act 1960** → **JJ Act 1986** → **JJ (Care and Protection of Children) Act 2000** → **JJ Act 2015**.
xa: The **1960** Act was for **Union Territories**; the **1986** Act was the first uniform law (boys **16**, girls **18**).
The **2000** Act made the age uniform at **18** and was amended in **2006**.
The **2015** Act came into force on **15 Jan 2016** and was amended in **2021**.

138.s: Which feature distinguished the Juvenile Justice Act, 1986?
o: It was the first uniform juvenile law, prescribing different ages for boys and girls
It prescribed a uniform age of 18 years for all children
It applied exclusively to Union Territories
It introduced the transfer system for 16–18-year-olds
138.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 1986 was the first uniform law and prescribed an age of 16 years for boys and 18 years for girls.
138.tq: Compare the age provisions and territorial scope of successive juvenile laws.
xs: The **JJ Act 1986** was the **first uniform** juvenile law, with **different ages for boys and girls** (boys **16**, girls **18**) — option **(1)** is correct.
The uniform age of **18** came with the **2000** Act; the **Children Act 1960** was for Union Territories.
The **transfer system** for **16-18** came with the **2015** Act.
xa: The 2000 Act was amended in **2006**.
The **2015** Act followed the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)**.
The 2015 Act replaced "juvenile" with "**child**".

138.s: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, the age of a juvenile was made uniform at:
138.x: The JJ Act, 2000 prescribed a uniform age of 18 years and was amended in 2006.
138.tq: Distinguish the uniform age under the 2000 Act from the gender-based ages under the 1986 Act.
xs: The **JJ Act 2000** made the age uniform at **18 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
Earlier, the **1986** Act used **16** for boys and **18** for girls.
xa: The 2000 Act was amended in **2006**.
The **2015** Act brought the transfer system for **16-18**-year-olds in heinous offences.
**Children Act 1960** applied to **Union Territories**.

138.s: The punitive turn associated with the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 followed which event?
o: The Delhi gang rape case of 2012
The enactment of the CPCR Act in 2005
138.x: The 2015 Act followed the punitive policy response triggered by the Delhi gang rape case of 2012.
138.tq: Link the legislative change to the event that acted as its immediate trigger.
xs: The punitive turn of the **JJ Act 2015** followed the **Delhi gang rape case (2012)** — option **(2)** is correct.
It brought the **transfer system** for **16-18**-year-olds accused of heinous offences.
The **CPCR Act 2005** created the NCPCR; the **Sivakasi** case (**1996**) concerned child labour.
xa: **Heinous offence** = minimum **7 years or more**.
The JJB's **preliminary assessment** decides on a transfer to the **Children's Court**.
The 2015 Act came into force on **15 Jan 2016**.

138.s: The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) was given statutory status by the:
o: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
138.x: The JJ Act 2015 made CARA a statutory body. HAMA 1956 is a separate adoption route for Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs; the 2021 amendment gave District Magistrates the power to decide adoptions; the CPCR Act 2005 created the NCPCR.
138.tq: CARA statutory: JJ Act 2015; DM decides adoption: 2021 amendment.
xs: The **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015** made **CARA** (Central Adoption Resource Authority) a **statutory body** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **2021** amendment gave the **District Magistrate** power to decide adoptions; the **CPCR Act 2005** set up the **NCPCR**.
xa: **Adoption Regulations 2022** came with the 2021 amendment.
AP CWCs declared **55** children legally free for adoption in FY **2025-26**.
The 2015 Act replaced "juvenile" with "**child**".

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Juvenile Justice Boards and Child Welfare Committees:
1. Every district has both a Juvenile Justice Board and a Child Welfare Committee.
2. Each of them must have at least one woman member.
3. Children in Conflict with Law are dealt with by Child Welfare Committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Every district has both bodies and each must include at least one woman member. Statement 3 is false because Children in Conflict with Law are dealt with by Juvenile Justice Boards.
138.tq: Find the institutional mismatch in the third statement while retaining the composition facts.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: there is a **JJB and a CWC in every district**.
Statement 2 is correct: each has **at least one woman member**.
Statement 3 is wrong: **Children in Conflict with Law** go to the **JJB**, not the CWC.
xa: JJB = **Principal Magistrate** + **2 social workers**; CWC = Chairperson + **4 members**.
In AP, JJBs are headed by a **female Principal Magistrate**.
**Mission Vatsalya** funds JJBs and CWCs in every district.

138.s: A Juvenile Justice Board consists of:
o: A Sessions Judge and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers, at least one of whom is a woman
A Chairperson and four members, all of whom must be social workers
A District Magistrate and five elected representatives
138.x: The Board comprises a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class serving as Principal Magistrate and two social workers, with at least one woman among the social workers.
138.tq: Test composition by separating the judicial member from the social-worker members.
xs: A JJB has a **Principal Magistrate** and **two social workers**, at least one a **woman** — option **(2)** is correct.
The Principal Magistrate is a **Metropolitan/Judicial Magistrate First Class**.
"Chairperson and four members" describes the **CWC**, not the JJB.
xa: ⚠ JJB = Magistrate + **2**; CWC = Chairperson + **4**.
The **Children's Court** (Sessions Court) tries transferred cases.
AP CWCs handled **4,189** cases and disposed **3,691** in FY **2025-26**.

138.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Juvenile Justice Board from the Children's Court?
o: The Children's Court deals only with children requiring care and protection
The Board handles children in conflict with law, while the Children's Court tries cases transferred to it
The Board tries all transferred cases, while the Children's Court conducts preliminary inquiries only
Both bodies have identical jurisdiction in every case
138.x: The Juvenile Justice Board handles children in conflict with law, whereas the Children's Court, a Sessions Court, tries cases transferred to it.
138.tq: Compare jurisdiction and identify the body assigned the transferred trial.
xs: The **JJB** handles children in conflict with law, while the **Children's Court** tries **cases transferred** to it — option **(2)** is correct.
Children needing care and protection go to the **CWC**, not the Children's Court.
The **JJB** does the **preliminary assessment**; the Children's Court (a **Sessions Court**) tries the transferred case.
xa: Transfer applies to **16-18**-year-olds accused of **heinous** offences (minimum **7 years**).
JJB = Principal Magistrate + **2** social workers.
The guiding principle is the **best interests of the child**.

138.s: The guiding principle in inquiries and proceedings involving children under the Juvenile Justice system is:
o: Best interests of the child through child-friendly and rehabilitation-oriented justice
Detention in every case until adulthood
Retributive punishment as the primary objective
138.x: The system is guided by the best interests of the child and follows child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice rather than a punishment-centred approach.
138.tq: Identify the governing principle from the stated purpose of the legal process.
xs: Proceedings follow the **best interests of the child** through **child-friendly, rehabilitation-oriented justice** — option **(1)** is correct.
The system is about rehabilitation, **not punishment**, so detention or retribution is wrong.
xa: Juvenile delinquents are dealt with by **juvenile courts** (APPSC **2019**).
The principle was asked in APPSC **2019** and **2024**.
The **National Policy for Children 2013** also puts best interests first.

138.s: Each Child Welfare Committee in Andhra Pradesh consists of:
o: A District Magistrate and four police officers
A Principal Magistrate and two social workers
138.x: Each Child Welfare Committee consists of one Chairperson and four members.
138.tq: Avoid confusing the composition of a Child Welfare Committee with that of a Juvenile Justice Board.
xs: Each **Child Welfare Committee** has a **Chairperson and four members** — option **(1)** is correct.
"Principal Magistrate and two social workers" is the **JJB**.
xa: AP CWCs handled **4,189** cases and disposed **3,691** in FY **2025-26**.
**55** children were declared legally free for adoption.
Selection for CWCs and JJBs is being done in AP's **13 new districts**.

138.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated feature of Juvenile Justice Boards?
o: They deal with children in conflict with law.
They aim at rehabilitation of children.
They decide adoption cases as the final authority.
138.x: JJBs deal with children in conflict with law and focus on rehabilitation. Adoption cases are decided under the adoption framework, with the District Magistrate acquiring this role after the 2021 amendment.
138.tq: Find the institution-function mismatch by separating rehabilitation from adoption authority.
xs: JJBs do **not decide adoption cases** — option **(4)** is the wrong feature.
After the **2021** amendment, the **District Magistrate** decides adoption cases.
JJBs are **child-friendly**, deal with **children in conflict with law** and aim at **rehabilitation**.
xa: **CARA** is a statutory body under the **2015** Act.
JJB = Principal Magistrate + **2 social workers**, at least one a woman.
In AP, JJBs exist in the **erstwhile 13 districts**.

138.s: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by which Ministry of the Government of India?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
138.x: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
138.tq: Identify the ministry associated with the legislation rather than its implementing agencies.
xs: **POCSO** was drafted by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** — option **(1)** is correct.
The Act came into force on **14 November 2012**.
xa: A child = below **18 years**, **gender-neutral** for child and offender.
POCSO remains a separate special law after the **BNS 2023** replaced the IPC from **1 July 2024**.
The **NCPCR and SCPCRs** monitor POCSO.

138.s: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, which one of the following is correct regarding the definition of a child?
o: A person below 16 years, only if female
A person below 14 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 21 years, irrespective of gender
A person below 18 years, irrespective of gender
138.x: POCSO treats every person below 18 years as a child and applies in a gender-neutral manner.
138.tq: Distinguish the age and gender-neutral definition under POCSO from other child-related laws.
xs: POCSO defines a child as a person **below 18 years**, **irrespective of gender** — option **(4)** is correct.
The Act is **gender-neutral** for both child and offender.
xa: Consent below **18** is **legally irrelevant** ("statutory rape").
**BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps the age of consent at **18**.
⚠ Marriage age is distinct: **18** for women, **21** for men.

138.s: Under the POCSO Act, an offence committed by a person in a position of trust is treated as
o: an offence applicable only to institutions
138.x: The Act treats offences committed by a person in a position of trust as aggravated offences.
138.tq: Test the legal consequence attached to a special relationship of trust.
xs: An offence by a person in **trust or authority** is an **aggravated** offence — option **(4)** is correct.
Examples: **police**, **security forces**, **public servant**.
xa: POCSO offences: **penetrative** and **non-penetrative** assault, aggravated forms, **sexual harassment**, **child pornography**.
**2019**: aggravated penetrative assault minimum **20 years**, up to **life or death penalty**.
Penetrative sexual assault minimum: **10 years**.

138.s: The 21 April 2018 Ordinance relating to the POCSO Act primarily provided for
o: replacement of mandatory reporting with voluntary reporting
harsher punishment for rape of young girls
lowering the age of a child to 14 years
138.x: The Ordinance of 21 April 2018 introduced harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
138.tq: Match the dated legislative measure with its principal substantive change.
xs: The **21 April 2018** Ordinance provided **harsher punishment for rape of young girls** — option **(2)** is correct.
POCSO still keeps **mandatory reporting**, **Special Courts** and the age of **18**.
xa: **2019 Amendment**: penetrative assault minimum **10 years**; aggravated minimum **20 years**; up to **death penalty**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.
The 2018 date was asked by APPSC.

138.s: Which of the following correctly describes the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: It introduced the death penalty for aggravated penetrative assault and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years
It removed the punishment of imprisonment for aggravated penetrative assault
It made all POCSO offences compoundable
It reduced the minimum punishment to 7 years
138.x: The 2019 amendment provided for the death penalty in aggravated penetrative assault cases and prescribed a minimum punishment of 20 years. The POCSO Rules were framed in 2020.
138.tq: Use the precise punishment figures to distinguish the amendment from neighbouring provisions.
xs: The **2019** amendment brought the **death penalty** for **aggravated penetrative assault** and a minimum of **20 years** — option **(1)** is correct.
It raised punishments, so options (2) and (4) are wrong; the penetrative minimum is **10 years**, not 7.
xa: ⚠ **10** = penetrative minimum; **20** = aggravated minimum.
Storing child pornography without deleting/reporting: fine at least **Rs 5,000**; repeat **Rs 10,000**.
It also punishes giving **chemicals to hasten sexual maturity**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding consent under the POCSO Act:
1. Consent of a person below 18 years is legally irrelevant under the Act.
2. Sexual activity with a person below 18 may constitute statutory rape even where apparent consent is present.
3. The Act treats the age of consent as 16 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because POCSO fixes the relevant age at 18 years.
138.tq: Split the options by checking the statutory age against the debated age of consent.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: consent below **18** is **legally irrelevant**.
Statement 2 is correct: such acts are "**statutory rape**" even with apparent consent.
Statement 3 is wrong: POCSO fixes the age at **18**, not 16.
xa: The **MP High Court** asked the Centre to lower it to **16** (APPSC **2022**).
SC in **State of UP v. Anurudh** urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT an offence specifically identified under the POCSO Act?
o: Child marriage as an independent POCSO offence
138.x: POCSO identifies penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault, aggravated forms, sexual harassment and child pornography. Child marriage is not listed as an independent POCSO offence in this classification.
138.tq: Find the item outside the statutory list of offences.
xs: **Child marriage** is not an independent POCSO offence — option **(4)** is correct.
POCSO offences: **penetrative** and **non-penetrative** assault, aggravated forms, **sexual harassment** and **child pornography**.
xa: Child marriage is a form of **social** abuse in the notes.
NFHS-5: over **27%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**.
**2019**: child pornography defined; fine at least **Rs 5,000** for storing it.

138.s: Under Section 19 of the POCSO Act, information about an offence is required to be reported to the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights only
Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police
138.x: Section 19 requires information about a POCSO offence to be reported to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police.
138.tq: Identify the authority responsible for receiving mandatory reports.
xs: **Section 19** requires reporting to the **Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police** — option **(4)** is correct.
Anyone, **including a child**, who knows of an offence must report.
Failure to report: up to **6 months** and/or fine.
xa: **False complaints** are punishable (**Sec. 22**), except good-faith ones.
Burden of proof on the accused — **presumption against the accused** (**Sec. 29-30**).
Special Courts: investigation in **2 months**, trial within **1 year**.

138.s: Which one of the following is inconsistent with the child-friendly procedure prescribed under the POCSO Act?
o: The statement should preferably be recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank who is not in uniform.
The child’s statement may be recorded at the child’s residence.
The statement may be recorded at a place chosen by the child.
The child must be questioned at the police station during the night to prevent interference.
138.x: A child must not be kept at a police station at night. The statement is preferably recorded by a woman police officer of at least Sub-Inspector rank, not in uniform, at the child’s residence or chosen place.
138.tq: Locate the reversed child-friendly safeguard.
xs: Questioning the child **at the police station during the night** breaks the POCSO procedure — option **(4)** is the inconsistent one.
**No child is kept at a police station at night**, and the child has **no contact with the accused**.
The statement is taken at the **child's residence or place of choice**, preferably by a **woman police officer (at least SI)** **not in uniform** — so (1), (2) and (3) are correct.
xa: **Special Courts** hold **in-camera** trials; investigation in **2 months**, trial within **1 year**.
Special Courts also order **compensation and rehabilitation**.
**NCPCR and SCPCRs** monitor the Act.

138.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

List-I — Provision
 a. Section 19
 b. Sections 29–30
 c. Section 22

List-II — Subject
 i. False complaints
 ii. Mandatory reporting
 iii. Burden of proof on the accused
138.x: Section 19 concerns mandatory reporting, Sections 29–30 place the burden of proof on the accused, and Section 22 deals with false complaints, subject to the good-faith exception.
138.tq: Start from the sure statutory-section pair and eliminate inconsistent codes.
xs: **a–ii, b–iii, c–i** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Section 19** = **mandatory reporting** to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or local police.
**Sections 29-30** = **burden of proof on the accused** (presumption against the accused).
**Section 22** = **false complaints** punishable, except good-faith ones.
xa: Failure to report: up to **6 months** and/or fine.
Anyone, **including a child**, who knows of an offence must report it.
⚠ Investigation **2 months**; trial **1 year**; non-reporting up to **6 months**.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the trial framework under the POCSO Act?
o: Trial before the High Court within one month without compensation provisions
In-camera trial, with investigation targeted within two months and trial within one year
Open trial within two years after investigation by any police station
Trial only before a Juvenile Justice Board within six months
138.x: POCSO provides for in-camera proceedings, investigation within two months and trial within one year; special courts also address compensation and rehabilitation.
138.tq: Combine the court type and statutory time limits without reversing them.
xs: POCSO provides an **in-camera trial**, investigation within **two months** and trial within **one year** — option **(2)** is correct.
Trials are before **Special Courts**, not the High Court or a JJB, and are not open.
Special Courts also provide **compensation and rehabilitation**.
xa: Statement recorded preferably by a **woman police officer (at least SI)**, **not in uniform**.
No child kept at a police station at night; no contact with the accused.
**Disposals** of cases are up (**109%**) but convictions are falling.

138.s: Which additional conduct was specifically addressed by the 2019 amendment to the POCSO Act?
o: Failure to attend school up to 14 years
Employing a child in all forms of domestic work
Giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity
Permitting marriage below the statutory age
138.x: The 2019 amendment introduced punishment for giving chemicals to a child to hasten sexual maturity.
138.tq: Identify the specific conduct added by the amendment instead of a related child-protection offence.
xs: The **2019** amendment punishes **giving chemicals to hasten sexual maturity** — option **(3)** is correct.
School attendance, domestic work and marriage age are not part of the 2019 POCSO changes in the notes.
xa: 2019: penetrative assault minimum **10 years**; aggravated minimum **20 years**; up to **life or death penalty**.
2019: **child pornography** defined; storing it without deleting/reporting = fine at least **Rs 5,000**, repeat **Rs 10,000**.
**POCSO Rules 2020** replaced the 2012 Rules.

138.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: POCSO Act — law applicable only to female children
POCSO Act — separate special law retained after replacement of the IPC by the BNS
POCSO Act — subsumed entirely into the BNS from 1 July 2024
POCSO Act — law dealing exclusively with child labour
138.x: The IPC was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita from 1 July 2024, but POCSO continues as a separate special law.
138.tq: Distinguish repeal or replacement of the IPC from the continued existence of a separate special statute.
xs: POCSO remains a **separate special law** after the **BNS** replaced the IPC — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023** replaced the IPC from **1 July 2024**; POCSO was not subsumed in it.
POCSO is **gender-neutral** and deals with **sexual offences**, not child labour.
xa: **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps the age of consent at **18**.
Trafficking is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.
POCSO was drafted by the **MWCD** and came into force on **14 November 2012**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the POCSO Act, 2012:
1. It came into force on 14 November 2012.
2. The 2019 amendment raised the minimum punishment for penetrative sexual assault to 10 years.
3. The POCSO Rules, 2020 were added alongside the 2012 Rules, which continue in force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: POCSO came into force on 14 November 2012, and the 2019 amendment set a minimum of 10 years (extendable to life) for penetrative sexual assault. Statement 3 is wrong: the POCSO Rules 2020 replaced the 2012 Rules, so options B, C and D are wrong.
138.tq: POCSO 2019: penetrative min 10 yrs; aggravated min 20 yrs / death.
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(1)**.
Statement 1 is correct: POCSO came into force on **14 November 2012**.
Statement 2 is correct: the **2019** amendment set a minimum of **10 years** (extendable to life) for penetrative assault.
Statement 3 is wrong: the **POCSO Rules 2020** **replaced** the 2012 Rules.
xa: Aggravated penetrative assault: minimum **20 years**, up to **death penalty**.
The **21 April 2018** Ordinance brought harsher punishment for rape of young girls.
Full name: **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012**.

138.s:
Arrange the following stages in the history of the age of consent in India in chronological order:
A. Age of Consent Act fixed the age at 12 years
B. IPC amendment fixed the age at 14 years
C. POCSO fixed the age at 18 years
D. IPC 1860 fixed the age at 10 years
138.x: The sequence is IPC 1860—10 years, Age of Consent Act 1891—12 years, IPC amendment 1925—14 years, and POCSO 2012—18 years.
138.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest IPC provision and the final POCSO provision.
xs: The order is **D, A, B, C** — option **(1)** is correct.
xa: The age was raised to **16** in **1949**.
**CLA 2013** also kept **18**; **BNS (Sec. 63)** keeps **18**.
⚠ Marriage age is distinct: **18** for women, **21** for men.

138.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Justice Verma Committee recommended reducing the age of consent to 16 years.
2. The 240th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development, 2011, rejected the concept of minor consent.
3. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 retains 18 years as the age of consent under Section 63.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. The Justice Verma Committee supported 16 years, the 2011 parliamentary report rejected minor consent, and BNS Section 63 retains 18 years.
138.tq: Check recommendations and the current statutory position separately before selecting the combination.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the **Justice Verma Committee** wanted **16**.
Statement 2: the **240th Report** of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on HRD (**2011**) **rejected minor consent**.
Statement 3: **BNS Sec. 63** keeps **18**.
xa: **Standing Committee on Home Affairs, 167th Report (2012)** backed **18**.
**Law Commission 283rd Report (2023)**: lowering would make POCSO a **"paper law"**.
⚠ APPSC **2022** keyed as "true" that the committee recommended lowering the age from **18**.

138.s: The Madhya Pradesh High Court asked the Union Government to consider lowering the age of consent to 16 years primarily on the ground of:
o: early puberty associated with exposure through social media
the introduction of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
the difference between the age of marriage and voting age
138.x: The Madhya Pradesh High Court cited early puberty linked to social-media exposure while asking the Centre to consider lowering the age of consent to 16 years.
138.tq: Match the judicial observation with its stated rationale.
xs: The **MP High Court** cited **early puberty** due to **social-media exposure** — option **(1)** is correct.
It asked the Centre to lower the age of consent to **16** (APPSC **2022**).
xa: A **Private Member's Bill (Dec 2025)** seeks to lower it from **16 to 14** years.
The **Law Commission 283rd Report (2023)** opposed lowering it.
SC in **State of UP v. Anurudh** urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause** (Jan **2026**).

138.s:
With reference to the Supreme Court’s decision concerning a Calcutta High Court ruling on adolescent relationships, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling.
2. The Supreme Court excluded consensual adolescent relationships from the operation of POCSO.
3. The Supreme Court used Article 142 for sentencing flexibility.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false: the Supreme Court set aside the ruling that had excluded consensual adolescent relationships from POCSO; it did not itself create such an exclusion.
138.tq: Use the reversed judicial holding as the false statement trap.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: the SC **set aside** the Calcutta HC ruling.
Statement 2 is wrong: it was the **HC** that kept consensual adolescent relationships outside POCSO; the SC held that **a minor cannot consent**.
Statement 3 is correct: the SC used **Art. 142** for **sentencing flexibility**.
xa: In **State of UP v. Anurudh** the SC flagged **misuse of POCSO** and urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.
Debate: **close-in-age exemption** vs keeping the age at **18** with judicial discretion.
SC: child assessments must involve **"minimum intrusion"** where the child is an alleged abuse victim.

138.s: The age of consent under POCSO should not be confused with the legal age of marriage, which is:
o: 18 years for women and 21 years for men
21 years for women and 18 years for men
18 years for women and 18 years for men
16 years for women and 18 years for men
138.x: The age of consent under POCSO is 18 years. The legal marriage age referred to here is 18 years for women and 21 years for men.
138.tq: Separate two closely related but legally distinct age thresholds.
xs: The marriage age is **18 for women and 21 for men** — option **(1)** is correct.
It is distinct from the age of consent under POCSO, which is **18** for all.
xa: NFHS-5: over **27%** of women aged **20-24** married before **18**; newer figure **23.3%**.
Child marriage is listed as **social** abuse.
**APSES 2024-25**: **877** child marriages prevented in AP.

138.s:
With reference to the age of consent under POCSO, consider the following statements:
1. The Standing Committee on Home Affairs, in its 167th Report of 2012, supported retaining 18 years.
2. The Law Commission, in its 283rd Report of 2023, stated that lowering the age could make POCSO a “paper law”.
3. The Supreme Court in January 2026 urged consideration of a Romeo-Juliet clause for consensual adolescent relationships.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. The 2012 Standing Committee supported 18 years, the 2023 Law Commission warned against lowering it, and the Supreme Court suggested a Romeo-Juliet clause in January 2026.
138.tq: Arrange the reports and judicial development by institution and year before selecting the combined code.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: the **Standing Committee on Home Affairs, 167th Report (2012)** backed **18**.
Statement 2: the **Law Commission 283rd Report (2023)** warned lowering would make POCSO a **"paper law"**.
Statement 3: in **State of UP v. Anurudh** (Jan **2026**) the SC urged a **"Romeo-Juliet" clause**.
xa: The **Justice Verma Committee** wanted **16**.
The **240th Report** (**2011**, Standing Committee on HRD) rejected minor consent.
The **MP High Court** asked for **16**, citing social-media exposure.

138.s: Operation Smile and Operation Muskaan are primarily associated with:
138.x: These MHA-led drives trace and rescue missing children.
138.tq: Match the operation names with their distinctive field objective.
xs: **Operation Smile / Operation Muskaan** are **MHA**-led drives for **tracing and rescuing missing children** — option **(1)** is correct.
Child-care institutions, adoption and exams are not their purpose.
xa: The drives began in **2015**.
AP's **Operation Muskaan** rescued over **1,200 children** from railway stations, bus stands, markets and dhabas.
⚠ AP's **Operation Chinnari-Thalli** targets **sexual offences** against children.

138.s: Operation Smile and Operation Muskaan were initiated as drives in:
138.x: The drives to trace and rescue missing children were initiated in 2015.
138.tq: Distinguish the launch year from nearby years associated with other child-protection measures.
xs: **Operation Smile / Operation Muskaan** began in **2015** — option **(3)** is correct.
They are **MHA**-led drives to trace and rescue missing children.
xa: ⚠ **POCSO e-Box** = NCPCR, **2016**; **PENCiL** = MoLE, **2017**.
AP's **Operation Muskaan** task force rescued **1,200+** children (Feb **2026**).
**India rescues**: **40,000+** children in **2024-25**.

138.s:
The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 2013 widened the concept of trafficking to include which of the following?
1. Sexual exploitation
2. Slavery and servitude
3. Forced labour
4. Organ removal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: The widened concept includes sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and organ removal.
138.tq: Test the breadth of the statutory definition by retaining all listed forms of exploitation.
xs: **All four** — sexual exploitation, slavery and servitude, forced labour and organ removal — option **(4)** is correct.
The **Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013** widened the trafficking definition.
xa: The definition applies **irrespective of consent**.
Trafficking is now **Section 143, BNS 2023**.
**Anti-Human Trafficking Units** work in districts under **MHA** funding.

138.s: Under the widened legal understanding of trafficking, the listed forms of exploitation are covered:
o: Only when physical force is proved
Only when the victim is below 18 years
Only when the victim has not consented
138.x: The widened definition covers the specified forms of trafficking irrespective of consent.
138.tq: Identify the legal qualifier that prevents consent from excluding the conduct from the trafficking definition.
xs: The widened definition covers trafficking **irrespective of consent** — option **(4)** is correct.
So proof of force, absence of consent or the victim's age are not required.
xa: The widening came through the **Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013**.
It covers sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour and **organ removal**.
Related instruments: **UN CRC** and the **Palermo Protocol**.

138.s: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the:
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
State Commission for Protection of Child Rights alone
Ministry of Home Affairs’ Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre
138.x: The POCSO e-Box was launched in 2016 by the NCPCR for online complaints of child sexual abuse.
138.tq: Apply the ‘who launched it?’ test to distinguish the NCPCR from cybercrime authorities.
xs: The **POCSO e-Box** was launched in **2016** by the **National Commission for Protection of Child Rights** (NCPCR) — option **(2)** is correct.
It takes **online complaints** of child sexual abuse.
xa: **NCPCR** is statutory, set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005**.
NCPCR monitors **POCSO**, the **JJ Act** and the **RTE Act**.
⚠ **cybercrime.gov.in** is run under **I4C, MHA** — not the e-Box.

138.s: The portal cybercrime.gov.in is used particularly for reporting:
o: Cases relating exclusively to child marriage registration
Child sexual abuse material and other online abuse
Physical abuse occurring only in schools
Violations of minimum employment age only
138.x: The cybercrime portal cybercrime.gov.in is used for CSAM and other online abuse, under the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and the Ministry of Home Affairs.
138.tq: Identify the reporting channel from the nature of the abuse—online rather than physical or institutional.
xs: **cybercrime.gov.in** is for **child sexual abuse material and other online abuse** — option **(2)** is correct.
It is run under **I4C, MHA**.
xa: Over **4.5 lakh** CSAM cases were reported in India in **2023**.
CSAM is dealt with under the **IT Act 2000**; **IT Rules 2021** require automatic detection.
⚠ **POCSO e-Box** (**2016**, NCPCR) takes complaints of child sexual abuse.

138.s: The offence of trafficking of persons, widened by the Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013, is now dealt with under which provision?
o: Section 370, Indian Penal Code, which continues in force
138.x: Trafficking is now Section 143 of the BNS 2023. Section 63 BNS is the rape provision that keeps the age of consent at 18; Section 19 POCSO concerns mandatory reporting; the IPC was replaced by the BNS from 1 July 2024.
138.tq: Trafficking: CLA 2013 -> now Sec. 143 BNS.
xs: Trafficking is now under **Section 143, BNS 2023** — option **(2)** is correct.
**Section 63, BNS** keeps the **age of consent** at **18**; **Section 19, POCSO** is **mandatory reporting**.
The IPC no longer continues — the **BNS** replaced it from **1 July 2024**.
xa: The **Criminal Law Amendment Act 2013** widened trafficking, **irrespective of consent**.
It covers sexual exploitation, slavery, servitude, forced labour, organ removal.
**AHTUs** operate in districts under MHA funding.

138.s: According to Census 2011, the number of child labourers in the 5–14 age group in India was approximately:
138.x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14. The 4.35 million figure refers only to main workers.
138.tq: Separate the overall count from the narrower main-worker figure.
xs: **Census 2011**: about **10.1 million** child labourers aged **5-14** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **4.35 million** counts **main workers only**; **8 M** is the rural share.
xa: Split: **5.6 M boys**, **4.5 M girls**; about **8 M** rural, **2 M** urban — urban child labour is rising.
Decline **2001-2011**: only **2.2% a year** (CRY).
Global: **137.6 million** in **2024** (**54 M** in hazardous work).

138.s: Which of the following is the correct descending sequence of the states identified among the leading states in child labour?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh
138.x: The listed order is Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
138.tq: Preserve the sequence exactly when the question supplies a ranked list.
xs: The top states are listed as **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh** — option **(1)** is correct.
The other options shuffle the same five states.
xa: Census **2011**: **10.1 million** child labourers aged **5-14**.
**Main workers only**: **4.35 million**.
**India rescues**: **40,000+** children in **2024-25**.

138.s:
Which of the following sectors are associated with child labour as identified in the given context?
1. Brick kilns
2. Pesticide-heavy farm work
3. Work involving toxic chemicals
4. Tea stalls
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Brick kilns, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals and tea stalls are all identified sectors or settings associated with child labour.
138.tq: Include all sector examples and avoid narrowing the list to hazardous industrial work alone.
xs: **All four** — brick kilns, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals, tea stalls — option **(4)** is correct.
The notes also list **begging** among child-labour sectors.
xa: **India has the largest number of child labourers** in the world.
**Debt bondage** drives child labour in farms, brick kilns and domestic work.
**Mines Act 1952**: no one below **18**.

138.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a cause or contributing factor of child labour?
138.x: Poverty, debt bondage and weak enforcement are identified causes. Universal access to quality education is not a cause of child labour.
138.tq: Find the positive protective condition among the listed causal factors.
xs: **Universal access to quality education** is not a cause of child labour — option **(4)** is correct.
**Poverty**, **debt bondage** and **weak enforcement** are all listed causes.
xa: **Cheap labour**: employers get more work for less pay.
Other causes: family disorganisation, lack of awareness, **kidnapping**.
The **2016** ban for children below **14** is linked to the **RTE** age.

138.s: Why do employers often prefer child labour, according to the stated economic explanation?
o: Children can independently negotiate employment contracts
Children are legally entitled to higher wages
Children provide more work for less pay
138.x: Employers may obtain more work for less pay by employing children, creating an economic incentive for child labour.
138.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to the employer’s incentive.
xs: Employers get **more work for less pay** from children — option **(4)** is correct.
This **cheap labour** factor is an economic incentive; the other options are not in the notes.
xa: **Poverty** forces children to support families.
**Debt bondage** runs across generations.
The **Gurupadswamy Committee (1979)** called poverty the **root cause**.

138.s:
Debt bondage is associated with child and bonded labour particularly in which of the following settings?
1. Farms
2. Brick kilns
3. Domestic work
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: Debt bondage drives child and bonded labour in farms, brick kilns and domestic work.
138.tq: Test whether all the sectoral examples in the causal statement are retained.
xs: Debt bondage drives child and bonded labour in **farms, brick kilns and domestic work** — option **(4)** (**1, 2 and 3**) is correct.
The notes list all three settings together, so no option leaving one out can be right.
xa: Bonded labour was outlawed by the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976**.
Debt bondage runs **across generations**.
**29** Chenchu/Yanadi tribals from **Prakasam** were rescued from a coal kiln in **Telangana** (Mar **2026**).

138.s: The abolition of bonded labour is specifically associated with which law?
138.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 outlawed bonded labour.
138.tq: Match the social evil with the legislation that abolished it.
xs: Bonded labour was outlawed by the **Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **Mines Act 1952** bars anyone below **18** from mines; the **Factories Act 1948** bars children below **14**.
The **JJ Act 2015** deals with children in conflict with law and children needing care.
xa: Debt bondage drives child labour in **farms**, **brick kilns** and **domestic work**.
It runs **across generations**.
Under the **JJ Act 2015**, working children are **children needing care and protection**.

138.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of a child below 14 years after the 2016 amendment?
o: Employment is banned in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions
Employment is banned only in mines and factories
Employment is permitted in all non-hazardous occupations without restriction
Employment is regulated only through the Right to Education Act
138.x: After the 2016 amendment, employment of children below 14 years is prohibited in all occupations and processes, subject to specified exceptions.
138.tq: Separate the post-amendment blanket prohibition from the earlier listed-work model.
xs: After **2016**, a child below **14** is **banned in all occupations and processes**, subject to exceptions — option **(1)** is correct.
The ban is linked to the **RTE** age.
xa: Exceptions: helping **family/family enterprise after school hours**; child **artist** in audio-visual entertainment (not circus).
**Adolescents** (**14-18**) are banned only from **hazardous** work.
⚠ 1986 = only **18** occupations, **65** processes banned.

138.s: The original 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in how many occupations and processes, respectively?
138.x: The original law listed 18 prohibited occupations and 65 prohibited processes for children below 14 years.
138.tq: Match the two numerical components without reversing their order.
xs: The **1986** Act banned children from **18 occupations and 65 processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Other work was merely **regulated**, which clashed with the **RTE Act 2009**.
xa: ⚠ **83** was the number of entries in the earlier hazardous list, trimmed in **2016**.
Under the 1986 Act a child = one who has not completed **14 years**.
The **1986** year was asked in APPSC **2019**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the principal hazardous categories retained after the 2016 amendment?
o: Hazardous processes under the Factories Act
138.x: The retained hazardous categories are mines, inflammable substances and explosives, and hazardous processes under the Factories Act. All agricultural occupations are not included as a category of the hazardous list.
138.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the narrowed hazardous list.
xs: **All agricultural occupations** are not a hazardous category — option **(4)** is correct.
The list was trimmed to **mines**, **inflammable substances/explosives** and **hazardous processes** under the Factories Act.
xa: The earlier list had **83** entries.
The **Centre** may add or omit occupations.
**Adolescents** (**14-18**) are barred only from these hazardous occupations/processes.

138.s: Which authority may add or omit occupations from the hazardous list under the amended child labour law?
138.x: The Centre may add occupations to, or omit occupations from, the hazardous list.
138.tq: Apply the ‘who has the power’ method to identify the competent authority.
xs: The **Central Government** (the Centre) may add or omit occupations from the hazardous list — option **(1)** is correct.
The **District Magistrate** enforces the law but does not amend the list.
xa: The list was trimmed to **mines, inflammable substances/explosives and hazardous processes**.
**Amendment Rules 2017** were notified by **MoLE**.
Offences are **cognizable**.

138.s:
With reference to the exceptions under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. A child may help the family or a family enterprise after school hours.
2. A child may work as an artist in audio-visual entertainment, including circus.
3. The child-artist exception applies only if the child's schooling is not affected.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
138.x: Statement 1 is correct: helping the family/family enterprise after school hours is an exception. Statement 2 is wrong: the audio-visual entertainment exception excludes circus. Statement 3 is correct: schooling must not be affected. So '1 only' leaves out a true statement, and options containing 2 are wrong.
138.tq: Circus is always excluded from the child-artist exception; look for it as the planted error.
xs: Statements **1 and 3** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: a child may help the **family/family enterprise after school hours**.
Statement 2 is wrong: the audio-visual entertainment exception **excludes circus**.
Statement 3 is correct: the artist exception applies only if **schooling is not affected**.
xa: Child below **14**: banned in **all** occupations; adolescent **14-18**: banned in **hazardous** work only.
Penalty: **6 months-2 years** and/or **₹20,000-50,000**.
Fund: **Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund**.

138.s: The primary responsibility for enforcement of the amended child labour law is vested in the:
o: Chairperson of the Child Welfare Committee
Principal Magistrate of the Juvenile Justice Board
138.x: Enforcement powers under the amended framework rest with the District Magistrate.
138.tq: Use the authority-power trap by identifying the designated enforcement authority.
xs: Enforcement rests with the **District Magistrate** — option **(2)** is correct.
The **CWC** chairperson and the **JJB**'s Principal Magistrate belong to the JJ system, not child-labour enforcement.
xa: **State Governments** implement; the Centre frames policy.
Tools: **labour inspectors**, surprise inspections, rescue and rehabilitation.
Offences are **cognizable**.

138.s: The Gurupadswamy Committee, 1979, identified which of the following as the root cause of child labour?
138.x: The Gurupadswamy Committee identified poverty as the root cause of child labour and recommended banning hazardous work while regulating the rest.
138.tq: Link the committee with its central diagnosis and policy recommendation.
xs: The **Gurupadswamy Committee (1979)** called **poverty** the **root cause** of child labour — option **(2)** is correct.
It recommended **banning hazardous work** and **regulating the rest**.
xa: The **National Policy on Child Labour** followed in **1987**.
The **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act** came in **1986**.
**NCLP** started in **1988**.

138.s: Which policy followed the recommendations associated with the Gurupadswamy Committee?
138.x: The National Policy on Child Labour followed in 1987.
138.tq: Separate the child-labour policy of 1987 from later general child-policy instruments.
xs: The **National Policy on Child Labour, 1987** followed — option **(1)** is correct.
The **National Policy for Children 2013** treats everyone below **18** as a child — a different policy.
xa: **Gurupadswamy Committee** = **1979**; Child Labour Act = **1986**; **NCLP** = **1988**.
The committee's line: ban hazardous work, **regulate** the rest.
**NCLP** was run by **MoLE**, not MoSJE.

138.s: Which of the following correctly states the age limits under the Factories Act, 1948 and the Mines Act, 1952?
o: Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 16 prohibited
Factories Act: below 18 prohibited; Mines Act: below 14 prohibited
Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
Factories Act: below 16 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
138.x: The Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment of children below 14, while the Mines Act, 1952 prohibits anyone below 18 from working in mines.
138.tq: Compare the two age thresholds without interchanging the Acts.
xs: **Factories Act**: below **14** prohibited; **Mines Act**: below **18** prohibited — option **(3)** is correct.
The Factories Act is of **1948**, the Mines Act of **1952**.
xa: ⚠ Factories Act = below **14**; Mines Act = below **18**.
**2016**: **mines** stay on the hazardous list for adolescents.
The **1986** Act defined a child as one who has not completed **14 years**.

138.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, working children are treated as:
o: Adult workers requiring wage protection only
Children in conflict with law in every case
Children in need of care and protection
138.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 treats working children as children in need of care and protection.
138.tq: Identify the correct statutory child-protection category.
xs: The **JJ Act 2015** treats working children as **children in need of care and protection** — option **(4)** is correct.
Such children go to the **Child Welfare Committee**, not the JJB.
xa: ⚠ CCL → **JJB**; CNCP → **CWC**.
**CWC** = Chairperson + **4 members**.
The NCPCR campaign rescued **3,800+** children from child labour (**2026**).

138.s: Before the 2016 amendment, the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 provided that children below 14 years could not be employed in:
o: Only the occupations and processes listed in the Act
138.x: The 1986 law prohibited children below 14 years from employment in listed occupations and processes, while work elsewhere was regulated rather than completely prohibited.
138.tq: Compare the limited prohibition under the original law with the later wider prohibition.
xs: Before **2016**, children below **14** were barred only from **the occupations and processes listed in the Act** — option **(2)** is correct.
The list had **18 occupations, 65 processes**; other work was merely **regulated**.
xa: This clashed with the **RTE Act 2009**.
**2016**: children below **14** banned in **all** occupations.
The "**adolescent**" category came only in **2016**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements regarding enforcement and penalties under the amended child labour law:
1. Offences under the Act are cognizable.
2. The penalty may include imprisonment from six months to two years.
3. The fine may range from ₹20,000 to ₹50,000.
4. The Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund is established under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All four statements are correct. The amendment made offences cognizable, prescribed imprisonment and fines, and provided for a Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund.
138.tq: Combine legal character, punishment figures and institutional provisions in one coded question.
xs: **All four** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Offences are **cognizable**; imprisonment **6 months-2 years** and/or fine **₹20,000-50,000**.
The **Child and Adolescent Labour Rehabilitation Fund** is set up.
xa: Enforcement: **District Magistrate**.
Rules: **Amendment Rules 2017** notified by **MoLE**.
⚠ M.C. Mehta (**1996**): employer pays **₹20,000 per child** into a rehabilitation-cum-welfare fund.

138.s: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the category of 'adolescent'. Which of the following correctly describes it?
o: Persons aged 14-18, barred only from hazardous occupations and processes
Persons aged 14-18, barred from all occupations and processes
Persons aged 12-16, barred only from hazardous occupations
Persons aged 16-21, allowed in all occupations with parental consent
138.x: The 2016 amendment created the adolescent category (14-18), banned only from hazardous occupations and processes; children below 14 are banned from all occupations. Option B applies the child rule to adolescents, and C and D give wrong age bands.
138.tq: Below 14: total ban; 14-18 adolescents: hazardous ban only (2016).
xs: **Adolescents** are aged **14-18** and barred only from **hazardous occupations and processes** — option **(1)** is correct.
Option (2) applies the **child** rule (below **14**, all work banned) to adolescents.
Options (3) and (4) give wrong age bands.
xa: The adolescent category came only in **2016**.
Hazardous list: **mines**, **inflammable substances/explosives**, **hazardous processes**.
**Mines Act 1952** bars anyone below **18**.

138.s: PENCIL is the abbreviation for:
o: Project for Enforcement and Control of Illegal Child Labour
Programme for Education and Care of Neglected Child Labour
Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour
Platform for Elimination of Child Labour through National Law
138.x: PENCIL stands for Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour.
138.tq: Discriminate the exact expansion of an official acronym from plausible look-alike expansions.
xs: **PENCIL** = **Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is an online portal for enforcing the amended **1986 Act**; the other expansions are invented.
xa: Launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** on **26 Sep 2017**.
⚠ Trap: **SPARC**, **SRIJAN**, **YUKTI** were wrong options (APPSC-G2 **2025**).
Components: **Child Tracking System**, **Complaint Corner**, State Government, **NCLP**, Convergence.

138.s: The PENCIL portal is primarily intended for enforcement of:
o: The Right to Education Act, 2009 only
The amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986
The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 only
138.x: PENCIL is the online portal for effective enforcement of the amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.
138.tq: Match the portal with its governing legislation rather than with another child-rights law.
xs: PENCIL enforces the **amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986** — option **(3)** is correct.
It is not a portal for the RTE, JJ or POCSO Acts.
xa: Asked in APPSC-G2 **2025**.
Ministry: **Labour and Employment**; launched **2017**.
⚠ **POCSO e-Box** (**2016**, NCPCR) is the complaint channel for child sexual abuse.

138.s: Which Ministry launched the PENCIL portal?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
138.x: The PENCIL portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
138.tq: Use the ministry-body association trap by distinguishing labour administration from social welfare administration.
xs: PENCIL was launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **POCSO** was drafted by the **MWCD**; **NCLP** is under **MoLE**, not MoSJE.
xa: Launch date: **26 Sep 2017**.
PENCIL's components include the **Child Tracking System** and **Complaint Corner**.
**Amendment Rules 2017** were also notified by **MoLE**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the PENCIL portal?
138.x: The listed PENCIL components include the Child Tracking System, Complaint Corner, State Government, NCLP and Convergence. National Adoption Registry is not one of them.
138.tq: Find the component that belongs to adoption administration rather than labour-enforcement architecture.
xs: **National Adoption Registry** is not a PENCIL component — option **(3)** is correct.
Components: **Child Tracking System**, **Complaint Corner**, **State Government**, **NCLP** and **Convergence**.
xa: PENCIL = **Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour**.
Adoption is handled by **CARA** (statutory under the **JJ Act 2015**) and the **District Magistrate**.
PENCIL launched on **26 Sep 2017**.

138.s:
Arrange the following stages in the usual child-labour intervention process in the correct order:
A. Rehabilitation
B. Identification
C. Rescue
D. Provision of education, health and psychosocial support
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
138.x: The process begins with identification, followed by rescue and rehabilitation; rehabilitation includes education, health and psychosocial support.
138.tq: Start with the first operational stage and then place the rescue and rehabilitation stages.
xs: The order is **B, C, A, D** — **identification → rescue → rehabilitation** — option **(1)** is correct.
Rehabilitation provides **education, health and psychosocial support**.
xa: Identification: inspections by **labour inspectors**, police and NGOs.
**State Governments** implement; the Centre frames policy.
Tools: labour inspectors, **surprise inspections**, rescue and rehabilitation.

138.s: The National Child Labour Project was started in:
138.x: The National Child Labour Project was started in 1988.
138.tq: Distinguish the NCLP’s start year from the years of the Gurupadswamy Committee and National Policy on Child Labour.
xs: The **National Child Labour Project** started in **1988** — option **(3)** is correct.
**1979** = Gurupadswamy Committee; **1987** = National Policy on Child Labour; **1992** = India acceded to the UNCRC.
xa: NCLP is under **MoLE**, not MoSJE (UPSC **2007** key).
**Special Training Centres** serve rescued children aged **9-14** with bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and stipend.
NCLP was **merged into Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

138.s: The National Child Labour Project is run by the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
138.x: The NCLP is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment, not the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
138.tq: Apply the ‘wrong ministry’ trap by separating labour administration from social-justice administration.
xs: The **NCLP** is run by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** (MoLE) — option **(2)** is correct.
It is **not** under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** (MoSJE) — the UPSC **2007** key.
xa: NCLP started in **1988**.
⚠ **PENCiL** is also MoLE (**2017**); the **POCSO e-Box** is NCPCR (**2016**).
NCLP was **merged into Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**.

138.s: The principal objective of the National Child Labour Project is to:
o: Transfer all rescued children directly to juvenile courts
Regulate adult employment in hazardous industries
Withdraw children from labour and provide education and vocational training
Provide only financial compensation to employers
138.x: The NCLP withdraws children from labour and provides education and vocational training.
138.tq: Identify the scheme by its combined withdrawal, education and vocational-training objective.
xs: The NCLP aims to **withdraw children from labour** and give them **education and vocational training** — option **(3)** is correct.
It does not send children to juvenile courts, regulate adult work or compensate employers.
xa: **Special Training Centres** serve rescued children aged **9-14** before regular school.
They give **bridge education**, vocational training, **mid-day meal** and a **stipend**.
NCLP began in **1988** under **MoLE**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Child Labour Project (NCLP):
1. Its Special Training Centres cater to rescued children aged 9-14 before they enter regular school.
2. The Special Training Centres provide bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and a stipend.
3. The NCLP was merged into Samagra Shiksha from 2018-19.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
138.x: Statement 1 is correct: STCs are for rescued children aged 9-14. Statement 2 is correct: they give bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and stipend. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCLP was merged into Samagra Shiksha from 2021-22 (2018 is when Samagra Shiksha itself began). Hence only 1 and 2.
138.tq: Do not confuse Samagra Shiksha's start (2018) with NCLP's merger into it (2021-22).
xs: Statements **1 and 2** are correct — option **(2)**.
Statement 1 is correct: **Special Training Centres** are for rescued children aged **9-14** before regular school.
Statement 2 is correct: they give **bridge education, vocational training, mid-day meal and stipend**.
Statement 3 is wrong: NCLP merged into **Samagra Shiksha** from **2021-22**, not 2018-19.
xa: NCLP started in **1988**, under **MoLE**.
Process: **identification → rescue → rehabilitation**.
**India rescues**: **40,000+** children in **2024-25**.

138.s: Which online portal was launched in 2017 for effective enforcement of the amended Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act?
138.x: PENCiL (Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment on 26 September 2017. SPARC, SRIJAN and YUKTI are the wrong options used in the APPSC-G2 2025 question and are unrelated to child-labour enforcement.
138.tq: Child labour enforcement portal = PENCiL (MoLE, 2017).
xs: **PENCiL** was launched in **2017** to enforce the amended Child and Adolescent Labour Act — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **SPARC**, **SRIJAN** and **YUKTI** were the wrong options in the APPSC-G2 **2025** question.
xa: PENCiL = **Platform for Effective Enforcement for No Child Labour**.
Launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** on **26 Sep 2017**.
Components: **Child Tracking System**, **Complaint Corner**, State Government, **NCLP**, **Convergence**.

138.s: The judgment in M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) is popularly associated with which case?
138.x: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996) is associated with the Sivakasi case involving child labour in hazardous industries.
138.tq: Identify the landmark case through its popularly associated location or event.
xs: **M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)** concerned the **Sivakasi** units — option **(2)** is correct.
The **Delhi gang rape case (2012)** led to the JJ Act 2015's transfer system; construction-labour is **PUDR v. UoI (1982)**.
xa: Judgment date: **10 Dec 1996**.
It banned child labour in **hazardous industries** and ordered **rehabilitation**.
Employer pays **₹20,000 per child** into a **Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund**.

138.s: With reference to the directions issued in M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu, which one of the following is correct?
o: The offending employer pays ₹20,000 per child into a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund
The offending employer pays ₹5,000 per child directly to the child as compensation
The State pays ₹20,000 per child to the employer for rehabilitation
The family pays ₹20,000 per child into a welfare fund
138.x: The employer was directed to deposit ₹20,000 for each child into the Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.
138.tq: Match the amount with the authority responsible for making the payment.
xs: The **employer** pays **₹20,000 per child** into a **Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund** — option **(1)** is correct.
**₹5,000** per child is paid by the **State** (if it cannot give an adult a job), not by the employer to the child.
xa: The **State** gives a job to an adult of the family, or pays **₹5,000** per child.
The child gets **education**.
UPPSC **2003** key "All of the above": the **Constitution**, the SC judgment of **10 Dec 1996** and the **UN Charter**.

138.s: Which of the following directions was NOT associated with the Supreme Court’s Sivakasi directions?
o: Provision of education to the child
Automatic imprisonment of every employer without any welfare-fund contribution
Withdrawal of children from hazardous industries
138.x: The directions included withdrawal, rehabilitation, education and monetary contributions to the welfare fund. Automatic imprisonment without the specified welfare-fund arrangement was not the stated direction.
138.tq: Find the option that introduces a remedy not included in the stated judicial directions.
xs: **Automatic imprisonment** of every employer without a fund contribution was not a direction — option **(3)** is correct.
The SC ordered **withdrawal** of children from hazardous industries, **rehabilitation** and **education**.
xa: Employer pays **₹20,000 per child** to the welfare fund.
State gives a job to an adult of the family, or pays **₹5,000** per child.
The case concerned the **Sivakasi** units (**1996**).

138.s: Which one of the following cases held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights?
o: M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
138.x: PUDR v. Union of India (1982) held that child labour in construction violates fundamental rights.
138.tq: Use the case-year pairing to distinguish judicial precedents.
xs: **PUDR v. Union of India (1982)** held child labour in **construction** violates **Fundamental Rights** — option **(1)** is correct.
**M.C. Mehta (1996)** concerned **hazardous industries** at Sivakasi; **Bachpan Bachao Andolan (2011)** stressed stricter enforcement and rescue.
xa: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. UoI (**2011**): **rescue and rehabilitation** of child labourers.
M.C. Mehta: employer pays **₹20,000 per child**.
**NCPCR** was set up in **2007** under the **CPCR Act 2005** — a body, not a case.

138.s: Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011) is associated with which of the following?
o: Minimum age for admission to employment
Stricter enforcement, rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers
138.x: The 2011 Bachpan Bachao Andolan case emphasised stricter enforcement and the rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers.
138.tq: Match the case with its distinctive judicial emphasis rather than its subject alone.
xs: **Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. UoI (2011)** is about **stricter enforcement, rescue and rehabilitation of child labourers** — option **(3)** is correct.
Minimum age for employment is **ILO Convention 138**; uniform age **18** came with the **JJ Act 2000**.
xa: **PUDR v. UoI (1982)**: child labour in construction violates Fundamental Rights.
**M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)**: ban in **hazardous industries**.
**World Day Against Child Labour**: **12 June**.

138.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (ILO Convention)
 a. Convention No. 138
 b. Convention No. 182

List-II (Subject)
 i. Worst Forms of Child Labour
 ii. Minimum Age for Employment

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
138.x: ILO Convention No. 138 concerns the Minimum Age for Employment, whereas Convention No. 182 concerns the Worst Forms of Child Labour.
138.tq: Start with the convention numbers and match them to their distinctive subjects.
xs: **a–ii, b–i** — option **(2)** is correct.
**ILO Convention 138** (**1973**) = **minimum age** for admission to employment.
**ILO Convention 182** (**1999**) = **worst forms of child labour**.
xa: India ratified both in **2017**, to back "No Child Labour".
⚠ **138** = minimum age; **182** = worst forms.
**World Day Against Child Labour**: **12 June**.

138.s: In which year did India ratify both ILO Convention No. 138 and ILO Convention No. 182?
138.x: India ratified both ILO Convention No. 138 and Convention No. 182 in 2017.
138.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern.
xs: India ratified **ILO 138** and **ILO 182** in **2017** — option **(3)** is correct.
Both were ratified to back **"No Child Labour"**.
xa: Convention **138** (**1973**) = minimum age; **182** (**1999**) = worst forms.
**PENCiL** was also launched in **2017**.
India acceded to the **UNCRC** in **1992**.

138.s: Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, a child is generally understood as a person below which age?
138.x: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child treats a child as a person below 18 years of age.
138.tq: Distinguish the international child-rights age threshold from domestic employment thresholds.
xs: The **UN CRC** defines a child as a person **below 18 years** — option **(3)** is correct.
India acceded to the **UNCRC in 1992**.
xa: **National Policy for Children 2013** also treats everyone below **18** as a child.
POCSO: child = below **18**, gender-neutral.
Related instruments: **UN CRC** and **Palermo Protocol**.

138.s: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on:
138.x: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on 12 June.
138.tq: Recall the specific international observance date.
xs: The **World Day Against Child Labour** is on **12 June** — option **(4)** is correct.
The notes give no other date for this day; the other options are not linked to child labour in the notes.
xa: **ILO 138** = minimum age; **ILO 182** = worst forms of child labour; India ratified both in **2017**.
Global child labour: **137.6 million** in **2024** (**54 M** in hazardous work).
⚠ **10 Dec 1996** is the date of the M.C. Mehta (Sivakasi) judgment.

138.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Juvenile Justice Boards are headed by a
138.x: In Andhra Pradesh, Juvenile Justice Boards are headed by a female Principal Magistrate.
138.tq: Test the specific Andhra Pradesh institutional arrangement rather than the general national structure.
xs: AP JJBs are headed by a **female Principal Magistrate** — option **(1)** is correct.
The **CWC** has a Chairperson; the **District Collector** and police are not JJB heads.
xa: JJB = Principal Magistrate + **2 social workers**, at least one a woman.
JJBs function in the **erstwhile 13 districts**; selection done in the **13 new districts**.
AP CWCs handled **4,189** cases and disposed **3,691** in FY **2025-26**.

138.s:
Consider the following statements about the functioning of Juvenile Justice Boards in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Boards were functioning in the erstwhile 13 districts.
2. Selection was undertaken for Child Welfare Committees and Juvenile Justice Boards in the 13 new districts.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Juvenile Welfare Department also implements the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
138.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh had Boards in the erstwhile 13 districts, undertook selection for bodies in the 13 new districts, and its Juvenile Welfare Department also runs the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958.
138.tq: Combine administrative structure, reorganisation and departmental responsibility.
xs: **All three** statements are correct — option **(4)**.
Statement 1: JJBs function in the **erstwhile 13 districts**.
Statement 2: selection for **CWCs and JJBs** was done in the **13 new districts**.
Statement 3: the **AP Juvenile Welfare dept** also runs the **Probation of Offenders Act, 1958**.
xa: AP JJBs are headed by a **female Principal Magistrate**.
**55** children declared legally free for adoption in FY **2025-26**.
**Mission Vatsalya** funds JJBs and CWCs in every district.

138.s: Operation Chinnari-Thalli, launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026, primarily targets which of the following?
138.x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli was launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026 to target sexual offences against children.
138.tq: Identify the programme from its stated objective and implementing agency.
xs: **Operation Chinnari-Thalli** (AP Police, Feb **2026**) targets **sexual offences against children** — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **Operation Muskaan** is the rescue of children from urban hubs, not sexual offences.
xa: It keeps **Sexual Offender Sheets**.
Aim: **zero pendency** in POCSO cases; chargesheets within **60 days**.
"Good touch-bad touch" awareness by the **Women & Child Safety Wing**.

138.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Operation Chinnari-Thalli?
o: Providing free coaching for competitive examinations
Achieving zero pendency in POCSO cases
138.x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli includes Sexual Offender Sheets, zero pendency in POCSO cases and chargesheets within 60 days. Free coaching for competitive examinations is not one of its stated features.
138.tq: Find the option unrelated to the programme’s stated functions.
xs: **Free coaching for competitive examinations** is not part of Chinnari-Thalli — option **(3)** is correct.
Its features: **Sexual Offender Sheets**, **zero pendency** in POCSO cases, chargesheets within **60 days**.
xa: It was launched by the **AP Police** in Feb **2026**.
"Good touch-bad touch" awareness in schools and hostels by the **Women & Child Safety Wing**.
⚠ **Muskaan** rescued over **1,200 children** from urban hubs.

138.s: The “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programme in schools and hostels in Andhra Pradesh is conducted by which wing?
138.x: The Women & Child Safety Wing conducts “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programmes in schools and hostels.
138.tq: Match the activity with the specialised administrative wing.
xs: The **Women & Child Safety Wing** runs "Good touch-bad touch" awareness — option **(2)** is correct.
It is part of **Operation Chinnari-Thalli** in schools and hostels.
xa: Chinnari-Thalli targets **sexual offences against children**.
Chargesheets within **60 days**; **zero pendency** in POCSO cases.
**APSES 2024-25**: **342** street children rescued; **877** child marriages prevented.

138.s: A Private Member’s Bill reported in December 2025 sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold under the juvenile justice framework from:
138.x: The Bill sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold from 16 years to 14 years.
138.tq: Track the direction and magnitude of the proposed age change.
xs: The **Private Member's Bill (Dec 2025)** seeks to lower it from **16 to 14** years — option **(3)** is correct.
⚠ **18 to 16** is the earlier standing-committee recommendation (APPSC **2022**).
xa: Under the JJ Act 2015, **16-18**-year-olds accused of heinous offences can be transferred.
